**About Our Internship Program**Zoox's internship program offers hands-on experience with cutting-edge technology, mentorship from some of the industry's brightest minds, and the opportunity to make meaningful contributions to real projects. We seek interns who demonstrate strong academic performance, engagement beyond the classroom, intellectual curiosity, and a genuine interest in Zoox's mission. **Job Description**Data Science turns Zoox's driving, fleet and business data into decisions and automation. As a Data Scientist Intern, you may be assigned to one of the following teams: - Autonomy Software V&V: You will work on fleet metrics, behavior analysis, and performance evaluation of our autonomous vehicles. Analyze real-world driving data to identify patterns, measure autonomy performance, and inform stack improvements. Contribute to metrics platforms that track miles-per-disengagement, driving behavior clusters (PUDO, lane changes, pullovers), and safety-critical events across our L3 development and production service fleets. - Core/Domain Data Science: You will provide data solutions to deliver domain-specific analytical insights. In this role, you will have the opportunity to perform data analysis to develop and validate the simulation framework evaluating Zoox’s autonomous driving software. You collaborate with key stakeholders in the Simulation team to gain insight into the safety and comfort performance of our robotaxi. This internship will provide you with hands-on experience in building performance metrics and conducting in-depth data analyses, contributing to data-driven decision-making within the cutting-edge field of autonomous vehicles. ### In this Role, You Will... - Use coding and analytical skills to derive insights that inform decisions and automation - Test new frameworks and algorithms to improve model performance - Work on a project such as drift monitoring, automated model retraining, predictive modeling, similarity search or statistical testing ### Internship Requirements - Currently working towards a B.S., M.S., Ph.D., or advanced degree in data science, statistics, computer science, or a related engineering program - Good academic standing - Expected to graduate between Fall 2027 and Summer 2028, and enrolled at an accredited college or university throughout the internship - Able to commit to a full-time, 12-week internship beginning in May/June 2027 - Ability to relocate to the Bay Area, California, for the duration of the internship - Interns at Zoox may not use any proprietary information they are working on as part of their thesis, any published work with their university, or to be distributed to anyone outside of Zoox ### Qualifications - Proficiency in Python and SQL - Coursework in machine learning, computer vision, or NLP - Familiarity with software-engineering practices such as Git, unit testing, debugging, and code reviews - Understanding of supervised learning, model evaluation, and common sources of dataset bias and label noise. - Experience with data analysis and visualization - Ability to communicate data clearly to different audiences ### Bonus Qualifications - Experience with Databricks, Spark or cloud data tools - Experience with dashboarding or experiment design - Experience working with LLMs

**About Our Internship Program** Zoox's internship program offers hands-on experience with cutting-edge technology, mentorship from some of the industry's brightest minds, and the opportunity to make meaningful contributions to real projects. We seek interns who demonstrate strong academic performance, engagement beyond the classroom, intellectual curiosity, and a genuine interest in Zoox's mission. **Job Description** As an intern in the Infrastructure Operations team within Fleet Operations, you will support the critical infrastructure that keeps Zoox’s autonomous robotaxi fleet charged, serviced, and operating seamlessly. You will bridge operations, facilities, and engineering to tackle complex infrastructure readiness challenges across multiple depot sites and multi-generation vehicle platforms. ### In this Role, You Will… - Comfort working in a fast-paced, high-growth, and collaborative environment. ### Bonus Qualifications - Prior professional experience in the transportation, mobility, logistics, or automotive sectors. - Experience building complex financial, cost, or capacity models. - Background in operational strategy, program management, or supply chain infrastructure.

**Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The [AI & Human Systems](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/group/ai-human-systems/) group at Microsoft Research New York City (MSR NYC) and Microsoft Research New England (MSR NE) is seeking multiple Research Interns. AI & Human Systems brings together researchers and applied scientists who have been part of the [Fairness, Accountability, Transparency, and Ethics in AI](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/theme/fate/) (FATE), [Sociotechnical Alignment Center](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/group/stac-sociotechnical-alignment-center/) (STAC), [Economics and Computation](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/theme/economics-and-computation/), and [Computational Social Science](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/theme/computational-social-science/) (CSS) groups. This posting is for candidates interested in working with researchers and applied scientists across any of these areas. Group members collaborate extensively with one another and with other groups across Microsoft. The group shares a common goal: a world where AI boosts productivity, accelerates innovation, and helps people flourish by focusing their attention, enhancing their capabilities, and safeguarding their agency. Research Interns will contribute to this goal by working with mentors on research that advances it. Our research draws on diverse disciplinary perspectives to study, measure, and design AI systems and understand their effects on people, teams, organizations, markets, economies, and societies. Topics include, but are not limited to: AI measurement and evaluation; measuring the impacts of AI on individuals, organizations, and society; human–AI interaction and meaningful human engagement with AI; and the design of agentic systems, markets, and institutions that shape how AI participates in the economy and society. Applicants should demonstrate an interest in studying AI and human systems, a desire to work in a highly interdisciplinary environment, and experience using AI to thoughtfully enhance their own research. We welcome applicants pursuing a doctoral degree in technical fields (e.g., machine learning, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, statistics, computer science), economics, computational social science, or sociotechnical fields (e.g., human–computer interaction, information science, law, linguistics, science and technology studies) as well as JD candidates. Applicants should be proficient with AI tools. **Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We recommend submitting by December 1, 2026.** **Responsibilities** Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. **Qualifications** #### Required Qualifications - Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in a related field. **Other Requirements** - Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. - In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. - All applicants must submit a cover letter, which we will use to route your application to the appropriate researchers for review. Our group collaborates frequently across disciplines, but we also understand the value of pairing interns with mentors who work with similar vocabularies and tools. Because this document is for routing only, please do not invest much time in it and include only the information requested below. We are hiring for a wide variety of projects, and different projects require different skills, so it is fine to answer "not applicable." - Please explicitly list in your cover letter: 1. 1. A link to your research website/publications 2. Which of the following topic areas you are interested in (list all that are applicable): AI measurement and evaluation; measuring the impacts of AI on individuals, organizations, and society; human–AI interaction and meaningful human engagement with AI; or the design of agentic systems, markets, and institutions that shape how AI participates in the economy and society 3. What field is your PhD in 4. What kinds of methodologies you have applied in your research or are most familiar with (e.g., coding, statistics, large scale data analysis, theoretical/mathematical analysis, user studies, experimental design, ethnography) 5. Key toolkits, if applicable: web development (e.g., JavaScript, React.js, D3.js, etc.), analytic toolsets (e.g., R, Python, etc.), etc. 6. If appropriate, a link to any online code repositories (e.g., GitHub, OSF, Hugging Face) 7. Any researchers you are particularly interested in working with (and explain why in one sentence) To submit your cover letter, please navigate to the Action Center in your Careers Profile. You can upload other documents under the “Resume Manager” tab in the top right. #### Preferred Qualifications - Demonstrated ability to conduct original research. - Ability to collaborate effectively with other researchers and product development teams. - Demonstrated interpersonal skills and cross-group and cross-cultural collaboration. - Ability to think unconventionally to derive creative and innovative solutions. - Proficiency with AI tools. The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. ## **About Parspec** Founded in 2021, Parspec is revolutionizing the materials supply chain for the $13 trillion USD construction industry by digitizing and organizing the industry's product data. Our proprietary AI technology maintains a current and comprehensive catalogue of millions of products, enabling our customers to identify products that best meet their needs–instantly. Trusted by top designers, builders, distributors, manufacturers, and sales agents, and backed by leading venture investors, Parspec is paving the way for a more innovative, connected, and sustainable future in construction. Join us in building transformative technology that reshapes one of the world’s oldest and largest industries. ## **The Opportunity** We’re seeking an **Applied AI Engineer Intern** to join Parspec. This role is part of the **AI team** and works closely with **Product and Engineering** on fast-moving, real-world applications of AI. As an intern, you’ll apply modern AI and machine learning techniques to concrete product problems, such as understanding product specifications, improving product recommendations, and exploring early agentic AI workflows, while learning how AI systems are designed, built, evaluated, and shipped in the real world. This is an ideal role for a student who wants hands-on experience applying AI to complex, messy industry data and customer-facing product workflows. ## **What You Will Achieve and Key Responsibilities** - Contribute to AI-driven initiatives, from problem framing through experimentation and implementation - Build, prototype, evaluate, and iterate on models and AI-powered workflows used in customer-facing product features - Partner with Senior Applied AI Engineers and Product Managers to translate real customer problems into clear technical approaches and tradeoffs - Analyze structured and unstructured data (e.g., product specifications, documents, metadata) to improve model performance - Document assumptions, results, and learnings to support cross-functional alignment and decision-making ## **Why This Matters** Construction remains one of the world’s largest and least digitized industries. Construction teams rely on manual workflows to interpret product specifications, identify suitable materials, compare options, and make procurement decisions. Parspec applies AI to power workflows that help stakeholders evaluate products, surface better options, and act with confidence. As an Applied AI Engineer Intern, your work will directly support these capabilities and the decisions they enable. ## **Who You Are** You’re excited about applying AI to real-world problems that don’t come neatly packaged. You enjoy breaking down complex systems, working with imperfect data, and experimenting to find practical solutions. You’re curious, technically grounded, and comfortable collaborating with Product and Engineering partners to balance model performance, system constraints, and customer impact. **Qualifications** - Currently enrolled in a US-based, degree-seeking program (Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD) in Engineering, Computer Science, or related fields - Strong familiarity with core ML/AI concepts and tooling, such as model training(LoRA/QLoRA) and evaluation, embeddings, RAG systems, agentic frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI or related techniques. - Strong familiarity with ranking and recommendations techniques. - Hands-on experience applying AI or machine learning to real-world projects, including working with imperfect data, making tradeoffs, and iterating based on results - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills - Ability to work effectively in ambiguous problem spaces with guidance and mentorship - Clear written and verbal communication skills for technical and non-technical audiences. **Preferred Qualifications** - Exposure to B2B SaaS products, especially workflow-heavy or operations-focused software - Interest in or exposure to construction industry workflows, including materials procurement ## **What We Offer** - Competitive stipend for the duration of the internship - Hands-on ownership of meaningful product work that directly impacts customers - Mentorship from experienced Product, Design, and Engineering leaders - Flexible hybrid work environment to support both in-office collaboration and focused remote work - Exposure to a fast-growing AI-powered B2B SaaS company and real-world product decision-making - Opportunities for learning and professional development through regular feedback and collaboration ## **Join Us and Lead the Transformation!** At Parspec, we recognize that traditional job descriptions don’t always capture the full range of your unique abilities—and that’s perfectly okay. You may not meet every requirement, but if you bring a mix of experiences, fresh perspectives, and a passion that aligns with our mission, we want to hear from you! The Parspec team believes that varied backgrounds drive better outcomes and fuel innovation. We are a team of self-starters who lead from every seat. We think big, set a standard of excellence, and are committed to diversity and a discrimination-free workplace. We welcome applicants from all walks of life to join us and help shape the future of our industry.

role: Director, CMC Product Development - Late Stage, Operations
description: Purpose The Product Development Director (PDD) will be a member of the Operations Strategy & Pipeline Leadership (OSPL) team within the Product Development, Science & Technology (PDS&T) organization. Reporting to one of the Therapeutic Area Leads, the PDD will be responsible for pipeline programs from a Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC) perspective. They will lead the Product Presentation and Device Strategy Team (PPDST) and build the CMC development strategy for the late-stage assets, aligning with the clinical and regulatory development strategy from the Asset Strategy Team (AST). The programs can span modalities and presentations. Modalities can include small molecules, biologics (protein, gene therapy, toxin etc.) and antibody drug conjugates. Product presentations can include oral dose, parenteral and devices (therapeutics and aesthetic). The PDD is accountable for creating a CMC development plan in collaboration with line functions and ensures strategic alignment with the enterprise functions (Clinical, Regulatory and Commercial) cross-functionally at the AST. The PDD is the spokesperson for CMC-related aspects at asset-level governances and represents the assets within Operations to ensure support of late-stage development activities and readiness for launch. They are responsible for communicating development and regulatory risks and seeking feedback from CMC leadership. Responsibilities Represents all CMC areas on the AST serving as spokesperson for the CMC project team and ensures information flow among the AST and all line functions. Ensures high quality science, technology, deliverables, and collaborates to ensure compliance with global regulatory and quality requirements. Participates in interactions with Regulatory and Health Authorities. Critically evaluates and integrates drug substance, drug product, and device inputs to CMC team strategies and plans that align with corporate business objectives. Decision-making will often require assessment and integration of physical chemical properties, formulation science, engineering, analytical, and device technical information in conjunction with the project strategy, with full consideration of current regulatory and compliance requirements. Manages multiple projects and contributes to project prioritization. Negotiates for additional resources when required, influences project timelines to ensure proper completion of required activities. Implements creative approaches to conserve resources, and achieve efficiency with respect to time, and budget. Provides feedback to CMC management on resource and talent opportunities. Reviews contracts with external partners and consultants. Develops a budget in collaboration with AST and obtains resources from functional areas. Accountable for the success and overall CMC quality of a given project. Ensures timely execution of project plan to deliver high quality with respect to science, technology, compliance and cost effectiveness. Represents AbbVie on high profile partnerships and collaborations with other pharma/biotech companies and at the Joint Development Committee level driving decisions for the development programs. Promotes scientific and entrepreneurial thinking, encourage creativity and manage quality and results with respect to science, time, budget and resources. Ensures compliance with regulatory, health, safety and environmental requirements. Stay abreast of developments in global technical, regulatory and compliance arena and industry practice. Apprises CMC Management of plans and risks through regular communications and periodic reviews throughout development and in support of global filings, approvals and launches. Ensures high level of morale in the CMC team. Bachelor’s Degree with at least 18 years of experience in CMC functions required; Master’s Degree with at least 16 years of relevant CMC experience required; or PhD with at least 10 years of relevant CMC experience required to effectively manage global teams and all CMC activities with respect to science, technology, quality, regulatory/compliance requirements, budget and resources. Multiple product development experiences of leading a CMC team through regulatory submissions (NDA/BLA/PMA/510K preferred). Must possess good scientific writing skills and good verbal skills. Must have a good working knowledge of regulatory requirements and familiarity with relevant CMC development approaches. (Device regulatory requirements preferred.) Knowledge of pharmaceutical sciences and the drug/device development process. Must have CMC interdisciplinary experience and expertise. Possess negotiating, influencing and leadership skills. Creative in implementing entrepreneurial thinking and capable of making smart business decisions. college transcripts required - Strong written and verbal communication skills - Excellent research, analytical, and organizational skills - Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint - Ability to manage multiple assignments, meet deadlines, and work independently in a remote environment - Strong attention to detail and a willingness to learn new technical concepts and regulatory requirements - Internship, research, academic projects, or other experience related to environmental science or environmental consulting - Familiarity with federal, state, or local environmental regulations is preferred - Must currently hold or be able to obtain a Department of Defense Secret-level security clearance - Must be a U.S. citizen as this position is not eligible for Limited Access Authorizations

You’ll gain experience designing for complex, real-world environments while developing your product thinking, communication skills, and design craft. We expect you to bring curiosity, a developing foundation in product design, and a willingness to seek and act on feedback. Over the course of the internship, you’ll take increasing ownership of well-bounded deliverables with support from your manager and design partners. ## **How You’ll Make an Impact** - **Design for Trust:** Contribute to interfaces for autonomous flying robots that help operators understand what the system is doing and feel confident that the job will get done. - **Explore Complex Problems:** Partner with experienced designers to investigate challenges involving remote hardware sensing, 3D spatial awareness, and AI-driven missions. Use design and AI tools responsibly to explore ideas, test assumptions, and learn quickly. - **Contribute to the Team:** Participate in critiques, help document design decisions, and contribute to design-system patterns and team practices where relevant. ## **What Makes You a Great Fit** - **Portfolio or Work Samples:** You can share academic, personal, freelance, or internship projects that demonstrate your design process, problem solving, and ability to learn through iteration. - **Design Fundamentals:** You have a developing foundation in interaction design, visual design, prototyping, and user-centered problem solving. - **Prototyping Skills:** You are proficient with tools such as Figma and can turn ideas into wireframes, high-fidelity designs, or interactive prototypes. - **Curiosity and Growth:** You ask thoughtful questions, seek feedback, and are excited to build new skills in a fast-moving technical environment. - **Clear Collaboration:** You can explain your thinking, listen to different perspectives, stay organized, and work constructively with teammates from different disciplines. - **Interest in Complex Products:** You are excited by robotics, AI, hardware, mapping, navigation, or other technical products. Je duikt in alle AI Governance processen en AI-projecten die binnen KPN zijn ontwikkeld en stelt verbeteringen voor. Waar gaat het goed? Waar is nog ruimte voor verbetering? Het uitvoeren van onderzoek naar AI governance best practices, Responsible AI en relevante wet- en regelgeving. role: 2027 Summer Intern, PhD, Machine Learning - Generative World Models & Controllable Simulation
description: Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states. Software Engineering builds the brains of Waymo's fully autonomous driving technology. Our software allows the Waymo Driver to perceive the world around it, make the right decision for every situation, and deliver people safely to their destinations. We think deeply and solve complex technical challenges in areas like robotics, perception, decision-making and deep learning, while collaborating with hardware and systems engineers. If you’re a software engineer or researcher who’s curious and passionate about Level 4 autonomous driving, we'd like to meet you. Waymo interns partner with leaders in the industry on projects that create impact to the company. We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. Join us at Waymo for a fun and rewarding internship! **You will:** - Design, implement, and scale controllable generation and test-time compute algorithms, multimodal conditioning, and critic-guided flow/diffusion steering—for foundation world models. - Investigate multimodal sensor + semantic latent conditioning, and representation alignment to advance toward holistic world simulation. - Leverage learned realism critics and agentic autoresearch workflows on large-scale TPU clusters to evaluate closed-loop interactive realism, long-tail scenario synthesis, and multimodal consistency. - Write clean, modular, and well-tested JAX code in core simulation and world-modeling codebases, collaborating closely with researchers across Sim Realism, Foundation Models, and Closed-Loop Training teams. **You have:** - Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, or a related technical field, with an anticipated graduation date between December 2027 and August 2028 (returning to a degree program for at least one academic term after the internship). - Core Implementation Fluency (Mandatory): Strong tensor implementation and debugging skills in Python and JAX/Flax or PyTorch, with hands-on experience training and modifying modern neural architectures (such as Transformers, Diffusion/Flow-Matching models, or deep RL/critic networks). - Deep Research Expertise in Either: (a) Controllable Generative World / Sequence Modeling & Inference-Time Scaling (hands-on research experience in continuous flow matching / Rectified Flows, score-based diffusion guidance/steering, test-time compute / SMC, or parameter-efficient finetuning) OR (b) Multimodal Spatiotemporal Representation Learning & Closed-Loop Simulation (hands-on research experience in 4D/video tokenization, latent dynamics alignment such as REPA/DINO alignment, inverse RL / adversarial discriminators, or multi-agent trajectory modeling), with working familiarity in the other. **We prefer:** - First-author publications at top-tier machine learning, computer vision, or robotics venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ECCV, CoRL, RSS, ICRA, or equivalent venues) in generative world models, flow/diffusion steering, controllable generation, or autonomous driving simulation. - Experience with multi-agent closed-loop simulation, counterfactual/adversarial traffic generation, or Sim2Real discriminator/critic stabilization (e.g., Waymax, WOMD, NuPlan, MGAIL, or reward-hacking mitigation). - Experience profiling and scaling distributed training and inference workloads on TPUs or multi-node GPUs (such as XLA compilation, vectorized batched rollouts, and memory optimization) and interest in external conference publication on Waymax/WOMD. Note: This will be a hybrid onsite internship position. We will accept resumes on a rolling basis until the role is filled. To be in consideration for multiple roles, you will need to apply to each one individually - please apply to the top 3 roles you are interested in. The expected hourly rate for this full-time position is listed below. Interns are also eligible to participate in the Company’s generous benefits programs, subject to eligibility requirements. Hourly PhD Pay $85—$85 USD

role: Student, Co-Op/Placement (Research and Development Physicist / Biophysicist)
description: Union: Non-Union Number of vacancies: 1 New or Replacement Position: New Site: Princess Margaret Cancer Centre Department: Department of Medical Biophysics Reports to: Principal Investigator Salary Range: $20.00-$26.00 per hour Hours: 37.5 hours per week Shifts: Day Status: Temporary Full-time (4-8 months) Closing Date: November 10, 2026 Position Summary The Vitkin Lab, based at the Princess Margaret Cancer Centre (University Health Network) and the Department of Medical Biophysics, University of Toronto, develops and applies Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) to study tumour biology and the effects of novel radiotherapy techniques. We are part of an active, multidisciplinary research program investigating FLASH radiotherapy (ultra-high dose-rate irradiation) in preclinical mouse models, in close collaboration with the Radiation Medicine Program's medical physics team. We are seeking a highly motivated Co-op student to join our research team and contribute directly to in vivo FLASH irradiation studies. The student will work closely with senior research scientists, physicists, and engineers to acquire and analyze multimodal imaging data — including intravital OCT and 7T MRI — from a dorsal skinfold window chamber tumour model, to investigate how FLASH dose rate affects tumour and normal tissue microvasculature. Please note this role involves in-person laboratory and small-animal facility work at our downtown Toronto location. Students will be given specific training on all relevant laboratory, imaging, and animal-handling protocols before beginning hands-on work. The Vitkin Lab is dedicated to fostering the professional development of its trainees, and Co-op students are encouraged to participate in lab meetings, journal clubs, and other training activities taking place during their term. Duties The Co-op student will apply their scientific and technical skill set to support an active in vivo FLASH radiotherapy research program. They will work closely with senior lab members, under direct supervision, to advance project objectives and milestones. The main responsibilities of the position are listed below, but may be expanded upon based on the experience level of the candidate: Assist senior scientists and engineers in the design and execution of in vivo FLASH irradiation experiments using the dorsal skinfold window chamber mouse model Support animal preparation, handling, and monitoring in accordance with institutional animal care protocols Acquire longitudinal tumour and vascular imaging data using the lab's optical coherence tomography (OCT) system Assist with image acquisition on the 7T small-animal MRI system Process, analyze, and quantify imaging data using MATLAB and/or Python Assist in experimental design, including irradiation scheduling, imaging timepoints, and control-group planning Contribute to manuscript writing, including drafting sections, literature review, and reference management Produce publication-quality figures and data visualizations summarizing experimental results Prepare presentation materials (PowerPoint slides) for lab meetings, collaborator updates, and conferences Participate actively in weekly group meetings and present progress updates Accurately document all experiments, protocols, and results in laboratory notebooks/electronic records Perform all work in a safe manner and maintain a clean, organized laboratory and imaging workspace Work in accordance with approved protocols and standard operating procedures (SOPs) Other duties as assigned University student in Biomedical Engineering, Engineering Science, Medical Biophysics, Physics, or a related program Experience working in a research laboratory is preferred Strong interpersonal and communication skills (both oral and written), including experience or interest in scientific writing Must be a detail-oriented individual with excellent organizational skills and critical thinking Self-motivated individual with the ability to meet deadlines and prioritize across multiple concurrent projects Proficiency in MATLAB and/or Python for scientific data analysis is an asset Experience with optical imaging techniques (e.g., fluorescence, microscopy) and/or MRI is an asset Prior experience with small-animal handling or in vivo research is an asset (training will be provided) Familiarity with radiation biology, radiotherapy physics, or tumour vascular biology is an asset but not required Why join UHN? In addition to working alongside some of the most talented and inspiring healthcare professionals in the world, UHN offers a wide range of benefits, programs and perks. It is the comprehensiveness of these offerings that makes it a differentiating factor, allowing you to find value where it matters most to you, now and throughout your career at UHN. Competitive offer packages Government organization and a member of the Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan (HOOPP ) Close access to Transit and UHN shuttle service A flexible work environment Opportunities for development and promotions within a large organization Additional perks (multiple corporate discounts including: travel, restaurants, parking, phone plans, auto insurance discounts, on-site gyms, etc.) Current UHN employees must have successfully completed their probationary period, have a good employee record along with satisfactory attendance in accordance with UHN's attendance management program, to be eligible for consideration. All applications must be submitted before the posting close date. UHN uses email to communicate with selected candidates. Please ensure you check your email regularly. At University Health Network (UHN), artificial intelligence technologies may be used to assist in the screening, assessment, and selection of candidates for this position. Please be advised that a Criminal Record Check may be required of the successful candidate. Should it be determined that any information provided by a candidate be misleading, inaccurate or incorrect, UHN reserves the right to discontinue with the consideration of their application. UHN is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive recruitment process and workplace. Requests for accommodation can be made at any stage of the recruitment process. Applicants need to make their requirements known. We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted. UHN is Canada’s #1 hospital and the world’s #1 publicly funded hospital. With 10 sites and more than 44,000 TeamUHN members, UHN consists of Toronto General Hospital, Toronto Western Hospital, Princess Margaret Cancer Centre, Toronto Rehabilitation Institute, The Michener Institute of Education and West Park Healthcare Centre. As Canada's top research hospital, the scope of biomedical research and complexity of cases at UHN have made it a national and international source for discovery, education and patient care. UHN has the largest hospital-based research program in Canada, with major research in neurosciences, cardiology, transplantation, oncology, surgical innovation, infectious diseases, genomic medicine and rehabilitation medicine. UHN is a research hospital affiliated with the University of Toronto. UHN’s vision is to build A Healthier World and it’s only because of the talented and dedicated people who work here that we are continually bringing that vision closer to reality.

role: Stage - Business Analyst - Energie & Telecom - Nantes
location: Saint-Herblain, Pays de la Loire, France
description: En pleine transition énergétique, Sopra Steria accompagne les acteurs majeurs du marché de l’énergie dans leurs démarches afin de répondre aux enjeux sociaux, écologiques et environnementaux. Vous intégrerez un collectif travaillant pour un acteur majeur de l'électricité. Ce GRT (gestionnaire du réseau de transport) assure 100% du transport de l’électricité sur le territoire français métropolitain. Sa mission principale consiste à garantir en permanence l'équilibre entre l'offre et la demande d'électricité sur l'ensemble du réseau national. Par ailleurs, il est responsable du renouvellement d'un réseau vieillissant, de son adaptation aux changements climatiques (+4°C d’ici 2100), ainsi que du raccordement des nouveaux moyens de production et des usages émergents. Votre rôle et vos missions Intégré(e) dans une équipe agile, dynamique et soudée, vous serez guidé(e) et formé(e) tout au long de cette aventure ! Ce stage vous permettra de découvrir concrètement le métier de Business Analyst sur un projet à fort enjeu métier et technologique. Vous réaliserez les activités suivantes : L'analyse des besoins métiers et la formalisation en exigences fonctionnelles La rédaction de spécifications fonctionnelles détaillées La présentation des évolutions lors de séances d’affinage et le support quotidien à l’équipe La rédaction des tests fonctionnels et leur exécution dans les règles de l’art Le suivi de l’avancement de la qualification interne et l’analyse des anomalies associées L’analyse des retours de recette métier Le support aux utilisateurs et parties prenantes La mise en œuvre de l’IA sur les différentes activités du Business Analyst Apports du stage Renforcer vos compétences techniques et méthodologiques à travers des projets concrets et innovants. WHAT YOU WILL BE WORKING ON Your main challenge As a Game Cinematic Artist Intern , you will join our team in Barcelona and learn how cinematic sequences are created and implemented directly inside a real-time game engine. Working alongside our artists and game team, you will help create compelling camera shots and sequences for our games, from race introductions and menu sequences to in-game cinematics. You will develop your eye for framing, composition and visual storytelling while gaining hands-on experience with our cinematic tools and pipelines. What it means on a daily basis Create and adapt 3D camera shots and cinematic sequences inside our real-time game engine, including race intros, menu sequences and in-game cinematics. Work with 3D characters, vehicles and other game assets , positioning them within scenes and finding the best framing and composition. Learn and work with our existing real-time cinematic tools and pipelines , maintaining and updating sequences as the game evolves. Review and test your work directly in-game, identifying visual or technical issues and making the necessary adjustments. Collaborate with the game and art teams, responding to feedback and supporting new cinematic needs throughout production. WHAT SUCCESS WILL LOOK LIKE In your first 3 months , you will become familiar with our game engine, cinematic pipeline and existing camera sequences, progressively contributing your own shots with guidance from the team. As you progress , you will develop a stronger understanding of real-time cinematics and visual storytelling while contributing polished camera work that enhances the presentation of our games. WHO YOU WOULD BE WORKING WITH You will work closely with our Art and Game teams in Barcelona , collaborating with the people responsible for the characters, environments and game content featured in your cinematic sequences. You will receive guidance from experienced team members while gradually taking more ownership of your work as you become familiar with our tools and pipelines. YOUR RECRUITMENT JOURNEY Recruiter interview Portfolio/showreel review by our Hiring team Hiring Manager interview WHERE THIS ROLE CAN TAKE YOU This internship will give you practical experience in real-time cinematics within a professional game development environment , developing transferable skills in camera work, composition, 3D workflows and visual storytelling. You will also gain exposure to how Art and Game teams collaborate to take cinematic content from an initial idea to its final implementation in-game. WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED Basic understanding of 3D environments and workflows , including navigating scenes and manipulating 3D objects. Understanding of camera composition, framing and visual storytelling in a 3D environment. Familiarity with at least one real-time game engine , such as Unity or Unreal Engine. Ability to understand how positioning, framing and camera movement can help present 3D characters, vehicles and environments effectively. Good attention to both visual and technical details . Good level of English . Ability to sign an internship agreement with a school or university . WHO YOU ARE Curious about video games, film and visual storytelling . Eager to learn new tools, workflows and technical pipelines. Creative, with a good eye for composition and presentation. Comfortable receiving feedback and iterating on your work. Organized and able to work towards deadlines. Proactive while knowing when to ask the team for guidance. Detail-oriented and willing to test and review your own work. WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU​ Benefits Flexible schedule adapted to your student needs Flexible work from home hybrid model Life at Gameloft Our Barcelona studio offers real career development opportunities and a positive working environment in a centrally located office. We value supportive working conditions and a balanced work-life approach, and our teams work together with a collaborative mindset. Ready to level up your career? Apply now with your CV in English.

Navigate and contribute to an extremely large, complex codebase, applying knowledge of the Web security model and Chromium's architecture - Work with Web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) to develop and validate browser features - Collaborate async with a geographically-distributed, open source team using Git and GitHub ### **Working at Brave - What we offer** - Ability to work remotely at an exciting and well-funded international startup headquartered in San Francisco - Cutting-edge technology, allowing you to work with state-of-the-art tools and software solutions - Competitive compensation of $6000.00 per month for 4 months. - Great international exposure and team atmosphere **If you are currently a student at Waterloo University, we would love to hear from you. Die Sicherheit der BEW Berliner Energie und Wärme GmbH und ihrer Beschäftigten ist von grundlegender Bedeutung. Aus diesem Grund ist ein Pre-Employment Screening Teil des Rekrutierungsprozesses. Der Umfang der Überprüfung variiert je nach Funktion und Einsatzbereich. Das Screening wird von einem Drittanbieter, Signum Consulting GmbH, DISA, durchgeführt. * Damit meinen wir eine Wärmeversorgung aus erneuerbaren Energien, aus unvermeidbarer Abwärme oder einer Kombination aus beidem im Sinne des § 31 i. v. m. § 3 Abs. 1 Nr. 13, 15 und Abs. 4 Wärmeplanungsgesetz (WPG). Dieses Ziel wollen wir durch eine Reihe von Maßnahmen erreichen, welche wir in unserem Dekarbonisierungsfahrplan darstellen. ** Im Sinne des § 3 Abs. 1 Nr. 13 bzw. Abs. 4 Wärmeplanungsgesetz (WPG). Wärme und Energie sind unser Beitrag zur Lebensqualität – jeden Tag aufs Neue. Als BEW Berliner Energie und Wärme GmbH versorgen wir unsere Kund:innen mit Strom und Wärme. Unser Fernwärmenetz ist mit einer Länge von mehr als 2.000 Kilometern das größte Westeuropas. Wir beliefern etwa ein Drittel der Berliner Wohnungen mit Fernwärme. Mit dem Know-how unserer rund 2.400 Mitarbeitenden decken wir die gesamte Wertschöpfungskette der Fernwärme ab – von der Erzeugung über den Netzbetrieb und -ausbau bis hin zum Vertrieb. Parallel dazu arbeiten wir mit Hochdruck am Kohleausstieg bis 2030 und an einer klimaneutralen* Wärmeerzeugung ab 2045. Um dieses Ziel zu erreichen, werden wir den Anteil an erneuerbaren Energien und unvermeidbarer Abwärme** in unserem Fernwärmesystem schrittweise weiter ausbauen. Dieser Ausbau setzt einen grundlegenden Umbau vieler unserer Standorte und Anlagen voraus. Für diese Herausforderung und die damit verbundenen Aufgaben brauchen wir Menschen, die sich mit ganzer Kraft für unser gemeinsames Ziel einer lokalen Wärmewende engagieren – Menschen wie dich.

**Your Impact at LILA** This PhD-level co-op will join the Life Science AI team to contribute to applied ML research in protein engineering, including generative protein design, antibody engineering, developability, and wet-lab-informed model iteration. role: Motorsport Software and Data Analytics Graduate Intern
description: Job Description Welcome to Bosch Motorsport, a premier supplier of electronics, sensors, actuators, and engineering services to top racing series (Formula 1, IMSA, IndyCar, NASCAR, SuperGT, WEC, WRC), manufactures, and teams worldwide. Automation & Process Improvement: Develop scripts, dashboards, and automated analysis or reporting workflows using MATLAB, Python, C#, or similar tools. Required Qualifications Currently pursuing a Masters or PhD in Engineering, Computer Science, or Data Science or in a dual degree program from an accredited four-year college or university in Engineering, Computer Science, or Data Science/Analytics Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 Must be 18 years or older 3+ years of hands-on motorsport or relevant experience with vehicle, ICE and/or hybrid controls (industry, FSAE, EcoCar, etc.) Desired Qualifications Hands-on Automotive Experience: Practical, hands-on vehicle controls systems experience related to combustion engines, high voltage hybrid systems, data acquisition systems, wiring harness design, sensor application, and/or mechanical troubleshooting (e.g., project cars, Formula SAE, or shop experience). Appropriate and responsible use of AI for acceleration of both technical and daily tasks. Modeling and Simulation: Modeling and simulation experience (e.g., Matlab/Simulink) developing and refining plant models and/or developing and integration of Functional Mock-up Unit container files for Hardware-In-the-Loop or Driver-In-the-Loop test environments Automotive Communications and Networking: Foundational knowledge of automotive communications (e.g., CAN, Ethernet) and wired/wireless networking (e.g., LAN, WAN). Diagnostic Tool Proficiency: Experience with industry standard diagnostic, testing, and measurement tools (e.g., Vector tools, dSPACE products, oscilloscopes) Demonstrated Leadership & Technical Research: Project work with full end to end scope ownership in work delivery. Graduate research, technical leadership, design reports, publications, or significant independent projects related to automotive, motorsport, connectivity, simulation, telemetry, or powertrain engineering. Ideal Candidate Characteristics Motorsport Passion and Drive: Possesses a genuine enthusiasm for professional motorsport and an eagerness to make meaningful technical contributions. Proactive Self-Starter: Thrives in an agile, hands-on environment; takes initiative to ask questions, research solutions, and execute tasks with accountability. Data-Driven and Adaptable: Approaches engineering problems with objective logic, pivoting quickly when requirements change. Disciplined Team Player: Communicates test observations and data findings clearly (both verbally and in writing) while collaborating seamlessly within a multi-disciplinary team. Curiosity and Growth Mindset: Eager to step outside of immediate academic comfort zone to learn new software skills, hardware implementations, and systems. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a drug screen and background check. Candidates who have been offered the position must pass both screenings before their start date. role: Final year Internship - CIO, Data & AI Advisory
description: En tant que stagiaire de fin d'études CIO, Data & AI Advisory , vous rejoignez l’équipe Technology Advantage de Sia. Au sein de cette Business Unit, nos équipes interviennent auprès de l’ensemble des secteurs d’activités (transport, énergie, banque & assurance, secteur public…) sur les principaux leviers de la transformation numérique. Leurs missions : Éclairer nos clients sur l’IT, l’IA et la Data face à l’évolution rapide de technologies émergentes pour les aider à définir un cap stratégique adapté à leurs besoins Cadrer, orchestrer et accompagner opérationnellement ces transformations. Dans ce contexte, vous intervenez au sein d’équipes pluridisciplinaires sur des missions variées : AI Transformation : définir la stratégie d’adoption de l’IA (évaluation de maturité, feuilles de routes IA / IA gen, réflexions stratégiques), accélérer la mise en œuvre de cas d’usage IA (identifier et prioriser des cas d’usage IA , cadrage et pilotage des projets IA, évaluation de la performance et du ROI des initiatives IA), structurer la gouvernance et l’organisation IA (modèles organisationnel et opérationnels, cadre de gouvernance te conformité…), accompagner la transformation humaine et l’adoption de l’IA (IA responsable et centrée sur l’humain). Data Advisory : définir la stratégie data, contribuer à la valorisation des cas d'usage data, mettre en place la gouvernance et l’organisation autour de la Data, mettre en place le data management, assurer le data product management (mise en œuvre d’approches data mesh, data marketplace, data virtualisation ; pilotage de projets data), mettre en place l’acculturation et la montée en compétence des équipes sur la data. CIO Advisory : définir et mettre en place l’organisation, l’operating model, définir la stratégie opérationnelle et cadrer et piloter les projets de transformation (stratégies AI driven, carve-out…), définir et mettre en œuvre les moyens pour améliorer la performance opérationnelle (AI for Dev, AI for Ops, DevSecOps…), définir l’architecture et piloter l’innovation technologique, accompagner les transformations cloud et plateformes (stratégie cloud et IA, FInOps et GreenOps…), contribuer à l’optimisation des opérations et l’ITSM et développer la performance économique. Vous êtes également amené(e) à vous impliquer dans la vie interne du cabinet, autour de différents sujets : Le développement ou le renforcement de nos offres. La politique de publication (articles, études, parutions presse...). Le développement de nouvelles activités au travers de réponses aux appels d’offres et de propositions commerciales. Diplômé(e) d’une grande école d’ingénieur, de commerce, ou d’une grande université, vous justifiez idéalement d’une première expérience dans le conseil ou dans le secteur de la transformation digitale ou de l'innovation (stage ou premier emploi). Vous souhaitez développer une expertise mêlant des dimensions métier, technologique, organisation et innovation. Vous êtes curieux(se) et aimez travailler en équipe ? Vous êtes reconnu(e) pour votre sens de l’analyse ? Vous souhaitez rejoindre un environnement professionnel dynamique et motivant ? Vous partagez nos valeurs que sont l'excellence, l'entrepreneuriat, l'innovation, le partage, la bienveillance et l'équilibre vie personnelle/vie professionnelle ? Vous parlez français et anglais couramment dans un contexte professionnel ? Alors rejoignez-nous ! Locaux situés en plein coeur de Paris. Gratification: 2400€/mois Sia propose des stages de fin d’études responsabilisants, dans une logique de pré-embauche : nous rejoindre, c’est s’ouvrir à une possibilité de CDI. Sia est un employeur qui souscrit au principe de l’égalité d’accès à l’emploi. Tous les aspects de l’emploi, tels que le recrutement, les promotions, la rémunération, ou les sanctions sont basés uniquement sur les performances, les compétences, et le comportement des employés ou les besoins de l’entreprise. Sia est un groupe international de conseil en management de nouvelle génération. Fondé en 1999, nous sommes nés à l’ère du numérique. Aujourd’hui, nos services en stratégie et management sont augmentés par la data science, enrichis par la créativité et guidés par la responsabilité. Nous sommes "optimists for change" et aidons nos clients à initier, naviguer et tirer profit des transformations. Nous croyons que l’optimisme est un accélérateur de performance, permettant de réduire les risques et de maximiser les opportunités. Grâce à une expertise couvrant de nombreux secteurs et services, nos consultants accompagnent nos clients dans le monde entier. Notre expertise produit des résultats concrets. Notre optimisme change la donne.

At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. # **Role Overview** REGENT's Viceroy and Squire Seagliders rely on actuators and drive systems that have to perform flawlessly in a demanding, real-world environment, and getting them there starts in the lab. As an **Actuation Engineering Intern**, you'll work alongside our actuation engineering team to build test setups, run evaluations, and dig into vendor documentation to assess how different actuators and drives stack up against each other. You'll spend real time with real hardware, installing actuators on test stands, building jigs, and generating the data that directly informs which components earn a place on our Seaglider product line. This role sits within our Electrical Systems team, part of Engineering & Technology, where hands-on rigor and clear-eyed evaluation matter as much as clever design. You'll be given increasing independence as the term goes on, moving from guided lab work to running your own experiments and assembling findings into a presentation that will genuinely shape the actuation approach for Viceroy and Squire. If you've got your engineering fundamentals down and are looking for a chance to apply them to real test hardware on a team that's reinventing coastal transportation, you'll feel right at home here. ## **What You'll Do** - **Build Real Test Setups:** You'll construct test stands and jigs in the actuation lab, installing actuators and drives and getting hands-on with the hardware that powers our Seagliders. - **Evaluate Actuators and Drives:** You'll run performance evaluations on actuators and drive systems, comparing them against similar models to understand tradeoffs and capabilities. - **Dig Into Vendor Documentation:** You'll interpret datasheets and manuals and work directly with vendors to understand product specifications and communication requirements. - **Talk to the Hardware:** You'll use programming tools like Python to communicate with actuators and drives, pulling data and verifying behavior firsthand. - **Support Qualification Work:** You'll help qualify actuators and drives for service on Viceroy and Squire, contributing evidence-based assessments that inform real engineering decisions. - **Work With Assemblies and CAD:** You'll navigate CAD models and help arrange actuation equipment within assemblies as part of your evaluation work. - **Present Your Findings:** You'll compile the results of your assessments into a presentation for the mechanical and electrical teams, directly shaping the actuation approach used across our product line. ## **What You'll Bring** - **Engineering Fundamentals in Place:** You're a rising senior or grad student in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, mechatronics engineering, or a related field, with the core fundamentals already solid. - **Comfort With Hand Tools:** You're mechanically inclined and comfortable working with hand tools, building jigs, and handling hardware constantly. - **Basic Programming Ability:** You have working knowledge of a language like Python, enough to communicate with actuators and drives and make sense of the data they produce. - **Clear Communicator:** You write and speak clearly, including when working with outside vendors to interpret datasheets and learn about new products. - **Bonus: Actuator or Sensor Experience:** Prior hands-on exposure to actuators, communication protocols, or sensors such as temperature, force, strain, or position would give you a real head start in this niche domain. - **Bonus: CAD and Circuits Know-How:** Experience with 3D CAD and drawings, and comfort working with low-voltage DC power circuits, means less time spent learning the basics and more time in the lab. - **Bonus: MATLAB/Simulink Exposure:** Familiarity with MATLAB or Simulink is a plus, since it's key software for post-processing actuator data and modeling actuation systems. ## **Who We're Looking For** - **Collaborative Team Player:** You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. - **Creative Problem Solver**: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. - **Adaptable & Agile:** In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. - **Innovative Mindset**: You’re driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You’re passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance. ## **What We Offer** - Competitive compensation - **Housing Stipend** available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, **free catered lunches** - **Learning & professional development** opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members **If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you.** Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. **Equal Opportunity Employer** REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. **The [mission](https://www.nytco.com/mission-and-values/) of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.** ## About Us: [Interactive News Technology](https://github.com/newsdev/about-int) is a team of developer-journalists embedded in the New York Times newsroom. We power new [story forms](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/upshot/buy-rent-calculator.html) and build tools for [newsgathering](http://www.nytco.com/introducing-tipjar-nytimes/), while also supporting [breaking news](https://www.nytimes.com/2017/05/08/insider/how-we-beat-the-house-in-tallying-the-health-care-vote.html), [exclusive reporting](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/12/insider/jeffrey-epstein-files-documents.html) and [major events](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/11/03/us/elections/results-house.html). We’re looking for a paid summer 2027 intern to contribute to software used by hundreds of NYT journalists and projects that serve millions of readers. Our unique position between the newsroom and technology departments makes us instrumental to The Times’ most ambitious digital journalism. We work with a range of web technologies, primarily JavaScript, TypeScript, React and Svelte. We run Node.js servers which talk to PostgreSQL databases. We rely on hosted Google Cloud services and serverless technologies, manage code using Git and host it on GitHub, and use A.I. tools such as Cursor and Claude. This role is focused on software engineering in a newsroom environment. Daily work will be on a software development project team. Interns often have opportunities to contribute to opportunistic data or document journalism using our tools, but the core work is not writing stories or producing graphics. Previous interns have helped to wrangle [nationwide precincts data](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/us/elections/2024-election-map-precinct-results.html) and [international election results](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/06/09/world/europe/results-european-union-parliament-election.html), pitched in on [Olympics coverage](https://www.nytimes.com/2021/08/08/sports/olympics/world-records-tokyo-olympics.html) and [results](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/world/olympics-results-medals.html), added features to our live [World](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2023/upshot/womens-world-cup-standings.html) [Cup](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/07/15/sports/world-cup/france-vs-croatia-final.html) scores and standings, built technology to help reporters reach out to a diverse set of readers, implemented customizable layout configurations for elections results pages, and helped [unravel thorny data about metro transit woes](https://www.nytimes.com/2019/09/27/nyregion/njtransit-commuter-delays.html). ## About Our Summer Internships: - The duration is 10 weeks long, starting on June 7th, 2027 - The rate of pay for this role is $40 per hour. - Interns work 35 hours per week. - This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. The intern will work from the office at least 3 days per week. - Our intern program team can provide resources and recommendations related to housing and relocation to New York. ## Responsibilities: - You will work on one or multiple projects for the summer and collaborate with developers, designers and journalists to build newsroom tools which help our journalists report and tell stories - You will contribute to technical design and development of new features within team projects, and use these tools to help with opportunistic reporting - You will receive support and mentorship to meet professional goals and accelerate your learning - You will expand your understanding of building modern, scalable, software while immersed in a newsroom environment - Demonstrate support and understanding of [our value of journalistic independence](https://www.nytco.com/mission-and-values/) and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world ## Basic Qualifications: - Experience contributing to newsgathering, reporting, editing, and/or news presentation processes - Experience in JavaScript or TypeScript - Experience taking a technical project from concept to completion, contributing to concept definition, technical design, and technical implementation - Experience working as part of a team to develop software - Familiarity with AI-assisted software development best practices - Interest in a newsroom engineering role that combines technical and editorial thinking - Support for our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world - A portfolio of work showing innovations and ideas which demonstrate that you think critically about the news, and want to shape meaningful experiences for The New York Times readers ## Preferred Qualifications: The most competitive applications will demonstrate: - Experience collaborating with others to advance the purpose and ideas of a project - Interest in using software engineering skills to push the limits of what we offer to our readers ## How to apply: Please submit **a current resume tying your experience and interests to the qualifications**. **A cover letter describing your role in the portfolio projects, and your interest in a newsroom engineering role is required**. role: Center for Global Security Research (CGSR) Undergraduate Research Associate - Summer 2027
description: The Center for Global Security Research (CGSR) was established at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in 1996 to bring together experts from the science, technology, and policy communities to address pressing national security challenges. For over 20 years, CGSR has engaged diverse perspectives on topics important to national security, deterrence, diplomacy, dual-use technology, arms control, nonproliferation, space, cyber, biosecurity, and energy security. We have openings in Summer 2027 for undergraduate students to engage in practical research on global security topics. Students will work with CGSR over the duration of three to four months as a research associate (RA). RAs will engage in practical research to further their educational and career goals, while also supporting the development of strategies for national security and LLNL’s mission focus areas. Examples of relevant fields of research include nuclear deterrence, arms control, nonproliferation, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, space, biological & chemical security, and energy security. This position offers a hybrid schedule, blending in-person and virtual presence. You will have the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week. CGSR’s objectives are as follows: To explore the dynamics of potential 21st century strategic conflicts (i.e., those with a potential nuclear aspect) and to formulate ideas about how to achieve U.S. deterrence and other objectives in such conflicts. To explore the sources and characteristics of strategic competition in the emerging security environment and to formulate organizing concepts to enhance the competitive position of the United States and its allies and partners over the long term. To identify whether and how technically based approaches can address new challenges to national and international security. To catalyze broader national and international thinking about the requirements of effective deterrence, assurance, and strategic stability in a changed and changing security environment. To assist in the development of new generations of experts motivated by a clear view of the changed and changing security environment. More information on CGSR, its research focus areas, and its publications can be found at . This job will be closed to applicants on February 1, 2027. You will Conduct an independent research project on an agreed upon topic aligned with CGSR/LLNL research priorities under the supervision of CGSR staff. Support CGSR/LLNL through contributions to ongoing research activities. Tasks may include contributing to literature reviews, annotated bibliographies, and workshop summary reports. Attend relevant research seminars, speakers’ series, and workshops. Present research to LLNL staff at end of the assignment. Prepare end-of-assignment technical report or publication. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). See Additional Information section below for details. Must be currently enrolled in an accredited university or have completed AA/AS degree in a field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Areas of study include international relations and/or security, political science, economics, public policy, emerging technologies, nonproliferation, energy, biosecurity, foreign language studies, or related fields. Demonstrated academic and/or professional achievement in a relevant field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Strong record of independent research and publication, or a strong proposal of research to be done while at CGSR and in future academic and professional settings. Ability to work in a team environment. Pay Range $23.26 - $31.62 Hourly This position is under a step structure. Major Job Duties: Performing skilled preventive and corrective maintenance on standard MEP systems and documenting deficiencies and completed work; Troubleshooting malfunctioning HVAC and BAS components to maintain operability, including seasonal winterizing and de-winterizing; Diagnosing and repairing plumbing systems, including clearing traps, snaking drains, repairing pipes, and replacing fixtures; Assessing and repairing electrical systems such as outlets, fixtures, breakers, and related components; Responding to emergency service calls for MEP, life safety, and power generation systems, including coordinating temporary generator connections; Providing shift coverage at County facilities, including the Justice Center, during regular and emergency operations; Overseeing contractors to ensure proper completion of corrective and preventive maintenance tasks; Assisting leadership with equipment assessments and providing input for the Capital Improvement Plan; and Performing other job-related duties as assigned. The ideal candidate will be a dependable team member who performs effectively in a fast-paced environment, demonstrates strong troubleshooting skills, provides excellent customer service, and is willing to work any assigned shift, including callbacks. Minimum Qualifications: High School Diploma/GED or equivalent; and Trainee At least 2 years of related experience in commercial buildings or residential high-rise environments in more than one of the following areas: plumbing, electrical, emergency management equipment such as emergency generators and/or general mechanical repairs. Building Engineer I Three (3) years of related experience in commercial buildings or a similarly complex environment in more than one of the following areas: plumbing, electrical, emergency management equipment such as emergency generators and/or general mechanical repairs. Must possess the following Licensures/Certifications within the probationary period: ARC Flash and Confined Space Certifications. Building Engineer II Four (4) years of related experience in commercial buildings or a similarly complex environment in more than one of the following areas: plumbing, electrical, emergency management equipment such as emergency generators and/or general mechanical repairs. Must possess EPA Section 608 Universal Certification, ARC Flash, and Confined Space Certifications plus one (1) of the following licensures/certifications: Journeyman or Master Electrician License(s); and/or HVAC-R (VA Licensure). Desirable Qualifications: Preference may be given to candidates with experience or licensure/certifications in one or more of the following: Performing maintenance, diagnosing and repairs to mechanical, electrical, plumbing and building maintenance systems; Diagnosing malfunctioning power generating and life safety systems; Working in an environment with varied building portfolios; Working with mobile maintenance devices to receive and complete work orders; and Using computerized building automation control systems (BAS). Special Requirements Trainee Level: If an employee is hired at the trainee level, a training period will be established to last no longer than the equivalent of 12 months. At or before the end of the training period, the employee must meet experience, training, and proficiency requirements for the Level I position. Once the candidate qualifies, they will be appointed to the position. Certifications: You must obtain and maintain ARC Flash and Confined Space certifications within a 12-month probationary period. Background Check: A pre-employment criminal records check will be conducted. It will include checks of the following: criminal record, driving record, education, professional licensure, and credit history. You will be required to sign a release authorizing the County to obtain your background information. Driver's License: Applicant must possess, and maintain, a valid driver’s license, and must provide or authorize Arlington County to obtain a copy of official driving record. Any offer of employment may be contingent upon favorable review of the applicant’s driving record. Alternatively, the applicant must have the ability and willingness to use alternative methods of transportation to perform assigned duties and responsibilities at locations other than the primary worksite. Working Conditions: The worker must be available to work after hours and in emergency situations. Work is performed as part of a 24/7 operation and the worker must be available to work shifts as necessary. The worker performs activities inside and outside. The worker is subject to cold (below 32 degrees) for periods of more than one hour and/or temperatures above 90 degrees for periods of more than one hour. Consideration should be given to the effect of other environmental conditions such as snow, rain, hail, wind and humidity. The worker is subject to hazards: Includes a variety of physical conditions, such as proximity to moving mechanical parts, moving vehicles, electrical current, working on scaffolding and high places, exposure to high heat or exposure to chemicals. The worker is subject to one more of the following conditions: Fumes, odors, dusts, mists, gases or poor ventilation, oils, and other cutting fluids. The worker frequently is in close quarters such as manholes, small, enclosed rooms, small sewage and water line pipes, and/or narrow aisles or passageways. Physical Requirements: Medium Work: Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally and/or up to 20 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects. Please complete each section of the application including the supplemental questions. Your responses to the supplemental questions are required because they provide us with specific information necessary to evaluate your qualifications for this position. These responses are considered part of the selection process. A resume may be attached; however, it will not substitute for a completed application. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Please do not write "see resume" as a response to the questions. In accordance with § 19.2-392.15, applicants are not required to provide information regarding sealed arrests, charges, or convictions in response to any questions or inquiries during the hiring process. Additional Information Work hours: This position may be assigned to one of 3 shifts. Shift 1: Monday to Friday 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., to include one week of Tuesday to Saturday, 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. every 10 weeks. Shift 2: Tuesday-Saturday, 2:30 p.m.-11:00 p.m. Shift 3: Sunday-Thursday, 2:30 p.m.-11:00 p.m. Flexibility on variations of shifts or a rotation based upon departmental need is required. Additional flexibility is required to work shifts other than normal shift to provide coverage to Justice Center. Employee must be available for call-back and be willing to work after normal duty hours in emergency situations. This position is listed as "open continuous."
