At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ## Role Overview REGENT's mechanical team is in the middle of a defining stretch of work: carrying Squire, our production Seaglider, through a full design and release cycle, while simultaneously shaping Viceroy from early concept into preliminary design. As a **Mechanical Engineering Co-Op**, you'll be dropped right into both efforts — designing parts in CAD, producing drawings, and supporting release on a vehicle headed toward production, while also contributing iterative design work on a program that's still taking shape. This isn't an adjacent, watch-and-learn co-op experience; you'll be trusted with real parts, real drawings, and real ownership from day one. You'll join Hardware Engineering's Mechanical team, helping take Squire from prototype to production. The fast-moving team values sound judgment in early design and disciplined production execution. If you have a foundation in mechanical design and assembly complexity and want ownership of flight hardware bound for the water, this role could shape your education or launch a career building Seagliders that will reinvent coastal transportation. ## What You'll Do - **Design and Release Squire Hardware:** You'll design mechanical parts in CAD and carry them through release, stepping into a production cycle where your drawings become real hardware on REGENT's Seaglider platform. It's the kind of direct contribution that goes well beyond a typical co-op assignment. - **Help Shape Viceroy From Concept Forward:** You'll jump into Viceroy while it's still being defined, doing the iterative CAD work that shapes a vehicle's geometry before anything is locked in. Bring solid engineering instincts and your early ideas will hold up, not get reworked from scratch. - **Draft With Precision:** A large part of your time will go toward engineering drawings and tolerancing, turning design intent into documentation our team and manufacturing partners can actually build from. If you already have a good eye for drafting, this is where it gets put to work immediately. - **Support Manufacturing and Integration:** You'll work alongside technicians during build and integration, helping fit checks go smoothly and feeding what you learn on the floor straight back into your CAD models. It's a fast feedback loop that sharpens your design judgment quickly. - **Own Systems End to End:** You'll take a reasonably scoped project from concept through integration, with support from senior engineers, and build toward real ownership of at least one system on the vehicle. By the end, you'll have a portfolio of work that stands on its own, whether you're headed back to finish school or straight into a full-time role. ## What You'll Bring - **Comfort Inside Complex Systems:** Whether it came from an internship, a competition team, or a school project that got surprisingly real, you've worked inside assemblies where parts depend on each other. You're used to thinking several components deep instead of in isolation. - **CAD as Second Nature:** You're comfortable living in CAD day to day, not just opening it when a class requires it. Whatever your tool of choice, you pick up new CAD environments quickly. - **An Eye for Drawings:** You've spent real time with engineering drawings and tolerancing, enough to know that a good drawing is what keeps a part's design intent alive once it leaves your screen and heads to manufacturing. - **Instincts That Hold Up:** You have a working sense of load paths, material choices, and how manufacturing methods shape part design. That means your early ideas are something the team can build on, not something they have to rebuild. - **Steady Under Ambiguity:** You're not thrown off by incomplete information or a plan that's still taking shape. You can make a reasonable call, move forward, and adjust as new information comes in. - **A Builder's Instinct:** If you've spent time in a machine shop or messing around with rapid prototyping, you know the value of walking over, testing a quick fit, and bringing what you learn straight back into the model. That loop matters a lot while Viceroy is still taking shape. - **Real Pull Toward Vehicles:** You're genuinely into aerospace, marine, or vehicle programs, not just checking a box for your resume. You'll be helping shape hardware on a Seaglider headed toward production, and that should be exactly the kind of thing that gets you excited to show up. ## Who We're Looking For - **Collaborative Team Player:** You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. - **Creative Problem Solver:** You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. - **Adaptable & Agile:** In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. - **Innovative Mindset:** You're driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You're passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance. ## **What We Offer** - Competitive compensation - **Housing Stipend** available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, **free catered lunches** - **Learning & professional development** opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members **If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you.** Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! role: Machine Learning Engineer Intern, AI & Robotics
description: **Why RoboForce** RoboForce is an AI robotics company developing Physical AI–powered Robo-Labor for dull, dirty, and dangerous work. The company’s robots are engineered for demanding industrial environments, with a focus on real-world deployment and scalability. We are seeking a **Machine Learning Engineer Intern** to join us in developing advanced AI capabilities for robotics. The internship starts from **November 2026 for 3-6 months**. As part of our team, you will help build the foundational AI ecosystem, spanningdata collection, labeling, training, evaluation, and deployment. You will collaborate closely with a team of world-class AI engineers and gain hands-on experience solving real-world challenges at the intersection of artificial intelligence and robotics. **Responsibilities** - Train and improve robot foundation models, including vision-language-action (VLA) models and world-action models, for precise, contact-rich manipulation in industrial settings. - Explore new modalities and methods, including tactile and force-torque sensing, reinforcement learning, and simulation, to advance model capabilities. - Build data pipelines for robot learning, including data collection, curation, labeling, and dataset quality assurance. - Design and run evaluations in simulation and on real robots to measure and improve model performance. - Deploy models on robots and optimize them for real-time onboard inference. - Work closely with robotics, hardware, and product teams to bring models from research to production. **Requirements** - Currently pursuing an advanced degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, or a related field, with a graduation date in 2026 or 2027. - Proficiency in multimodal models, modern machine learning architectures (e.g., transformers and diffusion models), and reinforcement learning. - Proficiency in deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow. - **Requires 5 days/week in-office collaboration with the teams.** **Bonus Qualifications** - Exposure to robot learning using tactile and/or vision-based sensors. - Expertise in object pose estimation, bimanual manipulation, and synthetic data. **Duration:** - 3–6 months, full-time **Compensation:** - $5,000 - $6,500 monthly salary

role: Accelerated Science Intern, Bridging Atomistic Modeling to Real Electrochemical Systems
description: At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences. This is a paid 12-week internship opportunity and is a hybrid, in-office role. [Here’s a glimpse into the Internship experience from some of our TRI interns!](https://www.tri.global/tri-internship-program) **The Team** The long-term vision of TRI’s Accelerated Materials Design and Discovery (AMDD) program is to accelerate the development of truly emissions-free mobility. Realizing this vision will require the discovery of new materials and devices for batteries, fuel cells, and more. Our aim at TRI is to merge sophisticated computational materials modeling, new experimental data, artificial intelligence, and automation to significantly accelerate materials research in this area. Our focus is on developing tools and capabilities to enable this acceleration. We collaborate closely with a dozen universities and national labs and our colleagues across global Toyota. AMDD seeks to develop and translate the newest technologies into practice, both within Toyota and the open research community, more broadly. **This Internship** We are looking for an intern researcher to contribute to the development of atomistic catalysis modeling that bridges the gap between current simulation (e.g. DFT) and in-situ catalysis experiments. We will develop reasoning models with embedded chemical and atomistic descriptors as well as experimental parameters and measurements. Your day-to-day may include: literature review of computational methods and model construction and validation. We welcome you to join a unique team of scientists and engineers where you will constantly learn new skills at the interface of materials science and thoughtful ### Responsibilities - Research multiscale physics phenomena required in electrocatalysis modeling. - Data analytics for experimental electrocatalyst design and testing. - Identify key materials understanding that enable translation of existing models to new materials. - Develop new reasoning models incorporating atomistic modeling and experiments. - Collaborate with the team on automated reasoning methods. - Present findings within the team and to the greater group. ### Qualifications - Are currently enrolled in a doctoral program in STEM subjects (chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related discipline). - Hands-on experience with advanced 3-electrode cell catalyst electrochemical evaluation. - Experience with standard material characterization techniques (x-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, etc.). - Published manuscripts in the electrocatalysis field. ### Bonus Qualifications - Experience coding in Python. - Microkinetic modeling experience. - Experience in DFT simulations. - Experience in in-situ electrocatalysis characterization.

Halo is a hair technology company using breakthrough engineering to elevate everyday routines. We’re building the world’s first robotic hair-braiding system—integrating computer vision, robotics, compliant fiber manipulation, and novel mechatronic machines. This is one of the hardest unsolved problems in robotics, applied to a $300B industry. 8 billion hours are spent braiding hair each year. HaloBraid gives that time back. The system collaborates with professional stylists to reduce braiding appointments from 6 hours to minutes and grow their business. We’re moving from R&D into deployment with salons, well-funded by leading investors. This is a unique opportunity to shape the future of the hair styling industry. We are looking for a Spring 2027 Mechanical Engineering Co-op to play a pivotal role in developing our innovative hair braiding robotic system. ## Responsibilities: - ﻿﻿Contribute to the development of complex technology, product sub-assemblies, and test rigs - ﻿﻿Take an active, hands-on role to ensure that engineering problems are resolved thoroughly - ﻿﻿Utilize various rapid prototyping technologies to build, test, and iterate - ﻿﻿Use hand calculations, computer simulation, and/or lab-based testing to validate designs through the development process - ﻿﻿Conduct user testing and project the voice of the customer back into the design - Conduct various forms of testing, problem solving, and design iteration ## Requirements: - ﻿﻿At least one semester remaining in your undergraduate or graduate degree - ﻿﻿Experience with CAD (we use Onshape, experience with Solidworks or equivalent is acceptable) - ﻿﻿Experience with various rapid prototyping methods (3D printing, CNC, etc) - ﻿﻿Demonstrated design intelligence, mechanical intuition, creative problem solving, and strong attention to detail - ﻿﻿A willingness to fail and learn! ## Desired Skills & Experience (optional but the more, the better) - ﻿﻿Gone through (and documented!) the design process for a project, through school or on your own time - ﻿﻿Strong documentation skills and the ability to convey complex ideas in a team setting - Strong experimental rigor and testing process - Experience with complex CAD models with clear top down design - ﻿﻿Experience with consumer electronics, robotics, or hair styling tools - ﻿﻿Interest in hair braiding/styling - Interest in robotics and mechanisms - Complementary engineering experience: - Mechanisms, mechatronics, and moving components. - ﻿﻿Experience with design optimization using FEA/CFD simulation - Electronics prototyping and soldering **Working Style** - User centric, you want to build stuff people use and love - Low ego, adaptable, and collaborative spirit - Willing to learn through fast-paced iteration and feedback - Passionate, driven by innovation **Benefits of Working with Us:** - Company subsidized parking or commute for onsite employees **Onsite work** This is an onsite full time position at our office/lab in Cambridge, MA. We turn data from thousands of jurisdictions into clear, unbiased answers about how government spends money and what it achieves. No political agenda. No commercial motive. Just public service. Founded and funded by Steve Ballmer, former CEO of Microsoft, we work alongside Ballmer Group Philanthropy and Rainier Climate on civic impact. As an intern, you’ll join a collaborative, mission-driven team and learn how complex public data becomes something the American people can actually use. Here’s what to expect: *Pay* $33 per hour for at least 10 weeks, which comes to roughly $13,200 before taxes at 40 hours per week. Interns are overtime eligible, so hours over 40 per week are paid at time and a half. *Housing support* Relocating interns receive company-paid furnished corporate housing and a $1,000 travel reimbursement. Interns who live in the area and don’t need corporate housing can be reimbursed up to $2,000 per month for housing costs with a current rental agreement. *Paid sick days and holidays* 3 paid sick days and paid holidays for the duration of your internship. *Hybrid schedule* In the office Tuesday through Thursday, with lunches provided, and the flexibility to work remotely or in-office the rest of the week. *Transportation* You’ll receive either an ORCA card for local public transit or paid parking in or near the building. *Events, community, and opportunities* At USAFacts, we believe a great internship is about more than just the work. This intern position is a not-exempt role located in Bellevue, WA. The intern role is paid at a rate of $33 per hour. Interns are not eligible for the company’s standard benefits package, but you will receive the paid time off, housing support, and transportation support described above. Start and end dates are flexible between May and September to fit your school schedule, for a minimum of 10 weeks. description: **ABOUT ORCHESTRA** Orchestra is a strategic communications and marketing company built for today’s complex and fragmented world. From decoding audiences to designing bold strategies, Orchestra integrates people, platforms, and stories that stick to help clients build lasting influence. The company offers programs that span from the highest level strategic business counsel through to tactical execution. This is a hands-on opportunity for college graduates that provides meaningful experience across strategic communications, public affairs, media engagement, brand storytelling, and business operations. Fellows are embedded within a specific practice area and contribute to active client work and business initiatives while gaining exposure to how integrated communications strategies are developed and executed. **Duration:** January 13, 2027 - July 2, 2027 **Location:** Hybrid based in New York, NY; Waltham, MA; San Francisco, CA; Seattle, WA or San Diego, CA. Conduct research and monitor industry, market, and media trends - Draft content, reports, presentations, and communications materials - Support client and internal projects from planning through execution - Participate in meetings, brainstorming sessions, client calls, and events - Collaborate across teams on integrated initiatives - Gain exposure to strategic communications, public affairs, and agency operations in a fast-paced environment **QUALIFICATIONS:**Candidates should possess: - A bachelor's degree (or will graduate before the start date) - Prior internship or relevant work experience in their selected practice area - Strong writing, research, analytical, and communication skills - Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail - Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment - Proficiency with Google Workspace and Microsoft Office - Digital fluency and eagerness to learn new platforms - As part of the application, candidates will be asked to select one practice area of interest and complete a brief essay (500 words or less) describing how their experiences have prepared them for success in that area and why they are interested in pursuing a career in the field. **Application Deadline** - Friday, November 6th, 2026. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis beginning before the deadline, so we encourage candidates to apply early. *Due to application volume, we are unable to respond to all submissions. We will reach out directly to candidates selected for interviews. ## **Company Overview** At Skild AI, we are building the world's first general purpose robotic intelligence that is robust and adapts to unseen scenarios without failing. We believe massive scale through data-driven machine learning is the key to unlocking these capabilities for the widespread deployment of robots within society. Our team consists of individuals with varying levels of experience and backgrounds, from new graduates to domain experts. Relevant industry experience is important, but ultimately less so than your demonstrated abilities and attitude. We are looking for passionate individuals who are eager to explore uncharted waters and contribute to our innovative projects. **Position Overview** We're looking for an ambitious, multidisciplinary designer with exceptional taste, strong creative instincts, and the drive to help shape Skild AI's brand. As our Founding Brand Design Intern, you'll work hands-on across graphic design, motion, 3D, and AI-powered creative production, with meaningful ownership from day one. For the right person, this internship could evolve into a full-time role owning and advancing Skild's brand and creative direction. **Responsibilities** - **Elevate the brand:** Refine Skild's visual language and deliver distinctive, polished work across web, social, presentations, and campaigns. - **Design and animate:** Create graphics, typography, layouts, 2D motion, 3D renders, and product storytelling. - **Build AI creative pipelines:** Experiment with generative tools and coding agents to establish repeatable workflows for image, video, animation, and production. - **Support production:** Contribute to photo/video shoots, post-production, asset management, and external creative coordination. - **Take ownership:** Carry work from concept to final delivery, spot gaps, and proactively raise the quality bar. **Preferred Qualifications** - **Exceptional taste and trend leadership:** A standout portfolio, a sharp understanding of emerging design trends, and the creative vision to shape what comes next, not simply follow what exists. - **3D:** Proficiency in modeling, rendering, lighting, and animation (Blender, Cinema 4D, Claude Code / Codex, or equivalent). - **Motion:** 2D animation, motion graphics, and basic compositing (After Effects, Claude Code / Codex, or equivalent). - **Graphic design:** Image creation and manipulation, typography, and layout (Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, Claude Code / Codex, or equivalent). - **AI fluency:** Hands-on experience with emerging creative tools, coding agents, and workflow automation. - **High agency:** Resourcefulness, initiative, and the ambition to grow into an outsized brand leadership role. We care more about the quality of your work, your instincts, and your potential than years of experience.

description: We are seeking enthusiastic and motivated Civil & Structural Engineering Apprentices to join our Bridges team in Chesterfield. description: **About Us** SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. **Powered by two trusted, global brands, Shark and Ninja**, the company has a proven track record of bringing disruptive innovation to market and developing one consumer product after another has allowed SharkNinja to enter multiple product categories, driving significant growth and market share gains. Headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts with more than 4,100 associates, the company’s products are sold at key retailers, online and offline, and through distributors around the world. **AI at SharkNinja** At SharkNinja, we’re building an AI-native culture. We’re not waiting for the future; we’re creating it. Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. If you believe the best way to do your job hasn’t been invented yet, you’ll fit right in. **Location & Schedule:** This is a full-time, 40-hour-per-week position with a minimum of 5 days per week onsite in Needham, MA. **There is no relocation or housing assistance for this position.** **Join the SharkNinja Early Edge Experience:** Built for early career talent. Geared toward impact. Driven by speed. Whether you're in a co-op or internship, our early talent program is designed to provide valuable exposure to the industry and a fast-paced professional environment. You’ll dive into meaningful projects and tasks that sharpen your skills and deepen your knowledge. Along the way, you’ll benefit from professional development opportunities, community events, and connections that make your experience well-rounded and enriching. Your time with us will culminate in an opportunity to showcase your contributions and learnings to SharkNinja leaders because this is a program for those ready to shape what’s next - fast. **This role:** The Technical Project Management Co-op will support the Robotics team in firmware releases coordination, beta testing operations, and program data analysis. This role focuses on driving alignment, tracking execution, and ensuring visibility across interconnected workstreams in a fast-paced, global environment. You will partner with engineering, quality, product, and operations teams to help translate technical requirements into actionable plans, maintain program structure, and enable teams to deliver on time. You will also help organize tester feedback, coordinate issue follow-up, and turn technical and testing data into clear, actionable updates. The right individual will bring a strong “can do” mindset, thrive in ambiguity, and be energized by connecting the dots across systems, teams, and timelines. The main work of this team is to ensure programs are structured, tracked, and executed effectively across a highly matrixed organization, supporting both new product development and ongoing product improvements. **Here are some of the exciting things you’ll get to do:** - Support end-to-end program planning, including defining scope, timelines, milestones, and dependencies across multiple technical workstream - Use Jira and Confluence to manage workflows, track progress, and maintain centralized, up-to-date project documentation - Support testing operations, including participant communications, survey coordination, feedback review, and issue follow-up. - Coordinate across hardware, firmware, software, and data teams to ensure alignment on deliverables and timelines - Support technical issue tracking and triage by documenting issues, coordinating with responsible teams, and tracking follow-up actions through resolution. - Support technical issue tracking and triage, helping to surface blockers and drive resolution paths - Develop dashboards and reports using AI, Excel, Power BI, Amazon QuickSight, or similar tools to provide visibility into program health, risks, and performance metrics - Assist in preparing clear, concise program updates and executive-ready presentations - Identify process improvement opportunities to increase efficiency, transparency, and execution speed **ATTRIBUTES & SKILLS:** - **Education:** Current student in a bachelor’s or a master’s program or within 1 year of graduation from a bachelor's or master's program - Must be able to work a full-time, 40-hour-per-week schedule with a minimum of 3 days per week onsite in Needham, MA - Strong proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint - Prior experience with data visualization, reporting tools, or dashboard development; experience with Power BI, Amazon QuickSight, or similar tools preferred - Mandarin language fluency preferred - Hands-on experience or familiarity with Jira and Confluence preferred - Strong organizational skills, with the ability to track multiple priorities and follow through on assigned tasks - Analytical mindset with the ability to interpret data, identify trends, and support decision-making - Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate technical concepts into clear, actionable updates - High attention to detail with a structured, process-oriented approach to problem solving - Proactive, self-motivated, and brings a strong “can do” attitude - Ability to navigate ambiguity and work effectively across a matrixed, cross-functional environment - Foundational understanding of technical development processes across hardware and/or software systems - Embodies SharkNinja's success drivers: - Rarely Satisfied – Adopt a “no delays” mentality in delivering against market needs and timing - Progress over Perfection – Make quick, daily progress and continuously adapt to achieve results - Details Make the Difference – Ensure accuracy and consistency across timelines, plans, and deliverables - Winning is a Team Sport – Build strong cross-functional relationships - Communicate for Impact – Deliver clear, effective communication to stakeholders at all levels **Please note that, due to the high volume of applications for early talent roles, response times may vary depending on the specific role and timeline. ***Who are we?*** MATTE is a 360° full-service creative studio at the convergence of hype, storytelling and design. We bring people together to inspire new ways of engaging, to provoke long term progress, and to entertain audiences around the world, while helping forward-thinking brands and institutions nimbly and truly do the same. Our studio capabilities range from strategic ideation and insights, creative development, branding and identity, experiential, web design and development, campaigns and content creation, all the way through full-scale production and execution. ***About this role:*** As a **Content Production Intern** at MATTE, you’ll work alongside our Production team on photography, film, and social content projects. You’ll get hands-on experience across the production process, from researching locations and preparing for shoots to supporting the crew on set and helping organize final deliverables. This internship is a good fit for someone who loves visual storytelling, enjoys keeping details organized, and is curious about what it takes to bring a creative idea from brief to shoot to final delivery. #### ***Responsibilities & Learning Opportunities*** - Assist producers with pre-production logistics, including preparing call sheets, updating shoot schedules, and helping coordinate talent. - Research locations, talent, and creative references to support upcoming projects. - Help keep vendor lists, crew bookings, and production trackers up to date. - Support the Production team on shoot days with setup, check-in, and other on-set needs. - Assist with post-production coordination by updating delivery schedules and tracking feedback and approvals. - Help organize and archive production documents, wrap reports, and final assets. - Work alongside Creative, Strategy, and Operations to see how teams collaborate throughout a project. #### ***Skills & Capabilities*** - Interest in film, photography, social content, or the logistics behind creative production. - Strong attention to detail and an organized, reliable approach to assigned tasks. - Clear communication and a willingness to ask questions and take direction. - Ability to adapt when priorities shift, especially on shoot days. - Comfort with Google Workspace. Familiarity with StudioBinder, Dropbox, or Airtable is a plus. ***About the Internship:*** Get a closer look at life inside MATTE, a creative studio working across culture, brands, and experiences. Our internship program offers opportunities to learn from experienced professionals, contribute to projects, and build skills that support your career goals. ***What You’ll Gain:*** - Hands-on learning in a collaborative creative environment. - Guidance and feedback from industry professionals. - Exposure to the creative process, from initial ideas through execution. - Opportunities to build your professional network and explore career paths. - Academic credit, subject to your school’s requirements and approval. ***Program Details & Requirements:*** - Must be enrolled in a university undergraduate or master’s program. - Must be available for a minimum of 16 hours per week, working two days on-site at our New York City offices. - Must be available for the full program, from **February 3 through May 12, 2027**. All internships begin **February 3, 2027**. This is an **unpaid internship** that may qualify for academic credit. Interns are not eligible for employee benefits. Everyone is welcome at MATTE - we’re passionate about building a team that reflects the diversity of our community and creating an environment where our differences are celebrated. MATTE provides equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all persons regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. In addition, MATTE will provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

Analytical Mindset: Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to look at data through a critical lens. Career Growth: Gain deep insight into the HealthTech industry and the lifecycle of a high-growth SaaS startup. Grow your technical skill set and enhance your resume with real-world projects. Pronunciation: a:rine [uh-reen]. Noun: Arine is a name of Basque origin meaning "light." Arine illuminates the possibilities with medication management to deliver comprehensive economic and health outcomes. Based in San Francisco, Arine is a rapidly growing healthcare technology and clinical services company with a mission to ensure individuals receive the safest and most effective treatments for their unique and evolving healthcare needs. Frequently, medications cause more harm than good. Incorrect drugs and doses costs the US healthcare system over $528 billion in waste, avoidable harm, and hospitalizations each year. Arine is redefining what excellent healthcare looks like by solving these issues through our software platform (SaaS). We combine cutting edge data science, machine learning, AI, and deep clinical expertise to introduce a patient-centric view to medication management, and develop and deliver personalized care plans on a massive scale for patients and their care teams. Arine is committed to improving the lives and health of complex patients that have an outsized impact on healthcare costs and have traditionally been difficult to identify and address. These patients face numerous challenges including complicated prescribing issues across multiple medications and providers, medication challenges with many chronic diseases, and patient issues with access to care. Backed by leading healthcare investors and collaborating with top healthcare organizations and providers, we deliver recommendations and facilitate clinical interventions that lead to significant, measurable health improvements for patients and cost savings for customers. Why is Arine a Great Place to Work?: Outstanding Team and Culture - Our shared mission unites and motivates us to do our best work. We have a relentless passion and commitment to the innovation required to be the market leader in medication intelligence. Making a Proven Difference in Healthcare - We are saving patient lives, and enabling individuals to experience improved health outcomes, including significant reductions in hospitalizations and cost of care. Market Opportunity - Arine is backed by leading healthcare investors and was founded to tackle one of the largest healthcare problems today. Non-optimized medications therapies which cost the US 275,000 lives and $528 billion annually. Momentum That Matters - In just over eight years, Arine has grown into one of the fastest-growing healthcare AI companies, serving more than 45 million members through partnerships with leading health plans nationwide. Recognized on the Inc. 5000 list for two consecutive years, we're combining rapid growth with meaningful impact on the quality, cost, and outcomes of care.

Are you passionate about sandals, boots, and everything in between? Do you live and breathe sustainability? Do you have a creative eye, a hunger to learn, and a KEEN interest in the outdoor industry? If you said yes to any of the above, we have the perfect opportunity for you! **Position:** AI Product Management Intern **Location:** KEEN’s Global Headquarters in Portland, Oregon (on-site) **Duration:** 10 weeks **Compensation:** $22/hour **Program Duration:** Monday, June 14th – Friday, August 20th **What You'll Do** As an Intern at KEEN (KEENtern), you’ll dive into the exciting world of footwear, innovation, and community! You’ll get hands-on experience working alongside industry experts and contribute to shaping the future of KEEN. As an AI Product Management KEENtern, you’ll help KEEN identify, design, test, and scale practical ways AI can make a meaningful difference for KEENers, our fans, and the business. You’ll work across teams to understand how work happens today, where friction or opportunity exists, and where AI could help create better outcomes. You’ll turn those insights into clear opportunities, prototypes, pilots, and recommendations. **Essential Responsibilities** - Partner with teams across KEEN to map workflows, understand pain points, and identify high-potential AI opportunities. - Research emerging AI capabilities, tools, and relevant examples from consumer, retail, footwear, and other industries. - Help define AI use cases, including the problem to solve, intended users, desired outcomes, risks, data needs, and measures of success. - Help document pilots, lessons learned, adoption signals, and potential business value for leadership and project teams. - Create practical materials—such as playbooks, workflow maps, use-case briefs, training resources, or communications—that make new ways of working easier to understand and adopt. - Contribute to responsible AI practices with privacy, security, accuracy, bias, brand, and human oversight in project work. **Minimum Qualifications** - Currently pursuing or recently completed a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Business, Psychology, Information Systems, Data Analytics, Operations, Computer Science, or a related field. - Demonstrated interest in artificial intelligence, product management, process improvement, innovation, or digital transformation. - Familiarity with large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), prompt design, AI agents, and core concepts such as model limitations, evaluation, data quality, and human oversight; ideally demonstrated through hands-on projects, prototypes, coursework, research, or work experience building with AI. - Strong written and verbal communication skills. - Ability to solve problems, analyze information, synthesize findings, and turn them into clear recommendations. - Commitment to responsible handling of confidential information and sound judgment when using AI tools. **What We’re Looking For:** - We’re looking for a curious, action-oriented KEENtern who wants to help shape how work gets done in alignment with a human-centered and responsible AI approach - You see AI as more than a tool for doing today’s work faster. You’re interested in asking better questions: What could be simpler? What could be smarter? What could become possible if we redesigned the workflow from the ground up? - You bring a builder’s mindset. You are comfortable moving from ambiguity to action, listening closely to people’s real challenges, and turning ideas into practical experiments. You can balance optimism about emerging technology with sound judgment about people, brand, privacy, and responsible use. - You believe the best use of AI makes people more capable—not less human. You’re excited to help KEENers spend less time on repetitive work and more time creating, solving problems, making better decisions, and delivering better outcomes for our fans and the planet. We’re seeking someone who embodies our passion for creativity, sustainability, and the great outdoors. Our ideal KEENtern is: - **Passionate:**Whether you’re an outdoor enthusiast, committed to sustainability, or fascinated by footwear trends and innovation, you’re excited to engage with the world around you. - **Creatively Minded:** You’re detail-oriented, love bringing fresh ideas to life, and have a knack for solving problems. - **A Strong Communicator:** Whether it’s collaborating with a team or presenting ideas, you know how to express yourself clearly and effectively. - **Proactive & Eager to Learn:** You’re curious, ready to ask questions, take initiative, and dive into new challenges with enthusiasm. **Why Intern with Us?** Being a KEENtern means you’re not just an intern—you’re a valued part of our KEEN community. Here’s what you can look forward to: - **Meaningful Work:**Tackle real-world projects that make an impact, gaining valuable hands-on experience at a globally recognized brand. - **Collaborative Environment:**Partner with talented teammates and work on a group project with other KEENterns. - **Networking Opportunities:**Build connections with industry experts and mentors who can help shape your career. - **Perks & Benefits:**Enjoy product discounts, a subsidized cafeteria, and an inspiring workspace. - **Outdoor Adventures:**Immerse yourself in Portland – a vibrant city nestled between the mountains and the coast – a hub for all things outdoors, such as hiking, biking, rafting, camping, and climbing. **Program Requirements:** To qualify for this internship, you must: - Currently pursuing or recently completed a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Business, Psychology, Information Systems, Data Analytics, Operations, Computer Science, or a related field. - Be eligible to work in the U.S. without sponsorship - Commit to a 10-week program from mid-June through mid-August - Dedicate 40 hours per week during standard M-F work week - This is an onsite role located at our beautiful headquarters office in Portland, OR - Plan no more than four total days of vacation during the internship - Demonstrate proficiency in Microsoft Office programs, including Outlook, Word, and PowerPoint - Able to learn and adapt quickly to new software and tools - Demonstrate strong verbal and written communication skills, strong attention to detail in preparation of presentations, reports, and materials - Demonstrate strong organization skills with the ability to prioritize and manage multiple tasks - Proven ability to work independently as well as collaborate with a team - Able to perform the essential functions of the role, with or without reasonable accommodation, including using a computer for extended periods **Ready to Take the Next Step?** If you’re ready to take your passions to the next level and be part of a world-class team, please apply. **Other Requirements** Please note this job description is not designed to contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without cause. ***Fuerst Group, KEEN and Chrome are equal opportunity employers. We value an inclusive and diverse community. Qualified candidates of all backgrounds are encouraged to apply and will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, or disability.***

role: Junior Administrative Analyst (1820) - Multiple Departments Citywide (C00185)
description: Junior Administrative Analysts work at many City departments on a wide variety of teams, with essential duties varying depending on whether the role focuses on data, grants, contracting, budget, finance, and/or legislation. Current City policy requires on-site work with some flexibility for telecommute schedules. See below for examples of the range of duties by subject matter: Junior Policy Analysts work in teams to analyze performance data to identify operational challenges and develop policy recommendations as well as assist preparation of materials for publication such as policy memos and hearing materials. Key duties include assisting with analysis, building an understanding of department policy priorities and working with elected officials, and keeping track of relevant local, state, and federal legislation and regulations that may impact the department. Providing a real-world example, a Junior Policy Analyst for the Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector could involve working to improve financial access and inclusion, with a focus on community reinvestment. Junior Budget Analysts work in teams to develop budget proposals and financial models, track City revenues and expenditures, perform account reconciliation for budget period closing, and present analysis to stakeholders. Key duties include reviewing and exporting large datasets into reports, compiling budget requests, preparing budget reports and calendars, responding to budget requests and providing customer-service and thought partnership to internal and external partners. Providing a real-world example, a Junior Budget Analyst may have the opportunity to learn about the Human Services Agency’s $1 Billion annual budget providing a comprehensive safety net services for individuals, families, and the elderly. Junior Contracts Analysts work in teams to assist in the management of contract processes for their department throughout the full procurement process. They will collaborate and build relationships with other key departments overseeing contract monitoring and execution. Key duties include supporting the facilitation of informal and formal bid processes, reviewing department compliance with new and existing contracts, assisting in the creation of important contract documents, and being a valuable thought partner on contracts to department leadership and City vendors. Providing a real-world example, a Junior Contracts Analyst could assist with procurement and contract administration related to bond programs that fund construction and modernization of San Francisco public schools. Junior Data Analysts work in teams to support data and programmatic analysis using analytical programs. Using this information, analysts develop findings and actionable recommendations to inform programmatic and policy decisions. Key duties include conducting data queries from variety of databases and disparate spreadsheets, then performing data analysis. Additional duties could be creating data visualizations and maps for statutory reports, as well as developing streamlined dashboards using PowerBI, Tableau, or other dashboarding technologies. Providing a real-world example, a Junior Data Analyst might work with the San Francisco Planning Department to update the department’s data inventory and enhance data governance protocols in key areas including housing production, racial and social equity, and COVID-19 recovery. Junior Finance Analysts work in teams to assist with fiscal accounting, budget analysis and reporting, billing, revenue collection, and debt management. Key duties include analyzing the overall financial condition of a department, interpreting City contracting guidance and informing recommendations, preparing financial statements and reports to various funding agencies throughout the fiscal year, calculating debt capacity and exploring financing alternates, and using City financial systems. Providing a real-world example, a Junior Finance Analyst may work with the Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing, learning about and providing financial analysis on programs funding robust supporting housing programs to formerly homeless individuals. Junior Grants Analysts work in teams to assist in analytical work related to grants management and compliance. Key duties include reviewing and analyzing internal and external budget requests, learning about grant policies and compliance standards of different grantors, assisting with application and reporting processes for grant opportunities with department program staff. Providing a real-world example, a Junior Grants Analyst might assist the San Francisco Planning Department in writing grants to bring in critical funding towards the growth and development of San Francisco. Please note that incumbents in this classification may be required to perform the full range of duties as listed in the class specification . Education: Possession of a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university Substitution: May substitute up to 2 years of the required education with qualifying full-time, professional-level experience in budget analysis, financial analysis and reporting, legislative/policy analysis, data analysis, or contract/grant administration. One year (2,000 hours) of qualifying experience will be considered equivalent to 30 semester/45 quarter units Note: Candidates who are projected to graduate with a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university within six months of their application submission will be invited to participate in the recruitment process. Candidates in this situation who successfully pass the examination will be placed on the eligible list, and may participate in the final selection process. Such candidates may be given an offer of employment contingent upon submitting documentation of a degree prior to appointment. Applicants will receive a confirmation email from that their online application has been received in response to every announcement for which they file. Applicants should retain this confirmation email for their records. Failure to receive this email means that the online application was not submitted or received. Every application is reviewed to ensure that you meet the minimum qualifications as listed in the job ad. Review SF Careers Employment Applications for considerations taken when reviewing applications. Applicants may be required to submit verification of qualifying education and experience at any point during the recruitment and selection process. If education verification is required, information on how to verify education requirements, including verifying foreign education credits or degree equivalency, can be found at Note: Falsifying one’s education, training, or work experience or attempted deception on the application may result in disqualification for this and future job opportunities with the City and County of San Francisco. NOTE: Use your personal email —school and work emails may become inaccessible SELECTION PROCEDURES Junior Administrative Analyst Core Exam (Weight: 100%) Candidates self-certifying meeting the Minimum Qualifications will be invited to participate in the online Junior Administrative Analyst Core Exam. Candidates will be sent a web link via email that will allow them to take the online Junior Administrative Analyst Core Exam that is designed to measure knowledge, skills, and/or abilities in job-related areas which have been identified as critical for positions in the Junior Administrative Analyst classification. This computer-administered test can be taken at home or at a time and location of one’s convenience, but only within the time period specified on the test notification. Candidates must have access to a computer and reliable internet connection to participate in this exam. Score Banking: Scores attained on the Junior Administrative Analyst Core Exam will be 'banked' for three years, starting from the date of the examination. This means that, during this three-year time period, candidates need not take this test again. Rather, if another announcement you applied to and are deemed qualified for requires the Junior Administrative Analyst Core Exam and is held within one year of your Junior Administrative Analyst Core Exam date, your score will be automatically applied to that announcement. However, after one year, a candidate has the option to either (a) apply their test score to the other announcement or (b) re-take the test. Re-testing is permitted no sooner than one year from the date of the test and only in association with a candidate’s eligibility for another announcement to which the candidate has applied and is deemed qualified. If a candidate opts to re-test, the re-test score becomes the candidate’s official score since it is the most recent. If a significant modification is made to this exam in the future, the application of “banked” scores may no longer be appropriate. In such a rare circumstance, candidates with “banked” scores would be required to re-take the exam sooner than the three-year period specified above should they apply to another job opportunity where the modified exam is used. Eligible List/Score Report: A confidential eligible list of applicant names that have passed the civil service examination process will be created, and used for certification purposes only. An examination score report will be established, so applicants can view the ranks, final scores and number of eligible candidates. Applicant information, including names of applicants on the eligible list, shall not be made public unless required by law. However, an eligible list shall be made available for public inspection, upon request, once the eligible list is exhausted or expired and referrals resolved. The eligible list/score report resulting from this civil service examination process is subject to change after adoption (e.g., as a result of appeals), as directed by the Human Resources Director or the Civil Service Commission. Upon passing the exam, candidates will be placed on the eligible list for a period of 12 months. If you are passionate about making a difference at the local level, are a curious and open thinker, and enjoy analysis, this job may be the right fit. The City and County of San Francisco is looking to hire multiple analysts to be part of the City workforce of nearly 40,000 staff and growing. This is a unique opportunity to get direct insights into how San Francisco’s $14 billion budget is used to provide high-quality services for residents, workers, and visitors. Dit ga je doen Ben jij op zoek naar een meewerkstage waarin je data, analyses en procesverbetering combineert? Wil je ontdekken hoe je het verschil kan maken in een commerciële organisatie waarin je bijdraagt aan betere bedrijfsprocessen en besluitvorming? Dan is deze stage iets voor jou. Binnen het Data Quality-team werk je mee aan uiteenlopende vraagstukken rondom product- en artikeldata. Je onderzoekt hoe volledig en betrouwbaar gegevens zijn, brengt verbeterkansen in kaart en denkt mee over slimme oplossingen om de kwaliteit van data structureel te verhogen. Daarbij krijg je de kans om analyses uit te voeren, dashboards te ontwikkelen en processen te verbeteren, zodat data vanaf de bron direct goed wordt aangeleverd. Hoe ziet je werkweek als stagiair eruit? Onderzoek de kwaliteit, volledigheid en betrouwbaarheid van product- en artikeldata. Analyseer processen rondom data-aanlevering en identificeer verbeterkansen om gegevens in één keer juist vast te leggen. Controleer of productinformatie en categorisaties correct, compleet en consistent zijn. Ontwikkel en verbeter dashboards die inzicht geven in datakwaliteit en verbeteracties ondersteunen. Werk samen met collega's binnen het Data Quality-team en denk actief mee over nieuwe tools, werkwijzen en procesverbeteringen. Ben jij beschikbaar voor een meewerkstage van 32 tot 40 uur per week en wil je praktijkervaring opdoen binnen datakwaliteit en data-analyse? Dan maken we graag kennis met je! Dit krijg je ervoor terug Een inhoudelijk interessante meewerkstage op het gebied van datakwaliteit, data-analyse en procesverbetering. Een leerzame omgeving waarin je veel zelfstandigheid, verantwoordelijkheid en begeleiding krijgt. Een stagevergoeding van € 500,- per maand op fulltime basis. De mogelijkheid om samen te werken met ervaren collega's binnen een betrokken en deskundig team. Een waardevolle ervaring voor je cv én de kans om jezelf professioneel verder te ontwikkelen binnen het vakgebied data.

role: Manufacturing Science and Technology Process Engineering Co-Op
description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. **Position Summary** The MSAT PE Co-Op program is an excellent opportunity for aspiring engineers and scientists to gain hands-on experience in the fast-paced and evolving field of cell therapy manufacturing technology. This 6-month co-op program is designed to provide participants with valuable mentorship, executive exposure, and customized development opportunities that will enhance their technical, project management, and professional skills. The goal is to accelerate the participant's ability to deliver impactful results in a collaborative, dynamic environment. As part of the MSAT PE team, co-op participants will have the opportunity to contribute to key initiatives while learning about cutting-edge technologies in cell therapy manufacturing. The role involves a variety of technical tasks that will help build a strong foundation in the field. The full-time co-op will take place July - December 2027.**Key Responsibilities** - Experimental Design and Execution: Design, lead, and execute experiments to characterize and evaluate the limits of cell therapy equipment and processes. - Data Analysis: Analyze experimental data and/or continuous process monitoring data to draw actionable conclusions and improve understanding of manufacturing processes and cell therapy drug product and drive continuous improvement. - Technical Reporting: Communicate experimental results and technical findings effectively through detailed technical reports and presentations to key stakeholders. - Process Documentation: Support the creation and revision of process support documentation, ensuring accuracy and compliance with industry standards and internal requirements. - Database and Dashboard Management: Develop and maintain databases and dashboards to track experimental results and process performance metrics. - Continuous Improvement Initiatives: Contribute to continuous improvement efforts by identifying opportunities for enhancement throughout the cell therapy product lifecycle. - AI-Enablement: Lead projects using AI tools to improve the quality and efficiency of process engineering work. - Collaboration: Work closely with a multidisciplinary team of engineers and scientists to support various technical projects and process improvements. **Qualifications & Experience**Educational Background: - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree program in Biomedical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Biotechnology, Biological Sciences, or a related field. - Preference for students entering their junior or senior year, with a strong foundation in core scientific and engineering principles. - All candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and for the duration of their employment. Please note that visa sponsorship, including for student or temporary work authorization programs, is not available for this role. Candidates must have work authorization that does not require sponsorship now or in the future. Technical Skills: - Familiarity with basic laboratory techniques (e.g., cell culture, pipetting, sterile technique) and preferred experience with equipment used in biotech settings. - Basic understanding of statistical analysis and experience with data analysis software (e.g., Excel, MATLAB, R, Python, JMP for data visualization). Problem-Solving & Critical Thinking: - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down complex issues and find practical solutions. - Ability to think critically when designing experiments and analyzing data. - Familiarity with AI and other digital tools, with an interest in leveraging them to enhance problem-solving, analysis, and efficiency while critically evaluating outputs. Communication Skills: - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly convey technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences. - Experience in writing lab reports or academic papers is a plus. Project Management & Teamwork: - Ability to work both independently and as part of a cross-functional team. - Strong time management skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines in a dynamic environment. Software Proficiency: - Basic proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel). - Experience with database tools, dashboards, or statistical analysis software is a plus. Additional Qualifications (Preferred but Not Required): - Previous internship, lab, or co-op experience in a related field (biotechnology, engineering, or manufacturing). - Exposure to Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) in a manufacturing setting. description: **Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. We are hiring a Research Intern to make coding agents better, cheaper and faster through post-training: reinforcement learning, fine-tuning, distillation, compression and inference optimization. Coding agents now plan, edit repositories, run tests and fix failures over long, multi-step trajectories. Making them reliable and affordable is a post-training problem as much as a modeling one. Our team trains, evaluates and ships agentic coding models that power developer tools at scale. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. **Qualifications** **Required Qualifications** - Currently enrolled full time in a Doctoral Degree program in area in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related STEM field. **Other Requirements** - Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. - In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. **Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. Speech and audio Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology is one of the key drivers for advancing natural user interfaces with natural spoken language. The Speech and Audio Group is on a mission to develop the core speech technologies that empower millions of users to achieve more. Our group brings together talent in the areas of signal processing, speech recognition, speech translation, and speech and audio generation to develop and deliver robust, natural, and scalable speech experience across a rich set of scenarios and languages. We are seeking Research Interns to contribute to pioneering research in speech and audio. This includes areas such as end-to-end speech recognition and translation, speech and audio generation, and multimodal with Large Language Models (LLM). As a Research Intern, you will have the opportunity to conduct both fundamental and applied research in collaboration with our researchers and scientists. This position offers the opportunity to prototype, demonstrate, and publish your findings within Microsoft’s privileged. Most importantly, you will have the chance to push the boundaries of current technologies, making a significant impact on millions of users. **Responsibilities** Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. **Qualifications** #### Required Qualifications - Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in speech recognition, speech translation, separation, and enhancement, speaker recognition and diarization, speech and audio generation, audio processing, deep learning, machine learning, AI or a related field. **Other Requirements** - Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. - In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. #### Preferred Qualifications - 1+ year(s) of research experience in speech recognition, speech translation, speech and audio generation, speech LLM, deep learning, machine learning, AI or a related field. - Experience with open-source tools such as PyTorch, Tensorflow, etc. - Publication(s) in top-tier conferences or journals in related fields (e.g., ICASSP, Interspeech, ASRU, SLT, IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech and Language Processing, Speech Communication, Computer Speech and Language, etc.). - Demonstrated communication and writing skills. The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. role: Campus Fiber Infrastructure Construction Monitor, Data Centers
description: AECOM is seeking a Campus Fiber Infrastructure Construction Monitor to support construction of mission-critical data center campus fiber and telecommunications infrastructure in Texas. This field-based position is intended for an experienced construction professional with a strong understanding of underground utilities, telecommunications conduit systems, civil construction, construction drawings and field quality processes. The Construction Monitor will serve as AECOM's on-site representative, documenting whether observed work is consistent with approved drawings, project requirements, applicable construction standards and established quality requirements. The position requires a professional who can work effectively in an active construction environment, coordinate with construction managers, general contractors, subcontractors and technical teams, and maintain accurate, objective field documentation. This will be an on-site position at our offices in Houston, Texas. Key Responsibilities Construction Monitoring and Field Coordination Provide on-site monitoring of civil and telecommunications infrastructure construction. Monitor installation of underground conduit systems, duct banks, manholes, handholes, vaults, points of entry and related campus fiber infrastructure. Observe construction activities and document installation progress, field conditions and potential quality concerns. Monitor construction progress against planned activities and project milestones. Participate in construction coordination meetings and communicate field observations, outstanding items and potential schedule impacts. Coordinate with construction managers, general contractors, fiber teams and other project stakeholders. Identify potential conflicts, incomplete work and conditions that could affect future fiber installation or infrastructure readiness. Drawing and Design Review Read and interpret civil, telecommunications and fiber construction drawings. Review relevant CAD, BIM and GIS information to understand planned infrastructure locations and requirements. Compare observed field conditions with approved construction documentation. Identify apparent conflicts, omissions or deviations and escalate them through established project channels. Support pre-construction review of conduit routes, vault locations, points of entry and other telecommunications infrastructure. Quality Monitoring Observe installation of conduit, duct banks, vaults, manholes, handholes and related civil infrastructure. Document observed conduit routing, installation depth, materials and installation conditions. Observe conduit encasement and other critical construction activities when required. Monitor conduit proofing and mandrel-testing activities. Document nonconforming or potentially nonconforming conditions and communicate observations to the appropriate project representatives. Track identified issues through resolution and maintain clear supporting documentation. Support project closeout and verification of completed telecommunications infrastructure. Use GIS-based field applications to capture construction and inspection information. Maintain accurate location-based records for installed campus infrastructure. Capture photographs and supporting field information associated with observations. Support maintenance of accurate records for conduit, vaults, points of entry and other campus telecommunications infrastructure. Assist with verification of record and as-built information against observed field conditions. Maintain complete and organized field records suitable for project reporting and closeout documentation. Reporting and Communication Prepare clear and concise field reports documenting construction progress, observations, quality issues and outstanding items. Provide timely escalation of significant quality, schedule, safety or infrastructure concerns. Maintain issue and action-item tracking as required by the program. Communicate effectively with AECOM and client project leadership. Participate in recurring construction and program coordination meetings. Provide factual, objective and well-supported field documentation. Role Boundary The Construction Monitor documents observed conditions and provides recommendations based on those observations. Final acceptance of construction remains with the client or other designated project authority. The role does not relieve contractors of responsibility for construction means, methods, sequencing, safety, testing, workmanship or contractual compliance. Minimum Qualifications HS Diploma + 2 years of relevant field experience involving civil construction, underground utilities, telecommunications infrastructure, electrical infrastructure or comparable work. Experience working in active construction environments. Ability to read and interpret civil and/or telecommunications construction drawings. Working knowledge of underground conduit construction, vaults, manholes, handholes, trenching and duct banks. Understanding of construction sequencing, schedules and field quality-control practices. Experience documenting construction activities and preparing professional field reports. Ability to work independently while coordinating with multiple stakeholders. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to use computers, tablets and mobile field applications. Ability to travel among assigned project locations. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting data centers, mission-critical facilities, telecommunications networks or other technically complex programs. Background as a Construction Superintendent, Construction Manager, Field Engineer, Construction Inspector or Telecommunications Inspector. Experience with outside plant fiber and underground telecommunications conduit. Familiarity with ArcGIS Online and Survey123. Experience reviewing CAD and BIM construction information. Experience with Procore or similar construction-management platforms. OSHA construction safety training applicable to the assigned work. Experience coordinating directly with general contractors and construction-management teams. Relocation is not available for this role Sponsorship for U.S. employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position. **AI and ML at Flagship Pioneering:**Flagship Pioneering is a scientific innovation engine that invents and builds companies that change the world. We bring entrepreneurial scientists together with experienced company builders and assemble the capital to allow them to take courageous leaps in human health, sustainability, technology and beyond. Artificial intelligence is core to how Flagship conceives and builds companies. We call our approach *polyintelligence*: human creativity and nature’s intelligence integrating and coexisting with artificial intelligence. This model runs across our ecosystem, where teams pair advances in AI and machine learning with foundational science to move from idea to concept faster and build AI-native companies that were previously out of reach. **Who we are looking for:** Computational scientists and engineers with broad interests and experience applying deep technical experience to out of distribution scientific questions. Standalone implementation isn’t the goal, it is creatively spotting opportunities where extension, modification and combination of bleeding edge computational and technical approaches can unlock new capabilities to solve consequential problems. Strong candidates will combine software engineering fundamentals with a readiness to embrace agentic development tools/practices and have experience implementing machine learning models and workflows across multiple model classes or scientific domains. **The Experience:** You will collaborate with Flagship Origination Teams and fellow ML scientists/engineers to explore what is made possible by big leaps beyond the current capabilities of AI. You will begin by asking ‘What if’ across a variety of ideas and building a ‘future backwards’ case for what needs to be true for them to become a reality. You will explore the tradeoffs across multiple options, including what and how much data is needed and where it might come from. You will work towards implementation and evaluation plans that enable us to address the real uncertainties, not just what is easy to measure. With a project defined, you will begin to implement, evaluate and iterate. You will leverage Flagship's scalable GPU compute resources, data from our ecosystem, and the extensive expertise available across our teams. You will implement the benchmarking capabilities needed to measure what matters and evaluate your designs. We will learn along the way and be ready to pivot on methods. Final work products are never just a model or a paper, they are wholistic answers to the future backwards questions we ask ourselves when originating the next big leap company. The pay range for this role is $7,000 - $9,000 per month. This role is a short-term engagement that is not eligible for health and welfare benefits.
