role: Data Associate - Internship (6 months, flexible start)
description: ## **Health can’t wait**. Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t. Alan exists to end the wait. Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way. So we are building the **new standard in prevention insurance.** Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience. We are on an incredible journey to build a **global leading company, with a** [**unique culture**](https://alan.com/en/careers). We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR. Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond. ## ⭐ Data associate ⭐ *The position is a six-month end-of-studies internship in Paris, with a flexible start date.* Data Associates join a product or business crew and work alongside a senior member of the Data team, taking on a real share of their projects. It is the same work as the rest of the team, building insights and data-powered products that help our members stay healthy, at a pace and scope designed for someone starting out. Our team is full stack: each member sits in a crew next to engineers, product builders and designers and leads projects from A to Z, covering analytics, engineering and science. We mainly use SQL, Python, dbt, Airflow and Metabase, and Claude Code and AI agents are part of our daily workflow. Want to know more? Read [our vision for the Data team](https://medium.com/alan/vision-for-a-data-team-2eae845b8052) (old one, but still relevant) and how [our Data team is re-inventing its craft with AI](https://medium.com/alan/re-inventing-our-craft-how-alans-data-team-is-shaping-its-future-with-ai-e8d73d095ece). This is our first generation of Data Associates, and we built the program with one goal: **you join us full-time at the end of it**. That decision is made at your 5-month review. ## ⭐ Detailed missions ⭐ What you work on depends on the crew you join, something that is decided once you start your internship, but your six months will mix: - **Answering real business or product questions**: framing the problem, digging into the data and turning what you find into a recommendation your crew acts on. - **Building tools people use**: a dbt model, a dashboard a team uses every week, a tool powered by AI. You would ship them end to end, with your senior counterpart supporting you on key steps - **Growing with the Data community**: joining our main rituals (retros, insights sharing sessions, on-call shifts), and later helping us recruit the next generation of Data Associates **You won’t be alone**: from day one, you will benefit from a senior Alaner from the Data team to work with at the office and a coach from the Data team as well. ## ⭐ Is it you we're looking for? ⭐ Please note that for this internship, you need to: - Be based in Paris, France - Work from our Valmy office at least 4 days a week - Be in the final year of your studies (engineering or business, with a strong quantitative track), with an internship agreement from your school You would be a great fit if most of this sounds like you: - You want a career in **Data, across the whole spectrum**. If what you want above everything else is to build ML models, a research internship is probably a better fit for you - You have used **SQL and Python**, at school, in an internship or on a side project. We teach you the rest - **Analytical sense and rigor**: you ask the right question before you reach for the data, and you can tell a real signal from noise - **Business & product sense**: you care about what the numbers change for members and for the company - **Effective communication**: you explain a result simply, in writing and out loud - **High agency and growth mindset**: facing an unfamiliar problem, your first instinct is to find a way through, and you ask for feedback to grow - **AI fluency**: you already build with AI tools, and you are curious about where they fall short - You are fluent in English (no need to speak French!) **But above all, we are looking for high potential and curiosity: make sure to show us this when you apply! Everything else is a bonus.** For this internship, we are hiring at the A2 level of our [salary grid](https://alan.com/en/careers/a/salary-equity). ## 🎯 Important note: we hire people, not roles If you're excited about this opportunity but don't check every box, **we'd love to hear from you.** Everyone, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply as it can only bring learnings or success. **If you identify yourself as a woman**: Did you know that research shows women often apply only when meeting 100% of requirements? **Remember, this is just a guide, not a checklist.** We'll be thrilled to receive your application! 🔖 Check out our [About Alan](https://alan.com/about) and [Career](https://alan.com/careers) pages, as well as our [Medium](https://medium.com/alan), [blog](https://blog.alan.com/) and [Glassdoor page](https://www.glassdoor.com/Overview/Working-at-Alan-EI_IE1696043.11,15.htm) for more info. ## You want to know more about Alan? - 🙌 [Perks & Benefits](https://alan.com/en/careers/a/salary-equity): Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers. - 🤘 [A strong culture](https://alan.com/en/about/a/leadership-principles): people joining Alan are often surprised and delighted by our innovative working method. We have a set of cultural values that guide our approach to work. #LI-DNP

We’re looking for an analytically strong, business-minded student to make our forecasting more predictive and more robust. You’ll work deeply with Salesforce pipeline data and build models that segment and score opportunities, forecast revenue, and surface the leading indicators behind forecast outcomes. You’ll also turn that work into insights that shape business planning. **What You’ll Work On:** - **Predictive forecasting**: Develop and enhance predictive models that improve revenue forecasting accuracy, strengthen pipeline visibility, and give forward-looking insight into revenue performance. - **Continuous improvement**: Build scalable, repeatable analytical processes, and monitor, backtest, and refine models over time to improve forecast reliability. **Required Qualifications:** - Must be able to work on-site at our Durham, NC headquarters at least one day per week; two days preferred. - role: NIQ Early Career Program: Data and Client Operations Intern (English and German)
location: Warsaw, Gdanski Business Center II, Inflancka 4B and 4C Street Building C and D, 3rd and 4th Floor, Poland
description: Responsibilities and key learnings Understand a broad portfolio of NIQ solutions, such as market analysis tools, consumer behavior tracking systems, and data visualization platforms. Investigate, validate, and resolve client queries through efficient workflows. Perform feasibility studies and analyze data to determine the most appropriate solution. Work on diverse data challenges, always ensuring a combination of simplicity, scalability, reproducibility, and maintainability. Communicate results effectively to both internal and external stakeholders. Experience working with large real-world datasets and top FMCG companies in Europe. Gain insight into the retail and Consumer Insight business. Work as a member of a team, fostering collaboration, motivation, and cultivating effective team relations. During the full-time phase, employees benefit from a hybrid working model, combining remote and in-office work. We provide all the necessary equipment to ensure you can work effectively and comfortably, whether from home or the office. International Team - You’ll be working with a diverse, international team, interacting daily with colleagues and stakeholders from different countries. English will be your primary language, giving you the chance to work in a truly global environment. Skill Development - This role provides an exciting opportunity to develop expertise by working closely with diverse clients. You'll gain firsthand experience in understanding client needs, delivering tailored solutions, and managing complex projects, which will sharpen your analytical, communication, and client management skills. There are also opportunities for relocation within other departments or even countries, making your career pathway both dynamic and expansive. Exposure to Cutting-Edge Technology – Engage with the latest tools and innovations shaping our industry. People & Planet Day Participation – Take part in our global initiative focused on sustainability and community impact. Required Education, Skills and Experience Bachelor degree, which can be pursued concurrently with a Masters program if it allows for 3-days a week employment and transition to full-time after the first cycle. Fluent level of English is required, as well as fluency in German. Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to understand client needs, interpret data, and translate insights into actionable solutions. description: **Your Impact at LILA** Our team works on AI methods for therapeutic protein design, with a tight loop between computation and the wet lab. (1) Generative models and protein design pipelines: build, benchmark, and improve methods for designing proteins (such as antibodies and minibinders), with candidates tested in our lab so results are grounded in experimental data. (2) AI agents for protein design campaigns: build and evaluate agents that help plan campaign strategy (target and epitope selection, choosing methods and settings), execute campaigns (launching design and filtering runs, diagnosing failures, adapting the next round), and reason over biological priors from the literature alongside the outputs of domain-specific models. Either way, the co-op would own a well-scoped project, ship code and analyses that feed real design decisions and scientific outcomes. **What You'll Be Building** - Develop, evaluate, and apply agentic systems for protein design and/or deep generative models for protein design. **What You'll Need to Succeed** - Strong python and and computational science background. - Experience with coding agents. - Experience with machine learning for molecular design **Bonus Points For** - Experience with customizing agents, building harnesses, or using agents for scientific applications - Solid technical understand and experience with generative models. **About LILA** Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves. LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. role: Internship: Explainable AI for the qualification of aerospace algorithms
description: Background Machine learning is increasingly used in aerospace for tasks that have traditionally relied on human experts or on fixed rule-based procedures. For such tasks, data-driven algorithms promise gains in speed, consistency and sensitivity. Before they can be used in practice however, they must be qualified, which means it has to be demonstrated with sufficient substantiation that the algorithm performs its intended function reliably within a defined set of conditions. The qualification approaches used in the sector today were developed for human operators and for conventional systems whose behaviour can be traced back to explicit requirements. They do not translate directly to algorithms whose behaviour is learned from data, and emerging guidance from aviation authorities names explainability as a key ingredient of trustworthy AI, while leaving open how it should be demonstrated in practice. Performance figures on a test set do not show why an algorithm reaches a decision, whether it relies on physically meaningful information, or how it behaves outside the data it was trained on. Explainable machine learning offers a wide range of methods to address this, from feature attribution and saliency methods, to example-based and concept-based explanations, but it is still an open question which of these can provide evidence that is strong enough to support qualification. This project therefore investigates how explainability methods can contribute to the qualification of machine learning algorithms for aerospace, starting from an use case, and provides a comparative assessment of several methods. Assignment The assignment will include the following tasks: A literature study on the qualification of machine learning algorithms in safety-critical sectors and on explainability methods for machine learning (e.g., attribution and saliency methods, example-based and concept-based explanations, interpretable models, uncertainty quantification), including the ways in which explanations themselves are evaluated. A use case provided by NLR, for instance automated defect detection, and identification of the substantiation needed to qualify the algorithm, translated into criteria that explanations should meet. Implementing several explainability methods for the use case and analysing them against these criteria, for example their faithfulness to the model, their robustness and their usefulness to domain experts. Assessing how the resulting explanations can serve as evidence in the qualification of the algorithm, and formulating recommendations for the use of explainability in qualification. Results The final outcomes of this assignment will be: § A structured assessment, as part of a literature study, of explainability methods for machine learning and their suitability for qualification in aerospace, together with a justified selection of the use case. § An implementation and comparative evaluation of several explainability methods on the selected use case, with recommendations on how explainability can support the qualification of the algorithm. § A technical report, either an MSc thesis following the guidelines of your faculty or an internship report, describing the approach, results, and conclusions of the work. Duration For an MSc thesis, the standard duration of a thesis at your faculty applies (typically 9 months). For an internship, the duration is 6 months. Profile You are an MSc student in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Applied Mathematics or a similar master. You have a strong background in machine learning, preferably deep learning. Knowledge of explainable AI is a plus. You have experience with programming in Python and with machine learning libraries, for instance PyTorch or scikit-learn. You have an affinity with aerospace, inspection or certification, and are motivated to bring machine learning closer to qualified use in practice. role: Internship: Designing a flexible robotics research platform
description: Background The NLR carries out research on automated inspection, which may require robotic solutions. Such robotics research depends on experimental setups that change often. Robots, sensors and controllers are added, replaced or reconfigured from one project to the next, and new technologies need to be tried out quickly and efficiently. In practice, research setups are often built around one specific combination of hardware and software, which makes every change time-consuming. NLR therefore wants a robotics research platform in which components can be switched easily and new components can be introduced with little effort. The challenge lies in the overall design of such a platform. Flexibility has to be built into both the hardware and the software. On the hardware side, modular control systems such as the Beckhoff MX-System make it easier to add or exchange components. On the software side, open frameworks such as the Robot Operating System (ROS) offer standard interfaces and reusable building blocks. How such elements can be combined into one platform, with an operating environment that supports changing research needs, is an open question. This project aims to develop a high-level design of the overall system and its control, and shows the concept in a small demonstration. Assignment The assignment will include the following tasks: A study of approaches to modular and reconfigurable robotic systems, covering both control hardware and software frameworks (e.g., the Beckhoff MX-System and ROS). Drawing up the requirements for a flexible robotics research platform together with NLR researchers. Making a high-level design of the overall system and its control, including the interfaces that allow components to be switched and new components to be introduced, and the operating environment that enables this flexibility. Building a small demonstration of the concept. Results The final outcomes of this assignment will be: § An overview of approaches to modular and reconfigurable robotic systems, together with the requirements for the research platform. § A high-level design of the overall system and its control, including the operating environment. § A small demonstration of the concept. § A technical report, either an internship report or a graduation thesis following the guidelines of your programme, describing the approach, results, and conclusions of the work. Duration For an MSc thesis, the standard duration of a thesis at your faculty applies (typically 9 months). For an internship, the duration is 6 months. Profile You are an MSc student or HBO graduate student in Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Technical Computer Science or a similar master/bachelor. You have an interest in the system design and control of robotic or mechatronic systems. You have some experience with programming, for instance in Python or C++. Experience with robotics software or industrial control systems is a plus. You enjoy hands-on work with hardware and software, and are motivated to turn a design into a working demonstration. role: Director of Product, Clasp Student Finance
description: ### **Location** Open to Remote in EST or CST Locations. Up to 10% travel required. ### **About Us** Clasp is a mission-driven, venture-backed startup transforming access to education and career pathways. A college education was always meant to lead to economic mobility. But with rising costs and shrinking loan availability, many working-class and first-generation students don’t have the money they need to finish school. That’s where Clasp comes in. We’re the market leader in institutionally funded gap loan programs. We partner with schools to design, launch and manage lending programs that keep students enrolled, graduating and thriving. Fresh off our Series B, Clasp is entering its next phase of growth. Recent recognition includes: - TIME’s Best Inventions of 2026 (Loan-Linked Hiring) - Forbes Fintech 50 - Business Insider: *Top 14 Healthcare Startups to Watch in 2026* and *43 Startups to Bet Your Career On in 2025* Our work spans two business lines: Clasp Talent helps healthcare employers attract and retain critical talent by connecting them with diverse candidates and using student loan repayment as a powerful recruiting and retention tool. We meaningfully connect employers, educational institutions, and learners to drive mutual benefit. Clasp Student Finance equips colleges and universities with lending technology to launch and operate their own private student loan programs, enabling schools to step in and support their students directly with financial aid. Recent federal financial aid changes are reshaping how institutions think about supporting their students, and Clasp Student Finance is poised to meet this moment. This role is focused solely on Clasp Student Finance. You can learn more about this business line [here](https://www.clasp.com/studentfinance). ### **Who We Need** We are hiring a Director of Product for the Clasp Student Finance business line. We’ve seen rapid acceleration since recent federal student loan policy changes. We’re landing deals with large, name-brand universities who are seeing that Clasp’s offering is crucial for filling gaps in student loan financing. We have real product market fit, but there is a lot to build when it comes to scale, excellent borrower experience, and the enterprise features that large universities need. We're hiring a Director of Product to make the right calls on our product strategy to make sure we can capitalize on this momentum. You'll own the product strategy for Clasp Student Finance and work across our executive team, product, engineering, compliance and lending operations to deliver it. We want you to bring your own point of view, back it up with data, and push back when you think we're heading the wrong way. Some days you'll present the year's product plan to our executive team and board. Other days you'll be in refinement with engineering, making the call on a single feature. ## Teamwork makes the stream work. ### **Roku is changing how the world watches TV** Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers. From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines. **About the role** Join Roku as an Engineering Intern and help build the agentic AI powering America’s #1 TV streaming platform. Roku reaches more than 100 million households worldwide, and we’re building production-grade AI agents across the products and platforms that serve them. We offer a paid 12-week internship, running from June to early September 2027. As an Engineering Intern, you’ll be assigned a scoped project with one of our engineering teams and matched to the team that best fits your skills and interests. You’ll work on real problems, such as agents that investigate failures, automate workflows, review or generate code, or help people make complex decisions. You’ll learn how to take an AI-powered idea from prototype to something people actually use, with a mentor alongside you and real ownership from day one. Our teams work across a variety of languages and technologies, from user interfaces and embedded software to platform services, automation and developer tooling, and embrace AI-assisted development to boost productivity and quality. **What you’ll be doing** - Own a well-defined project that contributes to the success of your team, from defining the problem through to delivery. - Build and test AI agents, copilots and automated workflows that perform meaningful, multi-step work. - Connect agents to trusted data, services and internal tools, using approaches such as retrieval, tool calling and orchestration, and help define what an agent may do on its own and when it should hand over to a person. - Evaluate your work: measure whether it does the job well, check its reliability and failure modes, and keep improving it based on real feedback. - Use AI coding tools every day to move faster, and validate everything they produce through testing, review and your own judgment. - Write clean, well-tested, documented code, take part in code reviews, and collaborate with engineers, mentors and cross-functional partners. **Apply if** - You are a penultimate-year student, or a final-year student planning to go on to a one-year master’s course. - You hold a permanent right to work in the US. Unfortunately, we are unable to consider candidates on a student visa. - You are available for full-time work for the whole 12-week program, from June to early September. - You are keen to work with AI technologies and have previous experience building AI agents and automated workflows. **We’re excited if you have** - Currently enrolled in a degree program in Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Engineering or a related field. - Proficiency in Python, ideally with projects, open source or hackathon work beyond your coursework. - Hands-on experience building an LLM-powered or agentic system that does multi-step work, and ideally that someone other than you has used. - Familiarity with agentic patterns such as grounding and retrieval, tool use, orchestration, memory or conversational interfaces. - Sound engineering judgment: you check AI-generated work, understand how it can fail, and recognise when simple automation or a human review is the better approach. - A solid grounding in computer science fundamentals such as data structures, algorithms, and operating systems or networking concepts. - Strong problem-solving and technical communication abilities, and the ability to break down ambiguous problems and deliver in small steps. - Proactive mindset with passion for continuous learning and fast iteration. **How will I use AI at Roku?** At Roku, we don’t just use AI, we work with it. AI agents and smart tools help power drafts, analysis, and repetitive workflows, while our people bring direction, judgment, and accountability. We’re looking for curious, adaptable builders who can show how they’ve used AI or automation to move faster, raise the bar, and scale their impact. We value your AI skills if you have built fluency across the agentic engineering toolchain — coding harnesses like Claude Code or Cursor, MCP servers, custom skills, or agent frameworks. You know how to drive an agent, verify its output, and ramp up on an unfamiliar codebase with an agent helping you. ### **What's Roku's approach to hybrid working?** Roku fosters an inclusive and collaborative environment where teams generally work in the office Monday through Thursday. Fridays are generally flexible for remote work, except for employees whose specific roles or assigned office location require five days' a week attendance. ### **What are some of the benefits?** Roku is committed to offering a diverse range of benefits as part of our compensation package to support our employees and their families. Our comprehensive benefits include global access to mental health and financial wellness support and resources. Local benefits include statutory and voluntary benefits which may include healthcare (medical, dental, and vision), life, accident, disability, commuter, and retirement options (401(k)/pension). Employees are supported in taking time off, in accordance with local leave policies and other personal needs to support their evolving work and life needs. It's important to note that not every benefit is available in all locations or for every role. For details specific to your location, please consult with your recruiter. ### **Accommodations** Roku welcomes applicants of all backgrounds and provides reasonable accommodations and adjustments in accordance with applicable law. If you require reasonable accommodation at any point in the hiring process, please direct your inquiries to [EmployeeRelations@Roku.com](mailto:employeerelations@roku.com?subject=Job%20Application%20Accommodations). ### **What should I know about Roku's culture?** Roku is a great place for people who want to work in a fast-paced environment where everyone is focused on the company's success rather than their own. We try to surround ourselves with people who are great at their jobs, who are easy to work with, and who keep their egos in check. We appreciate a sense of humor. We believe a fewer number of very talented folks can do more for less cost than a larger number of less talented teams. We're independent thinkers with big ideas who act boldly, move fast and accomplish extraordinary things through collaboration and trust. In short, at Roku you'll be part of a company that's changing how the world watches TV. We have a unique culture that we are proud of. We think of ourselves primarily as problem-solvers, which itself is a two-part idea. We come up with the solution, but the solution isn't real until it is built and delivered to the customer. That penchant for action gives us a pragmatic approach to innovation, one that has served us well since 2002. To learn more about Roku, our global footprint, and how we've grown, visit . ### About Tensordyne AI is transforming our world. It can perform cognitive functions that previously only humans could do, such as perceiving interactions across different modalities and environments - with the ability to quickly learn and then solve complex problems. Tensordyne is an AI system solution company that builds very high-performance, low-power generative AI inference systems. Our mission, through the creation of custom silicon, hardware and software, is to enable multimodal Generative AI inference acceleration at scale, with safe, sustainable, high-performance systems for our hyperscaler and neocloud data center customers. We are at the leading edge of advancing the latest research and product improvements for generative Al inference solutions that will make Al even more advantageous for compelling new generative AI applications.Tensordyne is a well funded, fast-paced startup company with headquarters in both Sunnyvale, CA, and Munich, Germany. We also have many talented team members working remotely across North America and Europe. We take care of our people and their families with comprehensive benefits, competitive compensation, flexible spending options, and recognition programs, because building category-defining technology starts with a healthy, supported team. Come join us as we shape the future of multimodal generative artificial intelligence! ### About the Role How fast should an LLM building block run on our hardware? How fast does it actually run, and what would make it faster? As a Working Student, LLM Inference Performance, you'll help answer these questions by working directly with our hardware and software engineering teams. You'll write and optimize low-level kernels, benchmark performance on real silicon, and develop profiling tools that help engineers understand and improve LLM inference performance. You'll gain hands-on experience with our Rust programming stack and Python SDK, use AI coding agents as part of your development workflow, and collaborate closely with engineers working on compilers, runtimes, and kernel optimization. This is an opportunity to apply your academic knowledge to real-world AI hardware challenges while taking ownership of meaningful technical projects. ### What You'll Do - Understand our hardware: Learn how Tensordyne silicon processes data, manages memory, and synchronizes operations, and how key LLM components such as attention, MLP, and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routing map onto the architecture.. - Develop and optimize kernels: Implement, test, and tune low-level kernels to improve the performance of LLM inference workloads.. - Analyze performance: Build analytical and roofline performance models, compare predictions against simulator and real-silicon measurements, and investigate performance bottlenecks.. - Build benchmarking and profiling tools: Develop benchmark harnesses, profiling scripts, and trace visualizations that make performance easier to measure, understand, and improve.. - Work with AI coding agents: Explore workflows where AI agents assist with kernel development, optimization, and benchmarking, and identify the tools and context they need to work effectively.. - Collaborate across engineering teams: Work closely with compiler, runtime, and kernel engineers to translate performance insights into practical improvements.. Example project: Develop a benchmarking and profiling harness for an LLM building block, such as decode attention, at two abstraction levels. Compare measured performance against theoretical estimates and make the tooling accessible to AI coding agents. ### What We're Looking For - Currently enrolled in a Master's degree program in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, or a related technical field.. - Strong programming skills in Python and at least one of C, C++, or Rust.. - Understanding of computer architecture, memory systems, bandwidth, and parallel computing through academic coursework or personal projects.. - Interest in low-level programming, hardware performance, and optimization.. - Practical experience using AI coding agents in development workflows, with the ability to evaluate and improve their output.. - An experimental mindset, with the ability to form hypotheses, analyze measurements, and communicate technical findings clearly.. - Curiosity, initiative, and enthusiasm for learning new technologies.. ### Nice to Have Experience in one or more of the following areas would be a plus: - GPU or AI accelerator programming.. - Embedded systems or bare-metal programming.. - Performance profiling, benchmarking, or optimization.. - LLM inference fundamentals and architectures.. ### Why Join Tensordyne? - Work on cutting-edge AI technology: Contribute to the development of next-generation AI inference hardware and software.. - Gain hands-on experience: Apply your university knowledge to real silicon and challenging engineering problems.. - Own meaningful projects: Build tools and solutions that directly support our engineering teams.. - Learn from experienced engineers: Work alongside specialists in hardware architecture, compilers, runtimes, and performance optimization.. - Explore AI-assisted development: Gain practical experience building with AI coding agents and shaping how they interact with advanced hardware systems.. - Make a lasting impact: Help develop performance tools and workflows that will support both current and future generations of Tensordyne technology.. ### **Tensordyne's culture was built on the following values** - Put people first. We only succeed when our people succeed. - Ethics and integrity always. Be open, honest, and respectful of everyone. - Think Big. Be ambitious and have audacious goals. - Aim for excellence. ## **About us** Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia. We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do. Our co-founders are [Bret Taylor](https://www.linkedin.com/in/brettaylor/) and [Clay Bavor](https://www.linkedin.com/in/claybavor/). Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace. Sierra’s Applied Research team works to make the models behind our agents better, faster, and cheaper across many kinds of tasks. Our work covers post-training open-weight models for specialized capabilities, new approaches to voice AI, and the benchmarks the field uses to measure agents, including τ-bench. As an Applied Research Intern, you’ll join the team for a research project, working with a mentor, you’ll pick a problem that matters to how AI agents perform in the real world, run rigorous experiments, and potentially write up what you find for a top venue. If you want your research to reach both the research community and production agents used by millions of people, come do it at Sierra. ## What you’ll do - Own a research project from start to finish, from framing the question and running experiments to writing and submitting a paper. - Push agent evaluation forward, for example by extending τ-bench to new domains, modalities, or long-horizon tasks, or by building new ways to measure reliability and consistency. - Study how agents reason, use tools, and follow policies over multi-turn conversations, and find out where and why they fail. - Explore post-training methods such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to improve agent behavior, and measure the gains rigorously. - Work with large-scale, proprietary datasets of text and audio interactions to find research questions grounded in real customer problems. - Work with researchers and engineers across Sierra, and where it makes sense, turn your findings into improvements in production. ## What you’ll bring - Currently pursuing a PhD in computer science, machine learning, or a related field. - A research track record, such as first-author publications or submissions at venues like NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, Interspeech or ICASSP. - Strong experimental skills: you design clean experiments, build careful baselines, and are honest about what the results do and do not show. - Fluency in Python and modern ML tooling (for example, PyTorch, and LLM inference and training stacks). - High agency and a builder’s mindset. You’ll work across the stack to get an experiment running. - Clear, direct communication, both in writing and when presenting research. ## Even better - Research experience with LLM agents, tool use, or multi-turn dialogue. - Experience designing benchmarks or evaluations, especially ones tied to real-world outcomes. - Experience with supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or long-horizon optimization. - Experience with speech, voice, or multimodal models. - Open-source contributions to ML research code or benchmarks. ## Intern qualifications - The internship is open to students currently enrolled in a PhD program. - Duration and start dates are flexible. Interns are embedded with the Applied Research team and work under the guidance of a mentor. - The internship is based in our San Francisco office. We are in person Monday through Thursday. ## **Our values** - **Trust:** We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work. - **Customer Obsession:** We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it. - **Craftsmanship:** We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve. - **Intensity:** We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time. - **Family:** We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements. ## **What we offer** We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees: - Flexible (unlimited) paid time off - Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family - Life insurance and disability benefits - Retirement plan dependent on country of employment - Parental leave - Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot - Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized - Discretionary benefit stipend giving people the ability to spend where it matters most - Free alphorn lessons These benefits are further detailed in Sierra's policies, may vary by region, and are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation or benefits plans. Eligible full-time employees can participate in Sierra's equity plans subject to the terms of the applicable plans and policies. ## **Be you, with us** We're working to bring the transformative power of AI to every organization in the world. To do so, it is important to us that the diversity of our employees represents the diversity of our customers. We believe that our work and culture are better when we encourage, support, and respect different skills and experiences represented within our team. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. We strive to evaluate all applicants consistently without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

The lab has recently expanded its focus from crypto-focused research to include other emerging areas of technology, ranging from AI-enabled applications to new scientific developments in materials, energy, and hardware. Example research areas of interest include AI and machine learning, agentic commerce, cryptography, security, distributed computing, hardware design, economics (micro, macro, and empirical), energy, material science, biology, incentives, quantitative finance, market and mechanism design, foundations of computing, and pure mathematics. The Role: As a field-based Assistant Project Engineer Intern, you will: - Support project managers and field teams by assisting in project documentation, scheduling, and coordination of daily activities. - Review project drawings and specifications to ensure alignment with project goals and compliance with industry standards. - Track and document project progress, including daily logs, material deliveries, and work completed. - Participate in on-site meetings to gain exposure to real-time problem-solving and decision-making. - Assist in the preparation of RFIs (Requests for Information) and submittals to ensure project milestones are met. - Contribute to maintaining project safety standards by observing and reporting on-site conditions. - Engage with subcontractors and suppliers, supporting procurement and logistics activities. What Really Makes You Stand Out: - High emotional intelligence and the ability to build rapport with diverse individuals. - Proficiency in construction management software like ProCore, ViewPoint, or Microsoft Project. - A passion for innovation and problem-solving. What We Offer You: - Autonomy: We empower our interns to make informed decisions and contribute to the success of their projects. - Career Development: We invest in your growth, providing tools and resources to help you achieve your professional goals. - Challenging Work: You’ll be involved in diverse projects that keep you engaged and continuously learning. Join us at Granger Construction, where your internship is not just a stepping stone but a foundation for a successful career in construction. This is a paid position.

role: Research Intern - Office of Applied Research
description: **Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The Office of Applied Research in Microsoft seeks research interns to conduct state-of-the-art applied research. Applied research is impact-driven research. It applies empirical techniques to real world problems in a way that transforms theory into reality, advancing the state-of-the-art in the process. The Office of Applied Research brings together experts in frontier Artificial Intelligence (AI) model development and human-centered AI to tackle real-world challenges at scale in the enterprise AI space. We work closely with research and product partners to ensure Microsoft is advancing cutting-edge research aligned with our core product interests. Ideal candidates have proven experience in various fields such as Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), Natural Language Processing (NLP), Reinforcement Learning (RL), Learning from human feedback and Human-centered AI. We are particularly interested in candidates with expertise in areas such as reinforcement learning and model mid- and post-training, continual learning, differential privacy, human-AI collaboration, or the development and evaluation of enterprise AI agents, including learning from user feedback in real-world deployments. **Responsibilities** Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. **Qualifications** #### Required Qualifications - Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, Information Science, Statistics, Information Systems, Economics, Operation Research or a related STEM field. **Other Requirements** - Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. - In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. #### Preferred Qualifications - 1+ year(s) of experience in conducting research and writing peer-reviewed publications. - Ability to think unconventionally to derive creative and innovative solutions. - Actively conducting research in at least one of the following areas: - Collaborative or Multi-party AI Agents (e.g. AI teammates) - Mid- and post-training for LLMs / Agents - Learning from user interaction or feedback - Synthetic data generation for LLM evaluation and fine-tuning - Understanding, verifying, or evaluating LLMs outputs - Differential privacy for LLM and data - Continual Learning / Test-time Training - Agents (e.g. Memory, Goal management, Inter-Agent conversations) - Multi Agent Simulations (e.g. evaluating or training AI agents in collaborative settings) - Forward deployment for enterprise AI - Ability to collaborate effectively with your mentor and others in Microsoft on research projects. - Demonstrated interpersonal and communication skills, cross-group, and cross-culture collaboration skills. The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here: Microsoft accepts applications and processes offers for these roles on an ongoing basis throughout the academic calendar (September - April). This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. --- Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. If you need assistance with religious accommodations and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application process, read more about [**requesting accommodations.**](https://careers.microsoft.com/v2/global/en/accessibility.html)

##### **Position Overview |** ##### We are seeking a skilled IT Specialist to support and enhance our IT infrastructure, cloud services, and end-user experience. This role combines hands-on helpdesk support, network administration, cloud technologies, and IT asset management to ensure secure, reliable, and efficient systems across the organization. ##### **Key responsibilities|** **Helpdesk & End-User Support** - Provide Tier 1–2 technical support for hardware, software, and SaaS applications - Diagnose and resolve issues related to laptops, desktops, mobile devices, and peripherals - Support operating systems (Windows, macOS, Linux) and productivity tools - Document issues, resolutions, and procedures in the ticketing system **Cloud & Systems Administration** - Support and maintain cloud platforms (e.g., Google Cloud, Slack, etc….) - Manage user access, permissions, and identity services (e.g., Google SSO, IAM) - Assist with cloud-based backups, monitoring, and security best practices - Support SaaS applications such as Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack, Jira, etc. **Networking** - Monitor network performance and resolve connectivity issues - Assist with network security controls and access management **IT Asset Management** - Manage the full lifecycle of IT assets (procurement, deployment, tracking, maintenance, and decommissioning) - Maintain accurate asset inventory records and ensure compliance - Coordinate device provisioning, replacements, and returns - Support onboarding and offboarding processes **Security & Compliance** - Follow IT security policies and best practices - Assist with endpoint protection, patching, and vulnerability remediation (e.g., SentinelOne, Kandji/Iru MDM) - Support audits and compliance requirements as needed ### Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in computer science or - 4+ years provided support in the form of Linux\Windows\Mac OS architecture - Experience with supporting Video Conference Systems. (Google Meet / Logitech Room Systems) - SaaS / Cloud experience (Google Workplace / Slack / 1Password / SSO) - Understanding of system and application integration, as well automation engineering - Able to work off hours for maintenance and projects - Periodic travel to other offices to help support staff.

location: New York, New York, United States
description: Founded in Silicon Valley in 2009 by Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, Andreessen Horowitz (aka a16z) is a venture capital firm that backs bold entrepreneurs [building the future](https://a16z.com/news-content) through technology. We are [stage-agnostic](https://a16z.com/portfolio). We invest in seed- to venture- to [growth-stage technology](https://a16z.com/growth/) companies, across [AI](https://a16z.com/ai/), [bio + healthcare](https://a16z.com/bio-health/), [consumer](https://a16z.com/consumer/), [frontier](https://a16zfrontier.com/), [enterprise](https://a16z.com/enterprise/), [fintech](https://a16z.com/fintech/), [games](https://a16z.com/games), and companies building toward [American dynamism](https://a16z.com/american-dynamism/). a16z has $100B+ under management across multiple funds. We’ve established a [team](https://a16zfrontier.com/our-team/) that [is defined by](https://a16z.com/about/) respect for the entrepreneur and the company-building process; we know what it’s like to be in the founder’s shoes. Our team is at the forefront of new technology, helping founders and their companies impact and change the world. ## The Role a16z Frontier research is a [multidisciplinary lab](https://a16zfrontier.com/posts/focus-areas/research/) that bridges the worlds of academic theory and industry practice. The lab has recently expanded its focus from crypto-focused research to include other emerging areas of technology, ranging from AI-enabled applications to new scientific developments in materials, energy, and hardware. In addition to fundamental research, we collaborate with portfolio companies to solve hard technical and conceptual problems. Research interns will have the opportunity to learn from and collaborate with the firm’s investment and engineering teams. We are seeking students with a strong technical background and an interest in emerging technologies to join the group for the summer. Example research areas of interest include AI and machine learning, agentic commerce, cryptography, security, distributed computing, hardware design, economics (micro, macro, and empirical), energy, material science, biology, incentives, quantitative finance, market and mechanism design, foundations of computing, and pure mathematics. This list is not exhaustive and we encourage applicants with different backgrounds, who may have unique perspectives on the emerging technologies, to apply. We anticipate selecting a wide range of applicants, including ambitious undergraduate students with a unique grasp of emerging technologies, graduate students looking to transition from academic work to building and entrepreneurship, and PhD students pursuing a more traditional academic career. This role will be based in New York City, NY and requires in-office presence in our New York City, NY office. ## To join our team, you should be excited to: - Pursue fundamental research on topics relevant to the firm. - Collaborate with a16z Frontier’s full-time researchers and other student interns. - Collaborate with portfolio companies on technical research problems. - Quickly develop expertise in emerging areas of science and technology. - Take full advantage of the latest generation of AI tools. - Contribute to blog posts, white papers, and other public expository content. - Meet with visitors from academia and industry and attend research seminars. ## Preferred Qualifications - Pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in a relevant field such as computer science, economics, mathematics, operations research, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, materials science, physics, chemistry, biology, etc. - Passionate, knowledgeable, and optimistic about science and technology. - Experience with absorbing and producing fundamental research. ## Internship Details - A typical schedule will have an intern spending ⅔ of the time pursuing their own research (typically in collaboration with other lab members and visitors) and ⅓ of the time collaborating on portfolio-related problems. - In-person residency required in New York, NY. - Interns will have access to and will typically make heavy use of the latest AI tools. - Duration of internship **June 1, 2027 – August 20, 2027**(minimum residency 10 weeks, maximum 12 weeks). - The anticipated weekly rate is dependent on the current degree program. Actual starting pay may vary based on a range of factors which can include experience, skills, and scope: - PhD: $4,500 per week, plus $500 per week housing stipend - Masters: $4,000 per week, plus $500 per week housing stipend - Undergrad: $3,500 per week, plus $500 per week housing stipend ## Materials to Upload: - Resume/CV - List of publications/blog posts/any other public content (optional but recommended) - Twitter/X, github, personal website, public crypto wallet (optional) - Research statement (1-page max PDF, optional but recommended) - Letters of recommendation (one letter is required, a second letter is optional but recommended): recommenders should email their letters of support to [frontier-research-applications@a16z.com](mailto:frontier-research-applications@a16z.com), with the name of the applicant in the subject line - Please provide the name(s) of your recommendation letter writer(s) as part of your application - For full consideration, please submit applications by **12 p.m. PT on November 20, 2026** ## Notice **Export Control:** This position requires access to information and technology that is subject to U.S. export controls. Your responses to the questions below will be used solely to determine your eligibility under U.S. law to receive information and materials subject to U.S. export controls.We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, including international applicants. Employment is subject to applicable work authorization requirements in the country where the position is based. ## **a16z culture** - We do only first class business and only in a first class way - We take a long view of relationships, because we are in the relationship business - We believe in the future and bet the firm that way - We are all different, we recognize that, and we win - We celebrate the good times - We do it for the team - We play to win At a16z we are always looking to hire the absolute best talent and recognize that diversity in our experiences and backgrounds is what makes us stronger. We hire candidates of any race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, Veteran status, and any other status. These differences are what enables us to work towards the future we envision for ourselves, our portfolio companies, and the World. Our organization participates in E-Verify. Click [here](https://www.e-verify.gov/employees) to learn about E-Verify. ### About Nuuds Most clothes make you think twice. nuuds makes getting dressed easy, so you can walk out the door with confidence. We design clothes for real life and real bodies, through every stage, every season, every version of you. We obsess over fabric, fit, and feel so that getting dressed stops being a decision and becomes the easiest part of your day. nuuds is approachable, elevated essentials made to meet you exactly where you are. We're growing fast and building a team that's as thoughtful, real, and bold as the brand itself. As a lean team with ambitious plans for continued growth, we understand that our people are the foundation of everything we build. ### The Opportunity We're looking for a long-term, part-time Apparel Design Intern to join our design team and help bring seasonal collections to life, from first sketch to finished sample. This is a hands-on internship for someone who loves the details of the design process as much as the big creative vision. You'll work closely with senior designers on everything from flats and tech packs to sampling and presentations, gaining real exposure to how a design team actually operates day to day. Because this is a long-term role, you'll stay with us across multiple seasons, so you'll see collections move through the full development cycle and take on more ownership as you grow. Above all, we want someone who is eager to learn, takes pride in their work, and brings energy and positivity to a fast-moving team. If you're organized, adaptable, and excited to build your design career, we'd love to hear from you. ### Key Responsibilities - Assist senior designers with concept development, sketches, and seasonal line plans. - Create and refine flat sketches, tech packs, and print/graphic artwork using Adobe Illustrator. - Prepare and organize design files, color palettes, and trim/material references for each style. - Support the sampling process by tracking submissions, fit comments, and revisions. - Help maintain organized digital and physical files for color and pattern approvals. - Help prep materials for design reviews, presentations, and cross-team meetings. - Take on new tasks and responsibilities as they arise, with a proactive, can-do attitude. ### What You'll Gain - Hands-on experience across the full design and product development process, from concept through sampling. - Mentorship and direct feedback from senior designers. - Portfolio-ready work on real styles that go into production. - Continuity across multiple seasons, with growing responsibility over time. - A flexible schedule that works alongside school. ### What You'll Bring **Required Experience & Skills** - Working knowledge of Adobe Illustrator; comfortable creating and editing flats, prints, and graphics. - Solid computer basics: confident navigating file systems, email, and standard office software (Word, Excel, Google Suite, etc.). - Strong organizational skills with close attention to detail and accuracy. - Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines in a fast-paced design environment. - A go-getter attitude: self-motivated, resourceful, and eager to take initiative. - Strong communication skills and a collaborative, team-first mindset. - Genuine interest in apparel, fashion, and design trends. - Currently pursuing a degree or coursework in Fashion Design, Apparel Design, or a related field. - Availability to commit to a consistent part-time schedule on a long-term basis. - A portfolio showcasing flats, sketches, or design work is a plus.

GZA GeoEnvironmental, Inc. (GZA) is currently seeking an early-career Geotechnical Engineer with 0 to 5+ years of experience to join our team in our Providence, Rhode Island office. The successful candidate must have a strong academic record, solid understanding of civil and geotechnical engineering fundamentals, and a desire to work on a variety of exciting and challenging projects, both in the office and in the field. Assignments will span a wide variety of infrastructure, real estate/building development, and energy projects. Previous work experience is preferred but not required. Our close-knit culture here at GZA will help you to grow professionally while working on challenging, high-profile projects. You will be mentored by seasoned professionals, who will in turn look to you to share your technical knowledge and ideas. Our success relies on this collaborative environment and your growth. For candidates starting with little to no experience, you will work primarily on a variety of field assignments that support our geotechnical group, with periodic in-office duties that includes preparing detailed and accurate field documentation, evaluating data and performing engineering analyses, preparing technical reports, and implementing new technology. More experienced candidates may work primarily on in-office tasks, such as preparing designs and written engineering reports, and assisting GZA project managers and principals with management tasks. Primary Responsibilities (depending on experience): Perform field tasks and assist with the technical execution of projects. Oversee and log subsurface exploration and in-situ testing programs to evaluate soil and bedrock conditions in connection with foundation design & construction projects. Perform on-site construction oversight and inspections for earthwork projects, including in-place density testing of compacted soils using a Troxler nuclear moisture-density gauge. Perform field construction observation during installation and testing of shallow and deep foundations, underpinning, and other tasks related to underground construction and ground management for compliance with plans and specifications. Evaluate field data and performing engineering analyses/calculations, such as slope stability, bearing capacity, settlement, lateral pile analyses, and design/evaluation of earth support and underpinning systems (experience with software such as SLOPE/W, SEEP/W, LPile, and Plaxis is a plus) Writing drafts of field and engineering reports, technical specifications, and other technical documents Prepare construction cost/quantity estimates Assist with submittal reviews and requests for information during construction Communicate effectively and efficiently with prime contractors, sub-contractors, clients, and other project team members. Qualifications: BS degree in Civil Engineering with geotechnical focus. Master’s degree with geotechnical focus is preferred 0 to 5+ years of professional work experience Effective communication, problem solving and organizational skills Strong attention to detail with excellent analytical capabilities Ability to work independently or in a team setting Strong Microsoft Office skills Ability to work locally and regionally. Candidate must possess a valid driver’s license in good standing and have a consistent means of transportation to/from project sites Ability to work outdoors in all seasons through various kinds of weather and lift and use field equipment required to perform job functions The base salary for this position may range between $69,000 and $90,000. The actual base salary and total compensation will depend on many factors, including location, candidate experience, education, professional licensure, and other qualifications. About GZA: Become part of a growth-oriented firm; established in 1964. Nationally recognized for providing underground engineering excellence for foundations, tunnels, dams, buried utilities, marine facilities, highways, railroads, site development and temporary underground structures. Technical training and mentoring from experts in the industry. Professional development and enrichment. Exciting, collaborative, and friendly work environment. Eligible for annual performance bonus. Generous, company-subsidized benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, tuition reimbursement, and 401K retirement plan GZA is an employee-owned multidisciplinary engineering consulting firm with a history of more than 60 years of providing innovative solutions to engineering challenges for a diverse client base in the natural and built environment. We are an ENR Top 500 Design firm focused on geotechnical, environmental, water, ecological, and construction management services. GZA understands and prioritizes safety, proactive client service, risk management, and loss prevention. With a staff of interrelated professionals dedicated to providing high-level expertise on complex projects above, below and at ground-level, GZA provides seamless integration across practice areas, client type, and location. ## **About Base** Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time. ## **About the Role** As a Manufacturing Test Engineering Intern, you'll get hands-on experience with the test systems that check every Base battery before it ships. You'll work alongside experienced test engineers in a fast-paced, collaborative environment, supporting testers from first build through production. You'll learn by doing, and your work will directly affect how we deliver affordable energy at scale. ## What You'll Do - Help build, wire, and set up automated test equipment for battery and inverter systems. - Support troubleshooting when a tester faults or a unit fails, and help track down the cause. - Run tests on prototype and production units, and log the results. - Pull data from test runs, then build simple charts and summaries that show where testers are slow or failing. - Help document tester setup, calibration steps, and work instructions for technicians. - Join conversations with production teams to hear what's working and what's not on the line. - Work with engineers to try small improvements that boost uptime, cut test time, and raise first-pass yield (the share of units that pass test the first time). ## What You'll Bring - Current junior or senior in an undergraduate program, or a graduate student, in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field. - Solid grasp of electrical fundamentals, such as voltage, current, power, and basic circuits. - Passion for hands-on problem solving and getting equipment to work. - Some coding experience, such as Python, C, or MATLAB, and comfort reading simple code. - Comfort with basic lab tools like multimeters, power supplies, and oscilloscopes. - Able to share results in a clear way, in a chart, a short summary, or a quick conversation. - Curious, self-motivated, and eager to tackle hard problems with real-world impact. - Nice to have: exposure to LabVIEW, TestStand, or similar test software; familiarity with sensors, data acquisition, or PLCs from a class, lab, or project; basic knowledge of CAN bus, inverters, or power electronics; experience with Linux or Windows command-line tools; a personal, club, or class project where you built or tested hardware. ## **About This Team** Makers of the machines that power tomorrow. The Manufacturing Engineering team owns the interface between a proof of concept and a scalable, profitable product. Our team focuses on how a product can be built, defining the process technology and equipment solutions along the way. We are the feedback loop with the product design team to ensure designs are manufacturable both at cost and scale. The Manufacturing Engineering team owns every aspect of bringing the physical mechanisms of manufacturing a product into the factory. *Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.* ## **Our Values** - **First Principles Thinking:** Question assumptions. Principles > rules. - **Operate at Base Pace:** Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing. - **Give & Get Feedback:** Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset. - **Everyone’s an Owner:** Follow through on commitments and own results. - **Strong Opinions, Loosely Held:** Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information. - **Committed to the Mission:** Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in. - **Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit:** Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things. ## **Do the best work of your life at Base.**

description: **Your Impact at LILA** The PS AI team sits at the intersection of Physical Sciences R&D and AI/ML. Lila runs high-throughput experiments across electrochemistry, formulations, and advanced materials, generating rich datasets that demand more than black-box models. As a Co-Op focused on AI-driven equation discovery, you will develop and benchmark methods that extract interpretable governing equations directly from that data. Discovered equations reveal the underlying physics, make predictions explainable, and serve as mechanistic building blocks for digital twins and closed-loop optimization. You will work alongside PS AI researchers and physical scientists, helping shape how Lila turns experimental data into scientific understanding at scale. **What You'll Be Building** - Build end-to-end equation discovery pipelines from preprocessing through candidate generation and validation - Benchmark symbolic regression methods (SINDy, PDE-FIND, PySR, LLM-guided search) on Lila campaign data - Apply equation discovery to live electrochemistry, formulation, and materials datasets - Design evaluation harnesses measuring recovery rate, generalization, noise robustness, and physical consistency - Document and present findings across PS AI and domain science teams **What You'll Need to Succeed** - Pursuing a Master's or PhD in ML, CS, applied math, physics, materials science, or chemical engineering - Strong Python skills with hands-on experience in PyTorch, JAX, or similar - Experience applying machine learning to messy, real-world scientific or experimental data - Solid grounding in linear algebra, calculus, and probability - Comfort reading and implementing methods from ML research papers - Ability to frame open-ended scientific questions as concrete ML tasks - Clear communication across research, engineering, and physical science teams **Bonus Points For** - Working knowledge of symbolic or sparse regression methods (SINDy, PySR, PDE-FIND, or equivalent) - Experience with LLM-guided or agentic symbolic regression (LLM-SR, SR-Scientist, or similar) - Background in physics-informed ML, uncertainty quantification, or operator learning (PINNs, neural ODEs, FNO, DeepONet) - Exposure to digital twin or closed-loop workflows: model calibration, active learning, Bayesian optimization - Domain knowledge in electrochemistry, formulations, superconductors, or materials science **About LILA** Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy.
