The Junior QA Automation Engineer supports the design, development, execution, and maintenance of automated software tests to help ensure the quality, functionality, reliability, and performance of applications and systems. This role develops and maintains test scripts, executes test cases, identifies and documents defects, and assists with troubleshooting and debugging software issues. Working under the supervision of senior QA engineers, software developers, and technical leads, the Junior QA Automation Engineer follows established testing procedures and technical specifications to validate application functionality and identify opportunities to improve software quality. The position collaborates with development and project teams throughout the software development lifecycle and contributes to the continuous improvement of testing practices, automation tools, and quality assurance processes. ### Key Responsibilities ### **Test Automation and Development** - Develop, execute, and maintain automated test scripts based on established requirements, technical specifications, and test plans. - Write and modify test code to validate application functionality, system behavior, and expected results. - Assist in creating automated tests for new features, enhancements, bug fixes, and existing application functionality. - Update, repair, and expand existing test scripts and automation frameworks under the guidance of senior team members. - Support the development and maintenance of reusable test components to improve testing efficiency and consistency. - Execute automated and manual test cases as needed to validate application functionality. - Assist with integrating automated tests into continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) workflows. ### **Software Testing and Quality Assurance** - Perform functional, regression, integration, and smoke testing to verify that applications meet established requirements. - Review requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria to understand expected application behavior and identify test scenarios. - Validate application outputs, data processing, user interactions, and system responses against expected results. - Identify, document, and report software defects with clear reproduction steps, supporting evidence, and expected versus actual results. - Retest corrected defects and perform regression testing to ensure changes do not introduce new issues. - Assist with testing across different browsers, environments, configurations, and platforms as required. - Follow established QA procedures, test standards, and documentation practices. ### **Debugging and Issue Resolution** - Investigate test failures and assist in determining whether issues originate from application defects, test scripts, test data, or environmental conditions. - Debug and troubleshoot basic automation scripts and testing issues under the guidance of experienced team members. - Collaborate with software developers to reproduce defects, clarify findings, and verify corrective actions. - Update test scripts and test cases as applications and requirements change. - Escalate complex technical issues, recurring failures, and potential quality risks to senior QA engineers or technical leads. ### **Documentation and Collaboration** - Maintain accurate test cases, test scripts, test results, defect reports, and related technical documentation. - Participate in requirements reviews, sprint planning, daily stand-ups, and other Agile development activities as appropriate. - Collaborate with QA engineers, software developers, business analysts, and project stakeholders to support quality objectives. - Assist with identifying gaps in test coverage and recommend improvements to test scenarios and automation processes. - Follow established coding standards, version control practices, and software development procedures. - Perform other related duties as assigned. ### Minimum Requirements - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or Associates degree plus two years' experience. - 0-2 years of experience in software testing, quality assurance, test automation, or application development. Relevant internships, academic projects, and practical training may be considered. - Foundational knowledge of programming concepts and at least one programming or scripting language, such as Python, Java, JavaScript, or C#. - Understanding of software testing principles, including test cases, test execution, defect reporting, and regression testing. - Basic ability to read, write, and troubleshoot automated test scripts. - Familiarity with software development lifecycles and Agile development practices. - Strong analytical, problem-solving, and attention-to-detail skills. - Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical issues clearly. - Ability to follow technical specifications, work under guidance, and collaborate effectively with a development team. - Must live in the Continental US. - Be either a US citizen or Permanent Resident due to the work we do. - Depending on agency requirements, you may need to possess or obtain a Public Trust designation or security clearance. Regardless of the specific requirement, all positions require the successful completion of a background check, background investigation, and the standard onboarding process. ### Preferred Qualifications - Experience in government contracting, healthcare CMS (Center of Medicare & Medicaid) or in the health industry. - Exposure to test automation frameworks or tools such as Selenium, Playwright, Cypress, or comparable technologies. - Familiarity with API testing tools such as Postman. - Basic understanding of SQL and database validation. - Exposure to version control tools such as Git. - Familiarity with CI/CD tools and automated testing within build and deployment pipelines. - Experience using defect tracking and test management tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, or comparable platforms. - Understanding of web applications, RESTful APIs, and client-server architecture. - Experience working on academic, internship, or personal projects involving software development or automated testing. - Qualified individuals living in HUBZone-certified areas are strongly encouraged to apply. In practice that means early access to new model releases, direct engineering channels to the labs, funded certifications, and the freedom to pick the right tool, not just the one you're locked into. Help apply data protection and AI regulation requirements (GDPR, EU AI Act, model licences) to your work, following the guidance your senior colleagues set. Support user adoption: prepare documentation, contribute to training sessions, and collect feedback on what works and what doesn’t. Measure how solutions perform in use, and suggest improvements to your senior colleagues. Share progress in clear written and verbal updates to both technical and business audiences. You have 0 to 2 years of experience, whether professional, from internships, or from a research or academic setting. You write Python that’s clean enough for a colleague to read, and you’re willing to learn whatever language a client’s stack requires. You’re comfortable calling APIs and connecting different systems, even if you’ve done it mainly in side projects. You’re starting to understand what makes a result useful to a client, and you can prioritise tasks with guidance. You enjoy explaining technical ideas to non-technical people, and you listen carefully so you can bring them along. You want to grow quickly, take on more responsibility over time, and learn from experienced colleagues in a fast-growing AI practice. You speak French and English. German is a strong advantage. Experience deploying a project to a cloud environment (AWS, Azure, or GCP), even a small one. Je maakt deel uit van het engineering team en werkt in multidisciplinaire teams aan projecten voor diverse klanten. De projecten verschillen aanzienlijk in inhoud, waardoor geen enkele werkweek hetzelfde is. Dit zijn enkele van je verantwoordelijkheden: Werken op het snijvlak van infrastructuur, software en data; Ontwerpen, ontwikkelen en onderhouden van data gedreven oplossingen; Analyseren van klantbehoeften en helpen bij het vertalen naar technische oplossingen met behulp van data-gerelateerde technologieën, waaronder Databricks, Snowflake, Apache Spark; Samenwerken met senior engineers om data pipelines, architecturen en datamodellering te ontwerpen en te verbeteren; Deelnemen aan team- en trainingssessies om je vaardigheden te verbeteren en bij te dragen aan de ontwikkeling van de data engineering capability. Natuurlijk weet je anderen te inspireren en communiceer je effectief complexe ideeën en analyses. Bovenal durf je jezelf te zijn. De ware jij. Met je eigen sterke punten, blik op de wereld en persoonlijkheid. Verder heb jij als Data Engineer: Een afgeronde (technische) universitaire Masteropleiding; zoals Computer Science, Information Science, Software Engineering, of een andere master met sterk technisch component; Basiskennis of ervaring met het ontwerpen en implementeren van data pipelines, bij voorkeur met tools en frameworks zoals Apache Spark, Apache Airflow, of vergelijkbare technologieën voor ETL; Een goed begrip van logische en fysieke datamodellen om bedrijfsprocessen effectief weer te geven en ervoor te zorgen dat data efficiënt kan worden opgeslagen en opgehaald; Ervaring met een programmeertaal zoals Python, goede basis in SQL, en/of ervaring met data‑verwerkingsframeworks zoals Apache Spark (PySpark); Bekendheid met cloud platforms zoals AWS, Azure of Google Cloud Platform (GCP) is een pluspunt; Capaciteit om effectief samen te werken, zowel met klanten als interne collega’s; De skills om problemen goed te kunnen structureren en oplossingen te bedenken, én de wil om deze oplossingen te realiseren; Een groot verantwoordelijkheidsgevoel, veel ambitie, en sta je open om te leren; Een uitstekende beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal, in woord en geschrift. Heb jij een passie voor het ontwikkelen van data-gedreven oplossingen? Wil je de toekomst van onze klanten helpen vormgeven en versnellen? Sluit je dan aan bij het Platform Development & Integration-team binnen Deloitte Engineering. Je werkt aan uiteenlopende projecten, zoals het ontdekken van trends in financiële data of het zo efficiënt mogelijk bouwen van datamodellen en samen met de klant data gedreven oplossingen ontwikkelen. Samen kunnen we data omzetten in bruikbare inzichten, infrastructuren moderniseren en organisaties helpen meer data-gedreven te werk te gaan. Door jouw betrokkenheid en leergierigheid zorg je ervoor dat projecten op tijd worden geleverd en aan de hoogste kwaliteitsstandaarden voldoen, wat resulteert in tevreden klanten. Zo lever je een tastbare bijdrage aan het realiseren van grote data en cloud gedreven technologie transformaties. Breng verandering teweeg door technologie en data, werk samen aan transformerende projecten, geniet van groeikansen en lever hoogwaardige oplossingen die een betekenisvolle impact hebben. Bij Deloitte.

location: San Francisco, New York City, Seattle
description: ## **Who we are** ### **About Stripe** Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. ## **What you’ll do** ### **About the internship** Stripe's Applied ML, Data Science, Risk, and Payments organizations are excited to offer PhD machine learning engineering internships for the summer of 2027. This is an exceptional opportunity to contribute to critical projects that directly enhance Stripe's suite of products, focusing on areas such as foundation models used for dozens of tasks e.g. fraud detection, enhanced support, and predicting user behavior. As an intern, you'll tackle challenging problems at the intersection of finance, technology, and data. You'll have the chance to work on creative projects like the Stripe Assistant and the Stripe Foundation Model, which leverage machine learning to revolutionize how businesses interact with financial services and data. ### **Responsibilities** - Develop and deploy large-scale machine learning systems that drive significant business value across various domains. - Engage in the end-to-end process of designing, training, improving, and launching machine learning models. - Write production-scale ML models that will be deployed to help Stripe enable economic infrastructure access for a diverse range of businesses globally. - Collaborate across teams to incorporate feedback and proactively seek solutions to challenges. - Rapidly learn new technologies and approaches, demonstrating a strong ability to ask insightful questions and communicate the status of your work effectively. ## **Who you are** ### **Minimum requirements** - A deep understanding of computer science, obtained through the pursuit of a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a closely related field, with the expectation of graduating in winter 2027 or spring/summer 2028. - Practical experience with programming and machine learning, evidenced by projects, classwork, or research. Familiarity with languages such as Python, Scala, Spark and libraries such as Pandas, NumPy, and Scikit-learn. - Expertise in areas of machine learning such as supervised and unsupervised learning techniques, ML operations, and possibly experience in Large Language Models or Reinforcement Learning. - Demonstrated ability to work on collaborative projects, with experience in receiving and applying feedback from various stakeholders. - A proactive approach to learning unfamiliar systems and a demonstrated ability to understand complex systems independently. - Intent to return to the degree-program after the completion of the internship/co-op. ### **Preferred qualifications** You Might Also Have: - Two years of university education or equivalent experience, with in-depth knowledge in specific domains of machine learning. - Published and presented peer-reviewed articles in top-tier venues. - Experience in writing high-quality pull requests, maintaining good test coverage, and completing projects with minimal defects. - Familiarity with navigating new codebases and managing work across different programming languages. - Excellent written communication skills to clearly articulate your work to both team members and wider Stripe audiences. ### **Application requirements** Please submit the following with your application: - A detailed resume or LinkedIn profile showcasing your work history. - Examples of relevant work and your approach to learning, such as GitHub repositories, StackOverflow contributions, or other project portfolios. Join us for an unforgettable summer internship and help shape the future of global commerce. At Stripe, you won't just be working on theoretical projects; you'll make a tangible impact on the world's economic infrastructure.

role: Data Governance Project Manager Assistant - Stage (6 mois) Mars 2026 (F/H/NB)
description: Au sein du siège international d’Ubisoft, vous rejoindrez l’Ubisoft Data Office, chargé de la stratégie et de la gouvernance des données d’Ubisoft, ainsi que d’une gamme de services et de produits destinés au stockage, au traitement, à la diffusion, à l’analyse et à la mise en valeur des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise. En tant que Data Governance Project Manager Assistant, vous ferez partie de l’équipe Data Governance qui œuvre pour rendre les données d’Ubisoft fiables et facilement accessibles, tout en garantissant leur sécurité et la conformité réglementaire. Contribuer à la direction, à la planification, à la mise en œuvre et au suivi d’une ou plusieurs initiatives de gouvernance des données, ainsi que de tous les volets de travail associés. Participer à l’analyse des besoins des équipes métier et techniques sous l’angle de la gouvernance des données, et contribuer à l’identification et à la mise en œuvre de normes et de solutions adaptées pour un ou plusieurs piliers de la gouvernance des données auxquels vous contribuez. Se familiariser avec l’inventaire des produits Data Domain et des ressources de données sous-jacentes, avec l’aide des équipes métier et des équipes chargées des données au sein d’Ubisoft. Se former aux initiatives de protection des données (par exemple, gestion des accès aux données et conformité réglementaire) et y contribuer. Collaborer étroitement avec les partenaires techniques (plateforme de données, architectes, etc.) pour définir et promouvoir des normes internes et des bonnes pratiques en matière de conception et de développement de produits de données (par exemple : modélisation, architecture, gestion des accès, gestion de la qualité des données, utilisation et interopérabilité des données de référence, etc.). Renforcer les compétences et la sensibilisation des équipes chargées des données en matière de gouvernance des données par le partage, l’organisation d’événements, le coaching et le mentorat, ainsi que par la promotion d’une culture des données au sein du personnel d’Ubisoft. Suivre et rendre compte des progrès et des réussites de vos initiatives, et améliorer/adapter en permanence le cadre de référence, notamment en ce qui concerne les piliers de la gouvernance des données auxquels vous contribuez. Vous tenir informé des tendances du secteur des données et les faire connaître au service des données et aux professionnels de l’ensemble de l’entreprise. Créer un réseau de soutien et d’expertise. Vous suivez actuellement un Master en systèmes d’information, en informatique, en mathématiques ou équivalent. Connaissances en matière de données, d’analyse métier ou de gestion de projet. Envie de diriger, de coordonner et de mener à bien des projets impliquant des composantes transversales et impliquant plusieurs équipes métier et techniques. Envie de découvrir la valeur de la gouvernance des données au sein d’une entreprise. Esprit critique et analytique Capacité à s’adapter rapidement au changement. Bonnes compétences interpersonnelles, de leadership et de communication. Bonnes compétences en communication écrite et orale en anglais. La maîtrise du français serait un atout. Processus de recrutement Si votre candidature est retenue, vous serez contacté·e dans un premier temps par un·e représentant·e de notre équipe Campus pour un échange téléphonique afin de déterminer si votre profil correspond bien à l’annonce mais aussi à vos envies. Si cet échange est concluant, un entretien en présentiel ou en visio sera par la suite organisé avec votre futur·e tuteur·trice de stage. Enfin, un entretien additionnel sera réalisé avec le directeur de l’équipe. Avantages en tant que stagiaire chez Ubisoft Gratification de stage selon le niveau d’études Carte Titres Restaurant Swile, remboursement de 50 % du titre de transport, 1 RTT par mois Réduction billetterie (concerts/spectacles), accès à la salle de sport Ubisoft à tarifs préférentiels Ubisoft veille à développer un environnement de travail inclusif qui reflète la diversité de sa communauté de joueurs dans ses équipes. En tant qu’employeur, Ubisoft offre à tous les mêmes opportunités d’accès à l’emploi sans distinction de genre, ethnicité, religion, orientation sexuelle, statut social, handicap et d’âge. Boîte à questions Ubisoft Comment préparer ma candidature chez Ubisoft ? Dans un premier temps, lisez attentivement la job description afin de mettre en avant vos expériences et vos compétences qui vous semblent pertinentes pour cette opportunité ! Un CV personnalisé et détaillé vous permettra à coup sûr de vous démarquer 😉 Lettre de motivation ou pas ? A choisir, nous préférerons toujours quelques lignes expliquant votre motivation à candidater, plutôt qu’un texte générique copié/collé ! Un encart est d’ailleurs spécifiquement prévu à cet effet lors de votre candidature. Je ne connais pas le secteur du jeu vidéo. Ai-je ma place chez Ubisoft ? Nous comptons dans nos rangs de nombreux profils qui ne sont pas des férus de jeux vidéo. Chez Ubisoft, nous cherchons à nous entourer de personnes passionnées, que ce soit par leurs spécialités, leurs métiers ou par le divertissement en général. A quoi m’attendre lors d’un stage ou d’une alternance chez Ubisoft ? Dès vos premiers jours, vous bénéficierez d’une Welcome Session vous présentant Ubisoft, son organisation et votre environnement de travail pour les prochains mois. Votre tuteur·rice et votre équipe vous accompagneront au quotidien, dans les premières semaines comme tout au long de votre expérience ! Une fois autonome, vos missions seront responsabilisantes et variées, peu importe le type de contrat. Travailler chez Ubisoft signifie travailler sur de vrais projets à mener au jour le jour. Un groupe Teams dédié vous permettra par ailleurs d’échanger avec les autres stagiaires et alternant·es. Quels sont les engagements sociétaux d’Ubisoft ? Nous cherchons à enrichir la vie des joueurs et joueuses par la création d’expériences de jeu originales et mémorables, et en nous appliquant à toujours améliorer l’impact positif de nos jeux. Afin d’y parvenir, nous créons un environnement de travail plus sûr et inclusif, nous soutenons les communautés dans lesquelles Ubisoft opère par le biais d’initiatives caritatives et nous nous efforçons de réduire l’impact environnemental de nos activités. Pour en savoir plus, rendez-vous sur la page Impact Sociétal . Je suis en situation de handicap, comment postuler ? Toutes nos équipes recrutement ont été sensibilisées aux sujets du handicap. Vous pouvez donc postuler normalement via notre plateforme SmartRecruiters en joignant votre CV et lettre de motivation. Si vous avez besoin d'une adaptation du processus de recrutement, notamment lorsque celui-ci implique des entretiens vidéo, précisez-le lors de votre candidature et/ou contactez l’équipe Mission Handicap par mail ( ). Ubisoft est une référence mondiale du jeu vidéo, avec des équipes réparties aux quatre coins du monde qui créent des expériences de jeu originales et mémorables, de Assassin’s Creed à Rainbow Six en passant par Just Dance et bien d’autres encore. Nous croyons que la diversité des points de vue fait progresser à la fois les joueurs et les équipes. Si vous êtes passionné·e par l’innovation et que vous souhaitez repousser les limites du divertissement, rejoignez notre aventure et aidez-nous à créer l’inconnu !

Most GenAI never leaves the demo. We hire for the people who get it into production, and into daily use. The Forward Deployed Engineer closes that gap: a field engineer who builds GenAI applications (agents, RAG pipelines, copilots) and makes sure they get adopted, embedded in daily workflows, and deliver measurable value. You quickly grasp a client's operational challenges, design a tailored response, deploy it, and bring teams along in the transformation. You will operate at the intersection of Data Science, ML/Platform Engineering, and client delivery, helping customers find the right level of sophistication, semantic search, RAG, agents, or fine-tuning, deliver measurable ROI in the most cost-effective way. Beyond crafting prompts, you will design and build robust, scalable products: benchmarking candidate Foundation Models across the model stack (from GPT-x, Claude, and Gemini to edge models like Mistral), rapidly iterating prototypes, and validating ideas directly with users using frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, and pgvector. We work closely with leading technology partners including Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI, Databricks, and AWS. In practice that means early access to new model releases, direct engineering channels to the labs, funded certifications, and the freedom to pick the right tool, not just the one you're locked into. What you'll actually do Spend time on client sites with a senior Forward Deployed Engineer, learning how their teams work and where AI can help. Help scope and build LLM-based solutions under guidance: RAG pipelines, tool-using agents, workflow automation, and chat interfaces. Connect these solutions to existing systems (APIs, databases, business tools) using established patterns and templates. Help apply data protection and AI regulation requirements (GDPR, EU AI Act, model licences) to your work, following the guidance your senior colleagues set. Support user adoption: prepare documentation, contribute to training sessions, and collect feedback on what works and what doesn’t. Measure how solutions perform in use, and suggest improvements to your senior colleagues. Share progress in clear written and verbal updates to both technical and business audiences. You’ll thrive here if You hold a Master’s degree in computer science, AI, or a related technical field. What matters most is that you can build things, so strong projects alongside your degree count just as much. You have 0 to 2 years of experience, whether professional, from internships, or from a research or academic setting. We hire for potential, so recent graduates with solid LLM projects are encouraged to apply. You’ve built with LLMs in some form, through coursework, your thesis, internships, or personal projects. That includes prompting, RAG, basic agent workflows, and checking model outputs with simple evaluation sets or tests. You write Python that’s clean enough for a colleague to read, and you’re willing to learn whatever language a client’s stack requires. You’re comfortable calling APIs and connecting different systems, even if you’ve done it mainly in side projects. You’re starting to understand what makes a result useful to a client, and you can prioritise tasks with guidance. You enjoy explaining technical ideas to non-technical people, and you listen carefully so you can bring them along. You want to grow quickly, take on more responsibility over time, and learn from experienced colleagues in a fast-growing AI practice. You speak Dutch and English. German is a strong advantage. If you’re not there yet, we’ll support you in learning it. Bonus points for Experience with applied AI frameworks or SDKs (LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI SDK, Anthropic SDK, etc.). Experience deploying a project to a cloud environment (AWS, Azure, or GCP), even a small one. Familiarity with MLOps or LLMOps practices, such as version control for prompts, simple evaluation pipelines, or basic monitoring. A working understanding of vector databases and core concepts like embeddings. Why join Sia You ship. Engagements are measured in weeks, not quarters. Your work goes live in front of real users and the client’s team, with a senior colleague alongside you. Range without job-hopping. You’ll work across several industries and architectures each year, which is one of the fastest ways to build judgement about what actually works. A practice that’s growing. The AI practice is young enough that you help shape how it delivers, and experienced enough that you’re never the only person who has solved a problem before. Direct exposure, with support. You’ll sit in on conversations with business decision-makers early on, with senior colleagues guiding you, which is one of the fastest routes to seniority. What we offer A competitive salary and benefits, including a hospital insurance, performance-related bonus and more. A dedicated learning budget, funded partner certifications (Anthropic, AWS, Databricks), and paid conference time. Hybrid working from our Amsterdam office, with real flexibility on where the deep work happens. A named mentor from day one and a clear path from delivery engineer to lead engineer or client-facing architect. We are unable to provide a work permit for this position. **SUMMARY** This summer internship will primarily involve working with the IT Service Desk team. They also work very closely with our IT Infrastructure and Cybersecurity teams on complex issues and requests. IT infrastructure solutions include, but are not limited to, collocation data centers, public cloud infrastructure (IaaS and PaaS), infrastructure automation, networking, storage, servers, end user technologies, and monitoring services. The IT Service Desk intern will start by getting trained on GCM’s end user technology stack which includes (but is not limited to) Microsoft 365, Azure Active Directory, Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows 11 administration, Active Directory, Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Microsoft Endpoint Manager, Atlassian (e.g., Jira Service Desk), Cisco Meraki and our GenAI solutions. Once the intern has the required foundational knowledge, they will start supporting our users and their technology needs by handling tickets or calls. The summer will culminate in a presentation to the Technology leadership team reviewing the intern’s summer experience and what they learned. The team is looking for a student who is passionate about technology, excited to grow in every way, unafraid to try new things and even to fail at times along the way. **RESPONSIBILITIES** The intern will be involved in the following activities: - Support end users seeking technical assistance over email, phone or in person as it relates to end user hardware (e.g., computers, phones, mobile phones, tablets, printers, etc.) as well as enterprise software solutions (e.g., Microsoft Office suite, Adobe, Foxit, SharePoint, Zoom, remote access, virtual desktop solutions, etc.). - Most GenAI never leaves the demo. We hire for the people who get it into production, and into daily use. You quickly grasp a client's operational challenges, design a tailored response, deploy it, and bring teams along in the transformation. Beyond crafting prompts, you will design and build robust, scalable products: benchmarking candidate Foundation Models across the model stack (from GPT-x, Claude, and Gemini to edge models like Mistral), rapidly iterating prototypes, and validating ideas directly with users using frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, and pgvector. Help apply data protection and AI regulation requirements (GDPR, EU AI Act, model licences) to your work, following the guidance your senior colleagues set. German is a strong advantage. If you’re not there yet, we’ll support you in learning it. Bonus points for Experience with applied AI frameworks or SDKs (LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI SDK, Anthropic SDK, etc.). Experience deploying a project to a cloud environment (AWS, Azure, or GCP), even a small one. Familiarity with MLOps or LLMOps practices, such as version control for prompts, simple evaluation pipelines, or basic monitoring. A working understanding of vector databases and core concepts like embeddings. Why join Sia You ship. Engagements are measured in weeks, not quarters. Your work goes live in front of real users and the client’s team, with a senior colleague alongside you. Range without job-hopping. Hybrid working from our Brussels or Antwerp office, with real flexibility on where the deep work happens. A named mentor from day one and a clear path from delivery engineer to lead engineer or client-facing architect. We are unable to provide a work permit for this position. Junior Software Engineer Are you tired of support roles where you just follow scripts and never touch real code? As a Junior Software Engineer at BodySpec, you’re part of our engineering team from day one. You’ll troubleshoot real technical problems, maintain and extend the tools our team and customers rely on, and learn to make design decisions that hold up as we scale. You’ll start close to our users, handling support and fixes, with a clear path to owning bigger pieces of our systems as you grow. First-year Junior Software Engineers in Austin can expect to earn up to $70,170 in total cash compensation, plus equity. You'll Love This Job If You Have: Technical Curiosity: You want to understand how systems actually work, not just restart them when they break. You dig into logs, trace errors, and don’t stop until you find the root cause. Systems Thinking: You know writing code is the easy part now, because AI tools draft a lot of it. What matters is deciding what to build and how it fits. You think about where a change lives, what it might break, who maintains it, and whether it makes sense for the business, not just whether it runs. Ownership: You close the loop. When you fix something, you write it up, and if it’s happened twice, you automate it so it doesn’t happen a third time. You don’t wait to be told to do the obvious next step. Communication Clarity: You can explain technical problems to non-technical people without talking down to them, and you write up issues and decisions so your teammates don’t waste time. Your Slack messages are clear, concise, and actionable. Knowing When to Ask: You know when to keep digging and when to ask a teammate. You don’t ping someone the moment you’re stuck, but you also don’t burn a day on something a five-minute conversation would solve. And you never sit on a critical issue trying to be a hero. Patience Without Passivity: You stay calm with frustrated users and stakeholders, but you’re not a pushover. No ticket is beneath you, and you push for real fixes, not just band-aids. What Will You Do? Troubleshoot technical issues across our website, admin systems, and internal tools, mostly via Slack with internal teams and external stakeholders Maintain and extend our internal and external tools, from small fixes to new features Write scripts and queries to diagnose problems, pull data, and automate repetitive fixes Learn our system architecture and contribute to design decisions: how a change fits the system, what it costs to maintain, and whether it’s the right fix for the business Provide weekend tech and dev support on a rotating schedule managed by the team Document solutions and build internal knowledge bases so problems get solved faster over time Grow from fixing and extending code to designing systems, with the goal of owning larger pieces of our stack Requirements Based in Austin, TX and able to work in person at our offices 0–2 years of experience in software development, technical support, or an engineering-adjacent role (flexible if you can demonstrate the skills) Strong programming fundamentals: comfortable in at least one language and able to learn others Experience with databases and writing queries (SQL or similar) Real interest in software design and architecture: you want to understand why systems are built the way they are Excellent written communication, since you’ll live in Slack and email Ability to thrive with direct, unfiltered feedback — we’ll tell you exactly what you need to improve Availability for rotating weekend support coverage Compensation Base Salary: $62,000 Performance Bonus: Up to 7% of base salary annually ($4,340) — half paid in cash ($2,170), half in stock options Team Revenue Bonus: $500/month when we hit monthly goals ($6,000 annually — we’ve hit our goals 7 out of 9 months so far in 2026) Total Cash Compensation: Up to $70,170 Equity: Stock options through performance bonus and additional grants based on performance All team members regardless of position are eligible for additional stock option grants and profit sharing based on performance. We expect both cash and equity compensation to grow as the company scales. Benefits Health, dental, and vision insurance 401(k) Paid time off Sick leave Company-wide peer bonus program for recognizing excellent teamwork Employee assistance program Regular team events (both virtual and in-person) Direct mentorship from experienced operators who’ve scaled companies before BodySpec is transforming how people understand and improve their health through accessible DEXA scanning. As a Mechanical Engineer, you’ll leverage your strong foundation in physics, mathematics, and materials science to process and resolve mechanical problems, design and implement custom mechanical tooling and associated processes, and enable the handling, assembly, and disassembly of parts, components, sub-assemblies, and final assemblies throughout the product life cycle. If you want to work beyond the cutting-edge, continuously pushing the boundaries of science and engineering to make possible the next generations of technology, join us to Make Possible a Better Future. ### Senior Precision Stage Architect **Role Summary** Owns the end-to-end architecture of high-precision motion stages and their mechatronic subsystems, spanning mechanical structure, actuation, sensing, metrology, and motion control. Sets the technical direction for stage performance — translating positioning, dynamic, and throughput requirements into a coherent mechanical/control co-design — and serves as the senior technical authority guiding the multidisciplinary team that executes it. Key Responsibilities - Completes definition and design of complex precision-stage mechanical components, modules, and mechatronic sub-systems, treating mechanics and controls as a co-designed system rather than separate disciplines. - Defines the **control system architecture** for precision stages — servo loop topology, loop partitioning, feedforward strategy, sensor/actuator selection, and the mechanical/control trade-offs that govern positioning accuracy, repeatability, and settling time. - Sets and drives the **technical direction** for stage controls: establishes the controls roadmap, error budgets, and quantitative performance targets (nanometer-class positioning, dynamic following error, settling time, throughput), and directs the engineers working against them. - Regarded as the technical expert in precision motion and stage control. Demonstrates in-depth expertise in own discipline (mechanics + motion control) and broad knowledge of adjacent disciplines (electrical, physics, algorithms, software) within the function. - Anticipates business and regulatory issues; recommends product, process, or service improvements. - Solves unique and complex problems with broad impact on the business; requires conceptual and innovative thinking to develop solutions across the mechanical–control boundary. - Impacts the direction and resource allocation for program, project, or services; works within general functional policies and industry guidelines. - Contributes to the system engineering specification both within precision stage/control expertise and broadening into other disciplines. - Develops dynamic models of stage mechanics (structural dynamics, resonances, mass/stiffness budgets) and integrates them with control design, including active vibration isolation, disturbance rejection, and damping strategies. - Specifies and integrates position feedback and metrology (laser interferometers, encoders, capacitive/optical sensors) together with real-time control hardware (motion controllers, FPGA/DSP, drives, amplifiers) and the full sensor-to-actuator signal chain. - Defines, tunes, and validates multi-axis servo loops, feedforward, and trajectory/motion profiles to meet positioning and dynamic performance under production conditions. - Ensures designs meet Market Requirement Specifications (MRS). Coordinates with project marketing and management to understand subsystem requirements. - Chairs architecture brainstorming meetings and drives the systems process to down-select to a final stage architecture, including the control system architecture and the mechanical/control partition. - Conducts detailed engineering analysis of subsystems — control-loop stability and bandwidth analysis, error budgeting, modal/structural dynamics, thermal and dynamic error sources — using deep design knowledge in field of expertise and broadening into other disciplines. - Assists in creating concepts for architectural design approaches. **About Northwood:** Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array and parabolic ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it. **Role** Northwood engineers and operators run hardware and software across a global network of antenna ground stations and the cloud services behind them. No one sells a platform for running a network like this at scale, so Northwood builds its own. Platform Engineering builds the software that takes Northwood products from first prototype to full operation. That covers how code is built, tested, and released, how every site and service is monitored, and how hardware in remote locations is brought online, updated, and kept healthy. Every one of these problems has to work across every site, service, and customer at once. Few organizations get to build this kind of software in house. What this team builds will shape how a global network of antennas is operated for the missions that depend on it. Every new antenna, site, and customer Northwood adds runs on this platform, and it sets how fast the network can grow. As an early-career Software Engineer on the Platform team, you'll ship to real production systems from your first weeks, with close mentorship, and take on more ownership as you show you're ready. You don't need to know every part of the stack today. You need to learn fast, reason clearly through problems you haven't seen before, and care a lot about what you build. **Key areas of focus** You'll work across these areas over time. No one is expected to own everything listed. - **Delivery and release** - Build the CI and release pipelines that take code from commit to production, in the cloud and at ground stations around the world. - Make shipping safe and continuous, with staged rollouts and fast rollback, so no one has to test in production. - **Simulation and test** - Build simulated ground stations and lab test benches running real hardware, so every release is tested against realistic conditions before it reaches a live site. - Build tools that replay real recorded data through the system to catch problems early. - **Ground station operations** - Automate how new sites are brought online, configured, and updated, in remote locations with few or no people on site. - Write software that runs on the servers that sit next to the antennas, and keep a global fleet of them healthy. - **Observability** - Build the monitoring, logging, and alerting that show the health of every service and site. - Turn raw telemetry into signals engineers and operators can act on before a problem reaches a customer. - **Internal platform and tools** - Build the backend services and web interfaces engineers and operators use every day to create, ship, and run software. - Talk directly with the people who use what you build, and turn their feedback into improvements. - **Infrastructure and security** - Define the cloud and site infrastructure the platform runs on as code. - Build identity, secrets management, and least-privilege access into the platform, so every service gets them by default. **Basic Qualifications** - 0 to 2 years of professional software experience. It doesn't have to be a full-time role. Internships, research, open source, and projects outside the classroom all count, so tell us about them. - Bachelor's degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, math, or a related field. This is a soft requirement: if you didn't pursue a degree, tell us what you did instead. - Has written real software in at least one general-purpose language (such as Python, Go, Rust, TypeScript, or C++) beyond required coursework. - Has built and shipped something other people used or relied on. - Has solved a hard technical problem largely on their own, such as debugging a non-obvious failure or designing a system from scratch. **Preferred Qualifications** We don't expect you to have everything below. We do expect you to go deep where your strengths are, and to take ownership of what you work on. - **Languages:** proficiency in one or more languages (such as Python, Go, Rust, or TypeScript), with opinions about which one fits which job. - **Full stack:** has built a backend API and a frontend that uses it (such as a React app on a REST API). - **Shipping software:** exposure to CI pipelines (such as GitHub Actions or GitLab CI), containers (such as Docker), a cloud platform (such as AWS), or infrastructure as code (such as Terraform or CloudFormation). - **Systems:** day-to-day comfort with Linux and the command line, or coursework and projects in operating systems, networking, or distributed systems. - **Tools for others:** built a tool, script, or library other developers used. - **Hardware and space:** projects involving hardware, embedded systems, RF, robotics, or space, such as a CubeSat, rocketry, or robotics team. - **Drive:** a track record of going past what was asked, such as side projects, competitions, research, or things built because you wanted to. - **AI tools:** comfort with AI coding tools (such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor). **Additional Information:** *To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.* Northwood Space is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Northwood Space is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status. ### About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. role: Human Interactive Driving Research Intern, World Models

# **Electrical Engineer, Early Career (Embedded Systems & Tools)** #### Sunnyvale, CA (onsite) · Engineering · Full-time ## **About Noble Machines** Noble Machines builds multipurpose robots to support human workers in the world's toughest jobs—turning dangerous work from a necessity into a choice. Recent graduates are welcome. - At least two hardware internships or co-op terms, or equivalent hands-on work on a student engineering team. - At least one PCB you designed yourself (schematic and layout) and brought up, in Altium, KiCad, OrCAD or similar. - Experience with microcontrollers and common interfaces (I2C, SPI, UART), and enough C to read and debug firmware. - Comfort in the lab with oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies and soldering. - A design portfolio: schematics, layouts, photos or write-ups of projects you built, and what you personally did on each. - Clear written communication and the habit of documenting your work. - Ability to work onsite in Sunnyvale five days a week. ### **Nice to have** - Hardware internships at robotics, automotive, aerospace or consumer electronics companies. - Formula SAE, robotics, rocketry, solar car or similar student teams, especially if you owned the electrical system. - Power electronics or motor-control projects: a motor driver, DC/DC converter or battery charger you designed. - Built a test fixture or test automation in Python. - Exposure to CAN, Ethernet or USB hardware design. - Sensor integration: IMUs, encoders, current or force sensors. - Experience taking a board through a contract manufacturer. ### **Compensation and benefits** The expected base salary for this role in Sunnyvale, CA is $120,000 - $150,000 per year, in line with California's pay transparency law (SB 1162). We welcome applicants who need accommodations during the hiring process and will work with you to provide them. ### **How to apply** Apply directly on our website at [](https://www.noblemachines.ai/company#jobs), and include a link to your design portfolio.

Ben jij een jong academisch béta-talent die klaar is om één van de architecten te worden van ’s werelds meest innovatieve simulatie & trainingssystemen binnen de militaire en civiele luchtvaartwereld? Wil jij je technische kennis inzetten voor de ontwikkeling van baanbrekende simulatietechnologieën of deze je eigen maken? Dit alles doe je bij ons samen met een multidisciplinair team van professionals in een inspirerende hightech omgeving. Daarbij krijg je niet alleen de ruimte voor persoonlijke groei, maar ook de middelen om daadwerkelijk impact te maken bij onze stakeholders! Het succes van luchtvaartoperaties wordt niet langer in de lucht bepaald, maar door de geavanceerde simulaties en trainingen die eraan voorafgaan! Wat ga je doen? Als R&D engineer trainingssystemen richt je je op een brede kennisontwikkeling van de allernieuwste simulatie-technologieën, componenten en architecturen, en hoe deze vervolgens smart te combineren en integreren tot effectieve, beveiligde en duurzame trainingssysteem-oplossingen voor de luchtvaart. Dit vereist van jou een oplossingsgerichte en agile mindset om tot een optimale afstemming te kunnen komen tussen gebruikerseisen, gewenste en noodzakelijke functionaliteit, en de haalbaarheid op technisch, financieel en organisatorisch vlak. Vanuit jouw eigen team werk je regelmatig samen met collega’s uit onze andere teams aan diverse soorten projecten die hoogwaardige technologische simulatie en trainingsoplossingen leveren aan eindgebruikers in de luchtvaartoperatie. Denk daarbij aan (inter)nationale netwerken met - next - generation vliegsimulatoren voor het gezamenlijk trainen van piloten en andere bemanningsleden in complexe operationele omstandigheden, immersieve XR-omgevingen voor vliegtuig-onderhoudsopleidingen of het met AI-aangedreven simulatiesystemen ondersteunen van operationele gebruikers van autonoom vliegende systemen. role: Human Interactive Driving Research Intern, Learning-Based Control for Safe Autonomous Driving
description: At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences. This is a paid 12-week internship opportunity and is a hybrid, in-office role. [Here’s a glimpse into the Internship experience from some of our TRI interns!](https://www.tri.global/tri-internship-program) **The Team** Within the Extreme Performance Intelligent Control team, we are developing techniques to advance vehicle safety and performance capabilities using tools from machine learning, optimization, and control theory. We pursue a hybrid approach to high-performance driving that unites physics-based optimal control with data-driven learning. By embedding vehicle dynamics and optimization structure into learned controllers, we aim to build systems that adapt to uncertainty and match or exceed expert drivers while retaining the interpretability and guarantees of classical methods. **The Internship** We are seeking a motivated intern to join our team, focusing on cutting-edge research combining machine learning with physical system knowledge and control theory to develop reliable controllers for autonomous vehicles. Potential research areas include designing learning-based control methods that enforce forward invariance, stability, and constraint satisfaction; and incorporating vehicle dynamics and other physical knowledge into learning and control amid challenging driving scenarios. This role provides an exciting opportunity to explore approaches to machine learning for control that support safe, intuitive, and responsive driving systems. Along the way you will apply your knowledge to tackle novel research questions and work towards a publication with professional researchers. The internship will be in our headquarters in Los Altos, CA and includes competitive compensation befitting the challenging, but fun, nature of the research work at TRI. Applicants with relevant publications in the fields above and good collaboration skills are highly encouraged to apply. ### Responsibilities - Work with researchers to develop and then undertake a well-scoped research project in a relevant area. - Extend existing controls/AI/ML algorithms or design new algorithms for control at a vehicle’s performance limit. - Explore approaches to formalize guarantees of safety for machine learning algorithms. - Implement algorithms on a full scale vehicle research platform. - Publish your original research at a high impact conference. ### Qualifications - Ph.D. or M.S. student in relevant fields - ML/AI, robotics, computer science, mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or similar. - Proficient in scientific Python, Unix, and robotic frameworks (e.g. ROS2.0). - Knowledge of machine learning, nonlinear system control, and optimal control. Vehicle dynamics knowledge is a plus. - Experience working on joint scientific and engineering projects. - Familiarity with or interest in racing or high-performance driving is a plus.

Our Technical Support team helps connect player experiences with the teams working on our games. We support players, investigate reported issues, and turn player feedback into relevant insights for teams across the studio. As a Junior Technical Support Specialist , you'll help players resolve technical and gameplay-related issues while providing valuable insights from player reports to our development and other teams. You'll communicate directly with players, investigate reported issues, document your findings, identify recurring patterns, and make sure relevant information reaches the right people. We're looking for someone who enjoys video games, helping others, and solving problems. You don't need to have all the answers right away. What matters is your curiosity, willingness to investigate unfamiliar issues, and ability to find solutions, even when they're not immediately obvious. We value attention to detail, clear communication, and a collaborative approach. You'll be part of a team where sharing knowledge, asking questions, and learning from feedback are all part of everyday work. Daily Responsibilities Respond to player reports and provide clear, helpful troubleshooting guidance. Investigate technical and gameplay-related issues using available documentation, internal tools, testing, and independent research. Identify recurring issues and patterns, ensuring they're appropriately categorised, prioritised, documented, and escalated. Help develop and improve troubleshooting solutions, internal knowledge resources, and player-facing support content. Collaborate with other teams, including development, legal, and communications, to share relevant information. Organise and manage your workload while maintaining clear communication and accurate documentation. Continuously expand your knowledge of our games, platforms, tools, and the teams involved in supporting them. Put CD PROJEKT RED's values into practice through respectful communication, teamwork, and a player-focused approach. At least 1 year of experience in customer-facing roles, such as customer service, customer support, community support, technical support, or similar positions involving direct interaction with customers or users. Very good English communication skills, both written and spoken, with the ability to explain technical information clearly to different audiences. Good analytical and problem-solving skills, with curiosity and a willingness to investigate unfamiliar issues. Strong interest in video games and understanding of player experiences. Attention to detail and the ability to document information clearly and accurately. Ability to collaborate with others, ask questions when needed, and use feedback to improve your work. Good organisational skills and the ability to manage recurring tasks consistently. Nice to Have Basic understanding of PC hardware, software, and common troubleshooting methods. Experience with ticketing systems, bug-tracking tools, game testing, modding, moderation, or supporting players in gaming communities. Knowledge of additional languages that can help us support our international player communities, particularly French, German, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Mandarin Chinese, or languages spoken in Eastern Europe. How to Apply Please attach your CV and cover letter in English as a single file . We’d like to hear more about what interests you about this role, why you’d like to join our Technical Support team and briefly on your gaming background. At the end of your cover letter, please include a brief 1–2 sentence explanation of the difference between a game remake and a remaster. Applications without the required attachments will not be considered. Working mode In-office in a hybrid or full-time capacity in Warsaw, Poland. Relocation is required. Life insurance — comprehensive pension and insurance plans to protect you and your loved ones. Annual screenings for cancer prevention covered by the company. Psychological and psychiatrist care — free mental health support and various well-being initiatives. Sports card — gain access to a wide number of sporting and fitness facilities across the city. Menstrual leave — employees who menstruate can take one extra day off when experiencing period pain. RED Parents Network — support for working parents, including childcare benefits, and family-friendly events. RED Summer Camp for Kids — a fun summer program for children aged 5–12, majoritively paid by the company. Polish lessons for foreign employees — and for your spouse or partner, too. Paid Leave — from 20 to 26 days of holiday per year, and paid sick leave. Perks & Professional Growth A welcome pack filled with goodies — to help you feel right at home once you join the team. Trainings, lectures, and courses — workshops and trainings for each employee, knowledge-sharing initiatives, online tutorials, and e-learning classes are all available. There’s always something to learn! REDs have access to the cafeteria platform through which they can receive subscription benefits, additional medical packages or vouchers and codes to shops, cinemas, and public transport reimbursement. Gifts for newborn rebels and regular chances to nab some cool swag! Social Activities & Life in the Office Dog-friendly office — dog owner? Social events — we host regular gatherings at the studio where we can all unwind, play games, and just have some fun together. Healthy selections — ​​canteens. We operate four health centers and offer telehealth statewide as part of a network of 600 Planned Parenthood affiliates nationwide. ## About the Opportunity We are seeking a graduate-level Social Science Research Practicum Student to support our Social Science Research Program. This practicum placement offers an opportunity to gain hands-on experience in public health and social science research, with a particular focus on translating research findings into accessible, engaging materials for diverse audiences. Conduct data collection as needed. - Complete additional research-related duties as directed. **OTHER DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:** - Participation in PPLM’s efforts to achieve goals for productivity - Perform other duties and special projects as assigned. - Ability to work 10-15 hours per week from January-May with flexibility based on program requirements ### Qualifications: - Current enrollment in a graduate program in public health, sociology, social work, women’s and gender studies, statistics, health communications, or a related social science field. - Ability to read scholarly work and interpret research results into digestible content accessible to a broad audience. - Experience with digital media and/or design, experience creating art - Interest in sexual and reproductive health research and research ethics. - Strong organizational skills and ability to follow study protocols. - Effective verbal and interpersonal communication skills. - Ability to interact respectfully with individuals of diverse backgrounds, identities, and experiences. - Ability to travel to health center sites as necessary. - Prior research or clinical experience is beneficial but not required. - Familiarity with RedCap data management software is beneficial but not required. - Contribute to the preparation of technical reports, calculations, specifications, and presentation materials. Support the use of digital engineering, CAD, Civil 3D, and BIM tools in the development and delivery of highway projects. Maintain accurate project records and assist with general project administration. Work collaboratively with engineers, technicians, project managers, and other disciplines to deliver high-quality solutions for clients. Develop an understanding of relevant highway design standards, legislation, health and safety requirements, and industry best practice. Participate in training and professional development activities as part of the apprenticeship programme. This role is suited to school leavers with an interest in developing a career in highway and civil engineering and the following: Minimum of 5 GCSEs (or equivalent) at Grade C/4 or above, including Mathematics and English. Three A-Levels (or equivalent, such as BTEC Level 3 in Civil Engineering), including Mathematics and a physical science at Grade C or above, where required for the Level 6 Degree Apprenticeship. Genuine interest in highway engineering, civil engineering, and the design and development of transport infrastructure. Aptitude for technical drawing, engineering design, and computer-based applications, with an interest in developing skills in tools such as AutoCAD and 3D modelling software. Basic proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Strong analytical and numerical skills, with a methodical approach to problem-solving. Ability to work collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary team, while demonstrating initiative when working independently. A willingness to learn, adapt, and develop new technical skills and knowledge. A creative, practical, and solutions-focused approach to engineering challenges. Commitment to continuous learning and professional development throughout the apprenticeship. ## **About Base** Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time. ## **About the Role** As a Power Systems Engineering Intern on Base’s Risk & Trading team, you’ll help model how our network of distributed residential batteries interacts with the grid, at both the distribution and transmission levels. During your internship you’ll be tasked with important problems for the business and expected to deliver just like any other full-time member of the team. You’ll work alongside Base’s power systems engineers on power flow studies, grid models, and the analysis behind where our batteries are deployed and how they’re dispatched. This is hands-on engineering work with real stakeholders. The studies and tools you build will be used by Base’s operations and business development teams and can shape how we work with utilities and grid operators. You’ll own a scoped project end to end, from defining the study and building the model to presenting what you found. ## **What You’ll Do** - Help design and run power flow studies (e.g., steady-state and contingency analyses) for Base battery aggregation use cases. - Build and validate distribution and transmission system models, using standard test topologies such as the IEEE test feeders. - Write Python to automate studies so they can be solved programmatically and run on a recurring basis. - Analyze and visualize study results and grid data, and turn them into clear recommendations, such as where on a feeder Base’s systems create the most value. - Compile and present your results to power systems engineers and the broader Risk & Trading team. ## **What You'll Bring** - Currently pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, or a related technical field. - Coursework, research, or project experience in power systems: power flow, per-unit systems, and three-phase analysis. - Proficiency in Python for data analysis and visualization (e.g., pandas, NumPy, matplotlib). - A strong foundation in linear algebra and numerical methods (e.g., Newton-Raphson). - A strong ownership mindset and the ability to clearly explain your assumptions, methods, and results. - Nice to have: exposure to power flow tools such as OpenDSS, GridLAB-D, CYME, PSS/E, PowerWorld, PyPSA, or pandapower, or to optimal power flow and electricity markets (e.g., ERCOT). ## **About the Team** Base’s Risk & Trading team is tasked with ensuring the grid-support performance and profitability of Base’s distributed battery fleet. This encompasses device communications with balancing authorities, telemetry analysis, algorithms for fleet aggregation and economic dispatch, through to financial portfolio management in wholesale energy markets. Our power systems engineers are the team’s experts on how the fleet interacts with the grid, from distribution feeders to the bulk transmission system. Our team is made up of physicists, economists, computer scientists, and engineers; the best candidates will bring the day-over-day intensity of an operator with the foresight to drive the long term development of simpler, more performant automated control. Success looks like building the airplane as it falls out of the sky. *Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.* ## **Our Values** - **First Principles Thinking:** Question assumptions. Principles > rules. - **Operate at Base Pace:** Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing. - **Give & Get Feedback:** Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset. - **Everyone’s an Owner:** Follow through on commitments and own results. - **Strong Opinions, Loosely Held:** Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information. - **Committed to the Mission:** Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in. - **Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit:** Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things. ## **Do the best work of your life at Base.**

role: Civil Engineering Apprentice - Highways & Streets - St. Albans (2027 starts)
description: About the Role At AECOM, we’re delivering a better world by designing and developing sustainable, efficient, and inclusive infrastructure that connects people and communities. Our Highways and Streets team works on a diverse range of projects across the UK and Ireland, supporting the development and improvement of road infrastructure for local authorities, National Highways, and other public and private sector clients. There may also be opportunities to work on projects in other parts of the world. Our projects span the full lifecycle of highway infrastructure, from feasibility and concept development through to detailed design and construction. This includes major road schemes, junction improvements, highway upgrades, active travel infrastructure, and improvements to existing networks. The team also supports colleagues in other sectors including delivering energy and aviation projects. Joining us as an Apprentice means becoming part of a collaborative, multidisciplinary team while gaining practical, hands-on experience alongside structured academic study and other professional development activities. You’ll develop your technical skills and knowledge while working towards professional qualifications and building a rewarding career in civil and highway engineering. Role Overview As a Highways & Streets Civil Engineering Apprentice based in our St. Albans office, you’ll support experienced engineers and designers in the development and delivery of a wide range of highway and traffic engineering projects. You’ll gain practical experience across different stages of project development, developing an understanding of technical design principles, engineering standards, and project delivery. You’ll work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams and develop experience using industry-standard design and modelling tools, including AutoCAD, Civil 3D, and BIM software. As your skills and knowledge develop, you’ll gradually take on greater responsibility and contribute to increasingly complex project work. Key Responsibilities Assist with the preparation of design drawings, plans, details, and supporting technical documentation using CAD and design software. Support the development and delivery of highway and traffic engineering schemes from feasibility and concept design through to detailed design. Assist with the design of roads, junctions, pedestrian and cycle infrastructure, and associated highway elements. Support the preparation and development of highway layouts in accordance with relevant design standards, guidance, and specifications. Assist with site visits, surveys, and the collection of information to support design and assessment. Help analyse technical information, survey data, and existing highway conditions to inform design development. Contribute to the preparation of technical reports, calculations, specifications, and presentation materials. Support the use of digital engineering, CAD, Civil 3D, and BIM tools in the development and delivery of highway projects. Maintain accurate project records and assist with general project administration. Work collaboratively with engineers, technicians, project managers, and other disciplines to deliver high-quality solutions for clients. Develop an understanding of relevant highway and street design standards, legislation, health and safety requirements, and industry best practice. Participate in training and professional development activities as part of the apprenticeship programme. This role is suited to school leavers with an interest in developing a career in highway and civil engineering and the following: Minimum of 5 GCSEs (or equivalent) at Grade C/4 or above, including Mathematics and English. Three A-Levels (or equivalent, such as BTEC Level 3 in Civil Engineering), including Mathematics and physical science at Grade C or above, where required for the Level 6 Degree Apprenticeship. Genuine interest in highway engineering, civil engineering, and the design and development of transport infrastructure. Genuine interest in highways, road design, link road and junction design, active travel, transport planning, and the development of safe, efficient, and sustainable transport networks. Aptitude for technical drawing, engineering design, and computer-based applications, with an interest in developing skills in tools such as AutoCAD and 3D modelling software. Basic proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Strong analytical and numerical skills, with a methodical approach to problem-solving. Good attention to detail, organisation, and time-management skills. Effective written and verbal communication skills, including research, technical writing, and report-writing skills. Ability to work collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary team, while demonstrating initiative when working independently. A willingness to learn, adapt, and develop new technical skills and knowledge. A creative, practical, and solutions-focused approach to engineering challenges. Commitment to continuous learning and professional development throughout the apprenticeship. Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible since CVs will be reviewed, and candidates selected for an advanced offer start. Please include a covering letter with your application and provide all predicted and/or obtained academic grades. You must have permanent right to work in the UK as we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position. At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment. About AECOM AECOM is the world’s trusted infrastructure consulting firm, delivering professional services throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. On projects spanning transportation, buildings, water, new energy and the environment, our public- and private-sector clients trust us to solve their most complex challenges. Our teams are driven by a common purpose to deliver a better world through our unrivaled technical and digital expertise, a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, and a commitment to environmental, social and governance priorities. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm and its Professional Services business had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. See how we are delivering sustainable legacies for generations to come at and @AECOM. Freedom to Grow in a World of Opportunity You will have the flexibility you need to do your best work with hybrid work options. Whether you’re working from an AECOM office, remote location or at a client site, you will be working in a dynamic environment where your integrity, entrepreneurial spirit and pioneering mindset are championed. You will help us foster a safe and respectful workplace, where we invite everyone to bring their whole selves to work using their unique talents, backgrounds and expertise to create transformational outcomes for our clients. AECOM provides a wide array of compensation, benefits and well-being programs to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. We’re the world’s trusted global infrastructure firm, and we’re in this together – your growth and success are ours too. Join us, and you’ll get all the benefits of being a part of a global, publicly traded firm – access to industry-leading technology and thinking and transformational work with big impact and work flexibility. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in each person’s potential, and we’ll help you reach yours. We are a Disability Confident Employer and will offer an interview to applicants who have a disability or long-term condition, who meet the minimum/essential criteria for the role. Please let us know using this email address if you would like to apply through the Disability Confident Interview Scheme. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. Work with Us. Change the World. At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations. There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world. We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.
