role: Mandatory Internship in Agentic AI Harness, Generative AI & Agentic Workflows
description: Dive into the world of Agentic AI and Generative AI, explore the potential of LLMs and turn your ideas into innovative AI solutions with us. During your assignment, you will support the design and development of an agentic harness to orchestrate LLM-based agents, tools and function calling. You will build and improve agentic workflows for internal use cases, including planning, tool use, memory and multi-agent coordination. Additionally, you will integrate and evaluate Generative AI / LLM models and prompt strategies, including prompt engineering and guardrails. To measure agent quality, reliability and performance, you will develop evaluation and benchmarking pipelines. As part of your work, you will prototype proof-of-concepts and contribute to Python-based tooling, APIs and automation. Finally, you will document results and present your findings to the team. Education: studies in the field of Computer Science, Data Science, AI/Machine Learning, Software Engineering, Mathematics or comparable with good grades Experience and Knowledge: solid programming skills in Python familiarity with Generative AI / LLMs (e.g. prompt engineering, LLM APIs, frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph or LlamaIndex) understanding of REST APIs and Git basic awareness of agentic concepts (tool calling, RAG, multi-agent systems) exposure to cloud environments (AWS/Azure/GCP), containerization (Docker), CI/CD or ML/evaluation frameworks Personality and Working Practice: you are curious and eager to learn, approach tasks independently with a structured and analytical mindset, and enjoy collaborating with others through strong communication and team spirit Work Routine: we offer you the possibility to work remotely part of the time by arrangement Enthusiasm: passion for Generative AI, autonomous agents and building cutting-edge AI tooling Languages: very good in English and beginner in German Start: according to prior agreement Duration: 6 months (confirmation of mandatory internship required) We offer you 35 hours/week with flextime a permanent contact person who will accompany you during your internship a modern working environment, as well as mobile working by arrangement the opportunity to become part of our student network students@bosch Stuttgart discounts in our company restaurants Requirement for this internship is the enrollment at university. Please attach your CV, transcript of records, enrollment certificate, examination regulations and if indicated a valid work and residence permit. Diversity and inclusion are not just trends for us but are firmly anchored in our corporate culture. Therefore, we welcome all applications, regardless of gender, age, disability, religion, ethnic origin or sexual identity. Need further information about the job? The Robert Bosch GmbH is looking forward to your application!

role: Civil & Structural Engineering Intern, Data Center Infrastructure
description: Hut 8 brings exceptional people together to solve the world’s most consequential problems at the intersection of energy and technology. Today, that means building infrastructure for AI at a pace and scale without precedent. Tomorrow, it could mean powering a new era of innovation through robotics, advanced manufacturing, or an industry that does not yet exist. Whatever the technology demands, our ambition holds: to build the defining physical infrastructure company of our generation. We look for thinkers and builders with the rigor, humility, and ownership to solve problems at this scale. They start from zero and choose truth over tradition. They back the best idea, whatever its source. They bet on themselves and embrace the hard truths that force them to grow. Our commitment is to keep the path from idea to execution short, trust them with critical decisions and the work that follows, and surround them with colleagues whose curiosity extends beyond their expertise. **BUILT DIFFERENT** --- We believe there's a better way to build. One that moves faster, thinks bigger, and gives people the ownership to challenge what's been done before. We're not here to follow the standard. We're here to set a new one. We don't believe the best work happens inside rigid boxes. People are given real ownership, real responsibility, and the space to operate beyond a title. Scope grows with impact and responsibility grows with trust. And the people who step up help shape what comes next. We're building an organization around ownership, where your influence is defined by what you take on. An internship at Hut 8 provides you with the opportunity to take on real work and drive real outcomes. **ABOUT THE ROLE** --- The infrastructure is ambitious. The people behind it should be too. We’re looking for a Civil & Structural Engineering intern who is curious, asks “why,” and wants to do real engineering work from day one. You’ll work side by side with our engineers on live data center projects, contribute to designs and calculations that actually get built, and leave with work you can point to. **WHAT YOU'LL OWN** --- + Learn it: Get hands-on with the civil and structural systems behind a data center: foundations, structural steel and concrete framing, site grading and drainage, and equipment anchorage + Support it: Help our engineers with load calculations, member and foundation sizing, grading and drainage layouts, and drawing markups, with guidance and review from licensed PEs + See it built: Join site visits, follow field issues from question to fix, and watch a design turn into excavation, foundations, and structure + Challenge it: Ask hard questions about cost, constructability, and redundancy. Fresh eyes are an asset here, and safety and reliability always come first + Own it: Take on a defined project of your own, from first question to final recommendation, and present it to the team at the end of your internship **WHAT YOU BRING** --- + Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s or master’s program in Civil or Structural Engineering or a closely related field, such as Architectural Engineering (structural), Construction Engineering, or Environmental Engineering with a structures or site-design foundation + Graduating in December 2027 or June 2028 with an undergraduate or graduate degree + Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.3 + Coursework in structural analysis, reinforced concrete or steel design, geotechnical engineering, or hydrology + Real interest in site and structural design for data center infrastructure + Comfort with AutoCAD, MATLAB, or Python, and the ability to pick up new engineering software quickly + Track record of personal accountability, integrity, and respect for others, the company, and oneself + Exceptional interpersonal skills to support team cohesion and successful project execution + Strong written and verbal communication skills for working with diverse groups and individuals + Comfortable working in fast-paced environments with shifting priorities and multiple deadlines, while contributing to inclusive and cooperative teams + Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook **BUILT FOR THIS** --- If you are curious, hungry to learn, drawn to hard problems, willing to ask “why,” and ready to do real work from week one. **BONUS POINTS** --- + You’ve used structural analysis software (ETABS, SAP2000, RISA, or similar) in a class or lab + You’ve worked or interned in construction, geotechnical, or surveying settings, or built something hands-on **ABOUT THE WORK ENVIRONMENT** --- This role is in office at our corporate headquarters in the Brickell area of Miami, Florida. Previous experience in an analytical, technical or consulting role.

role: Marketing & Data Analytics Assistant - Stage (6 mois) Mars 2027 (F/H/NB)
description: L'équipe Marketing Analytics est chargée de collecter, structurer et analyser les données afin d'en tirer des informations pertinentes et exploitables qui permettent d'optimiser nos initiatives marketing. Cela inclut la conception et la gestion de solutions de collecte et d'analyse de données (par exemple, tableaux de bord, rapports sur les indicateurs clés de performance marketing), ainsi que l'analyse des performances des initiatives marketing et de leur impact sur l'engagement, la conversion et la fidélisation. Réaliser des analyses de données, des modélisations statistiques et des rapports afin d’identifier les tendances et les opportunités sur l’ensemble des canaux, des segments d’audience et des segments de joueurs ; Effectuer des analyses exploratoires de données à partir d’une variété de sources différentes ; Créer et diffuser des données et des informations via des outils d’analyse (SQL, Power BI, Excel, PowerPoint) ; Traduire les questions et les défis métier soulevés par les parties prenantes en projets analytics ; Communiquer les conclusions sur les performances des campagnes et piloter les décisions d’optimisation avec les parties prenantes. Vous suivez des études supérieures avec une spécialisation en données, en informatique ou en ingénierie ; Vous êtes capable de communiquer et d’interagir en anglais avec des interlocuteurs internationaux, tant à l’oral qu’à l’écrit ; Vous avez de l’expérience dans l’utilisation de SQL, Python et Power BI ou d’autres outils de visualisation de données. Une expérience avec Databricks est un atout ; Vous êtes capable d’analyser des données brutes, d’en tirer des conclusions et de les présenter de manière claire et convaincante ; Vous possédez d'excellentes compétences orales et de communication ; Une expérience dans le domaine du jeu vidéo et une connaissance du secteur constituent un atout. Processus de recrutement Si votre candidature est retenue, vous serez contacté·e dans un premier temps par un·e représentant·e de notre équipe Campus pour un échange téléphonique afin de déterminer si votre profil correspond bien à l’annonce mais aussi à vos envies. Enfin, un entretien en présentiel ou en visio sera par la suite organisé avec votre futur·e tuteur·trice de stage. Avantages en tant que stagiaire chez Ubisoft Gratification de stage selon le niveau d’études Carte Titres Restaurant Swile, remboursement de 50 % du titre de transport, 1 RTT par mois Réduction billetterie (concerts/spectacles), accès à la salle de sport Ubisoft à tarifs préférentiels Ubisoft veille à développer un environnement de travail inclusif qui reflète la diversité de sa communauté de joueurs dans ses équipes. En tant qu’employeur, Ubisoft offre à tous les mêmes opportunités d’accès à l’emploi sans distinction de genre, ethnicité, religion, orientation sexuelle, statut social, handicap et d’âge. Boîte à questions Ubisoft Comment préparer ma candidature chez Ubisoft ? Dans un premier temps, lisez attentivement la job description afin de mettre en avant vos expériences et vos compétences qui vous semblent pertinentes pour cette opportunité ! Un CV personnalisé et détaillé vous permettra à coup sûr de vous démarquer 😉 Lettre de motivation ou pas ? A choisir, nous préférerons toujours quelques lignes expliquant votre motivation à candidater, plutôt qu’un texte générique copié/collé ! Un encart est d’ailleurs spécifiquement prévu à cet effet lors de votre candidature. N’hésitez à consulter notre article JobTeaser pour plus de conseils ! Je ne connais pas le secteur du jeu vidéo. Ai-je ma place chez Ubisoft ? Nous comptons dans nos rangs de nombreux profils qui ne sont pas des férus de jeux vidéo. Chez Ubisoft, nous cherchons à nous entourer de personnes passionnées, que ce soit par leurs spécialités, leurs métiers ou par le divertissement en général. A quoi m’attendre lors d’un stage ou d’une alternance chez Ubisoft ? Dès vos premiers jours, vous bénéficierez d’une Welcome Session vous présentant Ubisoft, son organisation et votre environnement de travail pour les prochains mois. Votre tuteur·rice et votre équipe vous accompagneront au quotidien, dans les premières semaines comme tout au long de votre expérience ! Une fois autonome, vos missions seront responsabilisantes et variées, peu importe le type de contrat. Travailler chez Ubisoft signifie travailler sur de vrais projets à mener au jour le jour. Un groupe Teams dédié vous permettra par ailleurs d’échanger avec les autres stagiaires et alternant·es. Quels sont les engagements sociétaux d’Ubisoft ? Nous cherchons à enrichir la vie des joueurs et joueuses par la création d’expériences de jeu originales et mémorables, et en nous appliquant à toujours améliorer l’impact positif de nos jeux. Afin d’y parvenir, nous créons un environnement de travail plus sûr et inclusif, nous soutenons les communautés dans lesquelles Ubisoft opère par le biais d’initiatives caritatives et nous nous efforçons de réduire l’impact environnemental de nos activités. Pour en savoir plus, rendez-vous sur la page Impact Sociétal . Je suis en situation de handicap, comment postuler ? Toutes nos équipes recrutement ont été sensibilisées aux sujets du handicap. Vous pouvez donc postuler normalement via notre plateforme SmartRecruiters en joignant votre CV et lettre de motivation. Si vous avez besoin d'une adaptation du processus de recrutement, notamment lorsque celui-ci implique des entretiens vidéo, précisez-le lors de votre candidature et/ou contactez l’équipe Mission Handicap par mail ( ). Ubisoft est une référence mondiale du jeu vidéo, avec des équipes réparties aux quatre coins du monde qui créent des expériences de jeu originales et mémorables, de Assassin’s Creed à Rainbow Six en passant par Just Dance et bien d’autres encore. Nous croyons que la diversité des points de vue fait progresser à la fois les joueurs et les équipes. Si vous êtes passionné·e par l’innovation et que vous souhaitez repousser les limites du divertissement, rejoignez notre aventure et aidez-nous à créer l’inconnu !

role: Summer 2027 Learning Architecture and Design Intern
description: Divergent is building the new industrial age. Every day, our teams design, manufacture, and assemble advanced systems for some of the world’s most demanding industries. Our integrated engineering and manufacturing platform transforms complex designs into production-ready solutions, helping customers move faster, build smarter, and deliver critical systems when they matter most. Divergent is a qualified Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and supports leading U.S. aerospace and defense companies. Join us and help push the boundaries of what can be built. **Duration:** 12 weeks (summer 2027) **Location**: Torrance, CA (onsite) ## Purpose At Divergent, we are transforming how complex products—like performance vehicles and aerospace components—are designed, engineered, and manufactured. But our ability to scale isn’t just about technology. It’s about people. We’re building a next-generation internal learning academy to rapidly onboard, upskill, and reskill a diverse workforce—ranging from hands-on technicians to world-class engineers. This isn’t a traditional training department; it’s a design lab for experiential learning at scale. We’re seeking a graduate-level Learning Architecture and Design Intern to help architect, prototype, and evaluate high-impact learning experiences grounded in adult learning principles, performance enablement, and human-centered design. ## The Role **Instructional Design & Delivery** Design and prototype learning modules and pathways for **advanced manufacturing technician and engineering roles** using adult learning and instructional design principles (e.g., experiential learning, microlearning, spaced repetition, and blended learning). **Learning Experience Innovation** Explore how AI tutors, immersive simulations, and AR/VR environments can accelerate skill mastery and engagement across the workforce. **Curriculum Architecture** Partner with technical and operational leaders to translate job knowledge, skills and abilities and core values and behaviors into structured learning journeys and skill progression frameworks. **Learning Evaluation** Develop and apply learning success metrics tied to real-world performance outcomes. Analyze data on engagement, skill transfer, and behavior change. **Performance Enablement** Embed learning into our real-time feedback and capability-building systems—replacing static training with dynamic, in-flow development. **Change & Communication Design** Support adoption of new learning systems, tools, and rituals through targeted messaging and learner-centric enablement strategies. **Applied Research** Conduct focused research on adult learning, instructional design models, and technology-enhanced learning to inform continuous improvement. ## Basic Qualifications - Ability to lawfully access information and technology that is subject to U.S. export controls - Master’s or PhD candidate in Instructional Design, Learning Sciences, Adult & Continuing Education, or related field (Organizational Psychology or Behavioral Science welcome with strong learning design interest - Demonstrated experience designing learning materials, programs, or experiences (academic, professional, or applied) - Familiarity analyzing complex datasets to identify trends, patterns, and insights that support business decisions. - Experience creating reports and presentations that effectively communicate data-driven findings and recommendations to non-technical stakeholders. - Comfortable using AI tools to support writing, content creation, research, and workflow efficiency. - Understanding of adult learning theory, curriculum design, and instructional models - Strong research and synthesis skills—able to translate insights into actionable learning strategies - Growth mindset and eagerness to learn through feedback - Excellent written and visual communication skills along with a strong attention to detail - Track record of success in fast-paced, experimental, high-autonomy environments ## Preferred Qualifications - Exposure to learning design or authoring tools (Articulate, Captivate, Rise, etc.) - Familiarity with LMS environments and standards such as SCORM or xAPI - Exposure to learning technologies leveraging AI, AR/VR, or simulation - Familiarity with job task analysis, skills mapping, or competency frameworks - Comfort analyzing engagement and learning data - Prior experience in instructional design, L&D, or workforce development - Curiosity about AI, emerging technology, and the future of work ## Why This Internship? - This isn’t a typical HR or training internship—it’s an opportunity to design the future of learning in advanced manufacturing. You’ll help craft scalable, high-impact learning systems that empower technicians, engineers, and leaders to grow fast and perform at their peak. - You’ll prototype modern learning experiences—from adaptive simulations to AI-powered feedback loops—transforming how people learn and perform in a high-innovation environment. Stratolaunch accelerates the development of next-generation aerospace and defense technologies through reusable hypersonic flight testing. Our autonomous, air-launched Talon-A vehicles provide access to operationally realistic flight environments at speeds exceeding Mach 5, delivering critical data that helps customers validate system performance and advance technologies toward deployment. We will provide you with all the support and tools you need to achieve your professional development ambitions, including Chartership with the relevant international professional institution. Professional institute qualifications you may be able to work towards include EngTech then IEng acrreditation with ICE. This position is ideally suited to those that can demonstrate the following (predicted or obtained); SQA Highers at AABB or BBBBC (Mathematics desirable but not essential) A-Levels at ABC or BBB​ Scottish Baccalaureate Pass​ Int. Baccalaureate 29 points​ Foundation Apprenticeship in Civil Engineering in conjunction with SQA Highers at AAB (Mathematics desirable but not essential)​ A combination of qualifications totalling 96 SCQF credits at level 6 or Minimum 126 UCAS points Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible since CVs will be reviewed, and candidates selected on a rolling recruitment basis. role: CWMD- Junior Intelligence Analyst- Washington DC
description: *Barbaricum is a rapidly growing government contractor providing leading-edge support to federal customers, with a particular focus on Defense and National Security mission sets. We leverage more than 17 years of support to stakeholders across the federal government, with established and growing capabilities across Intelligence, Analytics, Engineering, Mission Support, and Communications disciplines. Founded in 2008, our mission is to transform the way our customers approach constantly changing and complex problem sets by bringing to bear the latest in technology and the highest caliber of talent.* *Headquartered in Washington, DC's historic Dupont Circle neighborhood, Barbaricum also has a corporate presence in Tampa, FL, and Bedford, IN, with team members across the United States and around the world. As a leader in our space, we partner with firms in the private sector, academic institutions, and industry associations with a goal of continually building our expertise and capabilities for the benefit of our employees and the customers we support. Through all of this, we have built a vibrant corporate culture diverse in expertise and perspectives with a focus on collaboration and innovation. Our teams are at the frontier of the Nation's most complex and rewarding challenges. Join our team.* Barbaricum seeks a Junior Intelligence Analyst to provide analytic support to a DHS customer. Analysts will support the Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction (CWMD) Office of Information Analysis Directorate and Strategy, Plans, and Policy Directorate with the mission of enhancing the Department’s ability to prevent terrorists and other threat actors from using weapons of mass destruction. The CWMD Office is responsible for coordinating federal efforts and developing strategy and policy to plan for, detect, and protect against the importation, possession, development, or use of unauthorized chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear (CBRN) materials, devices, or agents in the United States. **The Role:** The Junior Intelligence Analyst supports WMD threat analysis and production efforts under the guidance of senior analysts. This role contributes to the development of analytic products that inform DHS leadership, DHS Components, and federal, state, and local homeland security partners on emerging and evolving WMD threats and mitigation strategies. **Responsibilities:** - Conduct in-depth analysis of WMD and CBRN-related threats to support homeland security missions - Contribute to analytic products including written reports, briefings, and presentations for DHS leadership and partner organizations - Support the identification, assessment, and understanding of WMD homeland threats and assist in developing recommendations to mitigate and disrupt those threats - Serve as a contributing or primary author on select analytic products and projects, commensurate with experience level - Support coordination and collaboration efforts with DHS Components and other U.S. Government and Intelligence Community partners at the analyst level - Apply structured analytic techniques and intelligence tradecraft in support of mission requirements **Required Qualifications:** - Active DoD TS/CI Clearance - Bachelor’s degree (BA/BS) in a relevant field (e.g., Intelligence Studies, International Relations, Political Science, Security Studies, or related discipline) - Up to 3 years of experience in intelligence analysis or a related analytical field - Foundational understanding of intelligence analysis principles, processes, and reporting - Strong written and verbal communication skills - Ability to work collaboratively in a team-based analytic environment **Desired Qualifications:** - Previous experience supporting CBRN or WMD-related intelligence analysis - Familiarity with intelligence systems, tools, or law enforcement intelligence environments - Experience producing written analytic products for government or operational customers **EEO Commitment** All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, ethnicity, age, national origin, citizenship, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, pregnancy, family structure, marital status, ancestry, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran or military status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

GFT is seeking an Entry Level Geotechnical Engineer to join our Geotechnical Team in our Mechanicsburg, PA office. This role follows a hybrid work model, requiring a minimum 3 days of onsite office attendance. December 2026 and Spring 2027 graduates are also encouraged to apply! Joining the geotechnical team at GFT means contributing to innovative geotechnical solutions for sustainable infrastructure. Our team excels in water resources, transit, rail, highway and structural projects. With a focus on integrating technology, sustainability, and compliance, we consider each project a chance to innovate and evolve to protect public health and enhance quality of life. What you’ll be challenged to do: The Entry Level Geotechnical Engineer will assist in planning and overseeing subsurface explorations and performing analyses for transportation, facilities, water resources and other types of projects. In this capacity, the successful candidate will be responsible for the following: Perform geotechnical calculations and designs for various projects and facilities, including, but not limited to shallow and deep foundations, retaining structures, settlement, tieback anchors, soil nails, slope stability and seepage studies. Assist in the preparation of written reports and documentation, geotechnical correspondence, design and construction drawings and specifications. Assist in the planning of subsurface explorations and laboratory testing investigations. Execute subsurface investigations in support of geotechnical design and evaluation efforts, including test boring inspection, site reconnaissance, and other data collection activities as required. Provide specialty geo-construction observation during the construction phase of various projects. This position requires travel on an as-needed basis to other GFT offices, client offices, or project work sites and will include overnight/out-of-town travel. What you will bring to our firm: Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering from an ABET-accredited institution. 0-3 years of geotechnical experience with an emphasis in subsurface exploration and/or design and development of geotechnical deliverables including reports, drawings, and specifications. Demonstrated interest in geotechnical engineering through applied academic coursework, prior internships, or related work experience. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Strong analytical, organizational, and report writing skills. Ability to work independently and within a team environment. Excellent field observation and data collection/documentation skills. Must be able to physically work outdoors in all seasons including being capable of lifting 30 pounds and traversing steep slopes and rough terrain. Must have valid Driver’s License. Sponsorship is not being offered for this position. What we prefer you bring: Master’s Degree with a Geotechnical focus. Experience with MicroStation and/or AutoCAD. Engineer-In-Training (EIT) certification. Experience with common geotechnical software programs such as SLIDE, SLOPE/W, LPILE, APILE, GROUP, GRLWEAP, Settle3 and gINT. Compensation: The salary range for this position is $75,000 - $90,000. Salary is dependent upon experience and geographic location. Featured Benefits: Comprehensive benefits package including wellness programs, parental leave, and pet insurance, in addition to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance. Tax-deferred 401(k) savings plan. Competitive paid-time-off (PTO) accrual. Tuition reimbursement for continued education. Commitment to professional development, access to internal and external training programs, and support of active participation in professional organizations Incentive compensation for eligible positions. Preferred Qualifications • Experience supporting software used by federal government or defense customers. • Experience with C#, .NET, JavaScript, jQuery, JSON, MVC • Experience implementing application logic, integrating APIs or services, Tekerik, ORM (such as Dapper or Entity Framework) • Experience using Git or comparable version control, debugging tools, and automated testing to deliver maintainable code. • Experience with writing tests in code using testing frameworks • Experience modernizing existing applications and supporting production releases. • Experience with secure application development, accessibility testing, and resolving security scan findings. **The Organization** At USAFacts, we believe facts deserve to be heard. We turn data from thousands of jurisdictions into clear, unbiased answers about how government spends money and what it achieves. No political agenda. No commercial motive. Just public service. Founded and funded by Steve Ballmer, former CEO of Microsoft, we work alongside Ballmer Group Philanthropy and Rainier Climate on civic impact. As an intern, you’ll join a collaborative, mission-driven team and learn how complex public data becomes something the American people can actually use. To top it off, Fast Company has recognized USAFacts four years running, including the 2026 Most Innovative Companies list. Learn more at and LinkedIn. Learn more about us at [](https://usafacts.org/) and [](http://linkedin.com/company/usafacts). We’d love for you to bring your curiosity, and your conviction that facts matter, to your summer with us. #### **Your Internship with USAFacts** This is a paid, full-time internship for your penultimate year of undergraduate study, where you’ll do real work on real products. Here’s what to expect: *Pay* $38 per hour for at least 10 weeks, which comes to roughly $15,200 before taxes at 40 hours per week. Interns are overtime eligible, so hours over 40 per week are paid at time and a half. *Housing support* Relocating interns receive company-paid furnished corporate housing and a $1,000 travel reimbursement. Interns who live in the area and don’t need corporate housing can be reimbursed up to $2,000 per month for housing costs with a current rental agreement. *Paid sick days and holidays* 3 paid sick days and paid holidays for the duration of your internship. *Hybrid schedule* In the office Tuesday through Thursday, with lunches provided, and the flexibility to work remotely or in-office the rest of the week. *Transportation* You’ll receive either an ORCA card for local public transit or paid parking in or near the building. *Events, community, and opportunities* At USAFacts, we believe a great internship is about more than just the work. Throughout the summer, you'll have opportunities to connect with your fellow interns, build relationships across the organization, and make the most of your time in the Seattle area. From organization-wide events and team outings to boat rides, paddleboarding adventures, and sushi dinners, you'll have plenty of opportunities to build connections and have fun along the way. Each intern cohort receives a dedicated morale budget to plan activities together and make the summer their own. You'll also have the unique opportunity to present your projects and accomplishments directly to USAFacts founder and former Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer and other organizational leaders. #### **The Opportunity** As an **AI & Software Engineering Intern at USAFacts**, you’ll help build the data and software systems that turn complex government data into trusted insights used by millions of people. Working alongside experienced engineers and product managers, you’ll contribute to designing, building, and testing tools, pipelines, and product features that power USAFacts’ platforms. You’ll gain hands-on experience across parts of the technology stack, from helping develop data pipelines that integrate and prepare large public datasets to contributing to software features that make data accessible and useful. You may also explore emerging AI capabilities, such as preparing datasets for machine learning or supporting AI-enabled features. This internship is a chance to grow your technical skills, learn modern engineering practices, and work with a collaborative team dedicated to making reliable information about the country more accessible to everyone. #### **Key Priorities and Responsibilities** - Collaborate with engineers and product managers to design, build, test, and document software and data systems. - Build mission-critical AI applications, data analysis tools, and end-to-end app development. Products you may contribute to include a Claude Connector, ChatGPT Plugin and MCP Server. - Learn and apply modern development practices (version control, testing, debugging, evaluations platforms, CI/CD). #### **The Ideal Candidate** - **Rising senior pursuing a bachelor’s degree** in computer science, software engineering, data science, or a related field (this internship is for the summer before your final year of undergraduate study). - Strong programming foundation (Python required; JavaScript/TypeScript a plus). - Familiarity with databases and SQL. - Interest in both software development and data systems. - Curiosity about AI/ML and how data powers intelligent products. - Comfort working across different layers of the stack, from data pipelines to product features. #### Additional Information The position is based in Bellevue, Washington. USAFacts practices intentional hybrid work​: all employees are on-site Tuesdays through Thursdays, with Mondays and Fridays flexible between home and office. This is a non-exempt, hourly role paid at $38 per hour. Interns are not eligible for the company’s standard benefits package, but you will receive the paid time off, housing support, and transportation support described above. Start and end dates are flexible between May and September to fit your school schedule, for a minimum of 10 weeks. We’re not able to coordinate academic credit through your school. **Nonpartisan Commitment** USAFacts is a nonpartisan, not-for-profit organization dedicated to making government data accessible and understandable as a free public service. Consistent with our Political Activity Policy, and to preserve the trust and neutrality essential to our mission, all employees must refrain from political activity that could compromise our impartiality. This includes making political donations, volunteering for or publicly supporting political candidates, parties, or campaigns. Additionally, employees are expected to avoid expressing partisan views on public platforms where they are identifiable as affiliated with USAFacts. This policy helps ensure our work—and our organization—remains trusted, fact-based, and free from political influence. ###### *USAFacts is an equal-opportunity employer and is dedicated to building an inclusive workforce where diversity is valued. Individuals seeking employment at USAFacts are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, martial status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, or sexual orientation.*

Tinder's mission is to **bring people together** and create meaningful relationships. For over 10 years, Tinder has been *the* place to meet new people. The **new generations of daters** think differently about relationships. Today, they’re looking for more and new ways to connect and share experiences. Our team in Ghent focuses on these **New Experiences**: we design, test, and build innovative features that enable new forms of discovery on top of the existing Tinder experience. During this internship, you’ll contribute to an experiment that brings this vision to life. **The Assignment** Develop an innovative feature that helps users **find people in a new way** and/or tools that enable this. You’ll collaborate with our multidisciplinary Product, Design, Engineering & Analytics team. You’ll work on **Product Design** of this feature. You’ll work closely with the product managers to translate a product hypothesis into a feature, with a strong focus on UI and UX design. Final presentation to the team with lessons learned and a demo of the PoC. ### Way of Working - You’ll work in a **multidisciplinary team** with product, design, engineering, and analytics. - **Agile approach**: weekly check-ins, demos, and quick feedback. - Access to real methodologies we use daily: user interviews, surveys, usability testing. ### What You’ll Learn - How to build for an **app with millions of users worldwide**. - How to work in an **international, multidisciplinary team**. - How to make an **impact with state-of-the-art mobile & backend technologies**. - How to go through the **entire process**, from idea to prototype to live test.

role: Strada Education Foundation: Information Technology Intern
description: Are you currently enrolled in a postsecondary education program (an education or training program after completing a diploma or GED)? Are you eager to make a meaningful impact in communities across the nation and gain practical experience at the same time? Join Strada Education Foundation's summer internship program and be part of a national philanthropic organization focused on better connecting education after high school to meaningful employment and economic opportunity in the U.S. **Information Technology Intern:** As an Information Technology Intern, you will gain high-impact experience and exposure across key areas that advance Strada’s mission and operations. You will support the team’s goals through efforts in helpdesk support, cybersecurity, cloud engineering, relationship management, and project and communications work. **About Strada** Strada Education Foundation is a national nonprofit social impact organization that supports programs, policies, and organizations that strengthen connections between education and employment in the U.S., with a special focus on helping those who have faced the greatest challenges securing economic opportunity through postsecondary education or training (PSET). Our strategic plan focuses on five focus areas: clear outcomes, quality coaching, affordable PSET, work-based learning, and employer alignment. Strada works with partners in education and training, nonprofit organizations, industry, startups, and public policy. We leverage strategic philanthropy, investments, research, communications, advocacy, and collaborating organizations as tools to help advance equitable pathways to opportunity. Strada aspires to be a nonprofit partner of choice working with education and training providers and leaders, policymakers, and peer organizations. Strada offers a dynamic, collaborative, and inspiring professional environment that provides learning and professional development opportunities, both within the organization and with external partners. **Internship Overview** **Duration:** May 18, 2027 - August 13, 2027 **Hours:** Minimum of 30 hours per week (seasonal employee) **Pay:** $22.75/hour undergrad; $25/hour grad **Location:** (Hybrid) Indianapolis, IN or Washington, DC (in-office on Tuesdays + department-specific days and other days as needed for special events) **Travel:** Up to 15% for Professional Development **Program Experience** The Strada summer internship program offers a paid, 13-week, hands-on learning experience for students who are at least one year post-high school. This opportunity is ideal for those seeking to gain experience in social impact while engaging in meaningful functional work. As part of this cohort-based program, interns will gain exposure to nonprofit operations, engage with leadership, and build a network that spans both nonprofit and for-profit sectors. Interns will work on impactful projects, participate in skill-building activities, and attend professional development events such as speaker series and informational interviews. The internship program will run from May 18, 2027, to August 13, 2027. Interns must be based in Central Indiana or the Washington, D.C., area and available for the entire duration of the program. Interns will work in the office at least two days per week (Tuesdays and one additional department-specific day). Additional in-office days may be required for professional development workshops and special events. There may also be opportunities to travel to conferences and workshops during the program. ### What You’ll Gain: - **Exposure to Nonprofit, Postsecondary Education, and Workforce Development Sectors:**Participate in leadership speaker series, lunch-and-learns, and industry interviews. - **High-Impact Work Experiences:**Gain functional skills through rotational work and real-world projects with colleagues across diverse teams. - **Coaching, Mentorship, and Professional Networking:**Receive quality mentorship and coaching from supervisors and executives. Build your professional network through community events and leadership exposure. ### Qualifications: - At least one year out of high school and currently enrolled in or accepted into a postsecondary education or training program (college, apprenticeship, boot camp, etc.). - Demonstrated ability to learn quickly and contribute in a collaborative environment. - Strong communication skills, both written and verbal. - Excellent attention to detail, time management, and problem-solving abilities. - Proficiency with Google Workspace; familiarity with Zoom, Slack, and Microsoft Office is a plus. - Self-motivated, and able to work independently while being open to feedback. - Passionate about promoting equitable opportunities in education and employment. - Positive attitude with a strong willingness to collaborate, contribute, and enhance the experience of the entire internship cohort. ### To apply for the Strada Education Foundation Summer Internship Program, please: - **Attach Your Resume** - **Submit a Cover Letter**detailing your interest in the internship. - **Submit a Loom Video** (instructions attached) Incomplete applications may not be reviewed.

Overview Join us for the summer! National Beef, a national leader in the beef industry, is looking for college students ready to explore a career in Beef Production Engineering to join our family for the summer of 2027 as an Engineering Intern. With competitive pay and benefits, stable work, and a caring and supportive environment, National Beef could become your next career move. Our internship program will provide you with a hands-on opportunity to work in a Beef Processing facility from start to finish. You will be introduced to our company culture and work practices and learn how our departments function. We will place qualified interns in three locations: Liberal, Kansas; Dodge City, Kansas; and Tama, Iowa. This is a paid internship. Housing allowance is included where required. This is an on-site position. Program Length: 10-12 weeks Responsibilities Engineering Summer Internship responsibilities include but are not limited to: An engineering intern at National Beef will gain insight into the various mechanical, electrical, control, and utility systems used in a modern food processing facility. From overhead chain conveyors, belted product conveyors, mechanized processing equipment, mechanical refrigeration and air handling systems, automated material handling systems, and the maintenance team that helps support process equipment uptime. Engineering interns will work with maintenance and engineering staff at their assigned facility with an emphasis on safety, quality, and process optimization. Some key tasks include: Learning how complex manufacturing processes are designed and maintained within a modern food processing facility Learning how plant processes are monitored and controlled Observing/understanding how safety is incorporated into various production systems and areas Observing/supporting the design and implementation of new systems or equipment Working with plant personnel to ensure proper methods and procedures are followed for system and equipment operations Participating in the execution and oversight of preventative maintenance and repair tasks Collaborating with the Engineering Department and engaging in networking opportunities with senior leadership Preparing detailed reports for the senior management team and key department heads, summarizing key insights and experiences during the internship Other duties as assigned This is a safety sensitive position. This is not a remote position. Qualifications Qualified Candidates for the Engineering Summer Internship position should possess the following: Enrolled and have completed at least two years in an accredited college degree program focusing on Engineering, Industrial Design, or a related field Minimum GPA of 3.0 in core curriculum classes Demonstrated leadership abilities and on-campus involvement Strong analytical and critical thinking skills Ability to work independently and be self-directed on project work Proficiency with all Microsoft Office products Availability to work 40+ hours per week (some weekend work) on-site for the duration of the internship Must be at least 18 years of age or older. Applicants must be authorized to work for ANY employer in the U.S. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship at this time. Company Overview National Beef is a leader in producing fresh, chilled and further processed beef products for customers in the U.S. and worldwide. We offer a variety of employment opportunities in our production, packaging, and hide tanning facilities that stretch from the western plains to the east coast. We strive to be the preferred employer in every one of those communities, whether it’s measured by the number of people employed or the good we do in the area. We invite you to join our family, wherever you call home. National Beef is an equal-opportunity employer committed to workplace diversity. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, natural origin, age, gender identity, protected veteran status, or status as a disabled individual. #IND

Candidates should be equally comfortable ideating at the conceptual level, crafting quick user-focused prototypes, and iterating on designs with user testing and technical feedback. **Here are some of the EXCITING things you’ll get to do:** - Strong communicator who can convey ideas, concepts, and solutions effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences. - Strong intuition for mechanical engineering and physics principles, with an emphasis on applying this in product design, ergonomics, and human-centered engineering. - Analytical and detail-oriented, with a creative approach to identifying and addressing potential issues. - Demonstrates intellectual curiosity, a hands-on attitude, and commitment to developing elegant, innovative solutions that balance technical and user-focused design principles. - Skilled at juggling multiple projects, with flexibility to pivot as needed while keeping sight of broader design objectives **Please note that, due to the high volume of applications for early talent roles, response times may vary depending on the specific role and timeline. role: Research Intern - Machine Learning and Optimization - Redmond
description: **Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The Machine Learning and Optimization (MLO) group in MSR-Redmond performs research in the intersection of optimization, machine learning and systems. Our focus right now is in combining ML technology with optimization for efficient decision-making. Example projects include training Large Language Models (LLMs) for algorithm design (e.g., natural language to integer programming, heuristic design), accelerating optimization algorithms for interactive decision dialogues and designing novel algorithms for end-to-end supply chain management. More broadly, our research draws on theoretical insights to design algorithms and machine learning solutions that operate efficiently at scale. **Responsibilities** Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. Research Interns are expected to design algorithms/models and prototype them, conduct experiments, and analyze results. They are encouraged to show initiative throughout the research internship and suggest further directions for research. They are expected to document their ideas, and given suitable results, contribute to a paper. **Qualifications** #### Required Qualifications - Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, Operations Research or a related STEM field **Other Requirements** - Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. - In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. #### Preferred Qualifications - 3+ years of experience in C# or C++ or Python (or similar language) - Experience in optimization/algorithm design - Experience in machine learning and LLMs (e.g., data curation, post-training, agentic frameworks) - Demonstrated ability to run simulations and analyze results The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here: Microsoft accepts applications and processes offers for these roles on an ongoing basis throughout the academic calendar (September - April). This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. --- Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. Primary Function of Position The HEOR Intern will join Intuitive’s Future Forward Medical Affairs team for a 10–12 week summer internship, reporting to the Staff Epidemiologist, Future Forward Medical Affairs. The intern will own a defined, scoped real-world evidence project, using administrative claims data and reimbursement coding (CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, MS-DRG) to characterize patient populations, procedure volumes, healthcare resource utilization, and costs for a technology in development. Working alongside senior epidemiology, data science, and market access colleagues, the intern will contribute analyses that inform value propositions and may help translate findings into inputs for budget impact or other economic models. The internship culminates in a final presentation to Future Forward leadership and cross-functional partners. Essential Job Duties Real-World Data Analysis: With guidance from senior team members, conduct a retrospective claims-based analysis to characterize patient populations, estimate procedure volumes, and describe utilization, outcomes, and costs relevant to a Future Forward pipeline technology. Coding & Cohort Definition: Identify and validate CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, and MS-DRG code sets to define target populations, procedures, comorbidities, and outcomes; document code lists and assumptions so they can be reused by the team. Study Planning & Programming: Contribute to a brief study protocol and statistical analysis plan; write, document, and quality-check analytic code, partnering with the team’s data scientist on shared data pipelines. Evidence Review: Conduct a targeted literature review to inform study design, benchmark findings against published evidence, and surface evidence gaps for the technology under study. Economic Modeling Support: Where relevant, translate claims-based estimates (e.g., procedure volumes, event rates, costs) into inputs for budget impact or other economic models, and support model development or validation. Communication: Summarize findings in clear visualizations and slides; deliver a final presentation to Future Forward leadership; contribute to a draft abstract where findings warrant. Required Skills and Experience Hands-on experience with reimbursement coding systems (CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, and MS-DRG), gained through dissertation research, research-assistant work, or prior employment, including using codes to define cohorts, procedures, and outcomes. Demonstrated experience analyzing at least one large administrative claims or hospital database (e.g., Medicare MedPAR/SAF, MarketScan, Optum Clinformatics, Premier, PearlDiver, Komodo Health, or similar), from data extraction and cleaning through analysis. Proficiency in SAS and/or R and working knowledge of SQL Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to translate technical analysis for non-specialist audiences. Comfortable working on a defined deliverable under the guidance of senior team members, with the independence to drive it to completion within the internship period. Intellectual curiosity and comfort with ambiguity; this team works on problems that are not yet fully defined. University Hiring Program Eligibility Requirements: University Enrollment: Must be currently enrolled in and returning to an accredited degree-seeking academic program after the internship. Internship Work Period: Must be available to work full-time (approximately 40 hours per week) during a 10-12 week period starting May or June. Specific start dates are shared during the recruiting process. Required Education and Training Current enrollment in a Health Economics, Health Outcomes/Services Research, Health Policy, Pharmaceutical Outcomes Research, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, or related degree-seeking program at the Doctorate (PhD) level. Working Conditions None Preferred Skills and Experience Experience developing or adapting budget impact models or other health economic models (e.g., cost-effectiveness, cost-consequence) in Excel, consistent with ISPOR good-practice guidelines. Familiarity with Medicare payment methodologies (IPPS/MS-DRG, OPPS/APC, MPFS/RVU) and how coding drives payment across sites of service. Research experience in medical devices, surgery, or procedural care. Peer-reviewed publications or congress abstracts (e.g., ISPOR, AcademyHealth). Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI). Primary Function of Position The Robotics Engineering Intern will report to future forward research lad and contribute to creating a sim-to-real-to-sim platform for the Intuitive surgical robot system. The intern will enable rapid prototyping and de-risking of new controller architectures, particularly semi-supervised and supervised autonomous systems that are data-hungry and require extensive validation. Key functions include developing tools that systematically transfer and test controllers from simulation to robot hardware, building virtual models of the surgical field for simulation interaction, and closing the loop between simulation and reality to accelerate development and evaluation of autonomous controllers. Essential Job Duties Implement novel control architectures in high-level (e.g., MATLAB) and low-level (e.g., embedded C++) targets. Systematically test controller performance in simulation and on robot hardware. Create simulation environments that integrate constrained rigid-body dynamics (e.g., MuJoCo) and realistic texture and lighting (e.g., Isaac Sim). Synthesize simulated environments from video data, including geometry, texture, and inferred stiffness. Execute closed-loop round-trip tests: train a controller in simulation, test it experimentally, and use experimental data to construct new simulation environments. Required Skills and Experience University Hiring Program Eligibility Requirements: University Enrollment: Must be currently enrolled in and returning to an accredited degree-seeking academic program after the internship. Internship Work Period: Must be available to work full-time (approximately 40 hours per week) during a 10-12 week period starting May or June. Specific start dates are shared during the recruiting process. Required Education and Training Current enrollment in a Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or related degree-seeking program at the Master's or Doctorate level. Working Conditions None. Preferred Skills and Experience Experience with MATLAB and/or Python for control system design and analysis. Experience with MuJoCo or similar constrained rigid-body dynamics simulators. Experience with sim-to-real transfer methods for robotic systems. Familiarity with NVIDIA Isaac Sim or similar platforms for realistic rendering and simulation. Familiarity with embedded C++ for low-level controller implementation. Awareness of video-based 3D reconstruction and environment synthesis techniques. Awareness of autonomous or semi-autonomous control architectures. Primary Function of Position You will join Future Forward, Intuitive's advanced concepts group, and report to an engineering lead on the team building AI for the next generation of robotic-assisted surgery. You will own an open-ended research and prototyping project in areas such as supervised autonomy and automation for robotic-assisted surgery, and AI that helps care teams deliver care more consistently and efficiently. The work draws on computer vision, generative AI, robotics, and agentic AI, and we will shape the exact project with you based on your background and the team's priorities. A successful internship ends with a working prototype, clear evidence of how well it works, and findings the team can keep building on. Essential Job Duties Own an open-ended research and prototyping project, scoped with your mentor. Explore how computer vision, generative AI, and agentic AI can be applied to new problems in surgery and the operating room. Build working prototypes and evaluate them against clear baselines. Work closely with researchers, engineers, and clinical experts. Share your results through documentation and a final presentation and contribute to publications or patent filings where results warrant it. Required Skills and Experience Research or applied experience in at least one of computer vision, generative AI, robotics or autonomy, or agentic AI (LLM agents and tool use). Strong Python skills and hands-on experience with a deep learning framework such as PyTorch. A track record of taking a loosely defined problem to a result, shown through publications, open-source work, or projects others have used. Sound experimental practice: you can set up a fair comparison and tell a real improvement from noise. Clear written and verbal communication with both technical and non-technical audiences. Intern will work closely with Paragon Staff to draft, review, and analyze the research project. - Intern will be expected to complete work on the research project on Fridays (Paragon’s remote workdays). **Strong preference for full time, would be open to part time for the right candidate.** ### Qualifications: - Entrepreneurial self-starter with high initiative and intellectual curiosity, eager to explore complex policy issues and contribute to a fast-paced think tank environment. - Strong interest in health policy, with a demonstrated desire to learn about and engage with topics such as Medicare, Medicaid, the ACA, and health care financing in a freemarket oriented lens. - role: Werkstudent:in im Bereich Datenmanagement und Monitoring Engineering
description: Für die BEW Berliner Energie und Wärme GmbH suchen wir dich zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt als Werkstudent:in im Bereich Datenmanagement und Monitoring Engineering am Standort Berlin . Die Abteilung Monitoring Performance und Technik überwacht Zustand, Performance und Effizienz der Energieerzeugungsanlagen und unterstützt Betrieb und Instandhaltung mit datenbasierten technischen Bewertungen. Hierzu werden Betriebs- und Zustandsdaten zusammengeführt, aufbereitet, analysiert und in Überwachungsmodellen, Dashboards und Berichten nutzbar gemacht. Unsere bestehenden Monitoringlösungen müssen kontinuierlich gepflegt, überprüft und an Veränderungen der Anlagen, Messstellen und Datenstrukturen angepasst werden. Für diese operativ wichtigen Aufgaben suchen wir Unterstützung mit technischem Verständnis, Sorgfalt und Interesse an energietechnischen Daten. Deine Aufgaben Du unterstützt bei der Pflege und Qualitätssicherung unseres technischen Monitorings, z. B. für Prozesse, Komponenten, Schwingungen, Wasserqualität und Anlagenperformance. Du prüfst Betriebs- und Messdaten auf Vollständigkeit, Plausibilität und Konsistenz und unterstützt bei der Bereinigung fehlerhafter, fehlender oder nicht mehr benötigter Daten. Du pflegst technische Datenstrukturen, Metadaten und Anlagenhierarchien sowie die Zuordnung von Messstellen, Komponenten und Monitoringmodellen. Du unterstützt bei der Weiterentwicklung von Überwachungsmodellen, Dashboards und technischen Visualisierungen, insbesondere in PI Vision und Power BI. Du führst Datenaufbereitungen und technische Auswertungen durch und recherchierst dafür relevante Informationen aus Anlagen- und Betriebsdokumentationen. Du dokumentierst Datenquellen, Berechnungsgrundlagen, Modelllogiken und Änderungen strukturiert und nachvollziehbar. Du wirkst dabei mit, wiederkehrende Arbeitsschritte zu standardisieren und sinnvoll zu automatisieren. Du bereitest Analyse- und Monitoringergebnisse für Berichte, Präsentationen und die Zusammenarbeit mit unseren Fachbereichen verständlich auf. Was dich erwartet Ein praxisnaher Einblick in das technische Monitoring eines umfangreichen Energieerzeugungsportfolios. Arbeit mit realen Betriebs-, Zustands- und Performancedaten. Eine Verbindung aus Datenmanagement, technischem Engineering und energietechnischen Fragestellungen. Klar abgrenzbare Aufgaben mit direktem Nutzen für die Verfügbarkeit und Effizienz der Anlagen. Zusammenarbeit mit Expert*innen aus Monitoring, Betrieb, Instandhaltung, Engineering und Informationstechnik. Dein Profil Du bist immatrikulierte:r Student:in, vorzugsweise in einer technischen oder datenorientierten Fachrichtung, beispielsweise: Energie- und Prozesstechnik Verfahrenstechnik Elektrotechnik Energietechnik Informatik Data Engineering Data Analytics Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung. Du besitzt ein gutes technisches Verständnis und Interesse an Energieerzeugungsanlagen und industriellen Prozessen. Du arbeitest sorgfältig, strukturiert und zuverlässig, insbesondere bei der Bearbeitung größerer Datenmengen. Du kannst technische Sachverhalte und Bearbeitungsschritte nachvollziehbar dokumentieren. Du verfügst über gute Kenntnisse in Microsoft 365, insbesondere Excel. Idealerweise besitzt du erste Kenntnisse in einem oder mehreren der folgenden Bereiche: OSIsoft beziehungsweise AVEVA PI System, PI AF, PI Vision oder DataLink Power BI Datenbanken und strukturierte Datenhaltung Python, SQL oder vergleichbare Werkzeuge technische Datenanalyse und Messdatenbewertung. Grundkenntnisse zu Kraftwerksprozessen, Fernwärmesystemen, thermodynamischen Prozessen oder Instandhaltung sind von Vorteil. Du verfügst über sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift, mindestens C1. Du arbeitest eigenständig, stimmst dich aber zugleich gerne mit Kolleg:innen und fachlichen Ansprechpartner:innen ab. Du hast für mindestens 6 Monate Zeit und kannst uns mit mindestens 20 Stunden pro Woche unterstützen. Deine Benefits Flexible Gestaltung deines Arbeitsalltags mit der Möglichkeit im Home-Office zu arbeiten Benötigte technische Ausstattung wird dir selbstverständlich zur Verfügung gestellt Individuelle Entwicklung und Aufbau deines beruflichen Netzwerks Verbesserte Einstiegschancen nach abgeschlossenem Studium Bio-Betriebsrestaurant sowie kostenfreie Getränke (Wasser, Tee, Kaffee) und Obst an fast allen Standorten Verschiedene Angebote zum Thema Gesundheit, z. B. Unterstützung durch PME-Familienservice Deine Bewerbung Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung! Bitte sende uns deine vollständigen Bewerbungsunterlagen in deutscher Sprache und im PDF-Format (insb. ein Anschreiben , einen lückenlosen Lebenslauf sowie eine aktuelle Immatrikulationsbescheinigung ) bis spätestens 11.11.2026 zu! Für weitere Informationen zu dieser Position kannst du dich an die einstellende Managerin Tatiana van Tilburg Londono unter wenden. Fragen zum Bewerbungsprozess beantwortet dir gern der zuständige Recruiter Shawn Sieber unter . Du hast Interesse an unserem Angebot und möchtest gemeinsam mit uns die Berliner Wärmewende gestalten? Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung über unsere Karriereseite! Hinweise Wir sind davon überzeugt, dass Vielfalt dazu beiträgt, unser Unternehmen leistungsfähiger und attraktiver zu machen. Bewerbungen zum Beispiel von Personen jeglichen Alters, geschlechtlicher Identität, sexueller Orientierung oder ethnisch-kulturellen Hintergrunds sind herzlich willkommen. Schwerbehinderte Menschen werden bei gleicher fachlicher Eignung besonders berücksichtigt. Die Sicherheit der BEW und ihrer Beschäftigten ist von grundlegender Bedeutung. Aus diesem Grund ist ein Pre-Employment Screening Teil des Rekrutierungsprozesses. Der Umfang der Überprüfung variiert je nach Funktion und Einsatzbereich. Das Screening wird von einem Drittanbieter, Signum Consulting GmbH, DISA, durchgeführt. * Damit meinen wir eine Wärmeversorgung aus erneuerbaren Energien, aus unvermeidbarer Abwärme oder einer Kombination aus beidem im Sinne des § 31 i. v. m. § 3 Abs. 1 Nr. 13, 15 und Abs. 4 Wärmeplanungsgesetz (WPG). Dieses Ziel wollen wir durch eine Reihe von Maßnahmen erreichen, welche wir in unserem Dekarbonisierungsfahrplan darstellen. ** Im Sinne des § 3 Abs. 1 Nr. 13 bzw. Abs. 4 Wärmeplanungsgesetz (WPG). Wärme und Energie sind unser Beitrag zur Lebensqualität – jeden Tag aufs Neue. Als BEW Berliner Energie und Wärme GmbH versorgen wir unsere Kund:innen mit Strom und Wärme. Unser Fernwärmenetz ist mit einer Länge von mehr als 2.000 Kilometern das größte Westeuropas. Wir beliefern etwa ein Drittel der Berliner Wohnungen mit Fernwärme. Mit dem Know-how unserer rund 2.400 Mitarbeitenden decken wir die gesamte Wertschöpfungskette der Fernwärme ab – von der Erzeugung über den Netzbetrieb und -ausbau bis hin zum Vertrieb. Parallel dazu arbeiten wir mit Hochdruck am Kohleausstieg bis 2030 und an einer klimaneutralen* Wärmeerzeugung ab 2045. Um dieses Ziel zu erreichen, werden wir den Anteil an erneuerbaren Energien und unvermeidbarer Abwärme** in unserem Fernwärmesystem schrittweise weiter ausbauen. Dieser Ausbau setzt einen grundlegenden Umbau vieler unserer Standorte und Anlagen voraus. Für diese Herausforderung und die damit verbundenen Aufgaben brauchen wir Menschen, die sich mit ganzer Kraft für unser gemeinsames Ziel einer lokalen Wärmewende engagieren – Menschen wie dich.

Key Responsibilities: Support the production of electrical design layouts, mark-ups, schedules, and calculations under guidance. Assist with drafting technical specifications and reviewing supplier documentation. Contribute to the coordination of electrical services with other engineering disciplines. Use engineering software tools (e.g., Dialux, Amtech) to support design tasks. Attend internal team meetings and contribute to design discussions and coordination efforts. Support the review and integration of information from suppliers and contractors. Help maintain documentation, records, and project files in line with project standards. Learn about industry standards and codes relevant to electrical systems in infrastructure. Engage in site visits or inspections (as required) to better understand practical implementation. Essential: A degree in Electrical Engineering, Building Services Engineering, or related discipline. A basic understanding of electrical building services systems. Familiarity with design tools such as AutoCAD, Revit, Amtech, Dialux or Relux (training can be provided). Good written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a team environment. A proactive and enthusiastic approach to learning and development. Desirable: Internship or placement experience in an engineering design environment. Awareness of British Standards and electrical regulations (e.g., BS 7671). Exposure to BIM workflows and multidisciplinary coordination.
