**Who we are** Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress. Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that. Atoms builds Physical AI real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive. This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across AI, hardware, software, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale. We are researchers, roboticists, engineers, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life. If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us. **About the role** We are seeking an AI Research Intern to join our founding team and bridge the gap between high-level AI research and real-world physical actuation for our next-generation autonomous transport platforms. In this role, you will contribute to core research initiatives on Perception, World Models and Action models. You will help translate cutting-edge theoretical breakthroughs into scalable, real-world deployment on physical autonomous systems, driving how our platforms perceive, simulate, and navigate complex environments. **What you’ll do** - Integrate and adapt emerging AI research into internal model pipelines, validating performance on real-world datasets and simulation. - Prototype and evaluate RL, trajectory planning, and distillation algorithms based on state-of-the-art literature. - Train and fine-tune multimodal models that map real-time sensor inputs and behavioral goals to vehicle actuation. - Experiment with world model architectures using multi-sensor log data to improve simulation fidelity and trajectory querying. - Analyze edge cases and failure modes in novel driving environments to iterate on model performance and stability. - Run rigorous simulation experiments alongside research and validation teams to identify performance bottlenecks and track model improvements. **What we're looking for** - **Education:** Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's degree program in Computer Science, EECS, Robotics, AI, or a closely related field. - **Core Expertise:** Coursework, project experience, or research background focused on at least one of the following domains: - Generative World Models / Video Generation / Diffusion Models - Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models or embodied AI - Reinforcement Learning (RL), trajectory optimization, or decision-making systems - Large-scale multimodal Transformer architectures applied to robotics or spatio-temporal data - **Framework Fluency:** Advanced hands-on proficiency with PyTorch or JAX for training and fine-tuning large-scale neural networks. - **Programming:** Proficiency in Python and working knowledge of C++. **Preferred Qualifications** - Prior research, project, or internship experience in autonomous driving, mobile robotics, or spatial AI. **Why join us** At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow. **What else you need to know** This role is based in our Mountain View or San Francisco office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change, we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week. The hourly pay range for this internship role is **$70/hr per hour.** Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications. Atoms accepts applications on an ongoing basis. **Ready to join us as we serve those who serve others?** *#LI-Onsite*

role: 2027 Summer Intern, MS/PhD, Sensor Performance Engineer Intern
description: Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states. The Waymo Laser team is a diverse, innovative, and collaborative group of electrical, mechanical, optical and software engineers. We design, build and perfect our cutting edge automotive lidars, and evaluate the lidars that are on the market, and integrate them into Waymo products. Waymo interns partner with leaders in the industry on projects that create impact to the company. We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. Join us at Waymo for a fun and rewarding internship! **You will:** - Sensor Data Analysis: Process and analyze complex sensor datasets to extract key insights. - Experimental Setup: Design and execute rigorous experiments for validation and testing. - Performance Engineering: Develop robust performance metrics and streamline operational processes. - Stakeholder Collaboration: Partner effectively with cross-functional teams to align project goals. **You have:** - Currently enrolled in an MS or PhD program in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Computer Science, or a related field. - Hardware Experimentation: EE or physics-based experimental design - System Prototyping: Modeling and rapid prototyping of complex hardware - Data Analysis: Evaluating performance metrics and experimental results - Technical Scripting: Automation using Python, SQL, and scripting **We prefer:** - Signal Processing: Advanced filtering, algorithm design, and data extraction - Sensing Systems: Experience with LiDAR, radar, camera, and general perception hardware - Technical Communication: Clear presentation of complex concepts to cross-functional teams Note: This will be a hybrid onsite internship position. We will accept resumes on a rolling basis until the role is filled. To be in consideration for multiple roles, you will need to apply to each one individually - please apply to the top 3 roles you are interested in. role: Data Center Construction - Junior Project Manager Cost Focus
description: ## It’s an exciting time to join MGAC! MGAC is a global boutique consultancy dedicated to managing and representing our clients’ best interests. Our success is rooted in hiring exceptional people who are driven to do challenging work with the unique blend of experience, integrity, creativity, and commitment that separates us from our competitors. **We have three simple goals:** to do the most interesting and challenging work, to have fun working together, and to build a successful business in the process. This position requires local support, with approximately **4 days per week onsite in Columbus, OH**, subject to client needs. --- ## Unlock Your Potential We’re looking for candidates eager to take ownership of challenging projects and grow their careers. Here’s what will set you up for success at MGAC: - 3+ years of experience in construction project management with a thorough understanding of the building design and construction process. - Bachelor’s, Associate’s, or equivalent experience in a construction-related discipline. - 2+ years of construction cost management experience. - 2+ years of experience managing critical environment construction projects (e.g., data centers, labs, hospitals). - MEP experience in ground-up construction. - Excellent analytical, organizational, problem-solving, presentation, interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills. - Ambitious, construction and project management-focused, and seeking a modern and energetic business that will empower you to grow your career. ## What You’ll Be Doing MGAC’s Critical Environments team manages the construction of data centers and hospitals with deep industry expertise. We act as owner’s representatives—resolving issues, managing conflicts, and guiding informed decisions to keep projects on track. You'll own a defined research project with mentorship from ML scientists, and you'll work closely with experimental scientists to connect your models to real biological data. Present findings to the team and contribute to research write-ups, and where possible to external publications or presentations. **What You'll Need to Succeed** - Currently enrolled in an MS or PhD program in machine learning, computational biology, bioengineering, computer science, statistics or a related quantitative field. - Experience with sequence-to-function models, genomic language models, or models trained on MPRA, reporter assay or other functional genomics data. - Familiarity with RNA secondary structure prediction, UTR or codon design, or inverse design methods. - Experience with generative modeling, active learning or Bayesian optimization. - Exposure to wet-lab data or collaboration with experimental scientists. - A research publication, preprint or open-source project in ML or computational biology. - Experience using or building with large language or reasoning models, AI agents, or LLM-based tools for scientific tasks. **About LILA** Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves. LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. Learn more at . Guided by our core values of truth, trust, curiosity, grit, and velocity, we move with startup speed while tackling problems of historic importance. role: Robotics Intern, Trustworthy Learning under Uncertainty
description: At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences. This is a paid 12-week internship opportunity and is a hybrid, in-office role. [Here’s a glimpse into the Internship experience from some of our TRI interns!](https://www.tri.global/tri-internship-program) **The Team** Our [Trustworthy Learning under Uncertainty (TLU) team](https://www.tri.global/trustworthy-learning-under-uncertainty-tlu) in the Robotics division is looking for Research Interns for Summer 2027 in a variety of areas such as Policy Evaluation, Failure Detection and Mitigation, as well as (Inter)Active and Continual Learning in the context of World Foundation Models (WFM) for Robot Manipulation. Our topics of interest include but are not limited to: Multi-Modal Foundation Models, Generative Modeling, Imitation Learning, Reinforcement Learning, Planning & Control, Statistics, Uncertainty Estimation, Out-of-Distribution Detection, Safety-Aware & Robust ML, (Inter)Active Learning, and Online / Continual Learning. We are aiming to make progress on some of the hardest scientific challenges around the safe and effective usage and development of machine learning algorithms within Robotics. To this end, the research mission of the TLU team is to enable the robust and reliable deployment of embodied foundation models at scale in human environments, while allowing for efficient adaptation to novel settings. **The Internship** As a Research Intern, you will work with a multidisciplinary team proposing, conducting, and transferring pioneering research in Machine Learning for Robot Manipulation. You will use large amounts of sensory data and simulation to solve open problems, work towards publications at top academic venues, and test your ideas in the real world, including on our robots, of course! ### Responsibilities - Conduct daring research primarily in Robot Manipulation that solves open problems of high practical and/or ethical value and validate it in real-world benchmarks and systems. - Push the boundaries of knowledge and the state-of-the-art in Robot Manipulation and foundation models. - Partner with a multidisciplinary team, including other research scientists and engineers across the TLU team, Robotics division, TRI, Toyota, and our [university partners](https://pressroom.toyota.com/toyota-research-institute-launches-next-phase-of-collaborative-research-with-diverse-roster-of-world-class-academic-institutions/). - Stay up to date on the state-of-the-art in Machine Learning ideas and software. - Present results in verbal and written communications at international conferences, internally, and via open-source contributions to the community. ### Qualifications - Currently pursuing a Ph.D. in Machine Learning, Robotics, or related fields. - Publication or desire to publish at high-impact conferences/journals (e.g., CoRL, ICLR, NeurIPS, ICML, UAI, AISTATS, AAAI, TMLR, RSS, ICRA, IROS, RA-L, T-RO, CDC, L4DC, etc.) on some of the aforementioned topics. - Passionate about large scale challenges in Machine Learning grounded in physical systems, especially in the space of Robotics. - Proficiency with one or more coding languages and systems, preferably Python, Unix, and a Deep Learning framework (e.g., PyTorch). - Ability to collaborate with other researchers and engineers of the TLU team, and, more broadly, the Robotics division to invent and develop interesting research ideas. - A reliable teammate who loves to think big, go deeper, and deliver with integrity.

At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. Swarm Aero is redefining air power, building the largest swarming UAV and the most versatile swarming aircraft network in the world. The company is moving quickly to launch the first aircraft designed specifically for swarming, as well as the Command & Control software to mobilize swarms of thousands of heterogeneous autonomous assets and empower human operators to achieve superhuman results. The team has created and exited multiple startups, negotiated defense deals worth billions of dollars, and designed and built 30+ novel aircraft, with aerospace experience from Scaled Composites, Airbus, Archer Aviation, Blue Origin, and Boom Supersonic. Legion's Command & Control platform lets a single operator plan, direct, and execute missions across a networked swarm of heterogeneous aircraft, in real time, over intermittent comms, at a scale nobody else in the industry is attempting. That means distributed state under unreliable networks, dense telemetry moving fast enough to strain anything you've built before, and interfaces for a problem space that barely has prior art. You'll work across the stack, wherever the hard problem is that week. **WHAT YOU'LL DO** - Build and ship features in the C2 system that directs swarms of heterogeneous aircraft - Work on systems that hold state and stay responsive when comms degrade or drop entirely - Move between the interface layer and the services behind it, following the problem rather than a job description - Prototype new ways to represent and control vehicle telemetry, sensor data, and scheduling - Take features end to end, from a rough problem statement through design, implementation, and deployment - Ship early and often, backed by strong CI/CD, QA, and DevSecOps **WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR** - Degree in Computer Science, a related technical field, or equivalent self-taught depth - Real strength in fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, concurrency, networking, systems - Evidence you've built something hard because you wanted to. A renderer, an emulator, a game, a compiler, a multiplayer server, a robotics project, a serious open source contribution. We care more about what you've built than where you worked - Comfort writing code at more than one layer of the stack, and no strong attachment to staying at one - Willingness to work on problems where the right answer isn't known yet, and to be wrong in public on the way to finding it **WHAT SETS YOU APART** - Competitive programming background (ICPC, IOI, Codeforces, USACO, Putnam) - Game development, game jams, engine work, or simulation - Performance-sensitive work: profiling, frame budgets, memory pressure, running on constrained hardware - Real-time or distributed systems experience: multiplayer netcode, streaming, pub/sub, robotics middleware - Graphics: WebGL, OpenGL, Vulkan, shaders - Working fluency in Go, C++, or Rust - Familiarity with video streaming protocols or geospatial applications - Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance. Active Secret clearance preferred but not required. **WHY THIS ROLE** You'll be one of the earliest engineers shaping how humans command autonomous systems at scale, work that's currently being defined in real time, by a small team, with your fingerprints on the architecture. If you want to build the future of human-swarm interaction rather than maintain someone else's, this is that seat. **ITAR requirement** To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Swarm Aero is an equal opportunity employer. We value diverse backgrounds and experiences and make employment decisions without regard to race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, or disability. **What We Offer** - Meaningful equity in a high-growth defense technology company - Competitive base salary commensurate with experience - Medical, dental, vision, and 401k - PTO and paid sick leave - Monthly wellness stipend - Daily catered lunch (office) - Paid parental leave - Direct impact on a critical national security mission - A world-class team of engineers and operators solving genuinely hard problems

role: Robotics Intern, Post-Training and Continual Learning
description: At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences. This is a paid 12-week internship opportunity and is a hybrid, in-office role. [Here’s a glimpse into the Internship experience from some of our TRI interns!](https://www.tri.global/tri-internship-program) **The Team** Our team in the Robotics division is developing pretrained generalist policies that can support a broad range of tasks, environments, and robotic systems. A central scientific challenge is determining how these broadly pretrained policies can be efficiently adapted to new target tasks while achieving the reliability, precision, and robustness required for real-world use. Pretraining can provide a policy with broad behavioral capabilities, but those capabilities may not immediately translate into dependable performance in a specific deployment setting. Effective post-training methods are therefore essential for converting general capabilities into policies that can adapt quickly, learn from limited additional data or interaction, and perform consistently on demanding downstream tasks. **The Opportunity** Our research interests include reinforcement learning, imitation learning, human-in-the-loop learning, simulation, world models, policy distillation, and large-scale robot learning. We aim to advance the scientific foundations of policy adaptation while developing methods that may ultimately be evaluated or deployed within internal research projects involving real-world industrial tasks. Potential research directions include, but are not limited to: - Offline-to-online reinforcement learning - DAgger, imitation learning, and human-in-the-loop policy improvement - Sim-to-real policy distillation and adaptation - Policy improvement, planning, or data generation using world models - Data-efficient adaptation to new tasks and environments ### Resposibilities - Develop post-training methods that adapt pretrained generalist robot policies to new tasks, environments, and robotic systems. - Design and conduct rigorous experiments in simulation and, where appropriate, on real robotic systems. - Analyze results, communicate findings, and contribute to research publications and internal technical reports. ### Qualifications - Currently pursuing a Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, or a related field. - Research experience in robot learning, reinforcement learning, imitation learning, generative modeling, world models, or a related area. - Interest in open research problems involving large-scale machine learning grounded in physical systems. - Proficiency in Python and a deep-learning framework such as PyTorch. - Ability to collaborate effectively with researchers and engineers and communicate research findings clearly. ### Bonus Qualifications - Experience with pretrained generalist policies, foundation models, or large-scale robot-learning systems. - Familiarity with offline or online reinforcement learning, DAgger, interactive learning, or human-in-the-loop methods. - Experience with simulation, sim-to-real transfer, policy distillation, or robotic manipulation. - Experience with learned world models, model-based reinforcement learning, or planning. - Publication record or interest in publishing at leading venues such as CoRL, NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, RSS, ICRA, IROS, or related conferences and journals. - Interest in translating fundamental research into reliable methods that can be evaluated on real robotic systems and practical downstream tasks.

role: Autonomy Engineer Intern, Autonomy Infrastructure, Systems and Tools, 2027 (Zurich)
description: Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from [utility inspectors](https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities) to [first responders](https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety), [soldiers in battlefield scenarios](https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr), and [beyond](https://www.skydio.com/solutions). ## **About the Role:** The core of our system is the computer vision algorithms that allow drones to understand the world around them. You will architect and implement the algorithms that run on every drone powered by Skydio as part of a world class computer vision and deep learning team with researchers who have pushed the state of the art in academia and industry. As a Research Intern, you will be paired up with one or more members of our core software development team, assuming direct ownership of a project that meaningfully advances the capabilities of our team and products. If you have a strong foundation in math, theory, and software development and you are interested in directly contributing to the development of the next generation of autonomy algorithms and pushing them into real products, we would love to hear from you. ## **Areas of Responsibility:** - **Design and build robust replay and analysis systems** that enable engineers to inspect and reproduce recorded autonomy behavior, with fine-grained control over system state, perception outputs, and decision-making at every stage of the stack. - **Develop scalable infrastructure for automated testing and failure triage**, expanding our simulation and log-driven test coverage while accelerating root-cause analysis through automated log processing and diagnostics. - **Operate at the interface between autonomy software and core robotics middleware**, defining clear APIs, data contracts, and performance requirements for messaging, state propagation, and coordination across subsystems, while partnering closely with downstream teams to support their implementation and integration. - **Design and implement high-quality developer infrastructure and tools** that prioritize reliability, performance, and usability, enabling rapid iteration, safe experimentation, and sustained velocity across the autonomy organization. ## **What You’ll Do:** - Lead the design and implementation of scalable tools used across autonomy development and testing workflows. - Collaborate with autonomy, QA, and infrastructure teams to gather requirements, align on priorities, and deliver impactful tooling. - Build tools that streamline stages of the robotics development process. - Take ownership of internal services from concept through deployment and monitoring. - Contribute to the long-term vision and roadmap for developer tools that improve debugging efficiency, test coverage, and system understanding. ## **Qualifications:** - Proficiency in C++ and Python, with a strong grasp of performance-sensitive and multi-threaded systems. - Experience with simulation frameworks, time-synchronized data systems, or state-machine-driven applications. - Familiarity with structured data visualization, log processing, or developer tooling design. - Strong communication skills and the ability to partner effectively with cross-functional teams. - Comfort operating in a fast-paced environment where requirements evolve and priorities shift. ## **Bonus Experience:** - Experience building performance-sensitive systems (profiling, multithreading, real-time constraints) in robotics, aerospace, automotive, or similar domains. - Exposure to robotics / simulation / physics engines. - Background in telemetry systems, log ingestion pipelines, or automated test environments. - Front-end development skills in modern web frameworks (e.g., React, TypeScript, Three.js, Plotly) with a focus on data interaction and visualization. - Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from [utility inspectors](https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities) to [first responders](https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety), [soldiers in battlefield scenarios](https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr), and [beyond](https://www.skydio.com/solutions). **About the role:** Skydio builds the world’s most advanced autonomous drones used across inspection, public safety, defense, cinematography, and more. Your research won’t languish in a paper: it will **fly**, shaping how pilots and operators complete real missions in complex environments. Develop and deploy **reinforcement learning** (and adjacent policy-learning methods) that make Skydio aircraft **plan, navigate, and control** themselves more intelligently, safely, reliably, and efficiently across our ecosystem: handheld apps, ground control, cloud autonomy services, and fleet workflows. **How you'll make an impact:** - **Navigation & avoidance in the wild:** Train policies that adapt online to cluttered 3D scenes (forests, bridges, urban canyons), complementing our stack for robust obstacle avoidance and dynamic goal-seeking. - **RL-augmented planning:** Fuse learned cost shaping / value functions with trajectory optimization for smooth, agile flight with tight safety envelopes and mission constraints. - **Sim to Real at scale:** Build scalable datasets and training loops with Isaac Lab, domain randomization, residual learning, and safety filters; validate on real drones weekly. - **Human-in-the-loop shared control:** Learn assistive policies that blend pilot intent, autonomy priors, and uncertainty-aware behaviors for intuitive control handoffs. - **Fleet & multi-agent:** Explore decentralized coordination for coverage, pursuit, and collaborative mapping with minimal comms. **What makes this internship different:** - **Real hardware cadence:** Prototype in sim, then flight test on production-ready aircraft and edge compute. Your work is meant to make a difference in the real world, not just in simulation. - **Safety-first learning:** We pair RL with formal constraints, estimation of uncertainty, and conservative action filters for dependable deployment in human environments. - **Cross-disciplinary mentorship:** Collaborate with perception, mapping, controls, and product teams to close the loop from research to field ops. **What makes you a strong fit:** - PhD student in Robotics, Machine Learning, Controls, or related field. - Strong fundamentals in **RL**, control theory, and motion planning; comfort with safety/robustness concepts. - Proficient in **Python** (PyTorch/JAX/Ray RLlib) and at least one of **C++** or CUDA. - Hands-on experience with **robotics simulation** (Isaac Lab/MuJoCo/PyBullet) and sim2real techniques. - Experience training/deploying policies for navigation, manipulation, or locomotion on real robots or autonomous vehicles. **Nice-to-Haves:** - Publications (CoRL, ICRA, IROS, RSS, NeurIPS). - Experience with onboard inference optimization (TensorRT, quantization, sparsity). - Familiarity with modern **policy learning** beyond vanilla RL: diffusion policies, IL/BC, offline RL, model-based RL. - Experience with multi-agent RL or distributed training. **Compensation:** The hourly rate for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Masters, and $70/hr for PhD students\*. ## **About Hiya** At Hiya, we’re making business calls more trusted, useful, and effective. Voice remains one of the most important ways businesses communicate with their customers, but the value of a call depends on trust. When customers do not recognize who is calling or why, important conversations are missed, customer relationships suffer, and business outcomes are harder to achieve. Hiya helps businesses create trusted calling experiences that benefit both sides of the conversation: enterprises can reach customers with confidence, and customers can answer with confidence. Our products support branded business calling, trusted caller identity, call performance insights, customer engagement, and voice security capabilities that help businesses strengthen relationships and improve outcomes. This role sits in a core business area for Hiya and is focused on helping SMB and enterprise customers succeed. ## **About the Role** The engineering intern position is for an individual contributor who is responsible for architecting, implementing, and maintaining significant systems that serve hundreds of millions of requests per month. Hiya provides high-availability, latency-sensitive capabilities to telecoms, mobile apps, and other partners. In addition, you'll work with engineering teams across Hiya, some in Seattle and some in Europe, to define and deliver shared components and services. From day one, you will be paired with a dedicated mentor who provides structured guidance, technical feedback, and ongoing career mentorship. ## **What You'll Do** Design, code, and operate high-performance services and data processing pipelines on a modern technology stack, supported by a structured technical crash course during your first two weeks covering our core tools, architecture, and repositories. Work at a supportive and fast-growing startup with a fantastic team, where you can collaborate with and learn from other great team members. Make an impact in the lives of hundreds of millions of consumers. Be supported in developing your skills and accelerating your career. ## **What We Are Looking For** - **Engineering:** CS majors - 2nd year (graduating 2028) - Excitement to work on innovative technology advancements - A philosophy of iteration and continuous improvement - Working knowledge of building services that adhere to operational SLAs - A preference for velocity over perfection - A commitment to respectful and impactful collaboration - Self-motivated and excited to learn about new technologies ## **Our Interview Process: The Hiya Voice AI Challenge** Once we’ve confirmed your eligibility, you’ll receive the Hiya Voice AI Challenge by email-- a chance to build a working prototype of a voice-driven product in one of five tracks: Accessibility, Productivity, Creative Voice, Security, or Real-Time Assistance. You’ll have one week to build it, with optional virtual office hours along the way if you’d like to pitch your idea and get steering from our team first. From there: - **Submit and get reviewed.** One of our engineers reviews your work. If we’d like to explore your project further, you’ll get a link to book a 30-minute virtual session with an engineer or two-- a quick demo, a walkthrough of your code, and some questions. - **Final interviews, in person at Hiya.** Candidates who advance join us for a final round in London (**2nd & 3rd of December)**: a debugging/fixing session, a chance to add a feature to your own project, and a conversation about Hiya’s values. AI tools are welcome and encouraged the whole way through. ## **What You Can Expect From Us** - Dedicated technical mentorship with structured, regular feedback check-ins - Clear project scope and goals provided right at the start of your internship - Comprehensive onboarding to get you up to speed on Hiya's tooling, codebases, and systems quickly - A supportive, collaborative environment built on psychological safety and genuine impact ## **How We Work** Hiya is not a passive environment. We expect people to take ownership, form opinions, and engage directly with hard problems. We work with a high degree of **transparency and autonomy**. Context is shared openly, and decisions are discussed, challenged, and then made. Once a call is made, we commit and move forward. You'll be expected to work through ambiguity, weigh tradeoffs, and take responsibility for results, while keeping a high bar for quality and customer trust. Every team member at Hiya is expected to live our core values: - Serve, our customers and partners by holding a high bar for trust and quality - Own, share in success and open up to failures - Lead, listen, show up with a point of view but commit entirely once a decision has been made - Improve, even if it means changing course or contradicting ourselves - Do, rather than observe ## **Come Work With Us!** We're building a team with diverse perspectives, identities, and professional experiences. We've been recognized by Built In, GeekWire, Comparably, G2, Forbes, and Deloitte Technology Fast 500 for our culture, innovation, leadership, compensation, and more. At Hiya, we're a people-centric company focused on helping each employee grow both personally and professionally. We create a culture of support and empowerment that challenges the status quo, resulting in an energized team that's passionate about their work. You'll love working here if you're looking for an innovative challenge that's disrupting an industry. Come join us! *Hiya is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to building an inclusive environment for all employees.*

role: Junior Structural Designer for industrial infrastructure (for projects in Switzerland)

In this position, you will have the opportunity to be mentored and trained by technical experts in the field of roadway transportation design. Working within our Design & Engineering teams, you'll create some of the world’s most iconic and ground-breaking structures and spaces that transform the world around us, from making journeys easier to opening public places that bring people together. role: Junior Engine Control System & Monitoring Engineer
description: Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity. ## About The Exploration Company At The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable orbital space vehicle that aims to eventually be refuelled in orbit, carrying cargo and potentially humans in the long run. The heart of a spacecraft lies in its engine, which is why we develop our own propulsion systems, aiming for the highest level of efficiency and reliability. ## Role Summary We are seeking a **Junior Engine Control System & Monitoring Engineer** to join the engine control and monitoring team of Storm, our high-thrust LOX/LCH4 cryogenic rocket engine. Working alongside senior control engineers, you will develop and test control and monitoring algorithms, work with the engine functional models provided by the functional team, contribute to setting up the controller development environment, and help verify the controller through Model-, Software- and Hardware-in-the-Loop testing and during engine test campaigns. This is an entry-level, hands-on role for a recent graduate with strong control fundamentals who wants to learn on real hardware and progressively grow into full ownership of safety-critical engine control functions. ## **Key responsibilities:** ### 1. Control & Monitoring Algorithm Development • Design and implement engine control and monitoring algorithms, following the software team's rules, guidelines and auto-coding practices. • Contribute to the definition of the engine regulation strategy (thrust and mixture ratio control, chill-down, start-up and shutdown transients) together with functional and system engineers. • Support the definition of control and monitoring requirements for engine subsystems (valves, pumps, sensors, controller, software). ### 2. Simulation & Controller Development Environment • Contribute to setting up the controller development environment: toolchain, model and code configuration management, auto-coding chain, and the MiL/SiL/HiL simulation and test infrastructure. • Integrate the engine functional models delivered by the functional team (turbopumps, valves, combustion devices, cryogenic feed lines; steady-state, transient and chill-down) into the control design and simulation environment, deriving simplified or linearised models for controller synthesis where needed. • Run closed-loop simulations to assess controller performance, stability margins and robustness to model uncertainties. • Feed test results back to the functional team to support model correlation, and flag model limitations that matter for control. ### 3. Health Monitoring & Fault Management • Contribute to the engine monitoring strategy that assesses the health status of the engine and its subsystems (combustion chamber, turbopumps, valves…). • Implement fault detection and sensor validation logic for both real-time protection and post-test analysis. • Support failure mode analyses (FMEA) and the management of failure modes, paving the way for engine reusability. ### 4. Validation, Testing & Documentation • Prepare and run Model-, Software- and Hardware-in-the-Loop (MiL, SiL, HiL) test campaigns to verify the control and monitoring functions at each step, from Simulink model to embedded code on target hardware. • Support Storm engine and component cryogenic (LOX/LCH4) test campaigns: test preparation, on-site support, data processing and post-test analysis. • Produce clear development documentation: specifications, test procedures, test reports and justification files. ## **What we would love to see from you:** • Master's degree (or equivalent) in Aerospace, Electrical, Control or Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline. • Recent graduate (or graduating within the next months); no professional experience required. A master's thesis, internship or academic project in control, propulsion or embedded systems is a strong plus. • Solid fundamentals in control theory, both classical and modern (state-space, robustness, digital control). • Practical use of MATLAB/Simulink and Python through coursework or projects; basic knowledge of C/C++. • Basic understanding of fluid dynamics and thermodynamics, and a strong interest in cryogenic propulsion and turbomachinery. • Fluent in English. ## Nice to Have: • Exposure to MiL/SiL/HiL testing or real-time embedded systems. • Experience with auto-coding from Simulink models. • Familiarity with safety-critical design practices, reliability engineering or failure mode analysis. • Interest or experience in data science applied to health monitoring and anomaly detection. • Knowledge of space standards (ECSS, MIL-STD, NASA-HBK…). • German and/or French. ## Skills & Behaviours: • Eagerness to learn and to take on increasing ownership under the guidance of senior engineers. • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to draw useful conclusions from partial or contradictory data. • Clear oral and written communication; comfortable working closely with engine, avionics, software and test teams. • Organised, able to prioritise tasks and deliver within time constraints. • Positive, flexible attitude and enthusiasm for space exploration. • Behaviour consistent with The Exploration Company's core values of Mission, Vision, Integrity, Excellence and Teamwork. **Why you should join us!** What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is: - We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind - We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them - We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge? We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly. *The Exploration Company is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability status. Relocation assistance is provided for those willing to relocate including visa sponsorship where applicable.* *All offers are contingent upon the successful completion of a background check, which will be subject to the country, role, and project you applied for. By submitting your application, you acknowledge and agree that any offer of employment may be conditional upon successful condition of this check. The Exploration Company partners with Zinc Work Limited located in the UK (Zinc), a third-party provider, to ensure this process as efficient and transparent as possible. If applicable, you will receive an email from Zinc upon acceptance of your offer with a link to a secure portal where you can provide the required information to Zinc.*

**About Sezzle:** With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with a wide range of flexible payment options designed to give customers more choice, accessibility, and a smarter overall experience. We're not just transforming payments; we're redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we're building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you're excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping! **About the Role:** We are seeking a curious, driven, and thoughtful Product Intern to join our Payments & Fees team. This role presents an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment within a growing team, with abundant prospects for career advancement. If you want to truly understand how fintech works, there's no better place to start than payments — and no better seat than product. The Payments & Fees team sits at the intersection of technology, data, and business, working with payment processors, payment method providers, and cross-functional partners across the company. As a product intern here, you won't be watching from the sidelines. You'll be in the room (or the channel) where decisions get made, picking up context fast and contributing to a team that moves quickly and takes its craft seriously. You'll support the product manager across a high-throughput environment: helping keep the backlog organized, digging into data to understand payment flows, and working alongside an efficient and technically sharp engineering team, as well as Design and Data teams. Product management is one of those rare roles where no two days look the same — you're constantly context-switching between technical conversations, business problems, and user needs, and that's exactly what makes it exciting. **What You'll Do:** **Ticket Management & Product Support** - Assist the product manager in drafting, organizing, and tracking tickets for changes and improvements to the payments service. Help ensure work is well-documented, properly prioritized, and moving through the backlog. Follow up on status and surface blockers when needed. **Context Gathering & Stakeholder Support** - Help the product manager stay on top of inputs from multiple stakeholders by gathering background context, summarizing key information, and preparing materials ahead of provider meetings. Respond to routine internal questions by pulling the right information from available resources. **Payment Workflow Analysis** - Learn and apply SQL to query payment data and support the creation and maintenance of dashboards that track payment performance, processing failures, and operational health. Help flag anomalies in payment flows and assist in assembling data for reviews and investigations. **Documentation & Process Tracking** - Maintain clear internal documentation for payment flows, fee structures, and operational processes. Help keep cross-functional teams aligned with concise, well-structured written updates. **Agile Meetings** - Participate in agile meetings and collaborate with engineering, operations, compliance, and support teams. One of the most valuable things a product manager does is serve as a bridge between tech and the business — translating technical challenges into clear language and business needs into actionable requirements. You'll get hands-on experience doing exactly that. **What We Look For:** - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Economics, Finance, or a related field - A genuine interest in payments, fintech, and how complex financial systems work under the hood - Natural curiosity and a logical mindset — you enjoy working through problems, aren't afraid to ask questions, and get satisfaction from figuring things out - Strong attention to detail — you notice when something's off and follow through until it's resolved - Comfort working with data and a willingness to learn SQL; prior experience is a plus but not required - Effective written and verbal communication — you can summarize a complex topic clearly and ask the right questions to fill in gaps - Prior experience in internships, projects, or extracurriculars related to product, fintech, data analysis, or startups is a plus — but we hire for potential, not just pedigree. - Demonstrated experience working with Claude or equivalent large language model tools is required; candidates must be comfortable leveraging AI to enhance productivity, research, and communication. **About You:** - You have relentlessly high standards — many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed. - You're not bound by convention — your success and much of the fun lies in developing new ways to do things. - You need action — speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking. - You earn trust — you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully. - You have backbone; disagree, then commit — you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly. - You deliver results — you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle. **What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome:** At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators. We believe in surrounding ourselves with only the best and the brightest individuals. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire. **Compensation**: The salary for the Product Intern is $800 USD Gross as an independent contractor. #Li-remote #Full-time

role: Stage(s) Learning & Development - Didactische innovatie & AI
description: Wil jij niet alleen leren hoe opleidingen worden ontwikkeld, maar ook onderzoeken hoe het beter kan? Heb je interesse in leren en ontwikkelen, didactiek, innovatie én de invloed van AI op onderwijs en toetsing? Dan hebben we binnen ons cluster Training & Advies een interessante stage voor je. Binnen The Safety Network werken Inprevo, Jonkman Opleidingen en Apply Opleidingen & Advies ieder vanuit hun eigen expertise aan hetzelfde doel: mensen leren om veiliger te werken. Van praktijkgerichte BHV- en veiligheidstrainingen tot logistieke opleidingen en meerjarige opleidingen voor veiligheidsprofessionals. We willen onze opleidingen en trainingen continu blijven ontwikkelen. Niet omdat iets nieuws per definitie beter is, maar omdat we willen weten wat écht werkt. Daar kunnen we jouw frisse blik en L&D-kennis goed bij gebruiken. Dit ga je doen Als stagiair Learning & Development werk je voor Inprevo, Jonkman Opleidingen en Apply Opleidingen & Advies. Je onderzoekt actuele ontwikkelingen binnen leren en ontwikkelen en vertaalt deze naar concrete verbeteringen in onze opleidingen. Je houdt je onder andere bezig met: onderzoeken welke actuele didactische inzichten relevant zijn voor onze opleidingen en trainingen; analyseren van bestaande trainingen, lesprogramma's, leermiddelen en toetsvormen; vertalen van theorie naar praktische en toepasbare verbeteringen; meedenken over activerende en praktijkgerichte werkvormen; onderzoeken hoe we kennis en vaardigheden beter kunnen laten beklijven, bijvoorbeeld door herhaling, scenario-based learning, blended learning en korte leerinterventies; ontwikkelen en testen van nieuwe werkvormen, formats of leermiddelen; meedenken over de rol van digitale leermiddelen en AI binnen onze opleidingen; in de praktijk meekijken bij trainingen en in gesprek gaan met trainers, docenten en deelnemers; pilots uitvoeren, resultaten ophalen en verbeteringen daadwerkelijk helpen implementeren. Je schrijft dus niet alleen een advies dat daarna ergens in een map verdwijnt. We willen samen met jou dingen uitproberen en kijken wat werkt. Een bijzonder vraagstuk: AI en toetsing Binnen Apply verzorgen we onder andere opleidingen voor veiligheidsprofessionals. De snelle ontwikkeling van generatieve AI roept daarbij nieuwe vragen op. Wat betekent AI bijvoorbeeld voor opdrachten, examens en andere vormen van toetsing? Wanneer mag een student AI gebruiken en wanneer niet? Hoe stel je vast of iemand de benodigde kennis en competenties daadwerkelijk zelf beheerst? En moeten we misschien andere manieren van toetsen gaan gebruiken? Je helpt ons onder andere bij het: onderzoeken van de invloed van AI op toetsing en examinering; inventariseren van mogelijkheden en risico's; ontwikkelen van uitgangspunten voor verantwoord gebruik van AI door studenten; nadenken over toetsvormen die ook in een wereld mét AI betrouwbaar en valide blijven; ontwikkelen van praktische handvatten voor docenten, beoordelaars en studenten. We zoeken daarbij nadrukkelijk niet alleen naar manieren om AI tegen te houden. We willen ook onderzoeken waar AI het leren juist kan versterken. Wat zou je aan het einde van je stage kunnen opleveren? Afhankelijk van jouw opleiding en interesses bepalen we samen de exacte opdracht. Denk bijvoorbeeld aan: een didactische scan van onze huidige opleidingen; concrete ontwerpprincipes voor onze trainingen en opleidingen; vernieuwde werkvormen of leerinterventies die je zelf hebt getest; aanbevelingen voor blended learning, herhaling en transfer naar de praktijk; een kader voor verantwoord gebruik van AI binnen onderwijs en toetsing; nieuwe of aangepaste toetsvormen voor Apply; Er is dus volop ruimte om hier een onderzoeks- of afstudeeropdracht aan te koppelen. Hier kom je terecht Je werkt binnen het cluster Training & Advies van The Safety Network en krijgt daarmee een bijzondere kans om bij drie verschillende opleiders mee te kijken. Inprevo richt zich sterk op praktijkgerichte en scenariobased veiligheids-, BHV- en EHBO-trainingen. Jonkman Opleidingen verzorgt onder andere logistieke, technische en veiligheidsopleidingen. Apply Opleidingen & Advies leidt professionals op binnen de arbeidsveiligheid. Die verschillen maken deze stage juist interessant. Wat werkt bij een eendaagse praktische training? Wat vraagt een opleiding die maanden duurt? Hoe zorg je dat iemand iets niet alleen tijdens de training begrijpt, maar het later op de werkvloer ook daadwerkelijk kan toepassen? Je werkt samen met trainers, docenten, opleidingskundigen, inhoudelijke specialisten en managers. Daarbij krijg je veel ruimte om vragen te stellen, kritisch te zijn en met nieuwe ideeën te komen. Dit neem je mee Je volgt een hbo- of wo-opleiding op het gebied van Onderwijskunde, Learning & Development, HRD, Toegepaste Psychologie of een vergelijkbare richting. je bent nieuwsgierig naar hoe mensen leren en hoe je dat leren effectiever kunt ontwerpen. je vindt het leuk om onderzoek te combineren met de praktijk. je hebt interesse in nieuwe technologie en de invloed van AI op leren en toetsen. je kunt zelfstandig werken, maar zoekt ook actief de samenwerking op. je durft bestaande werkwijzen ter discussie te stellen als je denkt dat het beter kan. je kunt complexe theorie vertalen naar iets waar een trainer of docent morgen mee aan de slag kan. je bent gedurende je stage ingeschreven bij een onderwijsinstelling. Je hoeft nog geen expert te zijn in veiligheidsopleidingen. Juist jouw kennis van leren en ontwikkelen is wat je bij ons komt toevoegen. Dit bieden wij jou een inhoudelijke stage waarin je daadwerkelijk invloed hebt op hoe we onze opleidingen verder ontwikkelen. een stageplek voor 32 tot 40 uur per week en een periode van ongeveer 4 tot 6 maanden; ruimte voor een onderzoeks- of afstudeeropdracht; begeleiding vanuit het cluster Training & Advies; toegang tot verschillende soorten opleidingen, trainers, docenten en deelnemers; de mogelijkheid om ideeën direct in de praktijk te testen; hybride werken en de mogelijkheid om op verschillende locaties binnen The Safety Network mee te kijken; een stagevergoeding conform onze stageregeling; Veel vrijheid om zelf richting te geven aan jouw onderzoek en ontwikkeling. Waarom deze stage anders is Je loopt geen stage op één opleidingsafdeling met één type onderwijs. Je krijgt te maken met korte trainingen, praktijkonderwijs, vaardigheidstrainingen én langere beroepsopleidingen. Daarmee kun je didactische theorie direct toetsen aan verschillende leeromgevingen. En minstens zo belangrijk: wat jij bedenkt, willen we ook echt gaan gebruiken. Interesse? Wil jij met ons onderzoeken hoe leren, trainen en toetsen er de komende jaren uit moeten zien? Dan maken we graag kennis met je. Vertel ons vooral waar jij nieuwsgierig naar bent binnen Learning & Development en welk vraagstuk jij tijdens je stage graag zou willen aanpakken.

role: SOC Analyst Internship Program - LSU Students Only
description: Have you thought about a career in cybersecurity? Ever daydreamed about sleuth-level mastery the likes of Charlotte Justice, Easy Rawlins, or Veronica Mars... or perhaps captivated by the show Mr. Robot, national news like the Log4Shell Zero-Day vulnerability and major ransomware incidents, or the topic of election security? Our Security Operations Center (SOC) Analyst internship may be for you! Let’s face it - **Finding hands-on opportunities to learn about cybersecurity can be tough, and there isn’t one set path into this field.** The industry needs organizations that are willing and able to train and equip the next generation of cybersecurity leaders, to secure our organizations, businesses, and nation. There is an imperative to break the mold of who is typically considered a cybersecurity professional, and it takes more than technical ability to succeed. With that in mind, we see the cybersecurity skills gap as an opportunity and are eager to be an on-ramp for those who want to learn and find a pathway into the constantly evolving, challenging world of online security. Sure, our team has plenty of people with traditional IT-related backgrounds, but we also have team members who have crossed into cybersecurity from completely unrelated fields ranging from Education to Emergency Medical Technicians. We believe that having technically competent analysts with diversity of thought, culture, and experiences not only creates a better world but also fosters a more inclusive work environment. This gives us a competitive advantage to better protect our range of clients with the ability to consider threats from more diverse perspectives. SOC analysts are the first line of defense for any of C3’s clients. Analysts have the critical responsibility to initially triage and make key decisions about how to identify, investigate, and address potentially malicious activity in a client’s network. This internship is designed to give students and aspiring cybersecurity professionals an opportunity to gain real-world experience working within a SOC, providing exposure to the technology, data, processes, and expectations that accompany a SOC analyst role. Guided coaching, paired with independently driven, hands-on activities will help you develop vital technical skills as well as soft skills. The internship offers ambitious students an opportunity to move from theoretical knowledge to practical experience. Intrigued? Awesome! Here’s what you need to know about us: Our SOC began as a homegrown Louisiana-based company, focused on establishing Louisiana as a cybersecurity center of excellence. That means being the best at what we do so that we can bring 5,000 industry jobs to the state of “Union, Justice, and Confidence”. We would love to provide this internship opportunity to a student or resident of the state. *As such, this cohort is only accepting applicants who are or will be enrolled in a Computer Science or Cybersecurity focused degree program within the **LSU System Schools in January 2027*** **C3's Core Values:** - **Team Human**: Respecting all humans is a critical part of who we are at C3. We practice integrity in all interactions, we empathize with others, we create a supportive work environment, and we support the communities in which we live and operate. - **Security First**: At the cornerstone of our business, we prioritize security above convenience, cost or efficiency. A “security-first” approach means we practice what we preach and we lead by example for our clients. - **Be an Advocate**: We are passionate in our advocacy for our customer’s success and a path to the best solution for their business. We embrace feedback, put ourselves in your shoes and advocate for your interests as our own. - **Embrace Change**: It's a practical necessity in an industry that never stands still. As a new entity born from the merger of two top-ranked CMMC-focused IT services companies, we're keenly aware that our success hinges on our ability to adapt - whether that means integrating new platforms, refining processes, or keeping pace with changing guidelines. - **Resilience**: Our ability to withstand adversity and accomplish objectives while maintaining professionalism and discipline is critical to successful crisis management and risk avoidance. **Internship Selection Process** **Phase I - Application** (until Nov 14) Applicants complete Internship applications. The C3 SOC Leadership Team will review and screen applicants and select candidates for Phase II. **Phase II - Assessment** Assessments will be assigned to candidates selected for Phase II. The C3 SOC Leadership Team will review Assessment results and select candidates for Phase III. **Phase III - Interview** Phase III candidates will be scheduled for a (virtual) interview with the Internship Panel. The Internship Panel and the C3 SOC Leadership Team will select Interns and Intern Alternates. **Responsibilities** As part of our Security Operations Center (SOC) team of analysts who actively monitor security alerts, perform threat hunting, and escalate tickets in order to manage potential threats/risks within our client environments, responsibilities include: - Complete the C3 SOC Analyst training program - Learn the basics of Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR), threat detection, and cybersecurity incident response (IR) - Monitor, detect and respond to security events from reviewing logs and alerts, and provide support when analysis confirms actionable incidents - Conduct network forensics, log analysis, and malware triage in support of threat hunting and investigations - Assist with auditing client security tool policies and configurations - Assist in projects to streamline, improve and create required operational tools, rule sets, processes, and documentation related to SOC workflows. - Assist in testing, analyzing, and evaluating existing or proposed SOC team tools, utilities, systems, and processes - Perform threat intelligence research with newly identified threats and vulnerabilities - Develop, document, and correlate recommendations for cybersecurity incidents and alert tickets **Basic Qualifications** - ***Enrolled in a relevant IT/Cybersecurity degree program in LSU or LSU satellite campus***. - Basic understanding of networks and technical environments, including conceptual knowledge of administering, defending, and analyzing servers or workstations - Experience working with Operating Systems (Windows, macOS, or Linux) - Basic analytical, problem-solving, time management, organizational, and project management skills - Effective verbal and written communication skills - Ability to work in a collaborative team environment, multitask, and prioritize during high-stakes security situations - Comfortable using and/or learning tools such as Teams and Office - Ability to follow defined processes and procedures, work independently and make decisions with minimal direction **Advanced Qualifications** For students further along in their IT/Information Security studies or individuals who have decided to pursue a career in cyber and have work experience or completed self-study training via platforms such as LetsDefend, TryHackMe, Hack The Box, RangeForce, Udemy, Cybrary, Coursera, etc.). - Experience with security tools in a work or lab\* environment (lab = academic lab or home lab set up with servers, big data, and security tools set up to conduct tasks specific to analysis and triage of security data and events) - If you meet these advanced qualifications, we might even have a job for you so definitely reach out! **Schedule:** 16-38 hrs/wk **Compensation:**$11 - $14 hourly, depending on experience. We will work with your academic institution if they offer academic credit. **Internship Length:** January 11, 2027 – May 14, 2027. **Location:** Remote (Louisiana) *C3 Integrated Solutions is an Equal Opportunity Employer encouraging diversity in the workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, gender identity/expression, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, genetics, veteran status, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by law.* *This is a general description of the duties, responsibilities and qualifications required for this position. Physical, mental, sensory, or environmental demands may be referenced to communicate the way this position traditionally is performed. Whenever necessary to provide individuals with disabilities an equal employment opportunity, C3 Integrated Solutions will consider reasonable accommodations that might involve varying job requirements and/or changing the way this job is performed, provided that such accommodations do not pose an undue hardship.*

Zorg voor stabiele netwerken en robuuste security. Als Network & Security Engineer bij AXI zorg je ervoor dat de IT-infrastructuur van onze klanten optimaal en veilig blijft draaien. Ons doel? To get IT right! We bouwen aan de IT-infrastructuur die organisaties en mensen helpt om het beste van zichzelf te geven en sneller hun doelstellingen te bereiken. Je komt terecht in ons gedreven Network & Security Team. Dit team is onderdeel van onze IT Services organisatie en is verantwoordelijk voor het ontwerpen, implementeren, beveiligen en proactief beheren van complexe netwerkomgevingen voor uiteenlopende klanten. Hoe ziet succes eruit? Als Network & Security Engineer los je het probleem op van kwetsbare netwerken, netwerkstoringen en geavanceerde beveiligingsdreigingen waar organisaties dagelijks mee te maken krijgen. Dit brengt operationele continuïteit, maximale digitale veiligheid en gemoedsrust op voor onze klanten. Je doet dit door: Het configureren, implementeren en optimaliseren van LAN, WAN, WLAN en firewall-oplossingen. Het bieden van first- en secondlinesupport via onze service desk. **2027 – Internship, Technology** **Programmes offered:** Final-year internship, penultimate-year internship **Location:** New York, Chicago **Programme duration:** 10-week summer internship **Who qualifies:** Penultimate or final-year students completing a bachelor’s or master’s degree Qube Research & Technologies (QRT) is a global quantitative and systematic investment manager operating across liquid asset classes and markets worldwide. Our approach to investing is scientific: we bring together data, research, technology and trading expertise to develop and run systematic strategies. Technology is central to how QRT works. Over the years, we have built a global research and execution platform spanning geographies, asset classes and trading horizons, from ultra-low-latency systems to large-scale research, analytics and risk infrastructure. We invest heavily in engineering, automation and scalable systems because better technology allows us to test ideas faster, operate more reliably and tackle harder problems. Our internships are designed to give students meaningful experience of that work. You’ll join a team, contribute to real projects and learn from engineers, researchers and traders working on live problems. The environment is technical, collaborative and demanding, with plenty of scope to ask questions, test ideas and take ownership. Strong performance during the internship may lead to consideration for a full-time graduate role. **Your future role at QRT** As a Technology Intern, you’ll help build the systems, platforms and tools behind QRT’s research, trading and investment activities. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers, quantitative developers, researchers and traders, contributing to production technology and solving problems where performance, reliability and good engineering judgement matter. Depending on your interests and strengths, you may join one of four Technology disciplines. ### **Software Engineer (New York)** Build the technology behind QRT’s trading and investment activities, from ultra-low-latency execution systems to global platforms for analytics, risk management and reporting. Our engineers connect the firm to markets, brokers and data providers, developing systems that process large volumes of data reliably. You’ll work with experienced engineers, quantitative developers and researchers on a defined technical problem, making considered engineering choices and building something useful. Projects may include AI-powered static analysis, exchange simulator development, risk data platforms or trading interfaces. ### **FPGA Engineer (New York, Chicago)** Develop ultra-low-latency hardware that processes market data and executes orders. Working at the boundary between hardware and software, the FPGA team builds systems where small design decisions can have a measurable impact on latency, throughput and reliability. You’ll use SystemVerilog, C++ and Python to help design, test and integrate FPGA systems into our trading infrastructure. Alongside experienced engineers, you’ll develop new functionality, verify system behaviour and investigate performance improvements, gaining practical experience with the hardware and development tools used in live trading. ### **Security Engineer (New York)** Help protect the systems, data and infrastructure behind QRT’s global research and trading activities. Our Security team works closely with Cloud, Infrastructure and Network Operations to understand system behaviour, identify weaknesses and build practical ways to prevent, detect and respond to threats. You’ll contribute to security engineering, investigations and automation alongside experienced colleagues. Projects may include building agents to support cyber-security investigations, reproducing emerging attack techniques in isolated environments, researching vulnerabilities or developing tools that make security assurance more scalable and effective. ### **Infrastructure Engineer (New York)** Work on the on-premise hardware and operating systems behind QRT’s production trading environment. The Infrastructure team measures and optimises hardware performance, investigates Linux internals and tunes systems where small changes can make a meaningful difference to trading technology. Alongside experienced engineers, you’ll develop a detailed understanding of how hardware and software interact. Your work may involve investigating performance constraints, testing system configurations and assessing improvements to reliability. You’ll learn to use evidence and careful analysis to make production systems faster, more stable and more predictable. **Your current skillset** - Eligibility: Penultimate or final-year students pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s in a STEM discipline, such as Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics or a related Engineering or Security subject, on track for a 2:1 or above from a leading institution. - Interest in technology: You enjoy solving technical problems and are curious about how systems work. You’re interested in building things, not just studying them. - Software engineering experience: We value hands-on experience wherever you gained it — through personal projects, open-source contributions, hobbies, internships or academic work. - Interest in Software Engineering, Security, Infrastructure or FPGAs. - Programming: Proficiency in C++, C# or Python, Systems Verilog - Tools: Familiarity with scripting languages such as Python or Bash, and tools and technologies including Git, SQL, GCC and Linux. - Mindset: Curious, proactive and comfortable asking questions. You look for ways to make systems simpler, faster or more reliable and can turn those observations into practical improvements. - Approach: Self-motivated, thoughtful and comfortable taking ownership of a problem. **Interviewing** - **Application** – Submit your application online. We review applications on a rolling basis, so applying early is recommended. - **Technical Assessment** – Selected candidates will complete a coding challenge focused on core programming and problem-solving skills. - **Interviews** – Shortlisted candidates will take part in interviews, either on-site at an assessment centre or via Microsoft Teams. We’ll explore your technical thinking, how you approach unfamiliar problems and how you work with others. At QRT, interns join a team from day one, working on real problems alongside experienced colleagues. You’ll contribute to meaningful projects, learn by doing and have the support to ask questions, explore ideas and develop your skills throughout the programme. The annualised base salary for these US positions is $178,000, prorated to reflect the duration of the internship. Interns also receive a signing bonus and a competitive benefits package, including healthcare coverage, access to a 401(k) plan, and breakfast and lunch. Beyond the work, there’s plenty happening in the office, from gym sessions and board game nights to team socials and opportunities to get to know colleagues across QRT. *QRT is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome diversity as essential to our success. QRT empowers employees to work openly and respectfully to achieve collective success. In addition to professional achievement, we are offering initiatives and programs to enable employees achieve a healthy work-life balance.*

Wage: Level 1 Position Purpose: Dryer Feeder will keep the veneer dryer at least 97% full of quality veneer while maintaining safety and quality by feeding sheets into the dryer. The worker will feed while moving back and forth on a platform in front of different sized stacks of green veneer. Feeder will keep up with the pace of the dryer, while maintaining safety and quality standards as outlined in the Job Hazard Analysis, Standard Operating Procedures, and other requirements as directed by the supervisor for the safe and efficient operation of the plant. Position Functions: Dryer Feeder: Essential Functions* These duties are designated as ADA Essential Functions and must be performed in this job. The worker is responsible for reaching forward, picking up individual sheets of veneer with one or both hands, and moving them forward several inches so that they can be picked up by the rollers of the veneer dryer equipment. Movement back and forth on a platform as necessary, pushing sheets forward and properly aligning them to the receiving end of the dryer. Feeder will remove overlaps, ensure all fed sheets are unstacked, and discarding wane sheets as necessary. Feeder must ensure dryer is full of veneer sheets and fed timely with each dryer cycle, according to supervisor expectations and production needs. The worker will be responsible, through a series of pedals and buttons, for moving green veneer onto a scissors platform and maintaining the proper height at that platform at a comfortable waist/chest level. At times, the machine will jam or plug up which will at times require the worker to remove or assist in removing the blockage. Both human and mechanical assistance will be available upon request, should the worker be unable to perform this activity alone. Proper Lock-out-tag-out procedures must be performed. Worker must use and understand dryers’ manual button operating system for power control.
