👋 Thanks for stopping by and learning more about this role at Sitemate! ✨🏗️ We'd love to hear from you 😊 👩‍💻👩🏽‍💻🧑🏿‍💻👨🏻‍💻 ## 📝 Overview **Build What Matters** The Full Stack Engineer is an ownership role responsible for product outcomes end-to-end: from shaping technical approaches and building features through to release, reliability, and production performance. At Sitemate, engineers combine strong technical craft with product thinking and delivery ownership. You'll work in small, high-trust teams alongside Product Design Managers to define problems, shape solutions, implement clean and scalable systems, and take responsibility for what ships — including how it behaves once live. Engineering, product, and delivery are not separate handoffs here; they operate as one integrated team. We believe the future of product development in an AI-accelerated world belongs to engineers who can think beyond tickets - they own outcomes and deliver at speed with AI. ## **Employment:** - Full-time - Based: Sydney, Australia or Melbourne, Australia - Remuneration (Including Super): AUD $85,000 - $115,000 pending your experience ## **About Sitemate** Sitemate builds best-in-class software and AI agents for the built world, helping construction, infrastructure and industrial companies work smarter and faster. Our mission is to multiply the engineering power of the built world. Storm is the #1 data capture agent for the front line of the built world - converting audio, photos and videos into clean structured records. With conversational support in-app and across SMS, Whatsapp and phone calls, Storm is shifting front line workers from paperwork and clunky digital forms, to natural language and multi-channel data capture. Our core platforms are Dashpivot (safety, quality and field reporting), Gearbelt (fleet and asset management), Flowsite (no-code integrations), and the Sitemate mobile app for every worker on site. We have strong product-market fit, generating thousands of new leads per month through word of mouth and organic channels. We are backed by Blackbird, with 200 people across 18+ countries and entities in Australia, the UK, the US and Canada. ## **Why Join Sitemate** At Sitemate, you’ll join a global team that values transparency, high velocity, hustle, diversity, and innovation. We’re open about our metrics, honest about challenges, and obsessed with improving how the world’s most important industries operate. Our environment is flexible, fast-moving, and outcome-driven - designed to help you do the best work of your career. You’ll be surrounded by people who take pride in their work, care deeply about results, and believe that great culture is built on trust, respect, and continuous learning. ## **How We Work** - **Transparency at every level:** Monthly Allhands meetings share key company metrics, updates, and customer stories. We also spotlight a team member’s “Life Story” each month - it’s one of the ways we stay connected as a global team. - **High velocity, low friction:** Our systems are modern and fully integrated, so you’ll spend your time solving problems - not fighting tools. - **Performance-driven growth:** Seven of our last ten pay increases were made proactively, based on impact and results. - **True flexibility:** We focus on outcomes, not hours. You’ll have autonomy to manage your time and work where you perform best - with no time monitoring or unnecessary meetings. - **Collaboration:** You’ll work closely with other teams - engineering, product, design, marketing, and customer success - to move fast and deliver meaningful results. - **Sydney HQ perks** - rooftop garden, wellness centre, showers, and cycle storage in Haymarket - **Melbourne office perks** - micro-roasted coffee bar, on-site parking & bike storage, wellness & mothers rooms, opposite Southern Cross station ## **What We Offer** - **Competitive, performance-based remuneration** - **Equity options** - own a piece of what you’re helping to build - **20 days of paid annual leave**, plus sick, carer’s, and compassionate leave - **Paid parental leave** - 16 weeks for primary carers, 6 weeks for secondary carers (including adoption and stillbirth support) - **Professional growth budget** and a transparent career development framework - **Laptop and home-office setup budget** - **Flexible work** - remote or hybrid, plus the ability to work from anywhere for a few weeks each year - **Community & connection** - weekly team lunches, global offsites, and our signature “Life Story” sessions ## **Diversity & Inclusion** We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer. Sitemate welcomes people of all genders, ethnicities, ages, sexualities, and abilities. 55% of our team identify as coming from underrepresented ethnic backgrounds, 43% identify as female, and our team spans ages 22–51. We believe our diversity makes us stronger - and we’re committed to creating an environment where everyone can do their best work. ## **Learn More About Sitemate** 🎧 **Podcasts** - [2026: CRO Lance Hodgson - on why the built world is jumping straight to AI and what that changes](https://open.spotify.com/episode/3FmGd8G95ZfGBfv3XIdU5x?si=910a9dc029234378&nd=1&dlsi=36f922f07fb44516) - [2024: CEO Hartley Pike - on scaling Sitemate, diversity, and culture](https://open.spotify.com/episode/2dC9gsDQRH8IKBgylSZisV) - [2022: CTO Tim Bray - on building quality features that solve real customer problems](https://open.spotify.com/episode/7geTCUHFxZUKZ8Yrae4iR7) 💬 **Want to know what it’s like to work at Sitemate? Hear it straight from the team**: [People of Sitemate](https://sitemate.com/au/resources/careers/people-of-sitemate/) ⭐ **Read what our customers say:** [G2 Crowd](https://www.g2.com/products/dashpivot/reviews), [Trust Radius](https://www.trustradius.com/products/dashpivot-by-sitemate/reviews?o=recent) 🎥 **Team Offsites:** [2022](https://sitemate.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/HOR/pages/3087761409/Job+Listing+v2+Draft#), [2023](https://sitemate.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/HOR/pages/3087761409/Job+Listing+v2+Draft#), [2024](https://sitemate.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/HOR/pages/3087761409/Job+Listing+v2+Draft#), [2025](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NyAzozsK0zg) ## **🔧 What this role looks like at the junior level** You'll join a team attached to one of our products and learn by shipping. Senior engineers will pair with you, review your work, and invest in your growth - but you'll have real ownership from early on. You'll work across frontend, backend, and mobile: TypeScript, React, Node.js, Angular, MongoDB, and AWS. You don't need to know all of these, willingness to learn matters more than what you know today. **Two things make engineering different here:** - You'll develop a product mindset. Instead of just working through tickets, you'll start understanding why features matter to customers. Engineers here are closer to the problem than at most companies; your work has context and meaning from day one. - You'll build with AI from the start. We're moving toward agentic engineering where engineers define what to build and orchestrate AI agents to construct it. As a junior here, you'll develop AI-first habits that most engineers won't learn for years. ## **🔧 Day-to-Day** - Build and ship features with guidance from experienced teammates. - Work with AI tools daily, with the team's workflow skills for planning, implementation and review. - Fix bugs and improve product stability across web and mobile. - Investigate and resolve production issues. - Grow into more ownership over time, this role expands as you do. ## **✨ What's in it for you** - **Structured development from day one.** Every engineer gets a Sitemate Development Plan (SDP), quarterly reviews, and access to an L&D budget. You'll know exactly what growth looks like. - **AI engineering skills that put you ahead.** You'll learn agentic engineering practices now, building a forward looking skillset. - **Real impact from week one.** Your code powers wind farms, railways, highways, and mining operations in 100+ countries. You'll see the results of your work, not just a JIRA ticket number. - **Equity ownership.** ESOP participation on a standard vesting schedule, you own a piece of what you help build. - **Hybrid and flexible.** Sydney or Melbourne-based - **A team that actually supports you.** Intellect mental health platform, and a culture where Handle with Care is a real operating value. ## **⚡ Challenges** - Our products seem simple to users but contain a high degree of technical complexity — shared components across multiple products, backend services powering web and mobile clients. There's a lot to learn. - Pace: we move quickly, so you'll need to be excited to learn fast. - We have a strong culture based on core values and operating principles. You may need to unlearn some habits from previous experience. ## **✅ Who This Role is For** - You've built things you're proud of at a startup, in a side project, during a bootcamp, or at university. - You're deeply curious about AI-powered development and want to learn agentic engineering in a production environment. - You want to understand the customer problem, not just the code. - You're energised by learning fast in a supportive, high-tempo environment. - You want to be part of building something meaningful — our users build real infrastructure that shapes communities. ## **🚫 Who This Role is** ***Not*** **For** - You prefer a slow ramp with months of onboarding before touching production code — here you'll ship early, with support. - You're not interested in owning the end-to-end delivery of features. - You're not interested in AI-first engineering practices, this is core to how we work, not optional. ## **🎯 Skills & Tools** **Must Have:** - Curiosity, drive, and willingness to learn - Some experience building software (startup, bootcamp, university, side project) - Hands on experience with AI-powered developer tools and agentic engineering practices. - Product mindset — wants to understand customer problems, not just implement tickets **Nice to Have:** - TypeScript, React, Node.js, Angular, MongoDB, or AWS experience - Mobile development experience - Experience working in a fast-paced startup or product environment **Essential Tools:** - AI Coding Tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) - TypeScript / JavaScript - React or Angular - Node.js **Bonus Tools:** - MongoDB - AWS - React Native / mobile ***PLEASE Note:*** - ***We hire directly and don’t work with agencies***

role: Career Education and Co-op Program Coordinator, College of Engineering
description: Summary: The career education and co-op programming coordinator oversees the centre and leads the development, evaluation, revision, and delivery of co-operative program courses and career-related materials. This role coordinates co-operative education and experiential learning programs while supporting the creation and accreditation of new initiatives, including a master’s co-op program. It establishes and delivers career advising services and opportunities for undergraduate and graduate engineering students. This position collaborates with academic leaders, faculty, industry partners, and external stakeholders to align programming with strategic priorities and labour market demands. It contributes to student outreach, engagement, and success within a high-volume, student-centered environment. This role also monitors program outcomes and adapts programming to meet evolving institutional and industry needs. Duties and Responsibilities: Develops and submits proposals for new co-operative education programs, including policies, procedures, and resource plans. Secures accreditation for co-operative education programs through relevant governing bodies. Designs and leads the creation, revision, and delivery of co-operative courses and career programming. Integrates equity, diversity, and inclusion principles into program design and delivery. Oversees and operates the centre, including programming, budgeting, and reporting. Establishes and coordinates experiential learning and work-integrated learning initiatives. Identifies labour market trends and incorporates industry needs into program improvements. Builds partnerships with faculty, industry, and external organizations for program delivery and engagement. Supervises teaching assistants, including hiring, training, assigning duties, and evaluating performance. Develops and delivers workshops, sessions, and instructional materials for students. Coordinates course delivery activities, including content preparation, grading systems, and learning platforms. Provides one-on-one career advising and supports students in developing career plans and opportunities. Conducts program evaluations and analyzes data to inform continuous improvement. Liaises with academic teams and stakeholders to support program integration and collaboration. Monitors budgets and allocates resources to support programming and operations. Maintains and updates co-operative program content and career-related resources. Supports accreditation and reporting requirements related to professional engineering organizations. Oversees outreach, engagement, and student-focused initiatives within the college. Communicates and acts in a respectful and professional manner, collaborates effectively, abides by policy, and contributes to a positive and productive work and learning environment. Qualifications: A bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related field. Registration or eligibility to register as a Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) with the Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of Saskatchewan (APEGS) is preferred. Minimum of five years of experience in teaching, instructional support, or engineering education. Experience supervising and training teaching assistants and working with students in academic or career-focused settings. Experience with e-learning technologies and online course delivery, as well as managing work-integrated learning or experiential programs are assets. Familiarity with engineering-related technologies and learning systems. Familiarity with engineering academic programs and university environments is an asset. Ability to support engineering students with career development and employment opportunities. Strong interpersonal and communication skills. Ability to plan, maintain, and prioritize multiple projects and budgets. Effective judgment, professionalism, discretion, and confidentiality practices. Ability to conduct research, analyze data, and interpret labour market trends. Strong organizational skills with high attention to detail. Ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively in a team. Proficient computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications and media tools such as Adobe Premiere Pro.

Spirax Group, formerly Spirax-Sarco Engineering, is a global thermal energy and fluid technology solutions Group that supports industrial customers in transitioning to net zero. The Group designs technologies that improve the efficiency and safety of critical industrial processes behind everyday consumables, while delivering new decarbonisation solutions that electrify boilers and other process heating applications. Spirax Group consists of three world-leading businesses: Steam Thermal Solutions (including Spirax Sarco and Gestra), Electric Thermal Solutions, and Watson-Marlow Fluid Technology Solutions, all focused on resource efficiency and advancements in global health. Headquartered in Cheltenham, UK, Spirax Group is a FTSE 100 company with 37 manufacturing plants, approximately 10,000 colleagues in 66 countries, and 110,000 customers worldwide. About the role We are looking for a Junior Developer to join the team building the cloud platform behind our connected industrial products, a production industrial-IoT system that ingests telemetry from tens of thousands of sensors in customer plants, decodes and enriches it, runs engineering calculations over the resulting time series, and serves the results to internal engineering teams and to customers. This is a role for someone with roughly two to three years of commercial development experience who wants to go deeper. You will be writing production code within your first few weeks, but you will not be doing it alone: you will pair with senior engineers, your work will go through review, and you will be given a route into the codebase rather than a sink-or-swim start. We care more about how you think than about how many technologies you have already used. The platform runs on a broad stack, set out below, and we do not expect you to arrive knowing all of it. If you are solid in one or two of those areas and genuinely keen to learn the rest, we would like to hear from you. What you will be doing Build and maintain backend features in C# / .NET or TypeScript, following the patterns already established in the codebase, with tests written alongside the code. Work on the front end: React and TypeScript components and screens, taking a ticket or a design through to a merged pull request. Help develop the data pipelines that decode device telemetry and compute engineering values, starting with well-scoped changes and growing into larger pieces of work. Write and run automated tests, and treat a failing test as useful information rather than an obstacle. Take part in code review, as an author and as a reviewer. Reading other people’s code is the fastest way to learn a platform this size. Deploy your own work through our CI/CD pipelines, and build up an understanding of how the environments and infrastructure fit together. Investigate and fix defects in the running platform, with a senior engineer alongside you at first and increasingly on your own. Contribute in design discussions and stand-ups: ask the question you think might be obvious, because it usually is not. Keep the documentation honest as you change things, so the next person does not have to rediscover what you worked out. What we are looking for Around two to three years of commercial software development experience, or a comparable track record through an apprenticeship, a placement year, a bootcamp followed by real delivery, or substantial open-source work. A solid grounding in at least one modern language, ideally C# or TypeScript. Others count: if you have written good Java, Go or Python, the move across is very manageable. A working understanding of how a web application fits together: HTTP, REST APIs, JSON, and a database of some kind. Comfort with Git and a pull-request workflow. Some experience of writing automated tests, and a clear sense of why they matter. Clear written communication and the confidence to say when you are stuck. On a remote team this counts for more than it would in an office. A genuine appetite for cloud engineering. You do not need Azure experience; you do need to want it. The technology you will work with This is the stack the platform actually runs on, so you can see what you would be working with and learning. It is not a checklist you need to tick. We expect someone at this level to have used only a small part of it. Experience with any of it is welcome, none of it is essential, and we will teach you the rest. Backend and API development Technology Where it fits C# Our primary backend language .NET 8 The framework the backend services are built on Core 8 The REST APIs that serve the front end Node.js Services and tooling on the ingest side of the platform Python Data processing, analysis and integration scripts Cloud and Azure services Technology Where it fits Azure Functions Serverless compute: most ingest and background work runs here Azure Cosmos DB The document database holding equipment and configuration data Azure Data Explorer (ADX) The time-series store holding sensor history, queried with KQL Azure Event Hubs The event stream that carries telemetry through the platform Azure Stream Analytics (ASA) Streaming queries that decode and transform telemetry in flight Azure API Management (APIM) The gateway that sits in front of our APIs Azure Front Door (AFD) Global routing and TLS at the platform edge Infrastructure as code and DevOps Technology Where it fits Terraform Infrastructure as code for part of the Azure estate Bicep Azure-native infrastructure as code for the rest of it CI/CD pipelines How every change reaches an environment Azure DevOps Repos, Pipelines, Boards and Artifacts: our day-to-day tooling Frontend development Technology Where it fits TypeScript Used across the front end and parts of the backend React 18 The engineer-facing single-page application Vite The build and local development tooling for that application Nice to have None of these are required. Any of them would give us something to talk about. Exposure to a cloud platform, Azure, AWS or Google Cloud. A personal project counts. Experience with React, or another modern component framework. Curiosity about data and query languages: SQL, KQL or similar. Docker or containers, even at a hobby level. An interest in industrial engineering, energy or sustainability. A degree in computing, engineering, physics or mathematics, though we do not require one. About you Curious. You want to know why the code does what it does, not only that it works. Honest about what you do not know. Asking early is a strength on this team, not a weakness. Careful. You test your own work before you ask someone else to look at it. Coachable. You take code review as a gift, act on the feedback, and carry it forward. Communicative. Remote work rewards people who write clearly and post progress without being chased for it. Interested in the real world behind the data: the steam trap, the pump, the process that the numbers came from. Support and development We are hiring at this level deliberately, and we plan to invest accordingly. A named mentor from your first day, plus regular one-to-ones with your line manager. Pairing and code review with senior engineers as a normal part of the week, not a favour you have to ask for. Onboarding material written for newcomers, including an internal guide to how the platform fits together. Time and budget for learning: Microsoft certifications, courses and conferences. A written progression path towards Developer and Senior Developer, with the expectations for each level set out rather than implied. Work chosen to stretch you on purpose, starting well-scoped and growing as you settle in. How we work Remote-first, UK-based. The team works remotely across the UK, with occasional travel to Cheltenham or another Group site for planning, team events and customer workshops. Agile delivery in short iterations, with product owners and solution architects embedded in the team. Quality gates in the pipeline, not in a handover: automated tests, static analysis and build-enforced standards. Infrastructure as code by default. Environments are described in Terraform and Bicep and deployed through Azure DevOps. Documentation as part of the work, not a phase at the end of it. No blame when something breaks. We fix the system that allowed it, not the person who triggered it. Why join us You would work on a platform with a direct line to decarbonisation: the telemetry and calculations we build help industrial customers find steam leaks, cut fuel use and reduce emissions across thousands of sites. For someone early in their career it is an unusually good combination, a modern Azure estate with real scale and real customers, inside a stable FTSE 100 engineering group, on a team small enough that your work is visible and your questions get answered. Diversity, equity and inclusion Spirax Group is an equal-opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender identity, marital or civil-partnership status, pregnancy or parental status, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation. If you need an adjustment at any stage of the recruitment process, please tell us and we will make it. If you meet most of what is described above but not all of it, please apply anyway. We would rather read your application and decide together than have you rule yourself out.

role: 2027 Software Dev Engineer Intern (Machine Learning) - UK
description: Do you want to solve real customer problems through innovative technology? Do you enjoy working on scalable services in a collaborative team environment? Do you want to see your code directly impact millions of customers worldwide? At Amazon, we hire the best minds in technology to innovate and build on behalf of our customers. Customer obsession is part of our company DNA, which has made us one of the world's most beloved brands. Our Software Development Engineer (SDE) interns use modern technology to solve complex problems while seeing their work's impact first-hand. The challenges SDE interns solve at Amazon are meaningful and influence millions of customers, sellers, and products globally. We seek individuals passionate about creating new products, features, and services while managing ambiguity in an environment where development cycles are measured in weeks, not years. At Amazon, we believe in ownership at every level. As an SDE intern, you'll own the entire lifecycle of your code - from design through deployment and ongoing operations. This ownership mindset, combined with our commitment to operational excellence, ensures we deliver the highest quality solutions for our customers. We're looking for curious minds who think big and want to define tomorrow's technology. At Amazon, you'll grow into the high-impact engineer you know you can be, supported by a culture of learning and mentorship. Every day brings exciting new challenges and opportunities for personal growth. Amazon internships across all seasons are full-time positions, and interns should expect to work in office, Monday-Friday, up to 40 hours per week typically between 8am-5pm. Specific team norms around working hours will be communicated by your manager. Interns should not have conflicts such as classes or other employment during the Amazon work-day. Applicants should have a minimum of one quarter/semester/trimester remaining in their studies after their internship concludes. Key job responsibilities - Collaborate and communicate effectively with experienced cross-disciplinary Amazonians to design, build, and operate innovative products and services that delight our customers, while participating in technical discussions to drive solutions forward. - Break down complex, ambiguous problems into well-defined, solvable components before implementation. - Contribute to the design and development of scalable, reliable services, with distributed-systems scope varying by team. - Participate in code reviews as a core engineering practice, providing constructive feedback and validating correctness. - Contribute to clear and accurate technical documentation. - Use GenAI and AI-powered tools to enhance development productivity, and critically validate, verify, and integrate AI-generated code, exercising sound judgement about when to trust AI output. - Write clean, maintainable code following best practices and design patterns. - Work in an agile environment practicing CI/CD principles while participating in operational responsibilities including on-call duties. - Demonstrate operational excellence through monitoring, troubleshooting, and resolving production issues. A day in the life As an intern, you will be matched to a manager and a mentor and will have the opportunity to influence the evolution of Amazon technology and lead critical projects early in your career. In addition to working on an impactful project, you will have the opportunity to engage with Amazonians for both personal and professional development, expand your network, and participate in activities with other interns throughout your internship. No matter the location of your internship, we give you the tools to own your project and learn in a real-world setting. About the team Intern Community: As an Amazon Intern, you'll be part of a vibrant, supportive community that empowers your growth and development. You'll collaborate with interns from around the world, networking and participating in social events to broaden your perspectives. You can also join specialized groups focused on areas like sustainability to explore your diverse interests. Support: The internship program provides a robust support system, including weekly intern office hours, dedicated IT and HR support, and a program team committed to your success. This ensures you have the guidance and assistance needed to thrive. Learning Sessions: Exclusive learning sessions will further enhance your skills, granting you access to Amazon's cutting-edge learning platforms and the expertise of industry leaders. These structured development opportunities will prepare you for the next step in your career. Opportunities: Upon successful completion of the internship, you may be considered for a graduate role or a second internship, allowing you to continue your journey with Amazon. Additionally, you'll enjoy a competitive monthly salary, relocation support, and access to a range of employee benefits.

The team is ultimately responsible for project oversight and review of all disciplines including electrical, mechanical, controls, and architectural. A fundamental understanding of these systems is required, as the individual will be expected to identify areas for improvement as well as act on data provided from other teams and organizations. Ideal candidates will possess the ability to design, develop and deploy innovative solutions to address operational challenges. This role requires both independent contribution as well as the ability to work within multi-disciplinary teams. The scope of projects will include but is not limited to the improvement of electrical, mechanical, fire detection and building automation system. A day in the life If you are passionate about the Customer Experience; you think and act globally; and you want to contribute to the operational excellence of Amazon data centers, then this may be the challenge you have been looking for! This position will be hands on in one of our data centers in Virginia, Oregon, Ohio, Mississippi, or California. Daily onsite hours could begin as early as 6am. This position will require the ability to communicate with a variety of vendors, people, and teams with a high level of customer service.

role: Student Aide - Career and Technical Programs
description: Schedule The work schedule will depend on the student’s availability, with a maximum of 20 hours per week. The Cybersecurity & Risk Internship is an 11-week, hands-on experience where interns contribute to real-world cybersecurity projects that help protect ADT’s technology, systems, and data. Interns may gain experience across areas such as application security, vulnerability and threat exposure management, cybersecurity risk, security automation and AI, and security data and reporting. Along the way, they’ll build technical and professional skills while working with teams across ADT to analyze security challenges, test solutions, and help strengthen ADT’s overall security posture.

Applied Materials’ Gloucester Applications Lab, Metrology team is seeking a motivated Co-op to help modernize statistical process control (SPC) and tool-health monitoring. The successful candidate will organize and streamline existing SPC charts and protocols, develop intuitive dashboards for rapid review, and improve how process technicians receive pass/fail SPC status and exception notifications. This role combines data analytics, visualization, process improvement, and hands-on collaboration in a semiconductor applications-lab environment. **Key Responsibilities** · Review, organize, and standardize existing SPC charts, control plans, and monitor protocols across metrology systems and process tools. · Support the lab data-repository initiative by consolidating and migrating data from legacy metrology tools, including TW and Rs systems, to a centralized network location to improve data accessibility, traceability, and long-term lab modernization. · Assess current SPC performance and identify charts, limits, or workflows that require investigation or improvement, including processes with weak capability indicators such as Cpk. · Develop a centralized dashboard and data-visualization solution that enables engineers and technicians to review SPC trends, tool health, and exceptions efficiently. · Create clear pass/fail status indicators and an alerting workflow to notify process technicians when a tool passes or fails an SPC check. · Automate or simplify recurring data collection, chart generation, review, and reporting steps where practical. · Partner with engineers and process technicians to define user requirements, test solutions, document workflows, and support adoption. · Prepare concise technical documentation and present project progress, findings, and recommendations to the Applications Lab team. **Co-op start date is January 2027, onsite at our Gloucester, MA location** **Qualifications** - Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or Ph.D. in Mathematics, Statistics, and Data Science. - Must be available to work full-time for a 6–8 months internship/co-op assignment and in student status - Demonstrated programming experience and strong knowledge of statistical process control (SPC) using Statistical SW (such as JMP), Python, MATLAB, or similar computational tools. **Functional Knowledge** - Demonstrates strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills, independently leading technical investigations and driving business productivity with minimal supervision. - Rapidly adapts to new equipment, processes, and technologies while effectively operating in shared research facilities and adhering to cleanroom protocols. - Communicates technical findings clearly and effectively through written, verbal, and presentation skills, enabling collaboration across multidisciplinary teams. Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from [utility inspectors](https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities) to [first responders](https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety), [soldiers in battlefield scenarios](https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr), and [beyond](https://www.skydio.com/solutions). **About the role:** The core of our system is the computer vision algorithms that allow drones to understand the world around them. You will architect and implement the algorithms that run on every drone powered by Skydio as part of a world class computer vision team with researchers who have pushed the state of the art in academia and industry. As an Autonomy Intern, you will be paired up with one or more members of our core software development team, assuming direct ownership of a project that meaningfully advances the capabilities of our team and products. If you have a strong foundation in math, theory, and software development with relevant research and you are interested in directly contributing to the development of the next generation of autonomy algorithms and pushing them into real products, we would love to hear from you. **How you'll make an impact:** - Enable rapid research and development of intelligent systems with advanced autonomous capabilities beyond anything that exists in the world today - Research, prototype, and generally assess the feasibility of new approaches - Imagine and then implement new features that unlock magic for our users - Characterize and quantify the performance of core components of the software and hardware stack **What makes you a strong fit:** - High proficiency in C++ and/or Python - Demonstrated enthusiasm for one or more of the following: computer vision, deep learning, motion planning, dynamics and controls, 3D graphics, embedded software/firmware, distributed systems, tools/infrastructure, mobile - Solid software engineering foundation and a commitment to writing clean, well-architected code - Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative, small team environment **Compensation:** The hourly rate for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Masters, and $70/hr for PhD students\*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. Interns are eligible to receive the following benefits: Paid vacation time, sick leave, holiday pay and 401K savings plan. This position and all associated benefits are subject to applicable federal, state, and local laws, as well as the Company’s policies and eligibility criteria. \*For some positions the pay may be dependent upon the individual's regional location. #LI-DK1 At Skydio we believe that diversity drives innovation. We have created a multidisciplinary environment that embraces the power of diverse perspectives to create elegant solutions for complex problems. We are committed to growing our network of people, programs, and resources to nurture an inclusive culture. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by federal, state or local anti-discrimination laws. For positions located in the United States of America, Skydio, Inc. uses E-Verify to confirm employment eligibility. To learn more about E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities, please visit

Strong academic background Strong analytical skills and be able to apply more creative and abstract thinking to help develop ingenious solutions. It’s rewarding to know that what we’re working on what matters most to our clients. We’re looking for a **Member of Technical Staff intern** to work hand-in-hand with our founders and team This is a hands-on role that combines engineering, storytelling, and community. You'll ship code alongside our product and engineering teams, and work closely with our GTM and DevRel teams to turn what we build into demos, content, and experiences that inspire builders. You'll be part of our mission of connecting AI agents to the web. ## **WHAT YOU'LL DO** - Take part in the development of new products and features built on top of Linkup's proprietary index. - Develop and maintain SDKs, templates, integrations, and reference implementations for AI and agentic workflows. - Build and ship polished demos, sample apps, and starter kits that showcase what's possible with Linkup's APIs. - Produce technical content: blog posts, tutorials, videos, and benchmarks that make complex tech approachable. - Collect and synthesize developer feedback to inform product and developer experience priorities. ## **WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS** Every demo, integration, and product you build helps define how AI agents connect to the web. You'll operate on the frontier between product and developers, bringing the voice of builders into everything we build and say. If you love blending engineering with impact, building things developers actually use: this role is for you. ## **YOU'RE A GREAT FIT IF YOU** - Have high agency: you see something that should exist, and you build it. You don't wait to be told what to do. What would be a big plus: - Hands-on experience with APIs, LLMs, agents, and DevTools. - A taste for turning technical depth into compelling storytelling. - Participation in active developer communities, hackathons, or open-source projects. . ## **DETAILS** You'll work shoulder to shoulder with the founders and the team, with real ownership from day one: your work ships to production and reaches thousands of developers. ## **ABOUT LINKUP** ## ### **OUR VISION** **We believe in a future of AI agents and the agentic web.** These digital entities can create more value for humanity than we ever could alone, but they depend on the internet to operate, collaborate, take action, and gather information. **AI agents need web search**. To perform well, they require information that is current, reliable, and context‑specific—not the diffuse, steadily aging knowledge frozen at their last training cut‑off. **Modern web search is built for humans, not AIs**. Instead of trusted facts, it serves links, ads, and click‑bait. People want visually engaging pages; AI systems need structured truth. An AI can absorb oceans of data, while human attention barely skims the surface. Humans think visually and intuitively; AI reasons in latent space. **Web 2.0 is sunsetting.** The deck is being reshuffled, and the Bing‑Google search oligopoly is crumbling. Indexing ever more pages is no longer the goal; semantically organizing facts for AI systems is. In the coming agentic web, Google's ad‑driven model has no natural home. **Search for AI must be rebuilt from the ground up.** We are reconstructing the web as a rigorously structured knowledge layer, mapping every concept, entity, and claim into a coherent semantic graph. This foundation delivers verified facts and rich context to AI instantly, unlocking faster reasoning, higher accuracy, and radically more useful answers for everyone. Humans search Google; AI searches Linkup. ### **OUR MISSION** Reality never stands still, and neither should intelligence. Linkup reconnects language models to a living stream of verified facts, ensuring AIs remain as current and insightful as the world they serve. Our mission is to deliver the world's freshest, most trusted knowledge to AIs. ### **OUR CULTURE** Our culture is built on the following values: - Mission. We believe we play a critical role in building the agentic web. We are 100% committed to our mission of bringing the reality of the world to AI agents. - Speed. We build fast, we build to last. We get things done, well. - Ownership. We empower every team member to take ownership of their projects, ensuring they see them through to successful completion. - Teamwork. Our strength lies in our unity. We rely on one another and embrace our diversity as a core asset. - Humility. We maintain low egos, showing respect for others and continuously learning from their insights and experiences. Previously launched Amundsen , an open source search engine. - Denis Charrier Founding Engineer at Niland, an audio search company (acquired by Spotify), then Staff Engineer at Spotify. 15y of software development experience. - Boris Toledano Led robotics at Carrefour, after 3y at McKinsey & Co working on public affairs and digital transformation.

Description When you walk into a building, do you wonder how it actually works? We do too. **Summer Consultants is looking for Mechanical Engineering Interns for Summer 2027.** This is an opportunity for an engineering student who is curious about building systems and wants to see how classroom concepts become real designs in real buildings. At Summer Consultants, we design the mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and fire protection systems that make buildings safe, comfortable, functional, and reliable. Much of our work involves renovating and modernizing existing federal, institutional, higher education, and historic facilities. That means our projects are technical, hands-on, and rarely routine. **As an intern at Summer, you will support real project work alongside experienced engineers. You may assist with surveys, calculations, equipment selection, ductwork and piping layouts, drawings, and other project activities appropriate to your experience and the needs of the team.** Existing buildings do not give you a clean sheet of paper. Our engineers spend real time in the field walking buildings, surveying and documenting existing conditions, tracing systems, observing constraints, and figuring out how a new design can actually work within the building that is already there. The challenge of renovation work is solving real problems: what is already there, what can change, what must remain operational, how equipment and systems fit within existing spaces, and how a design can actually be built. Field surveys are also an important part of how our interns learn. You may help observe and document existing mechanical and plumbing systems, ask questions about what you are seeing, and learn how field conditions affect design decisions. Seeing buildings firsthand helps connect engineering concepts, drawings, and calculations to the systems that are actually installed and operating. Curious about building systems? Let's see what we can do together. **WHAT SUMMER CAN DO FOR YOU** Summer Consultants will help you: - Gain real-world experience in the MEP/FP consulting industry. - Get hands-on experience with HVAC and plumbing design, calculations, equipment selection, layouts, documentation, and existing-building surveys. - Learn how engineers survey buildings, document existing conditions, and turn field observations into practical design decisions. - Build experience with tools such as Revit, AutoCAD, and applicable mechanical design and analysis software. - Work on varied projects. We rarely have "typical" projects because buildings are unique, and so are their systems and constraints. - Learn directly from experienced engineers in the office and in the field. - Collaborate with engineers across disciplines and see how building systems work together. - Work in a small, technically engaged environment where you can ask questions, receive feedback, and build practical engineering experience. **INTERN BENEFITS & SUPPORT** - **Paid sick leave:** One hour of sick leave earned for every 30 hours worked. - **Parking and business travel:** Summer provides parking at no cost and reimburses reasonable approved expenses associated with travel to job sites and other business travel. Requirements **WHAT YOU CAN DO FOR SUMMER** In this role, you may: - Support mechanical and plumbing design work on renovation and existing-building projects. - Participate in field surveys to observe and document existing building conditions and systems. - Assist with HVAC and plumbing calculations, equipment selection, ductwork and piping layouts, and related design activities. - Help translate survey information, calculations, and existing constraints into project drawings and design documentation. - Use tools such as Revit and AutoCAD to support project work. - Coordinate with engineers and designers from other disciplines. - Ask questions, apply feedback, and take on increasing responsibility as your skills develop. - Help solve client problems with curiosity, precision, quality, and follow-through. **WHAT YOU SHOULD BRING WITH YOU** - At least two years completed toward a Bachelor's degree in Architectural Engineering (HVAC focus), Mechanical Engineering, or Mechanical Engineering Technology. - Genuine interest in HVAC, plumbing, building systems, existing-building renovation, and learning how engineering works in practice. - Curiosity about how buildings are constructed, operated, maintained, and modified over time. - Willingness to spend meaningful time in the field surveying existing conditions. - Ability to learn from experienced engineers, ask questions, receive and apply feedback, and contribute as part of a project team. - Strong written and verbal communication skills. - Strong Microsoft Word and Excel skills. - AutoCAD and Revit experience preferred. - Ability to support day-long field surveys outdoors and indoors, including conditioned and unconditioned spaces, with or without reasonable accommodation. Field work may include walking 10,000 to 20,000 steps in a day, climbing up and down a 6-foot ladder, kneeling, squatting, and bending. - Ability to obtain site access at client locations, including federal facilities, as required by project assignments.

Description When you walk into a building do you immediately start analyzing it? Do you wonder about the life safety, fire alarm and automatic suppression systems? Well, so do we. We are looking for some passionate interns to join our team of folks who are curious about building systems. The bulk of our projects are renovations, frequently of only the MEP/FP systems, so it makes for some interesting and challenging projects. The fun of renovation work is dealing with the existing constraints imposed by the structure or building operations. We find ourselves regularly solving problems like how to make the equipment fit into an existing building or figuring out how the contractor will build your design. We are such great problem solvers that 95% of our clients would refer us to others. Clients choose us when they want the job done right the first time. We serve our clients' missions as if they were our own, whether supporting the warfighter or our nation's finest government and educational institutions. With our office located in Nation’s Capital Region, our interesting client list, and a focus on renovation, you will get to go into some interesting buildings, sometimes seeing history from the inside out. Check out our projects page for some examples of our work. Curious about building systems? Let’s see what we can do together! **WHAT SUMMER CONSULTANTS CAN DO FOR YOU** - Give real world MEP/FP industry experience. - Provide hands-on experience with tools such as Revit, AutoCAD, and hydraulic calculation software. - Provide you with different projects – we have never had identical projects and we rarely have “typical” projects. Buildings are unique and so are their systems. - Help you get your boots dirty learning from experienced engineers in the field. - Provide a fun, small, and exciting work environment. **WHAT YOU CAN DO FOR SUMMER CONSULTANTS** - Dive into designing quality projects from day one. Not just drafting them, but surveying existing conditions, analyzing life safety, layout fire alarm and fire suppression systems, and lots more fun stuff. - Help us tackle our clients’ problems. Requirements **WHAT YOU SHOULD BRING WITH YOU** - 2 years completed towards a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Fire Protection Engineering. - Excellent written and verbal English communication skills. - Strong skills in Microsoft Word and Excel. - AutoCAD and Revit experience a plus. - Ability to conduct day-long field surveys outdoors and indoors in conditioned and unconditioned spaces, including walking up to 10-20k steps in a day, climbing up and down a 6-foot ladder, kneeling, squatting, and bending. - Ability to obtain site access at client locations. **COMPANY BENEFITS** - Sick Leave: You will earn one hour of sick leave each 30 hours worked. - The company reimburses costs for parking and travel to job sites.

About Trace Trace is building the data, infrastructure, and research that enable robots to learn from the real world. General-purpose robotics requires a deeper understanding of how robots learn from real-world data. Our research explores how to transform human experiences, including egocentric video, demonstrations, hand-object interactions, and multimodal sensory signals, into transferable representations, actionable knowledge, and generalizable robot behaviors. At our Brooklyn research lab, we combine fundamental research in robot learning, computer vision, and embodied AI with large-scale datasets, machine learning infrastructure, and real-world robotic experimentation. Our goal is to advance the science of robot learning while developing the datasets and learning foundations for increasingly capable, adaptable, and reliable robots. About the role We are looking for highly motivated Research Interns to join our research team and work on challenging, high-impact problems at the intersection of robot learning, embodied AI, and learning from human experience. This internship is designed for PhD students and exceptional Master's students who are passionate about advancing the state of the art in robotics and machine learning. As a Research Intern, you will take ownership of a focused research project, working closely with our scientists and engineers to formulate research questions, develop novel methods, design rigorous experiments, and evaluate results using real-world datasets, simulation, and/or robotic platforms. We encourage ambitious, scientifically grounded research with the potential to contribute to top-tier robotics, machine learning, and computer vision conferences. You will have opportunities to pursue original research, collaborate with an interdisciplinary team, and help shape Trace's long-term research directions. Research areas Research projects may span one or more of the following areas, but are not limited to: • Learning from Human Experience and Egocentric Data • Human-to-Robot and Cross-Embodiment Transfer • Foundation Models for Robot Learning • Visual-Tactile and Multimodal Robot Learning • Data-Centric Robot Learning and Scaling • Dexterous Manipulation and Generalizable Robot Skills • Robustness, Generalization, and Reliable Robot Learning We particularly welcome candidates who bring novel perspectives, strong methodological expertise, or creative research ideas that complement these directions. What you'll do • Lead an original research project from problem formulation and hypothesis development through method design, implementation, experimentation, and evaluation, with guidance and collaboration from Trace's research team. • Develop and evaluate novel robot learning methods, including learning algorithms, representations, models, or training strategies that leverage human demonstrations, multimodal datasets, and robotic interaction data. • Design rigorous experiments and benchmarks to investigate fundamental questions about data quality, human-to-robot transfer, policy learning, generalization, and real-world robotic performance. • Work with diverse data modalities, potentially including egocentric video, human hand and body motion, teleoperation demonstrations, visual-tactile signals, force measurements, and robot trajectories. • Collaborate with research scientists and engineers to build reproducible experimental pipelines, train and evaluate models, and validate research findings in simulation and/or on real robotic platforms. • Analyze experimental results and failure modes, draw actionable scientific insights, and communicate findings through technical discussions, presentations, and written reports. • Contribute to high-quality research publications and open research artifacts, with opportunities to submit work to leading robotics and machine learning venues. What we're looking for • Currently pursuing a PhD or Master's degree in Robotics, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related field. • Strong research background in at least one relevant area, such as robot learning, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, computer vision, embodied AI, foundation models, dexterous manipulation, multimodal learning, or learning from human demonstrations. • Demonstrated research excellence and potential, evidenced by high-quality publications, impactful research projects, open-source contributions, or other substantial research accomplishments. Publications at leading venues such as RSS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, T-RO, IJRR, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, or CVPR are highly valued. First-author or co-first-author publications are a strong plus. • Excellent programming skills in Python and hands-on experience with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX. Experience with C++ and parallel programming, such as CUDA, is a plus. • Strong communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, interdisciplinary research environment. Nice to have • Experience with real-world robot learning experiments, robotic manipulation platforms, or deployment of learned policies on physical robots. • Experience with egocentric video, human demonstrations, hand tracking, pose estimation, motion retargeting, or cross-embodiment learning. • Experience with vision-language-action models, diffusion-based policies, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, or world models. • Experience with tactile sensing, force estimation, multimodal sensor fusion, or contact-rich manipulation. • Experience with robotics simulation environments and tools such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, or related frameworks. • Previous research experience in an industrial research lab or a collaborative, interdisciplinary research environment. How to apply Please submit your CV/resume, along with links to your Google Scholar profile, personal website, GitHub, or other relevant research portfolio, if available. Internship start dates are flexible. Academic credit may be available if required by your degree program, subject to institutional requirements. Trace is an equal opportunity employer.

**Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The Algorithms group at MSR Redmond is looking for doctoral students to work on theoretical computer science, in particular, algorithms for approximate nearest neighbor search, erasure coding for distributed storage, and theoretical aspects of Large Language Models. We value fundamental theoretical advances, while also supporting and actively helping Research Interns in connecting their theoretical work to practical challenges and real-world impact. Our researchers and Research Interns have been conducting influential research published in top-tier venues such as STOC, FOCS, SODA, NeurIPS, ICML, and ICLR. For more details on our research group and projects, please see: For the fullest consideration, please apply by January 1, 2027. **Responsibilities** Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. **Qualifications** **Required Qualifications** - Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, Mathematics, Electrical Engineering, or a related STEM field. **Other Requirements** - Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. - In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. able to manage multiple team relationships and projects at once - Interest in enterprise software, financial services, AI, or cybersecurity is a bonus **Sponsorship -** While we highly value all of our candidates, we are not offering visa sponsorship for this role. **Salary Range**: $17-25hr **Life at HERE** At HERE, we pride ourselves on fostering a friendly, collaborative, and supportive culture that truly respects the diversity of thought. **About Lumafield:** Lumafield was founded in 2019 to upgrade manufacturing. We are engineers with deep experience across the product development cycle, from initial ideas to shipping hardware, across industries and specializations, who became frustrated by the cost and complexity of modern manufacturing. So we decided to upgrade it. Engineers make million-dollar decisions every day, and they need tools that give them the greatest possible insight into their products. By offering unprecedented visibility into products, as well as AI-driven tools that highlight problems and generate quantitative data, Lumafield promises to revolutionize the way complex products are created, manufactured, and used across industries. We started with industrial CT scanning, which for us was the most valuable but underutilized tool in the manufacturing toolbox, enabling us to rapidly inspect essential components non-destructively. We rebuilt the whole system, from X-ray capture, to computer vision analysis, to web-based collaboration, to the entire business model, making the most advanced manufacturing tech more accessible to every industry. Our company, like our platform, is designed for upgrades. We’re building for greater intelligence, autonomy, and speed. For deeper vision, operational excellence, and powerful insights. And then we'll upgrade it all again. Lumafield is headquartered in San Francisco, CA. and has an office in Cambridge, MA. **About the role:** Lumafield is hiring a Finance Engineer into a three-year rotational program across Finance & Accounting. A Finance Engineer is a finance professional who wires systems together, builds AI agents and workflows, then uses them to own real analysis, close work, and operations. **Program overview:** - Three one-year rotations: FP&A (reporting to the Head of Finance), Finance Operations, and Record-to-Report (both reporting to the Head of Accounting). - A readout to Finance leadership at the end of each rotation covering what you owned, what you built, and what the next Finance Engineer inherits. - Rotation managers give structured feedback at the midpoint and end of each year. - On completing the third rotation you graduate into a senior role in Finance, Accounting, or another Lumafield team that needs an AI builder with finance judgment. **The working rule on this team:** If you do something twice, write a workflow; if you write the workflow twice, write an agent. The stack you will build on includes NetSuite, Maxio, Ramp, Numeric, HubSpot, Abacum, Databricks, and Claude. Each rotation adds domain context, so after three years you have analytical, modeling, AI building, and AI orchestration skills and broad context across Finance, Accounting, and Lumafield's business and operations. ### What you'll do: - Own the analysis, modeling, and deliverables for your area, and be accountable for their accuracy and timing. - Write skills and apps building on our data lake and source systems rather than waiting on engineering or exporting to spreadsheets. - Connect systems and remove workflow bottlenecks: integrations, GL mappings, data flows, and the controls around them. - Build and orchestrate AI agents and workflows for the team, with documented review points so the output is audit-ready. - Turn recurring work into documented, reusable workflows that the next Finance Engineer can run and improve. ### Rotation 1: FP&A - Own the operating model and forecast in Abacum, including headcount, revenue, cash, and runway, and the monthly variance analysis against plan. - Build the board and executive reporting package: ARR, backlog, bookings, deployments, liquidity, and OpEx trends. - Support capital markets and M&A work: data rooms, diligence requests, scenario modeling, and lender compliance reporting. - Build the forecasting and reporting agents that keep these packages current without manual rebuilds. ### Rotation 2: Finance Operations - Own collections and accounts receivable performance: aging, DSO, cash application, and customer AP portal resolution. - Own accounts payable and purchasing in Ramp, including approval workflows, vendor management, and the NetSuite integration. - Own monthly revenue recognition under ASC 606 and sales tax compliance in Maxio and Avalara. - Automate collections, billing, coding, and reconciliation workflows with AI tooling and measure the cash impact. - Own inflows and outflow forecasting of 13 week cash forecast ### Rotation 3: Record-to-Report - Run the month-end close for your areas, including balance sheet reconciliations, flux analysis, and audit-ready workpapers. - Own inventory, COGS, fixed assets, and manufacturing cost accounting for our scanner production. - Serve as a primary contact for external auditors on the areas you own and maintain the related process and control documentation. - Build close agents that draft entries, reconciliations, and flux explanations for human review. ### About you: - Agile: comfortable rotating into a new area every year and adapting as the team, systems, and priorities change. - Demonstrated Judgment: makes sound calls with incomplete information and knows when to escalate. - Builder mindset: wires systems together, writes skills and workflow automation, and prototypes rather than waiting for someone else to do it. - AI fluency: proficient in tools such as Claude and has shipped working workflows or agents with them. - Clear communicator and writer; documentation and workpapers can be picked up by someone else. - Attention to detail: numbers tie, workpapers stand up to audit, and errors are caught before they leave the team. - Continuous improvement mindset: treats every recurring task as a process to shorten, document, or automate. - High degree of ownership: takes an area end to end, from the first question to the posted entry, and is accountable for its accuracy and timing. - Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Engineering, or a quantitative field; MBA or CPA a plus. - 2 to 6 years work experience in finance, accounting, FP&A, finance systems, analytics, or a technical role that touched any of these. ### Bonus: - CPA or MBA (a plus, not a requirement). - Familiarity with SQL - NetSuite, Ramp, Maxio, Abacum, or Databricks experience. - Experience in a hardware, manufacturing, or mixed hardware/software business.

role: Co-Op/Intern Support and Learning Platform Administrator
description: About Kinaxis Are you looking to join an innovative, market-leading company where you can truly elevate your career? At Kinaxis we are serious about culture, we are serious about technology, we are serious about customers, and we are serious about not taking ourselves too seriously. If you are looking to be part of an incredible growth story, then we might just be the place for you! In 1984, we started out as a team of three engineers. Today, we have grown to become a global organization with over 2000 employees around the world, 6 global office and a best-in-class HQ in Ottawa, Canada. As winners of several Top Employer awards globally, we are proud to work with our customers and employees towards solving some of the biggest challenges facing supply chains today. Kinaxis is a global leader in modern supply chain orchestration, powering complex global supply chains, and supporting the people who manage them. Our powerful, AI infused platform provides full transparency and visibility across end-to-end supply chains, enabling our customers to make faster, better decisions. We are trusted by renowned global brands to provide the agility and predictability needed to navigate today’s volatility and disruption. With more than 40,000 users in over 100 countries, we are expanding our team as we continue to innovate and revolutionize how we support our customers. About the team We are seeking a detail-oriented and proactive Support and Learning Platform Administrator to join our team. role: Master Thesis Project: Evaluation of AI-based Surrogate Models for Structural CAE Analysis
description: Background Artificial Intelligence is rapidly being introduced into engineering simulation workflows. One promising application is AI-based surrogate models that can predict simulation results significantly faster than traditional finite element analyses. This thesis aims to evaluate the applicability and potential efficiency gains of surrogate models in structural CAE analysis. Objective The study should investigate: Prediction accuracy compared to traditional FE simulations Required amount of training data Potential reduction in simulation turnaround time Applicability for implicit and explicit analyses The final objective is to establish guidelines for when AI-based surrogate models should be used and when traditional FE simulations remain the preferred approach. Methods The study will use a finite element structure model as a case study. Surrogate models will be developed using data from both implicit and explicit analyses. The predictive accuracy, computational efficiency and required engineering effort will be compared with conventional FE simulations. Deliverables A report containing:  Evaluation of AI-based surrogate models for structural CAE  Assessment of accuracy and potential time savings  Evaluation of applicability for implicit and explicit analyses  Guidelines and recommendations for industrial use Master Student at Applied Mechanics or equivalent program. Thesis project will be performed in Trollhättan. In the department CAE & Vehicle Safety in Trollhättan, you will be part of the team that performs strength, durability and NVH analysis to develop the performance and attributes of vehicles and systems of the future. Our customers are both local and international. We aim to find two students that can do this project together. role: Data Scientist Assistant - Stage (6 mois) Mars 2027 (F/H/NB)
description: Au sein du département Publishing, vous rejoindrez l'équipe Audience Analytics , dont les missions visent à décrire, modéliser et prédire les comportements des joueur·euses, sous différents angles : engagement, motivation, comportement, etc. L’équipe est en charge de soutenir les décisions stratégiques de l'entreprise et de fournir des recommandations aux équipes business pour adapter leurs stratégies aux attentes des joueur·euses. Dans le cadre de nos missions, nous portons beaucoup d’attention à caractériser le comportement des joueur·euses au sein de nos jeux et de prédire leur comportement futur. Votre rôle sera notamment de : Définir des indicateurs d’engagement et de fréquence d’activité ; Comprendre et modéliser l’engagement des joueur·euses au sein de nos jeux ; Assurer une veille méthodologique et proposer de nouvelles approches théoriques ; Communiquer sur vos travaux et vos résultats de façon pédagogique auprès d’un public varié. Votre stage sera divisé en deux parties distinctes : 1e partie (4 à 8 semaines) : vous serez amené.e à découvrir l’écosystème data d’Ubisoft à travers la réalisation d’analyses statistiques descriptives répondant aux besoins de nos activités quotidiennes ; Une 2e partie (4 à 5 mois) : vous serez entièrement en charge d’un projet data science. Le projet aura une dimension méthodologique importante et sera défini durant la 1e partie de stage en fonction des besoins business. Étudiant·e issu·e d'une formation en statistiques, mathématiques appliquées ou équivalent, vous possédez de solides connaissances en matière de développement et de déploiement de modèles statistiques. Vous avez une très bonne connaissance de la théorie statistique (méthodes d'analyse de données, analyse de séries temporelles, analyse de données séquentielles, clustering, scoring). Vous savez faire preuve d’autonomie, êtes force de proposition et avez un excellent sens de l'organisation Vous parlez français et anglais couramment.
