role: KIP Spring 2027 - Research Intern - Citizens Against Government Waste
description: **[The Koch Internship Program](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/koch-internship-program/) (KIP)** is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the [admissions process](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/application-process/) early! [Citizens Against Government Waste](https://www.cagw.org/) (CAGW) offers a wide variety of opportunities to college students across the country. Unpaid research, communications, and government affairs internships are available on a year-round basis and can vary in length from a semester to a few weeks in duration. Interns can choose to work part-time or full-time, as hours of work are extremely flexible. Our daily work with Capitol Hill and the White House, as well as government agencies and other nonprofit organizations, provides a close and invaluable look at how Washington works. Many projects involve working closely with staff members, while others require a great deal of independence. Interns are considered important members of our staff and actively participate in staff meetings and other events. While interns will also be required to perform clerical duties from time to time, much of the work will be substantive. **Research Internship** Assist in formulating policy papers and collect data for original investigative studies. Research and write for CAGW’s annual publications, which include the Congressional Pig Book, Prime Cuts, Government WasteWatch eNews, and special projects, including issue briefs, and policy papers. Interns will have the opportunity to initiate projects. Research internships are also available in specific areas, including healthcare and science, technology and telecommunications, federal regulations and taxation. Interns may spend a majority of their time supporting the work above, but may also support other staff members as needed. This role is open to remote work, but priority is given to those available for in person work at our Washington, D.C office.

Patreon is a media and community platform where over 300,000 creators give their biggest fans access to exclusive work and experiences. We offer creators a variety of ways to engage with their fans and build a lasting business including: paid memberships, free memberships, community chats, live video, and selling to fans directly with one-time purchases. Ultimately our goal is simple: fund the creative class. And we're leaders in that space, with: - $10 billion+ generated by creators since Patreon's inception - 100 million+ free memberships for fans who may not be ready to pay just yet, and - 25 million+ paid memberships on Patreon today. *We're continuing to invest in building the best creator platform with the best team in the creator economy and are looking for a **Product Design Intern** to support our mission.* *This role is based in **San Francisco or New York** and open to those who are able to be in-office 3 days per week on a hybrid work model.* *Our summer internship is a 12-week program running **May–August 2027 or June–September 2027**. This internship is designed for students graduating between **December 2027 and June 2028**.* ## **About the Role** - **Make an impact.** You’ll build and ship a feature that directly supports the creator economy and helps your favorite creators turn their passions into sustainable careers. - **Collaborate with the best.** You’ll be embedded within a world-class product team, working closely with engineers, product managers, data scientists, and other designers to bring your project to life. - **Learn and grow.** With guidance from an experienced design mentor, you’ll tackle design challenges, gain hands-on experience, and grow your skills throughout the internship. - **Have fun!** Beyond building great products, you’ll join an intern cohort in San Francisco or New York City and participate in professional development opportunities and fun events. ## **About You** - Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Product Design, Interaction Design, UI/UX, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), or a related field. - You have a creative portfolio that showcases your experience bridging thoughtful product strategy with design execution through user-centered design. - Foundation in visual design, interaction design, and prototyping. - You’re curious, enjoy experimenting with new ideas, and are excited to build from 0 to 1. - Eagerness to learn, adapt, and grow through feedback. - Genuine passion for Patreon’s mission and supporting the creator economy. ## **About Patreon** Patreon powers creators to do what they love and get paid by the people who love what they do. Our team is passionate about making this mission and our core values come to life every day in our work. Through this work, our Patronauts: - **Put Creators First |** *They’re the reason we’re here. When creators win, we win.* - **Build with Craft |** *We sign our name to every deliverable, just like the creators we serve.* - **Make it Happen |** *We don’t quit. We learn and deliver.* - **Win Together |** *We grow as individuals. We win as a team.* We hire talented and passionate people from different backgrounds because workplace diversity and inclusion is critical to our ability to serve creators worldwide. If you’re excited about a role but your past experience doesn’t match with every bullet point outlined above, we strongly encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re a creator at heart, are energized by our mission, and share our company values, we’d love to hear from you. *Patreon is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We provide employment opportunities without regard to age, race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, disability, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other protected class. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the interview process, please let us know via email at accomodations@patreon.* *Patreon operates under a hybrid work model, where engineering interns are expected to come into the office three days per week, excluding sick time and leave. The goal of this policy is to be intentional about the in-person time we spend together to strengthen the feeling of community at Patreon.* *At Patreon, we believe in fair and transparent pay. In compliance with New York and California pay transparency laws, we are sharing the expected salary range for this role.* *The posted salary range is dependent on the location and the level. This range may encompass multiple levels within the role’s job family. The final offer will be based on candidate’s experience, skills, competencies, and geographic location, aligning with the appropriate job level within Patreon’s leveling framework.* *Patreon reserves the right to modify or update compensation and benefits at any time.*

Singlife is a leading homegrown financial services company, offering consumers a better way to financial freedom. Through innovative, technology-enabled solutions and a wide range of products and services, Singlife provides consumers control over their financial wellbeing at every stage of their lives. In addition to a comprehensive suite of insurance plans, employee benefits, partnerships with financial adviser channels and bancassurance, Singlife offers investment and advisory solutions through its GROW with Singlife platform. It also offers the Singlife Account, a mobile-first insurance savings plan. Singlife is the exclusive insurance provider for the Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Home Affairs and Public Officers Group Insurance Scheme. Singlife is also an official signatory of the United Nations Principles for Sustainable Insurance and the United Nations-supported Principles for Responsible Investment, affirming its commitment to finding a better way to sustainability. The merger of Aviva Singapore and Singlife was announced in September 2020 and created one of the largest homegrown financial services companies in Singapore in a deal valued at S$3.2 billion. It was the largest insurance deal in Singapore at the time. Singlife was subsequently acquired by Sumitomo Life in March 2024, one of Japan’s leading life insurers, which valued Singlife at S$4.6 billion, making the transaction one of the largest insurance deals in Southeast Asia. Requirements: •Education: Currently pursuing a diploma in Information Technology, Computer Science, Data Analytics, Engineering, Business IT or a related field. •Skills: Comfortable using Microsoft Excel and keen to learn testing and project tools such as JIRA, Xray, Zephyr, RTM and Confluence. •Interest: Curious about technology, software testing, digital projects and how teams use data to make better decisions. •Mindset: Detail-oriented, willing to ask questions, open to feedback and ready to learn by doing. •Teamwork: Able to communicate clearly, work well with others and support the team in a positive and reliable way.

## **Health can’t wait**. Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t. Alan exists to end the wait. Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way. So we are building the **new standard in prevention insurance.** Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience. We are on an incredible journey to build a **global leading company, with a** [**unique culture**](https://alan.com/en/careers). We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR. Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond. # 🛡️ The role Most GRC roles are about keeping auditors happy. This one is about earning our members' trust: every day, they share their diagnoses, their claims and their care with us. You'll join Alan's security team to help run our compliance and risk work across ISO 27001, HDS and DORA, across a growing number of countries and regulators. We just earned our HDS certification, and there's much more to build, including how we govern AI across our products: assessing AI risks, setting the controls, and keeping up with the AI Act. You'll learn alongside experienced security engineers, with a dedicated coach from day one. You'll take on real ownership early, and your scope grows as we scale from 1M to many millions of members. And you'll learn how we work at Alan: teams own their risks and controls, we automate wherever we can, and we focus on real outcomes, not paperwork. # 🚀 What you'll do - **Keep our certifications on track.** You run the day-to-day of the ISO 27001 and HDS audit cycles: collecting evidence, preparing internal audits, and following up on corrective actions until they're closed. - **Turn regulations into practical actions.** With Legal and the DPO, you help translate requirements like DORA, HDS, and GDPR into clear tasks for the teams, and track that they get done. - **Learn the health sector rules.** You build your knowledge of health-specific frameworks (ANS, HDS) and help apply them to how we handle health data. - **Contribute to risk management.** You help build and update our risk mapping, including AI risks, and follow up on the treatment plans with the teams who own them. - **Support the teams who own the controls.** You keep the controls framework up to date, answer teams' questions, and help explain security clearly to every stakeholder, from engineers to managers. - **Support incident governance.** You help classify and document incidents, keep Business continuity and Disaster recovery plans up to date, and prepare inputs for DORA incident reports. - **Automate what slows us down.** You spot repetitive compliance tasks and automate them with scripts, tools or AI. # 🏗️ What you'll help build - **One compliance backbone:** A single control system for several regulators in several countries, so Alan can scale without rebuilding compliance each time. - **An automated evidence engine:** evidence collected straight from engineering systems with scripts and AI, so audits run continuously instead of as a quarterly rush. You'll work closely with Legal, the DPO, Internal Audit and Risk, and day to day with engineering and operations teams. # ⭐ What we're looking for - You want to do the work yourself and grow with it: a permanent, hands-on role where you build things for the long run. - 2+ years in security, GRC or compliance (an audit background is fine if you want to move into building). - You've played a key part in a certification or audit cycle (ISO 27001, HDS, SOC 2 or similar). - You're curious about how things work technically, and you've automated at least one manual task (a script, a tool, an AI workflow). - You're fluent in French and English, and comfortable presenting in both. - You learn fast, ask for feedback, and go into the details when it matters. # 🌍 How we work **Location:** You must be legally eligible to work from France, Belgium or Spain. **Remote work:** We offer remote work flexibility. **Contract type:** Permanent contract only (no freelancing). ## **🎯 Important note: we hire people, not roles.** If you're excited about this opportunity but don't check every box, we'd love to hear from you. Everyone, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply, as it can only bring learnings or success. 🔖 Check out our [About Alan](https://alan.com/about) and [Career](https://alan.com/careers) pages, as well as our [Medium](https://medium.com/alan), [blog](https://blog.alan.com/) and [Glassdoor page](https://www.glassdoor.com/Overview/Working-at-Alan-EI_IE1696043.11,15.htm) for more info. ## **You want to know more about Alan?** 🙌 [Perks & Benefits](https://alan.com/en/careers/a/salary-equity): Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers. 🤘[A strong culture](https://alan.com/en/about/a/leadership-principles): People joining Alan are often surprised and delighted by our innovative working method. We have a set of cultural values that guide our approach to work

role: Stage - Product design - Design system et IA Literacy - F/H/N
description: Sujet de stage Stage - UI et Design system et son application à l'air de l'IA - F/H/N Sous-titre Explorer comment l'IA transforme les interactions, la gouvernance, la documentation et l'usage des design systems dans les équipes produit OCTO Le WHY Les IA exploitent déjà les Design Systems (DS) pour accélérer POC et prototypes. Ce stage vise à identifier comment OCTO peut structurer ses Design Systems pour réduire l’écart maquette-code et en faire un levier d’industrialisation, de qualité UI et de collaboration design/dev. Les missions Explorer l'état de l'art des Design Systems à l'ère de l'IA : gouvernance, composants, documentation, collaboration design/dev. Analyser des cas concrets chez OCTO, notamment des contextes multi-UI kits et équipes distribuées. Formaliser des recommandations actionnables pour faire du design system un levier de qualité, d'efficacité et de cohérence produit. Déterminer des règles d'usage (à la création de DS par exemple dans le but de créer un outil scalable) Comparer nos règles d'usage (Octo) à des DS existants Intégrer les notions d'accessibilité + RGAA Le déroulement du stage Étape 1 : Cadrage et immersion: clarifier les objectifs du stage, les attentes des encadrant·es et les terrains d'analyse. Comprendre les enjeux actuels des Design Systems chez OCTO : gouvernance, outillage, documentation, collaboration design/dev, cohérence UI et dette de conception. Étape 2 : Recherche et état de l'art: réaliser une veille sur les design systems à l'ère de l'IA : pratiques de marché, frameworks, outils, usages émergents, accélération de la documentation, génération de composants, contrôle qualité et maintien de la cohérence. Étape 3 : Analyse terrain et expérimentation : observer des projets OCTO confrontés à des enjeux de Design System, notamment des environnements multi-UI kits et équipes éclatées. Conduire des entretiens, cartographier les irritants, tester des pistes IA et identifier les conditions d'usage réellement utiles. Étape 4 : Synthèse et partage: produire une synthèse structurée : constats, typologies d'usages de l'IA, risques, opportunités, recommandations et scénarios d'application. Restituer les apprentissages à la communauté OCTO et contribuer à une vision cible du design system comme levier produit et direction artistique. Vous préparez un BAC+5 en design UX/UI, design de service, stratégie design ou innovation. Vous maîtrisez les méthodes de recherche, facilitation, prototypage et test utilisateur. Vous êtes à l'aise avec Figma, les design systems et les logiques produit. Vous vous intéressez à l'IA générative et à ses effets sur les pratiques de conception. Vous savez synthétiser, argumenter et restituer vos apprentissages à l'oral comme à l'écrit. Parce que ce ne sont pas que des mots, nous marquons au quotidien notre engagement en matière de numérique responsable : nous formons les Octos et nos clients à la Fresque du Climat / 2 Tonnes et œuvrons pour la sobriété numérique en interne et auprès de nos clients. Depuis 2021, nous sommes labellisés B Corp , et nous sommes fiers de renouveler cette certification toujours plus exigeante en 2025 ; Le management est un point central de notre culture . role: AI Consulting Associate Program (AI CAP) Product Manager Intern - Summer 2027
description: **About Us** DriveWealth is on a mission to make investing easier. We believe that everyone should have the ability to control their financial future, and that access to financial markets should not be limited by geography, wealth, or legacy systems. We are a global B2B financial technology organization dedicated to democratizing access to financial independence around the world. Our mission is realized through an API-based platform, empowering our partners to offer seamless investing and trading experiences to clients worldwide, all from their mobile devices. Our technology provides partners with a modern, extensible toolkit, enabling traditional investment workflows and innovative techniques like fractional share ownership. DriveWealth has evolved into a global platform offering trading of US equities, mutual funds, ETFs, fixed income, and options. There’s never been a better time to build a category-defining business and there has rarely been a team better positioned for this opportunity. Our culture blends the pace and agility of a fintech start-up with the impact, stability, and discipline of Wall Street. We encourage creativity and experimentation while ensuring institutional-grade execution and regulatory compliance in everything we do. Join us and help build the future of global investing! ### ***Interested*** to learn more about our AI CAP Program? We will have our in-person Open House at our CHI office office on November 23rd (RSVP here: ) ### **About the Role** We are seeking an AI Product Manager intern who will work on real AI agentic automation problems, designing, prototyping, and developing AI-powered agents to help the business and engineers achieve faster, smarter work. You will collaborate directly with senior engineers and architects, receiving mentorship and design reviews, and gaining exposure to modern GenAI patterns, including agent orchestration, tool-calling, retrieval, and evaluation, within an enterprise and fast-paced fintech environment. AI tools change every quarter. Your project will use the best models, agent frameworks, and protocols available in summer 2027. You will work on current practice, not today's stack. Launch your career developing real, impactful AI solutions in the lightning-fast world of fintech! **Program Details**Our summer program will be 10-12 weeks from May - August 2027 with the expectation of being in the office 3-4 days per week, as determined by the sponsor. Compensation will be set at an hourly rate of $35-40 per hour. Top performing associates may have the opportunity to be considered for full-time roles at DriveWealth at the conclusion of the program, based on performance and team needs. **Must have a graduation date from December 2027 to December 2028.** ### **What You’ll Do** - Design, prototype, and develop agentic AI workflows that automate or augment business or engineering tasks (for example, analysis, triage, documentation, and knowledge synthesis) - Build internal tools or proof-of-concept systems that combine LLMs, APIs, and automation frameworks into end-to-end agentic solutions - Experiment with different agent architectures (single-agent vs. multi-agent, planner/executor patterns, human-in-the-loop workflows) and document tradeoffs - Apply best practices when building AI-driven automation - Evaluate agent behavior for reliability, correctness, and failure modes, and propose improvements - Clearly document designs, experiments, and lessons learned so work can be reused or extended by the team - Demo your work directly to customers and the leadership team ### **What You’ll Need** - Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related technical field - Experience programming in Python (for automation, prototyping, and scripting) and SQL - Familiarity with APIs, JSON, and basic service integration - Foundational understanding of large language models and how they are used in applications (prompting, tool use, retrieval, etc.) - Strong curiosity and willingness to explore new, rapidly evolving technologies - A growth mindset: you ask questions and enjoy experimenting and iterating - Systems thinking: able to reason about workflows, edge cases, and unintended consequences - Clear written and verbal communication, especially when explaining technical ideas to non-engineers - Ownership mindset: you take responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks - Ability to accept feedback and iterate quickly Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. DriveWealth is unable to sponsor an employment Visa at this time. **Working at DriveWealth** We do our best work when we're in the same room. To maintain the speed our partners expect, our New York, Chicago, and Lithuania teams work in office on a hybrid schedule. We've found that being physically side-by-side is the only way to solve complex problems in real-time and stay truly accountable to the products we ship. When you're here, you're working directly with the people making the decisions. To support that work, we provide competitive compensation, equity, and a 401(k) match. We also offer Medical insurance, Dental insurance, Vision insurance, Disability insurance, and Paid Parental Leave, along with a wellness reimbursement, a company-provided phone, and a personal development allowance. Finally, we value the time you spend away from the office with generous Paid Time Off (PTO) and observed holidays. **Work Authorization** Applicants must possess the legal right to work in the country where the position is located at the time of application. DriveWealth requires all employees to provide original documentation verifying their work authorization on or before their first day of employment. For US-based roles: Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without the need for current or future visa sponsorship. DriveWealth does not provide visa sponsorship or support for employment authorization, including transfers, at this time. Offers of employment are strictly contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the Company. **How We Think About AI** We leverage AI to work smarter and move faster. We seek AI-curious talent who are proactive about using emerging tools to increase signal quality, reduce friction, and improve outcomes to deliver products faster, provide better service to our partners, and to streamline processes. Your ability to leverage our internal tools and technology to drive results is as important to us as your core domain expertise. **Compensation** Pay is generally based on the level, complexity, responsibility, location, and job duties/requirements of the specific position. We then source candidates with the requisite skills, expertise, education, training, and experience. If you are selected for an interview, please feel welcome to speak to a recruiter about our compensation philosophy and other available benefits. This role is eligible for base, bonus, equity, 401(k) match, and heavily subsidized benefits and perks. **Equal Employment Opportunity** To build technology and products that are used and loved by people and solve real-world problems, we need to build a team with many different perspectives and experiences. We are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply. **Agency Disclaimer** DriveWealth does not accept agency resumes. Do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, employees, or any other organization location. DriveWealth is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

role: Entry Level Civil Engineer - Land Development
description: **Build your civil engineering career in site design.** You'll work on real land development projects, design real sites, and grow through hands-on experience, professional development, and mentorship from engineers who want to see you succeed. **About the Role** Bohler’s Orlando, FL office is seeking an Entry Level Civil Engineer (Land Development) who is eager to learn, grow, and make a positive impact. In this role, you will work closely with engineers, designers, and project managers to bring exciting land development projects to life, including site planning, grading, utilities, and stormwater management. You will contribute to projects for well-known brands across commercial, residential, and mixed-use markets, all while laying the groundwork for a rewarding engineering career. **What You’ll Do** - Work on a variety of land development projects, including commercial, residential, industrial, and mixed-use sites - Partner with experienced engineers and mentors to learn every stage of site design, from concept through construction - Use AutoCAD Civil 3D to create site layouts, grading plans, and utility designs - Research and interpret design manuals, zoning ordinances, and jurisdictional regulations - Review and address regulatory comments and assist with project redesigns as needed - Support the preparation of stormwater management reports and construction submittals - Participate in professional and technical training through Bohler’s Learning & Development programs - Attend site visits to observe field conditions and coordinate with project teams - Engage in civic, professional, and business organizations to build your network - Perform other responsibilities in accordance with company policies and standards **What We Offer** - A supportive and flexible work environment that empowers employees to stay healthy, fulfill their passions, and balance work and life goals - The opportunity to take ownership of your career with an unsurpassed focus on career development and mentorship - A Learning & Development department that facilitates ongoing technical and professional growth, including individualized AutoCAD Civil 3D training - Complete visibility and exposure to all aspects of land development projects - The chance to immerse yourself in the design process while working side-by-side with talented teammates - Open and transparent communication with senior leadership and local office management - Team-building activities, office events, and a collaborative, high-energy environment **What You’ll Bring** - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Civil Engineering or a related field - 0–1+ years of residential, commercial, or industrial site design and permitting experience - Familiarity with AutoCAD Civil 3D (preferred; training provided if not yet proficient) - Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach to teamwork - Motivation to take initiative and contribute to shared goals - EIT certification is helpful but not required **Get hands-on experience contributing to real projects, and see how your work helps shape communities and your career.** #LI-Onsite

Power Your Curiosity at PA Why consider joining us? During your weeks as an intern at PA, you’ll learn some of what it takes to be a top-notch consultant. You’ll be coached and guided by experts and have opportunities to broaden your experience on a challenging project. Whatever you work on, you’ll be part of the team and free to build your contacts, both here at PA and beyond. PA’s ‘Networks Capability’ focuses on all non-consumer aspects of telecoms, blending expertise in technical, commercial and operational aspects. We focus on helping industry and enterprises maximise value from both next generation as well as critical, legacy connectivity. If you want a balance of technology, commercial and real-world applications, with an opportunity to work across a broad range of industry sectors, then this could be what you’re looking for. You may be involved in strategy for 5G train control, for blending LEO satellite and mobile for energy black-start scenarios, or managing communications obsolescence in defence. You will collaborate with expert consultants, be exposed to the latest advancements within telecoms (5G/6G, satcom, private networks, ML/AI integration), benefit from supportive mentoring, and gain skills through hands-on learning and peer support. What you can expect Joining us as an intern is the next step in starting your career. Whether you’re coming from a specialist background or from an unrelated subject, we want you to be bold, stay curious and dive into the opportunities we have to offer. You will work on real-world communication network technology challenges and solutions. Example projects and activities might include: Creating innovative software for advanced drone detection, Analysing the costs and benefits of communications technologies to support investment and business cases, Developing machine learning algorithms for patent identification, Research emerging communications technologies and assessing their potential applications, Assess options for upgrading critical infrastructure relying on legacy communications technology and Analysis of network performance data, identifying issues and producing recommendations. You will work directly with experienced Networks consultants who will work through technical problems with you, helping you structure analysis and develop your consulting skills. You will have the opportunity to experience all phases of an assignment, from understanding the problem and designing the approach through to analysing the evidence, developing recommendations and presenting your findings to key stakeholders. Essential requirements This role is open to undergraduates in their penultimate year of university. If you are currently a final year undergraduate and intend to return to university after the internship to complete an MSc / MEng, you will also be eligible for this position. Qualification: Working towards an undergraduate degree in Electronic / Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, Economics or another technical or numerate discipline is ideal but we welcome applications from a broad range of degree backgrounds. Wider interest in technology: you will be curious about emerging technologies, particularly telecoms and datacomms, and interested to solve complex problems – though we’re not expecting deep expertise, rather the desire to develop and grow. Curious and keen to learn: willing to take on unfamiliar problems, ask questions, and develop your understanding of new technologies and industries, supported by our experts. Collaborative and relationship-focused: able to work effectively with different people, build strong relationships with clients and colleagues, and support others to succeed. Clear and confident communicator: able to communicate complex ideas clearly, both written and verbal. Analytical and adaptable: able to structure unfamiliar problems, make sense of incomplete or messy information and develop logical, evidence-based conclusions. Modelling experience: experience using tools such as Excel, Python or MATLAB to analyse problems, build models, evaluate options or test hypotheses would be welcome. Understanding data: experience sourcing, processing, analysing and/or visualising data would be beneficial. The Offer You will work to ensure our clients stay informed about threats and are able to protect their digital assets and business systems. Since 2014, Wiremind has positioned itself as a technical company transforming the world of transport and events with a 360° approach combining UX, software, and AI . Our expertise lies primarily in optimizing and marketing our clients' capacity. We work on various projects such as ticket forecasting and pricing , 3D optimization of air freight or scraping competitor prices . Our applications are the preferred tool of companies such as SNCF, United Airlines, Qatar Airways or even PSG to visualize, analyze and optimize their capacity. Dynamic and ambitious, we strive to maintain our technical DNA which is the engine of our success. The company, profitable and self-financed since its creation 10 years ago, is mainly composed of engineers and experts and currently supports the growth of our business model based on "software-as-a-service" solutions. CARGOSTACK is a comprehensive SaaS solution that enables airlines to manage their air cargo operations. Build simple harness samples and install electrical components in heat pumps. Join lab troubleshooting sessions and assist with analyzing electrical issues. Help gather input for time plans. Support purchasing by reviewing specifications and participating in supplier meetings. Assist the manager with light administrative tasks. ## **About Storable** At Storable, we're redefining property management for specialty real estate. Powered by AI and three decades of industry data, Storable empowers over 33,000 self-storage facilities with the industry's only fully integrated technology platform. Our end-to-end solutions—from management software and demand generation to CRM tools and delinquency solutions—help storage operators streamline workflows, attract tenants, and grow revenue. Dedicated to empowering self-storage owners and operators, Storable helps you Win More every day. Explore our platform solutions at [](http://www.storable.com/). ## Overview Storable's centralized design team supports marketing and communications across RV/Camping, Marine, and Storage. As a Junior Graphic Designer, you'll turn clear briefs, templates, and brand guidelines into polished digital and print materials across channels. This hands-on role focuses on design execution with guidance from experienced designers. You'll develop your work through feedback, build strong production habits, and help the team deliver consistent materials across the business. This is a full-time role with three days per week in our Bellevue, Washington office, located near the light rail. ## **What you'll do every day** - Create digital and print materials, including campaign assets, presentations, sales collateral, and event materials. - Adapt designs for different formats, channels, and audiences while maintaining established brand standards. - Translate approved briefs and templates into accurate, polished design work. - Ask questions when requirements are unclear, share drafts for review, and communicate progress so the team can plan delivery. - Incorporate feedback and refine work through review cycles. - Prepare files for digital publishing and print production. - Check typography, layout, image quality, and visual hierarchy before delivery. - Organize source files, reusable assets, and final deliverables so colleagues can find and use them efficiently. - Improve templates and recurring production workflows as the team establishes consistent support across the business. - Use AI tools to explore concepts, adapt assets, and accelerate production while evaluating output for accuracy, accessibility, visual quality, and brand consistency. ## **What you need to bring** - A portfolio showing digital and print work with strong typography, layout, and visual hierarchy. Examples may be professional, academic, or self-directed and should demonstrate how you apply a brand system across materials. - Proficiency in Adobe Creative Cloud and Figma. - The ability to follow a brief, organize your work, communicate progress, and respond constructively to feedback. - A working understanding of preparing files for digital publishing and print production. - Experience using AI tools within design workflows, including exploration, asset adaptation, and production, with the judgment to evaluate and refine AI output. ## **Bonus points** - Experience supporting multiple brands, audiences, or business areas. - Familiarity with motion design, video, illustration, or basic animation. - Knowledge of accessibility principles for digital design. - Experience improving templates, asset libraries, or recurring production workflows. **All applicants must be currently authorized to work full-time in the United States and able to work a hybrid schedule in our Seattle, WA office.** *Storable is a fully distributed company, but is currently only registered for employment in certain states.* To be eligible for employment, you must reside in the following states: AL, AZ, CA, CO, CT, FL, GA, ID, IL, IN, IA, KS, LA, MD, MA, MI, MN, MO, MS, NC, NE, NJ, NV, NY, OH, OK, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA, WI, WY. **Benefits and Perks:** - Generous health coverage for you and your family, including fully paid short- and long-term disability coverage and two-times base salary life insurance. - 401(k) match after 60 days, 100% vested after 1 year. - Employer contribution to your HSA, plus an HRA to help offset your deductible. - Instant access to flexible vacation. **At a glance** **Location:** Cambridge **In-office expectation:** Usually once every two weeks, when your team is in **Employment type:** Paid internship, 10 weeks summer 2027 **Why this role exists:** To give people heading into their final year of university the chance to spend summer 2027 as a full member of one of our product teams, building software that database professionals around the world rely on. **About Redgate** Redgate brings together people who want to do their best work in an environment built on trust, accountability, and collaboration. We build solutions that help data professionals securely manage the data and databases that their organisations depend on. It’s a space that’s only becoming more critical as systems scale, data regulations increase, and AI adoption accelerates. **AI at Redgate** By 2028, Redgate will operate as an expert-plus-agent company: domain experts amplified by AI, delivering customer value at a pace our peers can’t match. AI handles the heavy lifting. Our people control the judgment. Everyone at Redgate works with Claude, giving you access to the best AI tools from day one. **Why join our software engineering team?** · You’ll join a product team as a full member, working on the same things as everyone else, not on a side project in a corner. · You’ll work in a team that cares about craft, collaboration, and quality. · There’s real support to grow, with your own intern manager for feedback and a buddy for everything else, plus protected time every week to learn and develop skills. **About the role** For 10 weeks, you’ll work alongside our engineers on real software, shipping features that real customers use. You’ll be part of the day-to-day life of the team, with the support and room to learn what a first role in software deserves. • Pair with engineers, get your code reviewed (and review theirs), and take part in standups, planning and retros. • Work on the same things as everyone else, using the same tools, including AI tools like Claude. • Spend every Friday afternoon (10% of your time) on learning, whether that’s lightning talks, a community of practice or building something of your own. • Last year’s interns merged code in their first week, shipped a feature customers had been asking for, fixed a customer support issue, ran team standups and retros, gave a talk to the wider company, and learned C# and .NET on the job to build their own project. *“I didn’t feel like an intern, I really felt like part of the team.”* **Kris Sananpanichkul, past software intern** **What makes you a great fit** You don’t need to tick every box. We care more about how you communicate, learn and work with others than how many lines of code you write. • You expect to graduate in 2028 with a degree in a relevant subject, and you’re available for the full 10 weeks. • You enjoy software and like figuring out how things work. • You communicate clearly, ask questions, and share what you learn. • You enjoy working as part of a team, including giving and receiving feedback. • You have the right to work in the UK (we can’t offer visa sponsorship for the internship). **How to apply** No cover letter needed. Just send your CV that includes: • **Education:** your course and year of graduation • **Work experience:** anything relevant, if you have it. It’s fine if you don’t. • **Something you’re proud of:** something you’ve built, fixed or figured out. It could be a uni project, a side project, a game mod, a Discord bot or a tricky bug. It all counts. • **What you want from this:** what you hope to learn or get out of the internship **What happens next?** Your application will be reviewed by a person. We don’t use AI or automated tools to assess applications. Every profile is read by one of our Talent Partners. You’ll hear back within a few days. Whether it’s a next step or a no, we aim to respond promptly so you’re not left waiting. **Belonging at Redgate** We believe that people do their best work in an environment built on respect, fairness, and trust, and that diverse perspectives lead to better outcomes. Redgate is an equal opportunity employer, and we make hiring decisions based on skill, potential, and alignment with our values. You can read more about how we approach belonging and inclusion at Redgate on our [Diversity at Redgate Software](https://www.red-gate.com/our-company/careers/belonging/) .

role: Extracurricular Internship: AI-Assisted Software Engineering Intern (f/m/div.)
description: Your contribution to something big: Join us in shaping the future of software engineering through Generative AI. As an AI-Assisted Software Engineering Intern, you will contribute to the development of innovative AI-powered solutions that support software engineers throughout the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC). Working alongside experienced engineers, you will research, prototype, and evaluate technologies that help improve development efficiency, software quality, and developer experience. In this role, you will: Research emerging AI-assisted software engineering workflows and identify opportunities to apply Generative AI across the SDLC. Design and develop automated solutions using LLM APIs, prompt engineering, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), AI agents, and context-window optimization techniques. Support the integration of AI-powered tools into software development workflows, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud environments. Define and implement metrics to evaluate the impact of AI solutions on productivity, software quality, usability, and adoption. Collaborate with software engineers to gather feedback, validate concepts, and continuously improve developed solutions. Contribute through code reviews, technical documentation, demonstrations, and knowledge-sharing activities. Explore and evaluate emerging AI technologies and translate them into practical developer tools. What distinguishes you? Education: Final-year Bachelor's or Master's student, or recent graduate (less than one year), in Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field. Experience: Initial academic, personal, or internship experience in software development or AI-related projects. Exposure to Generative AI technologies and modern software development practices is advantageous. Know-how: Knowledge of Python programming; experience with C or C++ is a plus. Familiarity with some of the following areas: LLM APIs, prompt engineering, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), AI agents, CI/CD pipelines, cloud platforms, or AI-assisted development tools. Understanding of software development processes and developer workflows. Languages: Good communication skills in English, both written and spoken. Working Style and Methods: Structured and analytical approach to problem-solving. Ability to learn independently and experiment with new technologies. Interest in transforming innovative AI concepts into practical engineering solutions. Personality: Curious, proactive, and eager to learn. Collaborative team player with strong communication skills. Passionate about software engineering, emerging technologies, and continuous improvement. What you can expect to learn How Generative AI can enhance software engineering activities across the Software Development Life Cycle. How to design, build, and integrate AI-powered developer tools using LLMs, RAG, AI agents, cloud services, and CI/CD platforms. How to measure the impact of AI solutions through meaningful metrics and developer-centric evaluations. How to bring innovative ideas from research and prototyping to adoption in real-world software development environments. How AI-driven engineering practices are applied in an international industrial environment. At Bosch, we value diversity and equal opportunities. The Bosch Group has more than 400 000 employees around the world, present in 60 countries, and we are proud to impact people’s lives and to work towards a more sustainable future. Bosch Car Multimedia, S.A. belongs to the Automotive Electronics division and is focused on making the vehicles our third living space. By including everyone and ensuring equal opportunities we unleash our full potential.

**PhD Internship 2027: Engineering - Boston** Boston, US | Full-time | Fixed-term| Hybrid Salary: $55.70 per hour, DOE **About us** Riverlane’s mission is to master quantum error correction (QEC) and unlock a new age of human progress. From advances in materials and climate science to complex chemistry simulation for new drug design, quantum computers will help humanity solve some of its most important challenges. But without QEC, the industry’s defining technical challenge, such breakthroughs can never be achieved. Riverlane is the world leader in QEC technology. QEC is a complex problem that requires a range of skills, talent, and passion. Having raised more than $125M in funding to date to accelerate our cutting-edge R&D in quantum error correction (QEC), Riverlane partners with many of the world’s leading quantum hardware providers and government agencies to make fault-tolerant quantum computing a reality. We’re making remarkable progress and growing fast. **About the role** Delivering practical quantum error correction requires tightly integrated quantum and classical systems. Decoding algorithms must process large volumes of error data within demanding latency, bandwidth, compute and power constraints. As an engineering Intern, you will investigate the classical computing architectures needed to support scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computers. Your project will sit at the intersection of quantum error correction, computer architecture and hardware-software co-design. Depending on the project, you could explore efficient QEC decoding or predecoding methods, model the classical resources required by fault-tolerant quantum programs, or investigate how decoding workloads can be distributed across different levels of a computing system. You will work alongside Riverlane’s researchers and engineers in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with support from a dedicated supervisor. Your work will contribute to our understanding of how QEC systems can meet the performance requirements of increasingly large quantum computers. **What you will do** - Contribute to a research project focused on the classical systems and architectures required for scalable quantum error correction - Investigate methods for reducing the compute, communication, memory, latency or power requirements associated with QEC - Develop algorithms, simulations or architectural models to evaluate potential approaches - Explore trade-offs between decoding performance, logical error suppression and classical resource requirements - Consider how QEC workloads could be implemented across software, FPGA, ASIC or other computing architectures - Collaborate with researchers and engineers working across QEC theory, decoding, software and hardware - Analyse results and communicate your findings through technical discussions, presentations and written reports - Produce clear, reproducible research code and supporting documentation **What we need** - You must be currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Mathematics or another related technical field - Research experience in at least one of the following areas: - Quantum error correction or fault-tolerant quantum computing - Computer architecture or quantum-classical systems - Decoding algorithms or error-correcting codes - FPGA, ASIC or digital hardware design - Experience developing computational models, simulations or research software - Proficiency in Python, C, C++ or another relevant programming language - A strong understanding of computer systems and architecture - Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills - The ability to communicate complex technical ideas clearly - The ability to take initiative and work effectively with researchers and engineers from different disciplines - Authorisation to work in the United States for the duration of the internship **Even better if…** - You have experience researching quantum LDPC or surface codes - You are familiar with QEC decoding or predecoding techniques - You have explored the classical resource requirements of fault-tolerant quantum computing - You have experience with hardware-software or compiler-hardware co-design - You have worked with RTL, SystemVerilog, FPGA or ASIC development workflows - You understand the latency, bandwidth or power constraints affecting quantum control and decoding systems - You have experience with scientific computing, quantum circuit simulation or QEC simulation tools - You have contributed to academic publications, open-source software or collaborative research projects **Important notes** - You must be legally authorized to work in the United States for the duration of the internship - If you intend to work under Curricular Practical Training (CPT), Optional Practical Training (OPT) or another form of student employment authorization, you are responsible for obtaining the necessary approval before your start date - Any offer of employment will be contingent upon verification of your identity and authorization to work in the United States, as required by law - You must be available to work full-time for 10 to 12 weeks - You will be required to sign an agreement assigning ownership of intellectual property produced during your internship to Riverlane - This internship is based at our US office in Cambridge, Massachusetts **How to apply** Please upload your CV and a cover letter. Your CV should include details of your education, research experience and relevant technical skills. Your cover letter should explain why you are applying for the internship and the skills and experience you would bring to the role. **Deadline** Please submit your application by **November 6th, 2026** **Pay and Expenses** We will reimburse reasonable expenses incurred as part of your role, such as approved travel to meetings or conferences. We are unable to cover the cost of travelling to Cambridge, Massachusetts at the beginning or end of the internship or accommodation during the internship. **What you can expect from us** You can expect a diverse and collaborative working environment that brings together experts in software and hardware development, quantum information theory, physics, mathematics and other technical fields. Our global team represents more than 20 nationalities. We also provide free snacks and refreshments and organize regular social and cultural events. If you have any questions, please contact [jobs@riverlane.com](mailto:jobs@riverlane.com). *Riverlane is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome qualified applicants and consider them for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law.* *We know that strong candidates may not meet every requirement listed. If you are interested in the opportunity and believe your experience could be relevant, we encourage you to apply.* *Riverlane provides reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. If you require an accommodation during the application or interview process, please let us know. We will be happy to help.*

La direction AI Digital Factory recrute un/une : Agro-Data Scientist F/H, pour un stage de 6 mois à Saint-Malo. Vous intégrez la direction AI Digital Factory, dont la mission est d'assurer la gestion et la valorisation des données du Groupe Roullier afin d'éclairer les décisions stratégiques et opérationnelles. En exploitant pleinement le potentiel de la data, cette direction joue un rôle essentiel dans l'optimisation des performances des activités du Groupe. Au sein de cette direction, l’Innovation Lab se positionne comme une cellule incubatrice d’idées, force de proposition de solution innovante pour la transformation des métiers et des activités du groupe. Le stage s’inscrit dans l’amélioration continue d’un outil d’OAD existant, reposant sur une combinaison de données satellitaires multi-temporelles (indices de végétation), de méthodologies statistiques et de machine learning et de courbes de référence de croissance. Plusieurs pistes d’amélioration de cet outil ont été identifiées. Le/la stagiaire sera amené(e) à les explorer à travers une démarche d’analyse structurée, à en évaluer les apports et les limites, et à être force de proposition dans la formulation de recommandations et de conclusions opérationnelles. Encadré(e) par un data scientist et en interaction avec des experts agronomiques, vous serez amené(e) à travailler sur tout ou partie des axes suivants, en menant une démarche scientifique structurée : - Analyser et améliorer des méthodologies statistiques appliquées à des données agronomiques et satellitaires (intervalles de confiance, loi de distributions, robustesse, biais, sensibilité aux paramètres) - Concevoir et tester des modèles de machine learning (classification, détection de dérives, exploitation de séries temporelles, approches multi-variables) - Travailler sur la qualité et la fiabilité des données (détection de données aberrantes, filtres qualité, impact des données imparfaites sur les modèles) - Exploiter et interpréter des indices de végétation et données d’imagerie satellite (compréhension agronomique, limites physiques, complémentarité des indices) Les différents axes traités lors du stage ainsi que le cadre de travail associé seront définis avec le/la stagiaire, en fonction de ses appétences, de ses compétences et de la durée du stage.

# Company Overview Each year, 2.5 trillion hours are spent on household chores. At Matic, we’re on a mission to recapture that lost time, and we’re doing it by revolutionizing home robotics. Our first product, also called Matic, is a Wall-E-esque floor cleaning robot. We've built what amounts to "full self-driving in the home” with real-time 3D mapping, adaptive path-tracking, and a precise semantic understanding of the home. Our breakthroughs in spatial AI allow Matic to work reliably in real homes, using only RGB cameras and neural networks running on-device. ## Privacy First What happens in the home, stays in the home. Our robots are private by design, with all data processing performed by the robot itself, not in the cloud. ## Our Approach Before the iPhone, consumers adopted several distinct devices; cell phones, PDAs, and portable music players each served a particular need. We believe in a similar progression for home robotics, starting with single-purpose robots and building iteratively toward more complex capabilities over time. ## Our Culture Matic is a tight-knit and collaborative team, singularly focused on building products our customers will cherish. We're ultra-hardworking people committed to solving tough problems that save precious time and energy. # **About the role** You'll own parts and sub-assemblies with support from experienced engineers, contributing from concept through high volume production. Our robots are shipping to customers today, which means the parts you work on get tooled, built at volume, and used daily in someone's home. You'll have the opportunity to see your work in the field within months, not years. This is an internship for someone who wants to get their hands on real hardware immediately and build the judgment that comes from watching designs succeed and fail in production. **What you'll do** - Design parts and sub-assemblies within a defined architecture, and help carry them through to mass production - Build your own prototypes, break them, and iterate fast - Run component level testing for performance, durability, and part to part variability - Help write and execute accelerated test plans that predict field behavior - Create production-ready 2D drawings with guidance and review from the team - Work with engineers, vendors, and CMs on DFM feedback, tooling reviews, and first article inspection - Collaborate with EE, firmware, software, and industrial design to keep your parts balanced against the rest of the system **What we look for** - Parts or assemblies you personally designed and built through internships, project teams, research, or personal projects, and the ability to explain your design decisions - Familiarity with high volume manufacturing processes such as injection molding, die casting, stamping, or metal injection molding, and an interest in learning how they shape a design - An understanding of tolerances and how individual part dimensions affect an assembly - Familiarity with engineering drawings and basic GD&T - SolidWorks proficiency and experience using CAD to build real hardware - A hands-on approach to prototyping, testing, and troubleshooting - An ability to reason from a failure back to a possible design or manufacturing cause - Comfort in a fast-paced startup where the answer is often “go build it and find out” Currently pursuing a degree in mechanical engineering or a related technical field, or demonstrating equivalent hands-on experience. Prior experience with FEA, PDM/PLM, or production hardware is a plus, but not required. **Engineering Culture at Matic** We're a small team building a hard product. The work doesn't sort itself into a clean design lane. During your internship, you'll work on concepts and CAD. You'll also build test fixtures, run tolerance studies, troubleshoot life tests, tear down returned units, update drawings, and learn how parts move from a design to a production line. None of that is beneath the job. All of it is the job, and most of it is where you'll get good. Our engineers own their parts from the first sketch to the last field failure, including every unglamorous step in between. As an intern, you'll take on meaningful pieces of that work with support and feedback from the team. We keep design, testing, supplier work, and documentation together on purpose, because that's how you build the judgment to design something that actually survives a home. The same goes past your own scope. If a fixture in the lab is broken, if data needs cleaning, if a different subsystem is blocking the build, people here move toward it. Scope is how we plan the work, not how we decide what's ours. That's the shape of the team we're building. Being excited about a particular kind of engineering is great and we want that. But the people who've done the most for this company are the ones who wanted Matic to win first and picked up whatever that took. **We'd love to hear from you if...** - You are genuinely motivated to help those around you - You are passionate about learning outside your normal comfort zones - You love diagnosing complex technical issues - You take pride in details nobody else would notice ## **Compensation** Base: $25- $35/hour. Actual Compensation will depend on skills, experience, and qualifications.

**About Amplify** Amplify helps teachers bring delight and rigor to students every day. We have become a leader in K–12 literacy, biliteracy, math, and science by building inspiring teaching and learning experiences based on research. The Amplify Classroom platform combines curriculum, assessment, and supplemental learning into one coherent high-quality instructional system. A pioneer in education since 2000, Amplify has developed deep relationships in states and districts by partnering with educators to drive implementation quality and improved outcomes. Today, Amplify serves more than 18 million students and teachers across all 50 states and on six continents. description: # **About Nu** Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services. Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability. Visit our [Institutional Page](https://www.nu.com/2026-en) ## **About the Program** The Nu AI Core Summer Internship Program is a research-focused internship for PhD students working at the frontier of artificial intelligence and machine learning. Over about 12 weeks, interns collaborate with engineers, applied scientists, and researchers on complex AI challenges. Each intern leads an end-to-end research or applied AI project that combines research methods with large-scale production environments. The program builds long-term relationships between industry and academia and with emerging AI research talent. # **Program Structure** - **Duration:** ~12 weeks - **Start dates:** May–June, aligned with US university calendars - **Location model**: Remote, with one in-person week at Nu's Palo Alto office in Silicon Valley, fully covered by us. **What you get** - Dedicated research mentor - Ownership of a scoped AI research project - Access to large-scale datasets and compute infrastructure - Research talks and technical seminars - Final research presentation to leadership and AI teams # **Research Areas** Interns may work on projects related to: - **Machine learning and deep learning** - **Large language models and generative AI** - **Recommender systems and ranking models** - **AI infrastructure and model optimization** - **Responsible AI and model evaluation** Projects typically combine **research experimentation with applied system development**, including model design, experimentation, and large-scale evaluation. # **Candidate Profile** This program targets **PhD students conducting research in AI and machine learning** who are interested in applying their work to real-world systems. Applicants are typically pursuing a PhD in fields such as: - Computer Science - Machine Learning - Artificial Intelligence - Statistics - Mathematics - Computational Linguistics - Electrical Engineering - or related quantitative disciplines. # **Basic Qualifications (Application/ Screening Filters)** - Currently enrolled in a PhD program - Research focus in machine learning, AI, statistics or related areas - Strong programming skills in Python or similar languages - Experience working with machine learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) - Experience designing experiments and evaluating models - Experience working with large datasets or training ML models # **Preferred Qualifications** Strong candidates may also demonstrate: - Publications at top AI/ML conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, KDD, RecSys, CVPR, CIKM or equivalent-conferences for related fields) - Experience working with large-scale ML systems or distributed training - Experience with LLMs, generative AI, or foundation models - Open-source contributions in AI or ML - Experience collaborating in interdisciplinary research environments # **What We Value** We are particularly interested in candidates who demonstrate: - Strong research rigor and experimental methodology - Ability to translate research ideas into practical systems - Track record of identifying novel research directions or reframing existing problems - Intellectual curiosity and independent problem solving - Collaboration with engineers and cross-functional teams - Interest in deploying AI systems with real-world impact # **Benefits** - Top Tier Medical Insurance - Top Tier Dental and Vision Insurance - Life Insurance and AD&D - Extended maternity and paternity leaves - Nucleo - Our learning platform of courses - NuLanguage - Our language learning program - NuCare - Our mental health and wellness assistance program - 401K - Saving Plans - Health Saving Account and Flexible Spending Account # **Location for this opportunity** Remote, but only for USA PhD students ## Our recruitment process may involve the use of artificial intelligence–enabled tools, such as automated interview transcription and analysis, to support the evaluation process. Artificial intelligence is not used to make final hiring decisions; all decisions are made by human reviewers. To maintain a consistent and fair process for every candidate, Nu does not provide individualized technical feedback. Meter is a vertically integrated networking company. Hardware, software, services, ISP, and autonomous networks run on a single data pipeline, from the local network to the data center. Most of the networking industry treats hardware as a commodity–we don’t. Build the hardware right, and everything above it gets better. Meter designs its own Firewalls, Switches, Wireless Access Points, PDUs, and Gateways because customers subscribe to the network instead of buying individual boxes; we're accountable for how the hardware performs for years. We sweat details most people never see, like the logo stamped inside the enclosure and the sound spec on our fans. Great hardware takes more than designing circuits and shipping products: It means thinking hard about performance, reliability, manufacturability, supply chain, installation, sustainability, and the full product lifecycle. We’re hiring Hardware Engineering Interns to solve real technical problems across Meter’s hardware engineering and operations teams. Over 12 weeks, you’ll own a well-scoped project picked to fit your interests, your experience, and the problems that matter most to Meter: - Next-generation power adapters: Prototype compact, efficient power supplies that could ship in future Meter products. - Hardware lifecycle and sustainability: Figure out how Meter hardware can be refurbished, reused, or recycled, and what it takes to extend its life. - Installer tooling: Build tools, fixtures, or diagnostic devices that make Meter networks faster to install and troubleshoot. - Acoustics and thermal systems: Design quiet, efficient cooling for future high-performance networking and data center products. - Supply chain intelligence: Use component and supplier data to spot risks and bottlenecks before they hit a hardware build. ## **What success looks like** You’ll take a meaningful hardware problem from an open question to a recommendation backed by evidence, and leave behind something the hardware team can use: data, prototypes, test results, engineering requirements, supplier evaluations, or tools. Your day-to-day will depend on your project, but you may: - Design, build, and test electrical or mechanical prototypes for future Meter products - Evaluate components, technologies, architectures, materials, and suppliers - Write test plans and characterize performance, reliability, thermals, acoustics, power, and other system-level behavior - Work with our manufacturing partners in Taiwan to understand their capabilities, constraints, cost, and scalability - Present your findings and recommendations to the hardware team at the end of the internship ## **Who you are** You’re curious, hands-on, and you learn by building. You’re a good fit if: - You’re pursuing a degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related technical field - You like taking an ambiguous technical problem and breaking it into questions you can answer through engineering and experimentation - You’ve built, tested, debugged, or taken apart hardware on a design team, in a lab, or at home, or you’re eager to start - You’re comfortable working with physical systems: PCBAs, mechanical assemblies, test equipment, prototypes, manufacturing data, or supplier samples - You can explain technical findings clearly and turn your work into recommendations others can act on Experience with PCB design, CAD, embedded systems, thermal design, or data analysis is a plus, but none of it is required. Above all, we’re looking for people who want to understand how great hardware gets built. ## **Why Meter?** The internet runs the world. Every purchase you make and every video call you join is packets moving through networks. But those networks haven’t changed in decades. They’re brittle, complex, and surprisingly hard to set up for a business. We started Meter to build better networks, and that meant building everything ourselves: our own enterprise hardware, intuitive software, and streamlined operations. Today we deploy those networks at scale. Bridgewater, Lyft, Reddit, and the San Antonio Spurs rely on Meter to keep thousands of employees and locations online. Our bet is simple: Everyone will use the internet more than they do today. Meter is building the networking stack that makes connectivity as easy and reliable as water or electricity. ## **Compensation** - The estimated pay for this role is $40–$50 per hour. This role is also eligible for a relocation and housing stipend. By applying to this job you acknowledge that you've read and understood [Meter's Job Applicant Privacy Notice](https://www.meter.com/careers/job-applicant-privacy). ## **Timeline** - **Applications open through November 17:** We review applications on a rolling basis, so applying early is encouraged. - **Initial screens:** November - **Final interviews:** Early December. Final interviews may be held in person. - **Offers extended:** Mid-December - **Offer decision deadline:** End of December

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. **ABOUT THE TEAM** The Air Dominance and Strike Low Observable Team are advancing into the next generation of LO Technology to enhance the survivability and effectiveness of unmanned air systems. Our Low Observables engineering team is responsible for designing, analyzing, testing, and sustaining stealth features that reduce radar (RCS) and infrared (IR) signatures, ensuring our systems remain undetectable in contested environments. **ABOUT THE ROLE** This is an intern role open to engineers finishing a degree in aerospace, electrical, or mechanical engineering. Low Observables work sits at the intersection of all three: the shape of the air vehicle, the electromagnetic behavior of its surfaces, and the materials and processes used to build it. You do not need prior stealth experience. Almost nobody arrives with it, because most of it cannot be taught outside a cleared program. We will teach you the LO-specific methods. What we are looking for is strong engineering fundamentals, comfort picking up unfamiliar analysis tools, and the judgment to tell a real result from a bad one. You will be paired with an LO engineer and start on a scoped piece of a live program, not a training exercise. **WHAT YOU'LL DO:** - Run broadband Radar Cross Section (RCS) analysis on components and full air vehicles, and learn to judge when a prediction can be trusted - Support the design and development of Low Observable unmanned air systems, from early configuration trades through detailed design - Build and improve the analysis tools, scripts, and validation workflows the team runs on - Model LO materials and treatments, and help select and optimize them for specific components - Support manufacturing and validation planning, including tolerances, inspection methods, and what is actually producible at rate - Help plan and execute RCS measurement campaigns in indoor chambers and on outdoor ranges, then reduce and interpret the data - Compare measured results against predictions, chase down the disagreements, and feed what you learn back into the models **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS** - Must be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field. - Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester. - Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program. - Ability to complete an in-person 12-week internship in one of our offices in summer 2027. **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:** - Coursework in at least one of: electromagnetics or RF, aircraft or vehicle design, or materials and manufacturing processes - Working knowledge of a scripting or analysis language such as MATLAB, Python, or C++ - Familiarity with a 3D CAD package such as NX, CATIA, SolidWorks, or Creo - Demonstrated hands-on engineering work: a capstone or senior design project, internship, undergraduate research, or a student competition team - Ability to explain a technical result clearly, in writing and in a design review - Exposure to any electromagnetic simulation tool, such as HFSS, CST, FEKO, or COMSOL. X-Patch, SENTRi, and McMoM2D are government codes and we do not expect you to have used them - Coursework or project experience with composites, additive manufacturing, casting, or injection molding - Experience with laboratory RF measurement: network analyzers, anechoic chambers, or antenna pattern measurement - Experience reducing, visualizing, and sanity-checking measured data sets - A prior internship or co-op in aerospace, defense, or another hardware-heavy environment US Hourly Range $34—$50 USD The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only.
