At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. **About the Team:** The Stage Manufacturing team turns design into reality, owning the build of Terran R’s primary structures. This isn’t about turning the same bolt every day; it’s about building the systems to build the rocket. Engineers and technicians work side by side, with deep collaboration and real-time feedback, to shape how we build better and faster. With a manifest and a launch date, it’s up to the team to deliver on Terran R: solving challenges in real time, optimizing for scale, and constantly improving processes. As the vehicle evolves, so will the factory, with opportunities to apply automation, machine learning, and advanced technologies. What we build here sets the blueprint for the future of scaled launch. **About the Role:** - Own Forming operations within the work center, being responsible for delivery of all formed products and improving both roll forming and press brake process - Bring online a press brake work center and lead the development effort for the company to be capable of forming up to 20’ sheets of material for our rocket primary structure - Create work instructions, specifications, and best practices across multiple high-fidelity processes - Help standardize processes across the manufacturing team - Support the shop floor through live issue resolution and provide upstream feedback as we innovate the next generation of manufacturing technology - Provide Design for Manufacturing feedback to structures teams during the development phase and through the first prototype and flight builds **About You:** - Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing, mechanical engineering, or other engineering discipline - 1+ years progressive and related experience required, including internship experience - A history of improving manufacturing processes and the ability to independently identify and lead development projects needed to meet processing requirements - Strong engineering fundamentals in process improvement, forming, metallic processing, mechanics of materials - Deep knowledge of common metallic manufacturing processes, tools, inspection methods and GD&T - Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to interface with engineering and manufacturing groups to understand process constraints and provide design inputs for improved manufacturability - Strong 3D & 2D design/drafting skills per ASME Y14.5M (NX preferred) **Nice to have, but not required:** - Direct experience with roll forming and press brake forming aluminum alloys - New product introduction of an aerospace hardware system into a manufacturing, test, and production system with proven success - Experience in managing projects in a fast-paced environment At Relativity Space, we are committed to transparency and fairness in our compensation practices. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors. Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit [here.](https://px.sequoia.com/relativityspace) Hiring Range: $90,000—$136,000 USD **We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. description: ## About Us Founded in 1986, ChenMoore has grown into a highly regarded multi-disciplinary firm. ChenMoore’s areas of expertise include utility infrastructure, roadway, site development, electrical, planning, landscape architecture, and construction engineering services for both private and public sector clients. ChenMoore prides itself on working to be part of the fabric of the community. We are leaders in community service and the profession. Our staff and our activities are centered around making the community we work in a better place to live. ChenMoore promotes a fun and flexible work environment, taking pride in the quality of our work. ChenMoore promotes a team-oriented approach, both inside and outside of the office. ChenMoore's headquarters are in Fort Lauderdale with regional offices in Miami, West Palm Beach, Orlando, and Jacksonville. The firm also has satellite and/or project offices in Atlanta, Gainesville, Jupiter, Knoxville, Pensacola, Port St. Lucie, Raleigh, Sarasota, Tallahassee, and Tampa. ChenMoore currently employs over one hundred and seventy (180) professionals, which affords our valued clients a top-level service. ChenMoore is hiring Electrical Engineering Interns for our 2027 Internship Program. Through the firm’s paid internship program, you will gain exposure to real-world engineering projects, tools, and processes to bridge academic knowledge with applied practice. As part of the ChenMoore team, you will develop technical, professional, and collaboration skills in a culture rooted in our values: People-forward, Client-driven, and Community-centered. We offer internship opportunities both during the summer and throughout the academic year, with many interns returning for additional semesters and as full-time engineers. As an Electrical Engineering Intern, you will support our Power Delivery practice. You’ll also have opportunities to work with professionals across the firm and gain insight on diverse areas of expertise and perspectives that contribute to successful project delivery for the community. **Responsibilities:** - Work on challenging projects that require collaboration within and among various departments. - Contribute to team projects and individual tasks assigned in the discipline you support. - Prepare project design drawings within MicroStation and/or AutoCAD. - Develop project specific detail drawings. - Calculate project construction quantity estimates. - Assist with technical specifications, cost estimates, reports, schedules, and other related tasks. - Learn and adhere to client-specific standards. - Coordinate with team members and client representatives. - Periodic travel to project sites for field investigation and or construction support. - Demonstrate proactive, curious, and positive attitude. - Represent ChenMoore's values through engagement and professionalism. **Qualifications**: - Currently pursuing a Master's or Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, or related field. - Strong academic performance and interest in engineering consulting. - Demonstrated familiarity of engineering or drafting software (Civil3D, MicroStation, GIS). - Ability to quickly learn and apply complex systems. - Willingness to develop in ChenMoore's values rooted in community and client-service. ## ChenMoore's High Standard of Professionalism ChenMoore is a company which is unique in its commitment to quality. We are proud of our high standard of professionalism and the quality of service provided to our clients. We strive to establish a sense of pride and loyalty in our employees by maintaining a tradition of excellence in our work and a sense of family in our culture. We also aim to provide an environment that inspires and promotes individuals to reach the full extent of their potential and to continue in their personal “Search for Excellence.” We offer a career opportunity rather than a job – an opportunity that will take our employees as far as they want it to go. You will find that both the management and employees of ChenMoore are dedicated to high achievement and genuinely concerned about employee job satisfaction. In order for us to maintain high standards of excellence, we endeavor to have the finest personnel and only acquire those whom we consider to not only meet the high standards we set for ourselves as a firm, but those who will also blend with the firm culture. Your success is important to all of us. **ChenMoore is a Great Place to Work!** - Named "Top 500 Design Firm" nationally by ENR - Named ‘Best Places to Work For’ nationally by the Zweig Group in the Multidiscipline Firm Category from 2008-2010 and 2014–2025. - Named to the ‘Hot Firm’s List’ nationally by the Zweig Group from 2007-2011, 2014, 2016-2025. - ChenMoore is regularly recognized as a ‘Best Firm to Work For’ by the South Florida Business Journal, Civil + Structural Engineer, ENR Southeast, and various local branches of the American Society of Civil Engineers. **OUR BENEFITS** include: - Medical, Vision and Dental Insurance - Life and AD&D Insurance - Voluntary Life with Dependent Coverage - Short-Term and Long-Term Disability - Paid time off and paid holidays - Flexible Spending Accounts with Debit Card - Voluntary Plans (Supplement Health, Critical Illness/Cancer, Accident) - 401(k) Plan – Competitive Employer Match - Supplemental benefits - Flexible work schedules - Continuing education - Mentorship programs - Professional societies - Community engagement - Cell phone We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. We’re looking for experienced engineers to join our fast-growing engineering team to help us develop a 24x7 global infrastructure system that powers DoorDash’s three-sided marketplace of consumers, merchants, and dashers. ## **About the Role** This intern will report into a manager on the Assignment Engine team. We believe interns are essential to our mission of attracting and retaining top talent. During the 12 week Operations Research internship, interns will be completely immersed in their teams and will have the opportunity to develop, maintain & ship products. As an intern, you will directly impact our business by collaborating with your team to solve real problems for our customers. Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. to be considered for this position. F-1 students are eligible if they are using Curricular Practical Training (CPT). DoorDash does not support students on J-1 visas at this time. This position will be hosted in person at the DoorDash office in Sunnyvale, CA. #LI-Onsite ## **You're excited about this opportunity because you will…** - Design and implement improvements to our real-time on-demand dispatching algorithm - Analyze data to understand each delivery at the lowest level of detail, perform cutting-edge research, and inspire new lines of work - Collaborate with engineers, data scientists, product managers, business operators, and more to develop cross-cutting and scalable solutions to guide value for our consumers, dashers, and merchants - Receive actionable feedback from your mentor and team members - Socialize with and learn from colleagues all across the company, through events including Lunch and Learns with executive members, game nights, movie nights, intern offsites, and more ## **We're excited about you because…** - Are a PhD student in operations research, industrial engineering, computer science or a related field graduating between Fall 2027 and Summer 2028 - Have research or industry experience working on complex optimization problems through mathematical programming or metaheuristics - Have strong programming fundamentals, experience in object-oriented and/or functional programming languages, and a solid understanding of algorithms - Have an excitement to analyze, iterate, and contribute to our state-of-the-art real-time dispatch system - Experience developing algorithms for logistics problems, especially VRP and real-time dispatching problem - Experience with mathematical programming software packages like Cplex, Gurobi, Coin-OR, or Xpress - Production experience with a JVM-based language (ie Java, Kotlin, Scala) - Experience with software development lifecycle (writing clean code, version control, unit testing, etc) - Production experience with modern web applications at scale - Experience with statistical analysis and machine learning algorithms - Proficient in SQL and a visualization tool (ie Tableau, Chartio, Mode) Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis **Compensation** Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location. Base salary is localized according to employee work location. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others. To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page [here](https://careers.doordash.com/). See below for paid time off details: - **For salaried roles:** flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year. - **For hourly roles:** vacation accrued at about 1 hour for every 25.97 hours worked (e.g. about 6.7 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 3.4 hours/month if working 20 hours/week), and paid sick time accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (e.g. about 5.8 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 2.9 hours/month if working 20 hours/week). The national base pay range for this position within the United States, including Illinois and Colorado. $130,600—$192,000 USD ## About DoorDash At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods. DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more. ## Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel. Statement of Non-Discrimination: In keeping with our beliefs and goals, no employee or applicant will face discrimination or harassment based on: race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, age, gender, marital/domestic partner status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability status, or veteran status. Above and beyond discrimination and harassment based on “protected categories,” we also strive to prevent other subtler forms of inappropriate behavior (i.e., stereotyping) from ever gaining a foothold in our office. Whether blatant or hidden, barriers to success have no place at DoorDash. We value a diverse workforce – people who identify as women, non-binary or gender non-conforming, LGBTQIA+, American Indian or Native Alaskan, Black or African American, Hispanic or Latinx, Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander, differently-abled, caretakers and parents, and veterans are strongly encouraged to apply. Thank you to the Level Playing Field Institute for this statement of non-discrimination. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, and any other state or local hiring regulations, we will consider for employment any qualified applicant, including those with arrest and conviction records, in a manner consistent with the applicable regulation. **If you need any accommodations, please inform your recruiting contact upon initial connection.** **Notice Regarding Use of AI and Automated Tools:** To streamline our hiring process, DoorDash utilizes an automated recruitment tool called Metaview. **How it works:**Metaview assists our recruiting team by evaluating job related qualifications and characteristics in connection with hiring. The tool is designed and used to support - rather than replace - human decision-making; trained personnel make final decisions with meaningful human review and oversight, and DoorDash does not use Metaview or other AI-enabled tool in a manner that has the effect of subjecting applicants or employees to discrimination based on any protected characteristic or proxy or for engaging in any protected activity under applicable law. **Data Retention, Privacy & Bias Audit:** Data collected during this process is retained in accordance with our Candidate Privacy Policy and applicable state laws. role: AI Research Intern: Wireless Foundation Models
description: At Bosch Research in Pittsburgh, we are looking for an enthusiastic research intern to advance the state of the art in foundation models for wireless sensing and perception. The intern will explore how large-scale self-supervised and multimodal learning can enable generalizable representations of human activities and environments from radio-frequency (RF) signals and wireless channel measurements. The research will focus on developing foundation models that learn reusable representations from diverse wireless sensing data and transfer across sensing tasks, environments, devices, and users. Potential applications include human presence detection, activity recognition, motion understanding, and fine-grained behavioral and contextual understanding. The intern will work closely with Bosch researchers on the following responsibilities: Develop novel foundation-model architectures and representation-learning methods for RF signals and wireless channel measurements. Investigate self-supervised, contrastive, generative, and multimodal learning approaches for large-scale wireless sensing data. Study model generalization and adaptation across environments, users, devices, and downstream perception tasks. Develop and evaluate methods for fine-tuning, few-shot learning, or zero-shot transfer to downstream wireless perception applications. Conduct comprehensive experimental evaluations and comparisons with state-of-the-art approaches. Develop a proof-of-concept demonstration of the proposed technology. Summarize research findings and contribute to a high-quality research publication and/or patent application. Required Qualifications: Currently enrolled in a PhD program in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, or a related field. Strong background in machine learning, deep learning, or representation learning. Experience working with wireless sensing or RF signal data, including channel measurements or related time-series signals. Strong understanding of modern deep-learning architectures and training techniques. 2+ years of programming experience in Python and strong proficiency with PyTorch. Ability to independently design, implement, and evaluate research ideas. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Experience with self-supervised learning, foundation models, transformers, contrastive learning, or generative models. Experience with wireless sensing for applications such as presence detection, activity recognition, localization, or smart-home sensing. Experience collecting and processing wireless channel measurements, complex I/Q samples, signal-strength data, or related RF sensing data. Experience with RF data-acquisition pipelines, wireless signal preprocessing, or time-series feature extraction. Experience with multimodal learning involving wireless signals, language, vision, audio, or other sensor modalities. Experience with large-scale model training, distributed training, or GPU-based experimentation. Strong publication record in leading machine learning, sensing, mobile computing, or robotics venues such as ICLR, NeurIPS, ICML, SenSys, IPSN, MobiSys, MobiCom, IMWUT/UbiComp, or IROS. L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale regroupant 38 pays Membres, qui œuvre pour la mise en place de politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. **About Clutch:** We’re on a mission to reinvent the way people buy, sell, and own cars. Are you game? Clutch is Canada’s largest online used car retailer, delivering a seamless, hassle-free car buying and selling experience to drivers everywhere. Customers can browse hundreds of cars from the comfort of their home, get the right one delivered to their door, and enjoy peace of mind with our 10-Day Money-Back Guarantee… and that’s just the beginning. Named to The Globe and Mail’s list of Canada’s Top Growing Companies for six consecutive years and also awarded spots on Deloitte’s Technology Fast 50™ and Fast 500™ lists, we’re looking to add curious, hard-working, and driven individuals to our growing team. Headquartered in Toronto, Clutch was founded in 2017 and currently services Ontario, British Columbia, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, and Prince Edward Island. Clutch is backed by a number of world-class investors, including D1 Capital, Altos Ventures, BMO Capital Partners, Canaan, Real Ventures, and others. To learn more, visit [](https://clutch.ca/). **What you'll work on** On an assembly line, every unit is the same. In our reconditioning facility, no two cars are the same. One car needs brakes and a detail; the next needs suspension work, bodywork and a part we have to order. Building standard work, staffing models and layouts around that kind of variation is the engineering problem you'll be working on. As a Production Development Engineering Intern, you'll own one main project, start to finish, and support one or two smaller ones. You'll agree on the main project and its target with your manager by the end of week two. Projects we expect to have this term include: - **Standardized work.** Time-study a process within our production areas (Inspection, Mechanical, or Detail). Separate the steps that add value from the ones that don't, and write the standard work the process runs on. - **Finding the bottleneck.** Use our production data to map cycle time and wait time across the stations, find where cars sit longest, and test a fix on the floor. - **QC and rework.** Break down why cars fail QC or come back for rework, pick the top causes, and work with mechanics and leads on a change we can measure before your term ends. - **Layout.** Redesign a bay or work area in CAD and make the case for it with data. - **Capital project support.** Help scope an equipment or facility project: gather vendor quotes and track timeline and budget. - **Present.** You will have an opportunity to present your achievements to the executive team at the end of your co-op. **What your term looks like** - **Weeks 1 to 2: Learn the floor.** Safety training, time at every station, and shadowing mechanics and production leads. You'll finish with a one-page project plan: the problem, the baseline number, and the target. - **Weeks 3 to 8: Measure.** Collect data, run your studies, and share what you're finding at a mid-term review with engineering. - **Weeks 9 to 14: Change something.** Pilot your recommendation on the floor with the team, and measure whether it worked. - **Weeks 15 to 16: Hand it off.** Present results to engineering and production leadership, and document your work so the team keeps using it after you leave. **What you'll get** - A weekly 1:1 with the Director of Engineering, and a buddy on the team for day-to-day questions. - Lean tools used for real (time studies, standard work, 5S, value stream mapping) in an operation where the input changes with every car. - A view of the whole business, from the day we buy a car to the day a customer takes delivery. - Gain hands-on experience delivering measurable improvements and building tangible project outcomes you can showcase in your engineering career. - Strong performers will be considered for future co-op terms and for our Production Engineering Analyst roles. **Who we're looking for:** We care more about how you think than about whether you have done this exact work before. If you like figuring out why something is slow and then fixing it, you will do well here. - Currently enrolled in Mechanical, Mechatronics, Management, Systems Design, or a related engineering program. - Comfortable working with data in Excel or Google Sheets (pivot tables, charts, basic formulas). - Some exposure to CAD (SolidWorks, AutoCAD, Fusion 360, or similar) through coursework, a design team, or a previous co-op. - Happy to spend a large part of your day on a shop floor, asking mechanics questions and listening to their answers. - Clear communicator who can explain a recommendation to both an operator and a director. **Nice to have:** - A previous co-op in manufacturing, automotive, logistics, or operations. - Coursework in operations research, lean manufacturing, or statistics (SPC, Pareto). - Experience on a student design team, such as Formula Electric or Midnight Sun. - Python or SQL, or experience using AI tools to speed up analysis. **Why You'll Love it at Clutch** - Make an Impact: Help shape the future of car buying and selling in Canada by leading a critical part of our customer experience. - Career Growth: Join a rapidly growing company with opportunities for leadership and professional development. - Great Team: Work alongside talented, driven, and collaborative colleagues who are passionate about what they do. **Location:** 3360 Wolfedale Road, Mississauga, ON (5 days a week on-site) **Term:** January–April 2027 (4 months), with the potential to extend through August 2027 **Schedule:** Full-time, Monday to Friday (8:30am-4:30pm) **Pay:** $26–$30 per hour This posting is for a new position, open vacancy. role: 2027 Summer Intern, PhD, Research Scientist, Visual Reasoning
description: Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states. The mission of the Waymo AI Foundations team is to develop machine learning solutions addressing open problems in autonomous driving, towards the goal of safely operating Waymo vehicles in dozens of cities and under all driving conditions. As part of our work, we also initiate and foster collaborations with other research teams in Alphabet. AI Foundations areas that we are currently focusing on include reinforcement learning, learning from demonstration, generative modeling, Bayesian inference, hierarchical learning, and robust evaluation. Waymo interns partner with leaders in the industry on projects that create impact to the company. We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. Join us at Waymo for a fun and rewarding internship! **You will:** - Research and develop novel visual and spatio-temporal reasoning methods for multimodal Perception Foundation Models using AV sensor data - Design and implement post-training recipes—including Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL)—to improve perception generalization in long-tail autonomous driving scenarios - Conduct large-scale experiments and ablation studies on autonomous driving benchmarks, with the opportunity to publish findings at top-tier AI/CV conferences (e.g., CVPR/ICCV/ECCV/NeurIPS/ICLR/ICML) **You have:** - Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, Electrical Engineering or a related technical field - Hands-on experience & strong publications in perception, and/or LLM/VLM - Knowledge of pre-training and post-training of the large foundation models - Strong Python coding skills with expertise in modern deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow) **We prefer:** - Experience with visual reasoning for LLM/VLM/robotics/driving - Experience with RL training in LLM/VLM/robotics - Experience with open-vocabulary perception Note: This will be a hybrid onsite internship position. We will accept resumes on a rolling basis until the role is filled. To be in consideration for multiple roles, you will need to apply to each one individually - please apply to the top 3 roles you are interested in. The expected hourly rate for this full-time position is listed below. Interns are also eligible to participate in the Company’s generous benefits programs, subject to eligibility requirements. Hourly PhD Pay $85—$85 USD

Boîte à questions Ubisoft Comment préparer ma candidature chez Ubisoft ? Dans un premier temps, lisez attentivement la job description afin de mettre en avant vos expériences et vos compétences qui vous semblent pertinentes pour cette opportunité ! Un CV personnalisé et détaillé vous permettra à coup sûr de vous démarquer 😉 Lettre de motivation ou pas ? A choisir, nous préférerons toujours quelques lignes expliquant votre motivation à candidater, plutôt qu’un texte générique copié/collé ! Un encart est d’ailleurs spécifiquement prévu à cet effet lors de votre candidature. N’hésitez à consulter notre article JobTeaser pour plus de conseils ! Je ne connais pas le secteur du jeu vidéo. Pour en savoir plus, rendez-vous sur la page Impact Sociétal . Je suis en situation de handicap, comment postuler ? Toutes nos équipes recrutement ont été sensibilisées aux sujets du handicap. location: Amsterdam, North Holland, Netherlands; London, England, United Kingdom; New York; Singapore
description: At Graviton, every strategy, model and edge begins not with instinct, but with someone asking a better question than everyone else. As a Quantitative Research Intern, you'll spend 10-12 weeks working on research that directly shapes how we understand markets and build trading strategies. You'll collaborate with researchers and technologists to investigate market behaviour, test hypotheses, build predictive models and solve problems where the answers aren't obvious. This isn't an internship where you observe from the sidelines. Outstanding work has the potential to shape production strategies and generate real, measurable returns. Ideal candidates are quantitatively sharp, practically minded problem solvers, programmers, mathematicians and scientists who are excited to solve the hardest problems in our field, across our offices in the US, Singapore, Amsterdam and London. **What You'll Work On** You'll work on real research problems, not simulated exercises, discovering predictive patterns from billions of market events, designing statistical models, and applying machine learning to open research problems. Your work would include: - Discovering predictive patterns from billions of market events - Designing statistical models that identify trading opportunities - Applying probability, optimization and machine learning to open research problems - Building AI-powered research agents that accelerate experimentation - Developing infrastructure for rapid, large-scale research - Designing experiments and backtests to evaluate hypotheses - Translating research into production-ready trading signals - Exploring new ML, AI and quant finance techniques to find the next source of alpha **What You'll Learn** Beyond the technical exposure, you'll learn how experienced researchers approach hard problems: breaking them down, questioning assumptions, and deciding based on evidence rather than intuition. You'll be paired with a mentor, reporting manager and buddy, with regular code reviews and feedback throughout the internship. **What Success Looks Like** Successful interns leave having delivered a complete research project from hypothesis to evaluation, built statistically rigorous models, and demonstrated curiosity, ownership and the ability to solve open-ended problems. **Who We're Looking For** We're looking for exceptional students who genuinely enjoy solving hard problems. - Full-time undergraduate, Master's or PhD student in a quantitative discipline (math, physics, computer science, statistics, or a related field), graduating 2028 - Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++ - Grounded in probability, statistics, linear algebra and optimization, with experience in machine learning, statistical modelling or data analysis, whether through coursework, research or personal projects - Comfortable working with large, complex datasets, with strong analytical thinking - A passion for applying quantitative thinking and rigorous research to solve open-ended problems in markets - Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly **Our Culture** More than specific technologies, we care how you think. We look for people who are curious enough to question assumptions, analytical enough to separate signal from noise, persistent enough to keep searching past the first answer, humble enough to keep learning, and excited by problems without textbook solutions. At Graviton, researchers sit alongside engineers to solve problems where milliseconds matter and better models create real competitive advantage. You'll get meaningful ownership from day one, in a culture built on intellectual honesty and continuous improvement. Your contribution won't be measured by hours spent, but by the quality of your thinking. Markets are among the most complex systems humans have ever created. Every day, someone discovers a better answer. This summer, that someone could be you.

location: Amsterdam, North Holland, Netherlands; London, England, United Kingdom; Singapore
description: At Graviton, every strategy, model and edge begins not with instinct, but with someone asking a better question than everyone else. As a PhD Quantitative Research Intern, you'll spend 10-12 weeks pointing the research skills you've spent years building at markets. You'll collaborate with researchers and technologists to investigate market behaviour, test hypotheses, build predictive models and solve problems where the answers aren't obvious. This isn't an internship where you observe from the sidelines, or re-run someone else's experiment. Outstanding work has the potential to shape production strategies and generate real, measurable returns. Ideal candidates are researchers who want to see their methods meet live markets: mathematicians, physicists, statisticians and computer scientists who are excited to solve the hardest problems in our field, across our offices in the US, Singapore, Amsterdam and London. **What You'll Work On** You'll work on real research problems, not simulated exercises. Your work would include: - Discovering predictive patterns from billions of market events - Designing statistical models that identify trading opportunities - Applying probability, optimization and machine learning to open research problems - Running large-scale simulations and experiments on high-performance research infrastructure - Designing experiments and backtests to evaluate hypotheses - Building AI-powered research agents that accelerate experimentation - Developing infrastructure for rapid, large-scale research - Translating research into production-ready trading signals - Exploring new ML, AI and quant finance techniques to find the next source of alpha **What You'll Learn** Beyond the technical exposure, you'll learn what changes when research meets live markets: why a result that would survive peer review can still fail as a trading signal, how costs and capacity constrain an idea that looks clean on paper, and how to tell a model that is right from one that is right for the wrong reason. You'll be paired with a mentor, reporting manager and buddy, with regular code reviews and feedback throughout the internship. **What Success Looks Like** Successful interns leave having delivered a complete research project from hypothesis through to evaluation under realistic market conditions, built statistically rigorous models, and demonstrated curiosity, ownership and the ability to solve open-ended problems. **Who We're Looking For** We're looking for exceptional researchers who genuinely enjoy solving hard problems. - Full-time PhD student in a quantitative discipline such as mathematics, physics, computer science, statistics or a related field, graduating 2028 - Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++ - Depth in probability, statistics, linear algebra and optimization, with research experience in machine learning, statistical modelling or data analysis - Comfort working with large, complex datasets, and strong analytical thinking - A passion for applying quantitative thinking and rigorous research to solve open-ended problems in markets - Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly **Our Culture** More than specific technologies, we care how you think. We look for people who are curious enough to question assumptions, analytical enough to separate signal from noise, persistent enough to keep searching past the first answer, humble enough to keep learning, and excited by problems without textbook solutions. At Graviton, researchers sit alongside engineers to solve problems where milliseconds matter and better models create real competitive advantage. You'll get meaningful ownership from day one, in a culture built on intellectual honesty and continuous improvement. Your contribution won't be measured by hours spent, but by the quality of your thinking. Markets are among the most complex systems humans have ever created. Every day, someone discovers a better answer. This summer, that someone could be you.

role: Remote Armed Security Officer (Rotational)- Kuparuk - CP
description: Job Description The Remote Armed Security Officer provides professional armed security services for commercial and industrial clients in remote environments where health, safety, and security are the highest priorities. Assigned to the Kuparuk oil field, this position is responsible for protecting personnel, facilities, equipment, and critical infrastructure through proactive security operations, access control, emergency response, and customer service while ensuring compliance with company and client policies. All duties are performed in accordance with NMS' mission, vision, and values. This position follows a two (2) weeks on, two (2) weeks off rotational schedule and is based at the Kuparuk oil field. Responsibilities Conduct routine armed security patrols of assigned buildings, facilities, and grounds by foot, vehicle, or electronic monitoring systems to ensure the safety and security of personnel, property, and critical infrastructure. Control access to client facilities by verifying identification and authorizing entry for employees, visitors, contractors, and authorized personnel. Inspect doors, windows, gates, fences, and other access points to ensure they are properly secured and report any deficiencies. Observe, document, and report property damage, unusual occurrences, suspicious activity, safety hazards, and security incidents. Enforce company and client policies and procedures by providing direction to individuals, addressing rule violations, and removing unauthorized persons from the property when appropriate. Notify personnel of visitors and coordinate visitor access in accordance with established procedures. Respond appropriately to alarms, emergencies, medical incidents, fires, and other critical situations to protect life, property, and client assets. Operate and maintain camp billeting, visitor management, and electronic access control systems while ensuring accurate documentation of authorized personnel and visitors. Monitor facility systems, including fire protection, security, lighting, heating, ventilation, and related building systems, and report operational concerns as required. Safely carry and maintain assigned firearms and security equipment in accordance with company policy, state regulations, and contract requirements. Provide transportation services using vehicles ranging from standard passenger vehicles to buses and off-road vehicles, as required. Provide emergency medical response, including CPR, AED use, basic first aid, and patient movement, within the scope of training and certification. Promptly report unsafe conditions, equipment deficiencies, or sanitation concerns to the appropriate supervisor. Complete incident reports, daily activity logs, and other required documentation accurately and in a timely manner. Perform other duties as assigned in support of departmental and operational objectives. Qualifications High school diploma or GED equivalent required. Minimum of three (3) years of full-time professional experience in security, law enforcement, or military service. Relevant post-secondary education may be substituted for a portion of the required experience. Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record for the previous three (3) years to be eligible under company vehicle insurance policy. Ability to obtain an Alaska Guard License prior to employment. The applicant is responsible for the applicable licensing fee. Must obtain and maintain a State of Alaska Armed Guard License upon hire. Must demonstrate safe handgun handling skills and successfully pass a law enforcement-style firearms qualification in accordance with contract requirements. Ability to qualify for required credentials and certifications, including but not limited to TWIC and ATF Explosives Possessor authorization, as required by the contract. Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and contract-specific software. Must successfully complete all pre-employment requirements, which may include a criminal background check, drug screening, physical examination, fit-for-duty assessment, and hearing test. Applicants who do not reside near an approved testing facility are responsible for travel expenses to the nearest testing location. Ability to reside in dormitory-style accommodations and comply with remote camp standards, including housekeeping and cleanliness requirements. Demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a team while maintaining positive relationships with coworkers, clients, and customers. Ability to exercise sound judgment and make effective decisions with minimal supervision, particularly during emergency situations. Ability to work a two (2) weeks on, two (2) weeks off rotational schedule. Ability to stand and/or walk for up to twelve (12) hours per shift and perform duties in remote Arctic weather conditions. Must be able to speak, read, write, and understand English as required by the contract. Must comply with all company and client safety policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements. CANDIDATES RESIDING OUTSIDE ANCHORAGE AREA: Candidates residing in the Lower 48 for any contract and/or hired for the BP contract: For the purposes of pre-employment testing, Anchorage will be considered the point of hire (with the exception of drug testing, which will be conducted near the candidate’s place of residence). Employee is responsible for any travel expenses and needed accommodations related to pre−employment tasks that need to be completed in Anchorage, AK. This includes, but is not limited to, any safety training requirements, required pre−employment testing and/or training such as physical, DOT physical/medical card, fit for duty, audiogram, and/or other testing required by contract/company (such as NSTC, APICC training, security licensing requirements, etc. Candidates residing in Alaska for Alyeska and Hillcorp contracts: pre-employment testing will be scheduled near the candidate’s area of residence within the state. The only exception is when the candidate lives in a region without the necessary service providers to complete all requirements. Flights to Remote Locations: All employees are responsible for all expenses related to reporting to point of hire (Anchorage, AK) for scheduled trips paid for by the company for remote locations. Working Conditions and Physical Requirements Weather: Indoors and Outdoors, frequently exposed to arctic outdoor weather conditions. Noise level: Moderate to Loud. Description of environment: This is a remote camp environment. Physical requirements: Employee is required to lift and/or move up to 50 lbs. Frequently to constantly required to sit, stand, walk, use hands/fingers to handle or feel, climb, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, talk/hear, see, taste/smell, and carry weight/lift. Fit For Duty Test: Lift: Lift 50 lbs. from floor to knuckle x2 Lift: Lift 50 lbs. from floor to waist x 2 Carry: Carry 35 lbs. with two hands for a minimum distance of 150 feet, self-paced Allow a 60 second rest break after 75 feet. Push: push horizontally with a peak force of 60 f-lbs. with two hands Pull: pull horizontally with a peak force of 60 f-lbs. with two hands. Stoop & Twist: Perform alternate cross over toe touches x 10 each side, self-paced but continuous. Kneel: Kneel on one knee and stand. Return to kneel on opposite knee. Repeat alternate kneeling sequence x 3 for each knee, self-pace but continuous. Stand from Supine Position Test: From a supine, recumbent position, while wearing arctic gear , test recipient must be able to stand without assistance x 3, self-paced (this task must be accomplished safely without significant loss of balance or falling.) Allow one re-test when there is a loss of balance considered unsafe or a fall. Walk: Walk on a treadmill at 3 MPH for 10 minutes with good balance, Stairs: Climb up and down 10 steps x 2 for a total of 20 steps, self-paced. Shoveling: Perform a shovel test for five (5) minutes self-paced but continuous (i.e., no breaks) using a standard snow shovel with a 3 lb. weight attached to the shovel blade. (e.g. sand bag weight securely taped to the shovel blade.) Stairs & Carry: Climb up and down 10 steps x 2 for a total of 20 steps while carrying 30 lbs. in one hand and using the other hand to grasp a railing for safety, self-paced. Allow a 60 second rest period after climbing up and down 10 steps while carrying. role: Research Intern, Scene Understanding and Planning
description: ### About Didi Autonomous Driving Founded in 2016, DiDi's autonomous driving unit is dedicated to developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology to make transportation safer, more efficient, and accessible. In 2019, the unit became an independent company, Voyager, to accelerate technology development, commercialization, and large-scale deployment. By combining DiDi's unique data advantage, operational expertise, and mobility ecosystem, we aim to build a reliable, scalable autonomous fleet that integrates seamlessly with human-driven services. **Driven by real-world customer needs and a strong commitment to safety and user experience**, our mission is to deliver autonomous mobility solutions that create meaningful value for riders and communities. ### ### **About the Role** We want our vehicles to understand the physical world as it is right now, instead of relying on a map drawn long ago. Roads change, and the world a car actually drives in is always more complex than any static record of it. We are seeking a Research Intern to help give our planner a more accurate and up-to-date picture of the world, so the vehicle handles complex real-world scenes more robustly. In this role, you will take on hard, open problems from real-world driving and solve them with frontier research methods. You will report directly to the team lead and work on the problem from definition to validated solution. Strong results will often be worth publishing, and we will support you in writing them up, but the goal is to solve problems that matter to the product. ### ### Responsibilities - Survey the latest research in scene understanding, prediction, and planning, and turn it into practical approaches that fit our system and constraints. - Design and implement deep learning models that build a richer, real-time understanding of the driving environment from onboard sensors and other available sources. - Train and evaluate models on large-scale data from our driving logs and on public benchmarks, and lead failure analysis to find out where and why models fall short. - Define metrics and evaluation methods that connect perception quality to how the vehicle actually drives. - Turn successful prototypes into solutions that work with our planning stack, with help from production engineers. - Collaborate with Perception, Prediction, Planning, and Mapping teams so results move from experiment to product. ## ### Qualifications - Currently enrolled in an M.S. or Ph.D. program in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related field, for the full duration of the internship. - Available for a full-time onsite internship of 3–6 months; start dates are flexible. - Strong programming skills in Python, and experience with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX. - Hands-on experience designing, training, and debugging deep learning models for computer vision, 3D perception, or sequential decision-making. - Solid understanding of autonomous driving fundamentals, including perception, prediction, and motion planning. - Ability to read research critically, form hypotheses, and turn them into well-controlled experiments. - Excellent communication and collaboration skills. ## ### Preferred Qualifications - Publications at top venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, ICRA, IROS, CoRL or IV. - Experience with multi-modal sensor fusion (camera, lidar, radar) or BEV representations. - Experience with transformers, graph neural networks, or other structured scene representations. - Experience with uncertainty estimation, or with learning-based prediction or planning. - Experience with large-scale model training and data pipelines. - Experience with public autonomous driving datasets such as nuScenes, Argoverse 2, or the Waymo Open Dataset. - Proficiency in C++ (CUDA is a plus) and experience with robotics systems. About Zendar : Zendar builds a radar-centric autonomy stack which makes any vehicle - from cars to robots - autonomous in any environment. With our deep radar DNA, we have architected our solution to put RF sensing at the core of all perception. The result is a system that handles long range, high speeds, and bad weather not as edge cases but as a core strength of the autonomy stack. Because radars naturally measure both 3D position and velocity for every object in the environment, radar-centric autonomy is extremely compute- and data-efficient. Our autonomous vehicle needs only a few thousand dollars of hardware to make it completely autonomous, making this the cheapest way to build an autonomous vehicle by far. See a demo of Zendar’s foundational RF perception and driving functions . To develop this capability we had to build the entire stack in house - from radar sensor hardware to signal processing to multi-modal perception foundation models and path and trajectory planning. As part of a small team, you will have a front-row seat to seeing how a complete autonomy stack is architected and how your engineering decisions improve the ability to navigate autonomously in the real world. Although AI is central to what we build, our hiring process is intentionally human: every résumé is reviewed by a real person. Role Overview: We’re looking for a recent graduate to join us for a 6-month intern-to-hire role working across our robotics stack: perception, controls, simulation, and robot applications such as asset tracking and site monitoring. The common thread is measurement. You’ll design experiments and build the tools that tell us whether our systems work, how well, and why, then share what you find with the ML and control engineers who act on it. Priorities shift quickly, so this role suits someone who enjoys ambiguous problems, picks up new domains fast, and is excited to grow into a full-time engineer on the team. Key Responsibilities: Design and run experiments and test scenarios to measure system performance across perception models, controllers, and robotic applications. Build and extend Python tools for evaluation, data analysis, and visualization. Support simulation workflows, data collection, and hands-on testing with vehicles, robots, and sensors. Help prototype and evaluate robotic applications, such as security monitoring and container inventory management. Present findings to ML, controls, and product engineering teams, collaborating to track and resolve identified issues. What We’re Looking For: Recent graduate (Bachelor’s or Master’s degree) in engineering, physics, mathematics, or a related technical field. Proficiency in Python; experience with C++ is a plus. Familiarity with Linux environments. Experience using agentic coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) Experience designing and conducting experiments from a scientific perspective and applying statistical analysis to extract insights from noisy, real-world data. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to clearly articulate technical results to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Comfort with ambiguity: ability to drive loosely defined projects, adapt to evolving requirements, and rapidly master new technical domains. Bonus Points For Experience with GCP, BigQuery, or SQL. Experience processing sensor data (e.g., radar, LiDAR, camera feeds). Experience with and enthusiasm for working directly with hardware and robotics platforms, including vehicles and sensor test rigs. Familiarity with ROS or robotics simulation software. Coursework or experience in controls, dynamics, or state estimation (e.g., MPC, Kalman filters, odometry). ### **About the Role** The Speculative Decoding team at Together AI builds the draft models and algorithms that let large language models generate faster without changing their outputs. Our speculators run in production on frontier open models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM. Our work sits at the intersection of model training, inference algorithms and serving systems, and we co-design all three to lower the cost and latency of generation. As a research intern, you will dive into open questions in speculative decoding: new drafter architectures and verification schemes, knowledge distillation and training recipes that align draft and target models, and drafters that adapt as traffic shifts. You will train and fine-tune draft models at scale on dedicated GPU clusters, and test your ideas against realistic serving workloads, including long-context and agentic traffic. Projects aim to answer important research questions in speculative decoding, enabling faster generation on frontier models, drafters that keep pace with changing workloads, and robust, reproducible evaluation under real traffic. ### Past Research Speculative decoding research by Together researchers, interns and academic collaborators includes: - [Speculative Speculative Decoding](https://openreview.net/forum?id=aL1Wnml9Ef) (ICLR 2026) - [When RL Meets Adaptive Speculative Training: A Unified Training-Serving System](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06932) (ICML 2026) - [Beat the Long Tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13841) (MLSys 2026) ### **Responsibilities** - Research and prototype new efficient speculative decoding algorithms and draft model architectures - Train, fine-tune and distill draft models, and design rigorous experiments to validate hypotheses. - Implement optimized version for serving engines to show efficacy in real world workloads - Communicate the plans, progress, and results of projects to the broader team - Share findings through technical write-ups and blog posts, and help bring successful ideas into production ### **Requirements** - Currently pursuing a Master's or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field - Strong knowledge of Machine Learning and Deep Learning fundamentals - Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning large models with distributed training frameworks (e.g., Megatron-LM, FSDP) - Familiarity with modern model architectures, such as Mixture-of-Experts and hybrid attention ### Preferred Qualifications - Prior research experience in speculative decoding, efficient inference, or efficient machine learning - Publications at leading conferences in machine learning or systems (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys) - Experience with knowledge distillation, post-training, or reinforcement learning - Familiarity with LLM serving engines (e.g., vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) - Contributions to open-source machine learning projects ### **About Together AI** Together AI, the AI Native Cloud, is purpose-built for AI engineers. AI application developers get high-performance inference that scales reliably, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for creating frontier-level specialized models, and pre-training at massive scale for fully custom intelligence, all around a marketplace of leading open models that teams can run, adapt, and own. Trusted by Cursor, Decagon, ElevenLabs, Salesforce, and Zoom, Together serves 400+ trillion tokens a month. ### **Internship Program Details** Our internship program runs 12 to 14 weeks, giving you the opportunity to work alongside industry-leading engineers and researchers across multiple teams. This cohort's internship dates span May 17th to August 6th or June 14th to September 3rd. ### **Compensation** We offer competitive compensation, housing stipends, and other competitive benefits. The estimated US hourly rate for this role is $58 - $70 an hour. Our hourly rates are determined by location, level and role. Individual compensation will be determined by experience, skills, and job-related knowledge. ### **Application Policy** Please read each role carefully and apply to the position best suited to you. Candidates are limited to 6 applications within a 90-day period, and applications beyond that limit will be automatically rejected. You may apply to additional roles 90 days after your last application. ### **Equal Opportunity** Together AI is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is proud to offer equal employment opportunity to everyone regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, veteran status, and more. **PhD Internship 2027: Boston Research** Boston, US | Full-time | Fixed-term| Hybrid Salary: $55.70 per hour, DOE **About us** Riverlane’s mission is to master quantum error correction (QEC) and unlock a new age of human progress. From advances in materials and climate science to complex chemistry simulation for new drug design, quantum computers will help humanity solve some of its most important challenges. But without QEC, the industry’s defining technical challenge, such breakthroughs can never be achieved. Riverlane is the world leader in QEC technology. QEC is a complex problem that requires a range of skills, talent, and passion. Having raised more than $125M in funding to date to accelerate our cutting-edge R&D in quantum error correction (QEC), Riverlane partners with many of the world’s leading quantum hardware providers and government agencies to make fault-tolerant quantum computing a reality. We’re making remarkable progress and growing fast. **About the role** Delivering practical quantum error correction requires tightly integrated quantum and classical systems. The quantum hardware connectivity, its physical error rates, circuit compilation, and compatible QEC codes all affect performance. On the classical side, decoding algorithms must process large volumes of error data within demanding latency, bandwidth, compute, and power constraints. As a Research Intern, you will investigate simulating, running, and decoding QEC experiments. Along with your supervisor, you will frame a research project. Your project will sit at the intersection of quantum error correction, computer simulations, computer architecture, and hardware-software co-design. Depending on the project, you could study noise models for quantum hardware, work on efficient simulations for QEC experiments, explore efficient QEC decoding or predecoding methods, model the classical resources required by fault-tolerant quantum programs, or investigate how decoding workloads can be distributed across different levels of a computing system. You will work alongside Riverlane’s quantum scientists and engineers in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with support from a dedicated supervisor. Your work will contribute to our understanding of how QEC systems can meet the performance requirements of increasingly large quantum computers. **What you will do** - Develop algorithms, simulations or architectural models to evaluate potential approaches - Investigate methods for reducing the compute, communication, memory, latency or power requirements associated with QEC - Explore trade-offs between decoding performance, logical error suppression and classical resource requirements - Collaborate with quantum scientists and engineers working across QEC theory, decoding, software and hardware - Analyse results and communicate your findings through technical discussions, presentations and written reports - Produce clear, reproducible research code and supporting documentation **What we need** - You must be currently pursuing a PhD in Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or another related technical field - Research experience in at least one of the following areas: - Running quantum circuits on quantum hardware - Decoding algorithms or quantum error-correcting codes - Experience developing computational models, simulations or research software - Proficiency in Python, C, C++ or another relevant programming language - A strong understanding of computer systems and architecture - Computer architecture or quantum-classical systems - Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills - The ability to communicate complex technical ideas clearly - The ability to take initiative and work effectively with researchers and engineers from different disciplines - Authorization to work in the United States for the duration of the internship **Even better if…** - You have experience researching qLDPC or surface codes - You are familiar with QEC decoding or predecoding techniques - You have explored the classical resource requirements of fault-tolerant quantum computing - You have experience with scientific computing, quantum circuit simulation or QEC simulation tools - You have contributed to academic publications, open-source software or collaborative research projects - You have experience with hardware-software or compiler-hardware co-design - You understand the latency, bandwidth or power constraints affecting quantum control and decoding systems **Important notes** - You must be legally authorized to work in the United States for the duration of the internship - If you intend to work under Curricular Practical Training (CPT), Optional Practical Training (OPT) or another form of student employment authorization, you are responsible for obtaining the necessary approval before your start date - Any offer of employment will be contingent upon verification of your identity and authorization to work in the United States, as required by law - You must be available to work full-time for 10 to 12 weeks - You will be required to sign an agreement assigning ownership of intellectual property produced during your internship to Riverlane - This internship is based at our US office in Cambridge, Massachusetts **How to apply** Please upload your CV and a cover letter. Your CV should include details of your education, research experience and relevant technical skills. Your cover letter should explain why you are applying for the internship and the skills and experience you would bring to the role. **Deadline** Please submit your application by November 6, 2026. **Pay and Expenses** We will reimburse reasonable expenses incurred as part of your role, such as approved travel to meetings or conferences. We are unable to cover the cost of travelling to Cambridge, Massachusetts at the beginning or end of the internship or accommodation during the internship. **What you can expect from us** You can expect a diverse and collaborative working environment that brings together experts in software and hardware development, quantum information theory, physics, mathematics and other technical fields. Our global team represents more than 20 nationalities. We also provide free snacks and refreshments and organize regular social and cultural events. If you have any questions, please contact [jobs@riverlane.com](mailto:jobs@riverlane.com). *Riverlane is an equal opportunity employer. role: Entry Level Civil Engineer - Land Development, December 2026 Grad
description: **Build your civil engineering career in site design.** You'll work on real land development projects, design real sites, and grow through hands-on experience, professional development, and mentorship from engineers who want to see you succeed. **About the Role** Bohler’s West Palm Beach, FL office is seeking an Entry Level Civil Engineer (Land Development) who is eager to learn, grow, and make a positive impact. In this role, you will work closely with engineers, designers, and project managers to bring exciting land development projects to life, including site planning, grading, utilities, and stormwater management. You will contribute to projects for well-known brands across commercial, residential, and mixed-use markets, all while laying the groundwork for a rewarding engineering career. **What You’ll Do** - Work on a variety of land development projects, including commercial, residential, industrial, and mixed-use sites - Partner with experienced engineers and mentors to learn every stage of site design, from concept through construction - Use AutoCAD Civil 3D to create site layouts, grading plans, and utility designs - Research and interpret design manuals, zoning ordinances, and jurisdictional regulations - Review and address regulatory comments and assist with project redesigns as needed - Support the preparation of stormwater management reports and construction submittals - Participate in professional and technical training through Bohler’s Learning & Development programs - Attend site visits to observe field conditions and coordinate with project teams - Engage in civic, professional, and business organizations to build your network - Perform other responsibilities in accordance with company policies and standards **What We Offer** - A supportive and flexible work environment that empowers employees to stay healthy, fulfill their passions, and balance work and life goals - The opportunity to take ownership of your career with an unsurpassed focus on career development and mentorship - A Learning & Development department that facilitates ongoing technical and professional growth, including individualized AutoCAD Civil 3D training - Complete visibility and exposure to all aspects of land development projects - The chance to immerse yourself in the design process while working side-by-side with talented teammates - Open and transparent communication with senior leadership and local office management - Team-building activities, office events, and a collaborative, high-energy environment **What You’ll Bring** - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Civil Engineering or a related field - 0–1+ years of residential, commercial, or industrial site design and permitting experience - Familiarity with AutoCAD Civil 3D (preferred; training provided if not yet proficient) - Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach to teamwork - Motivation to take initiative and contribute to shared goals - EIT certification is helpful but not required **Get hands-on experience contributing to real projects, and see how your work helps shape communities and your career.** #LI-Onsite

The NYC Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) protects public health and the environment by supplying clean drinking water, collecting and treating wastewater, and reducing air, noise, and hazardous materials pollution. DEP is the largest combined municipal water and wastewater utility in the country, with nearly 5,500 employees. DEP delivers more than 1.1 billion gallons per day of the highest quality drinking water to 8.3 million NYC residents and more than 1 million people in Upstate New York and has a wastewater conveyance and treatment system capable of processing over 1.3 billion gallons of wastewater per day to protect the environment and the city's surrounding waterways. The Bureau of Environmental Compliance's mission is the enforcement of environmental laws and regulations, which affect the health and safety of the public and environment. Specifically, the bureau enforces the City's Asbestos regulations as well as the Air and Noise Codes. The Bureau is comprised of the Division of Air & Noise Policy, Permitting and Enforcement and the Asbestos Control Program. These divisions respond to; air and noise code complaints; inspect and track asbestos removal projects; and foster the goals of environmental protection. The Environmental Engineering Intern will perform technical duties in support of the New York City Air Pollution Control Program. The selected candidate will receive training and develop proficiency in performance of the following duties: examine application requests to register and operate combustion and industrial process equipment; performs field inspections, including use of testing instrumentation of equipment to be permitted; preparing technical reports related to field inspections and other technical and regulatory matters; may also be assigned other duties related to stationary air pollution source control; inspecting premises and construction sites in connection with issuance of pertinent permits; inspecting an installation to assure adherence to specifications, plans and work permits; conducting engineering analysis and write preliminary report of new technologies presented to the Department. Valid NYS Driver's License is mandatory. ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING INTE - 20616 A baccalaureate degree in environmental, fire protection, chemical, mechanical, petroleum, aeronautical, or materials engineering from an accredited college; or A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college in environmental, fire protection, chemical, mechanical, petroleum, aeronautical, or materials engineering technology and two years of full-time satisfactory experience in environmental engineering work. You will be part of the EOS Storage Development and Operations team, delivering large-scale, reliable, high-performance storage services. Today, our infrastructure manages more than 1 Exabyte of disk storage and serves around 10 Exabytes of data annually to researchers and computing facilities worldwide. In this role, you will have an opportunity to learn, contribute and gain experience in operations and evolution of innovative, open-source storage platform. You will also work closely with developers and service managers to improve automation, observability, reliability and performance of CERN's storage services. Your responsibilities: Operate and maintain EOS large-scale distributed storage services supporting CERN's scientific programmes. Integrate, troubleshoot and optimise distributed storage systems at exabyte scale across software, hardware and network layers. Contribute to the development, testing, deployment and automation of EOS platform capabilities and operational tools. Liaise with users, developers, service managers and external collaborators to support the evolution of CERN storage services. ## **About Bitstack** It all started with an idea in 2021. Initially built to democratize Bitcoin in France, Bitstack has gone from a simple product that invests spare change in bitcoin, to a crypto-native bank bringing a better way to save, spend, and grow money to our 300K+ users. We want to rebuild finance from the ground up to empower people to achieve financial freedom by participating in a more open and inclusive financial system. We’re a small, ambitious team of operators. We believe in moving fast, sweating the details, and creating products people truly love. At Bitstack, you’ll have the opportunity to shape not just our products, but the culture and practices of our entire organization. Bitstack is backed by YC, leading VCs like 13books Capital, Stillmark, Serena, and many more. We are building a product our users love and we are just getting started! **The Role** Bitstack is a crypto-asset service provider authorised under the MiCA Regulation. As such, we are subject to strict requirements relating to anti-money laundering (AML), counter-terrorist financing (CTF) and fraud prevention. As part of the Compliance team, you will contribute to the day-to-day implementation of our compliance framework. You will review alerts and customer cases across three key areas: transaction monitoring, screening and KYC. **What You'll Be Doing** **1. Transaction Monitoring (Fiat & Crypto)** - Analyse and investigate transaction monitoring alerts across euro payment flows (card payments and SEPA transfers) and crypto flows (on-chain deposits and withdrawals). - Examine transaction patterns, counterparties and wallet exposure to assess each alert and determine whether it is a false positive or should be escalated. - Detect fraudulent activity, including payment fraud, account takeovers and scams targeting our users. - Document your findings and, where appropriate, prepare the supporting information for a suspicious activity report to TRACFIN, the French financial intelligence unit. - Contribute to improving detection scenarios and monitoring alert metrics. **2. Screening: PEPs, Sanctions & Adverse Media** - Review screening alerts and determine whether a match is genuine or a false positive. - Implement enhanced due diligence measures for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including checks on the source of funds and source of wealth. - Escalate confirmed matches against sanctions lists or adverse media findings in accordance with internal procedures. **3. KYC (Know Your Customer)** - Review and validate customer supporting documents, including proof of identity, proof of address, proof of income, source of funds and source of wealth. - Detect identity theft attempts and forged documents. - Assess consistency between the customer's profile, declared information and observed activity. - Request additional documentation and follow up on cases through to their final decision. You will also contribute to updating internal procedures and monitoring emerging fraud and money laundering typologies within the crypto ecosystem. You will gain hands-on experience with an AML/CFT framework at a regulated crypto-asset service provider. You will learn how alerts are handled from initial detection through to the final decision, how a risk-based approach is applied, how blockchain analytics tools are used, and how the Compliance team collaborates with Product, Operations and Customer Support. **What We're Looking For** - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Compliance, Law, Finance, Risk Management or a related field, and looking for an internship or work-study placement. - Previous exposure to AML/CFT, KYC or fraud prevention through an internship, coursework or certification is a plus, but not required. - Highly organised, rigorous and detail-oriented. - Able to draw well-reasoned conclusions and clearly document findings in writing. - Comfortable using spreadsheets (Excel or Google Sheets), with a strong interest in crypto-assets and blockchain technology. - Discreet and meticulous when handling sensitive personal data. - Fluent in French and comfortable working in English. **Perks & Benefits** 💻 3 days in the office and 2 days working remotely 🕑 Flexible working hours 🏄Team activities and annual offsites 🍉 Swile meal vouchers ## **Diversity & Inclusion** We hire talented and passionate people from all kinds of backgrounds, we don’t care about your age or where you studied. If you’re excited about the role but your past experience doesn’t match every bullet point in the job description, we still encourage you to apply. What matters most is that you’re a builder at heart, you share our values, and you’re enthusiastic about our mission. #LI-TT1
