role: Internship - Credit Analyst - Hedge Fund - London
description: Company profile Altana Wealth is an award-winning Asset Management Company based in London with an affiliate company based in Monaco, backed by partners’ money and with a wide range of funds across multiple asset classes. The company manages assets on behalf of professional clients and eligible counterparties. Altana Wealth is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority in the UK and by the CCAF in Monaco. Please visit for further information. Team profile Our team members come from a diverse range of backgrounds and cultures, with a common focus on high performance and differentiated sources of alpha. The credit team invests across the capital structure in bonds, credit derivatives and hybrid securities, with a focus on event-driven situations. We look at performing, stressed and distressed credits, on both the long and the short side and invest across industries with no specific bias, but currently the Technology sector, in particular Artificial Intelligence and Insurance are a focus. Your internship You will support the investment team across the full life cycle of idea generation, fundamental research, trade construction and implementation. You will receive training in fundamental research and relative value analysis, with formal review and feedback throughout. Duration: Up to 12 weeks, or longer depending on availability and workload, typically five days per week. Intakes: We run two intakes each year. The summer internship, starting in June or July 2027, is open to students entering the penultimate or final year of their degree or Master's. The off-cycle winter internship, starting in January or February 2027, is open to graduates, including Master's and MBA graduates, and to those seeking work experience. Prior professional experience is an advantage for both intakes. Please state in your covering letter which intake you are applying for, or whether you would like to be considered for both. Strong interns may be considered for an extended placement, a return internship or a full-time role where one becomes available. Key Responsibilities Bottom-up fundamental company and industry research to support idea generation. Gathering and synthesising macroeconomic, financial and operating information about companies and industries. Building and maintaining financial models. Using Claude alongside Bloomberg and Excel to accelerate research, verifying all output against primary sources. Drafting presentations and memoranda for internal and external audiences. Attending team discussions and ad hoc external stakeholder meetings. Candidate Profile We are looking for: Curiosity and Rigour: A genuine interest in how companies and markets work, and the intellectual honesty to follow the evidence. Interest in Markets: Demonstrable engagement with investing, such as running your own account, writing on markets or an investment society. Analytical and Communication Skills: Keen attention to detail and the ability to present a clear, concise view with diplomacy and confidence. Drive and Urgency: A bias to action and a record of achievement, with the reliability to deliver work to a high standard in a fast-paced environment. Technical Skills: Strong Excel skills are expected. Working knowledge of Python and practical experience using AI tools for research are a plus, as is the judgement to know where those tools fall short. Achievements: A strong academic record, ideally relevant internships or work experience, and accomplishments outside the classroom, such as sports, side projects or unusual interests. A degree in economics, finance, corporate finance or a related quantitative subject is preferred. We also welcome applicants from other disciplines who can demonstrate a genuine interest in markets and investing. To apply, please email a covering letter, CV and transcripts to . The process typically includes a written assignment, a case study and interviews. You may use AI tools in your application and case study; please tell us briefly how you used them, as you will be asked to discuss your work in detail at interview. You must be eligible to work in the UK for the duration of the internship. Two professional or academic references will be requested at a later stage. role: Rotational Security Officer (1 week on / 1 off, plus Benefits) - FedEx Anchorage
description: Job Description The Security Officer provides services for a variety of large and small business clients where health, safety, and security is our #1 priority. This is a public environment at the FedEx Shipping Center and surrounding areas with the corresponding levels of traffic (employees, visitors, customers, etc.). The schedule for this position is a rotational one (1) week on / one (1) week off schedule. The work week is Monday-Sunday, 12 hours a day working either 6:00am-6:00pm or 6:00pm-6:00am. Responsibilities Personally monitors either visually, electronically or audibly a variety of assigned areas, or grounds by working in a variety of assignments including but not limited to roving inside the facilities, roving in a vehicle, other locations deemed appropriate. Ensures own actions and those of others observe maximum level of safety and compliance. Will verbally de-escalate situations to ensure the safety of fellow employees, customers, and clients. Examines doors, windows, and other areas of the store to determine they are secure. Reports and records data such as property damage, unusual occurrences, accordance with company policies and procedures. Warns violators of rule infractions and may apprehend or expel violators. Notifies on site individuals of visitors wishing to see them. Assists in properly responding to a variety of emergencies or disasters in order to preserve life and property, including but not limited to fire safety, active shooter protocol May perform routine input or monitoring of safety and life support computer programs. May issue and record ID badges. May check heating, lighting, sprinkling, security, ventilation, fire, etc., systems to make sure they are operational. May also be combined with other position duties. Notify supervisor is safety and sanitation standards are not being met. This position has no supervisory responsibilities. Other duties that are pertinent to the department or unit’s success also may be assigned. Qualifications High school diploma or GED equivalent. At least two (2) years of security, law enforcement or military experience. A valid Driver’s License and an acceptable driving record for the past three (3) years to be eligible under NMS’ vehicle insurance policy. Must pass background check to obtain a Security Identification Display Area (SIDA) badge. Must be able to obtain and pay the Alaska Guard License fee of $98.25 prior to beginning work. Must be able to cooperate and work as part of a team with fellow employees, customers, and clients. Must be able to make decisions in the moment with little to no supervision. Must be able to be on your feet for 12 hours per shift for the scheduled rotation. Contract requires employees to speak, understand, read and write English. Must be safety oriented as this is a safety sensitive position. Must meet and adhere to all safety guidelines and regulations set forth by the company and client. Working Conditions and Physical Requirements Weather: Indoor/Outdoor. Frequently exposed to arctic conditions. Noise level: Moderate to Loud Description of environment: This is a public aviation facility. Must constantly be able to stand, walk, climb, push, pull use hands and arms, stoop, kneel and crouch. Physical requirements: Must be able to lift and move up to 50lbs. Must be able to work a rotational week on / week off schedule with 12 hour shifts.

Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. Do you want to help us build new things and evangelize use of AWS with customers? As an Associate Solutions Architect you will partner across AWS to help customers craft highly scalable, flexible and resilient cloud architectures that address customer business problems. As a trusted customer advocate, you will help organizations understand best practices around cloud-based solutions, and how to migrate existing workloads to the cloud. You will have the opportunity to help customers use AWS within their organizations ranging from new start-ups to large enterprise customers. This position is part of an accelerated career development program for those who want to advance both their technical and business skills. This is a unique opportunity for driven, self-starters to play a key role in a fast-growing business, and to deliver significant value to AWS customers of all sizes from nimble startups to global brands. The program will provide you with training and work experience that aligns in the field of technical training. This unique program consists of mentoring by subject matter experts, project-based learning curriculum and experiential learning assignments. If this sounds exciting to you - come build the future with us! Program Overview: This is a structured, cohort-based accelerated development program designed for early career Solutions Architects. You'll join a cohort of peers at one of our hub locations in Arlington VA, Austin TX, or Seattle WA, building a professional network from Day 1. You'll be embedded in a supportive team with a dedicated mentor, an onboarding buddy, and a manager who guides your technical and professional growth. You'll follow a structured learning journey that develops deep expertise in cloud architecture, AI/ML, and customer-facing solution design. Within weeks, you'll begin working directly with AWS customers — from startups to large enterprises — helping them architect cloud solutions that solve real business problems. Start Date Details: This is a cohort-based program where everyone is required to start on the same day. Start dates are tentatively set to occur January 25, 2027. Key job responsibilities - Create solutions that address customer business problems and accelerate the adoption of AWS services - Interface with customer stakeholders, including developers and team leads - Drive effective feedback gathering from customers, distill and translate feedback into clear business and technical requirements for product and engineering teams A day in the life No two days look exactly the same, and that's what makes this role exciting. Your morning might start with a team stand-up where you share wins and learning moments with your cohort and mentor, followed by a hands-on lab building a serverless architecture or working with an AI model on Amazon Bedrock. By midday, you could be on a customer call helping a CTO plan a cloud migration — whiteboarding an architecture, recommending services, and walking them through a proof-of-concept, with your mentor there to support you. In the afternoon, you might attend a technical session led by a senior SA on emerging technology, then spend time working toward your next AWS certification. Later, you'll collaborate with your cohort on a group project — building a customer-facing demo, writing a technical blog post, or preparing for your next development milestone. You'll also have opportunities to participate in leadership development programming and community events that go beyond your core technical work. About the team We are intentional about building pathways for early career talent, creating opportunities for people who bring fresh perspectives to cloud technology. This isn't a "sink or swim" program — you'll have a dedicated mentor who coaches you throughout the program, an onboarding buddy to help you navigate Amazon culture, and a manager focused on your development. You'll join a tight-knit cohort culture with regular team activities, peer learning, and social events — our hubs offer collaborative workspaces where you're surrounded by peers and leaders who want to see you succeed. You'll work across industries, customer sizes, and technology domains, giving you a breadth of experience that accelerates your career faster than a traditional single-team placement.

role: Data Center Technician - 2027 Internship, Data Center Operations
description: Important — Site Location & Commuting: This role is based at a data center facility in a remote location with no public transportation access. A valid driving license and access to personal transportation are required to commute to the site daily. Please consider this before applying. At Amazon Web Services (AWS), we are working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people. Are you ready to embrace the challenge? Come build the future with us. This is a unique opportunity to work in some of the most cutting-edge data centers in the world. Amazon data centers are large-scale, high-density facilities where you will help change the face of cloud technology in the region — and your work will directly impact millions of customers. This internship is designed as a potential pathway to full-time employment. Interns who demonstrate strong performance throughout their internship may be considered for a full-time Data Center Technician position, subject to available roles and business needs. Who Should Apply We welcome applications from: - Students in the last year of their Bachelor's degree in a relevant technical field such as Information Technology, Computer Hardware Repair, or similar. About the Role As a Data Center Technician Intern, you will work as part of the Operations team, whose primary responsibility is the maintenance and upkeep of the data center infrastructure. This position involves hardware and network diagnostics followed by physical repair. You will be exposed to both independent work and team-based collaboration. Prioritization, organizational skills, effective communication, and the ability to react quickly are critical to being successful. What You Will Do - You will provide our internal teams with infrastructure-related support, resolving tickets related to hardware (motherboards, Random Access Memory, Central Processing Units, Graphics Processing Units, and more) and networking (link-down events, optics replacements, switch replacements, and more). - In addition to hardware and network repair, you will learn how to install equipment, create documentation, innovate solutions, and fix complex problems within the data center environment. Your day-to-day duties include: - Troubleshooting server hardware alongside experienced AWS technicians - Meeting Service Level Agreements (SLAs) against assigned trouble tickets - Shadowing AWS technicians during network troubleshooting to build your diagnostic skills - Replacing media (Solid State Drives and Hard Disk Drives) in accordance with AWS Data Tech guidance - Performing regular server hardware repairs (drives, motherboards, and other components) under the guidance of experienced technicians - Interacting with third-party vendors and contractors working on site Internship Structure Amazon internships are full-time (40 hours per week) for 12 consecutive weeks, starting in summer 2027. This position requires the intern to report to work on site daily. Intern schedules are typically day schedules, Monday through Friday. Please note that a full-time Data Center Technician position could involve day, evening, or weekend shifts and on-call rotations. Candidates should be willing and able to commit to shift work upon transitioning to a full-time position. Diverse Experiences AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed below, we encourage you to apply. If your career is just starting, has not followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, do not let that stop you from applying. Your Career at Amazon — A Universe of Opportunity At Amazon, your career is not a straight path. It is a journey you build as you go. From your first day as an intern, you will own real work that matters. You will diagnose and repair the servers and networks that keep AWS running for millions of customers. Your mentors and teammates will champion your growth, helping you build skills you did not know existed — and you will see your work come to life at massive scale. - Impact. Your work shapes the infrastructure that millions of customers rely on every day. Every server you repair and every network issue you resolve keeps the cloud running. - Action. You will move fast, learn by doing, and solve real problems from day one. Your ideas do not get stuck in approval chains — they get tested, refined, and put into practice. - Curiosity. Every project teaches you something new. You will apply what you learned in the classroom to real challenges and explore different teams, technologies, and career paths within Amazon. - Mentorship and career growth. You will start with structured onboarding and get paired with experienced mentors. Our team is dedicated to supporting new members in an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing. Projects and tasks are assigned in a way that leverages your strengths and helps you further develop your skill set. Your journey here is yours to shape. A day in the life Watch a day in the life of a Data Center Technician About the team AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. We are the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. You will join a diverse team of engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You will collaborate with people across AWS to deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers — in an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them.

We are seeking a Junior Scheduler / Project Controls Consultant to support our growing project advisory and construction consulting practice. This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career professional with hands-on experience developing and maintaining construction schedules who is looking to expand their capabilities in project controls, schedule analysis, and construction advisory. The successful candidate will ideally have approximately two years of experience working with a general contractor, construction manager, specialty contractor, or similar construction organization, with direct exposure to developing, updating, and managing construction schedules. The role will support projects across the building and infrastructure sectors and will work closely with senior schedulers, project controls professionals, project managers, and technical experts. Key Responsibilities Assist in the development, review, and maintenance of detailed construction project schedules. Develop and update Critical Path Method (CPM) schedules based on project scope, construction sequencing, and contractor work plans. Support preparation of baseline schedules, schedule updates, recovery schedules, and short-term look-ahead schedules. Review contractor schedule submissions for completeness, logic, sequencing, durations, and compliance with project requirements. Monitor project progress and incorporate actual progress into schedule updates. Identify critical and near-critical activities, schedule constraints, and potential impacts to project milestones. Assist with analysis of schedule variances and changes to the critical path. Work with project teams to collect schedule information, progress data, and supporting documentation. Assist in preparing schedule narratives, progress reports, schedule graphics, and management presentations. Support schedule impact assessments and preliminary delay analyses under the direction of senior scheduling and claims professionals. Assist with evaluating change orders and potential time impacts. Review project documentation, including drawings, specifications, contracts, progress reports, RFIs, submittals, and change documentation, to understand project sequencing and schedule impacts. Participate in project meetings and schedule review meetings with clients, contractors, designers, and other project stakeholders. Support broader project controls activities, including progress measurement, reporting, cost and schedule integration, and project performance analysis. Maintain clear and organized documentation supporting schedule updates and analyses. Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Construction Engineering, Architecture, or a related field. Approximately 2 or more years of relevant construction industry experience, preferably working for a general contractor, construction manager, or specialty contractor. Practical experience developing or maintaining construction schedules. Understanding of construction sequencing, project milestones, and the relationship between design, procurement, and construction activities. Basic understanding of Critical Path Method (CPM) scheduling principles. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to organize and analyze project information and communicate findings clearly. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. Ability to work collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary project team. Preferred Experience using Oracle Primavera P6. Experience with Microsoft Project or other scheduling/project controls software. Experience working on commercial buildings, healthcare, higher education, transportation, infrastructure, or other complex construction projects. Exposure to schedule review, delay analysis, change-order evaluation, or construction claims. Familiarity with construction drawings, specifications, contracts, and project documentation. Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification or interest in pursuing professional certification is a plus. Ideal Candidate The ideal candidate has started their career working directly within the construction industry and understands how projects are actually planned and built. They have had hands-on exposure to construction scheduling and are interested in developing deeper expertise in project controls, schedule analysis, and construction advisory . This position is particularly well suited to someone who has spent the first few years of their career with a contractor or construction manager and is interested in transitioning into a consulting environment where they can work across multiple projects, clients, and construction sectors. What You Will Develop In this role, you will have the opportunity to develop expertise in: Advanced CPM scheduling Primavera P6 Construction schedule review and analysis Project controls and performance reporting Schedule risk and critical path analysis Change and delay analysis Construction claims and dispute support Project advisory and owner representation You will work alongside experienced construction, engineering, scheduling, and project controls professionals and gain exposure to complex projects from both the contractor and owner perspectives. For more information, please visit Job Type: Full Time (4 days a week in office with one hybrid/ remote day) The position may be based in our Atlanta, New York, or Boston office. role: Associate Consultant - Entry-Level Clinical Data Technology Consulting
description: Veeva’s Consultant Development Program (CDP) is an accelerated pathway that transforms early-career professionals into high-impact consultants who deliver cloud and AI solutions, helping global Life Sciences companies bring life-changing therapies to patients. ### The Role You’ll work hands-on with innovative Clinical Data Management technology, collaborating directly with internal teams and external customers to design, configure, and implement our clinical data software. In this role, you’ll learn our industry-leading clinical trial cloud platforms and work with cutting-edge AI solutions to transform how life sciences companies manage clinical trial data. Empowered from day one by a team-first culture, you will accelerate your career growth as a technical consultant who thrives in an environment where we work hard for our customers and each other. ### The Program As part of the Consultant Development Program, you will: - **Ramp up quickly:** Your journey begins with an intensive, team-based onboarding program that combines hands-on learning, transparent feedback, and active collaboration to develop the consulting skills and industry knowledge to make an impact right away. - **Learn by doing:** You won't be watching from the sidelines. You will take on real responsibility and work directly with customers to solve clinical data management problems within your first three months. - **Thrive together:** Grow alongside a supportive team of seasoned leaders and peers who actively champion your development through open communication and actionable feedback. - **Build your future:** Advance from Associate to Consultant in less than 2 years. More importantly, you’ll develop the foundation for a successful, long-term career where you can continually expand your technical expertise, lead complex projects, and evolve with our global and diverse team. ### What You'll Do As part of our Professional Services team, you are a strategic partner guiding clinical operations and data management teams through implementation. We will teach you how our CDMS software works, and you will use that knowledge to design, configure, and deliver solutions that drive real business value]. Your day-to-day will involve: - **Designing & tailoring the software:** You will lead the configuration of our Vault CDMS platform to fit each customer's unique clinical trial requirements—setting up study workflows, structuring clinical data models, and aligning system capabilities to study protocols. - **Conducting discovery workshops:** You will lead interactive discovery workshops with customer stakeholders (e.g., Clinical Data Managers, CRCs, CRAs) to gather business requirements, map out existing data management workflows, and translate their vision into actionable technical specifications. - .**Managing project scope & execution:** You will take ownership of core implementation deliverables by scoping study requirements, building timeline estimates, and keeping project milestones on track from study design through go-live. - **Guiding the customer as an expert:** You will lead the customer with best practices to ensure their clinical data collection and study management processes are optimized for maximum long-term value. ### What We Are Looking For | We are open to graduates of a variety of backgrounds and look for a specific mindset: **Education & Preferred Background** A Bachelor's or Master's degree in a quantitative or life science field is preferred, such as: - Biomedical Engineering, Health Informatics, Bioinformatics, Biostatistics, Data Science, Computer Science, Engineering - Clinical Research, Public Health, Biology, Pharmacology **Desired Experience** Prior experience (internships, co-ops, academic projects, or entry-level roles) in one or more of the following areas is highly valued: - Data entry or management in a healthcare/research setting, or experience at a CRO, as a Clinical Research Associate (CRA), or Clinical Research Coordinator (CRC) - Clinical trial operations, monitoring, or clinical data management - Data analysis using statistical software (SAS, SPSS, Python, R) - Design training, UX Design, or Human Factors Studies - Business or technical consulting - Speech and Debate or Manufacturing **Technical Skills & Mindset** - **Technical Familiarity:** Basic familiarity with database concepts. For example, SQL for querying relational databases and Python or R for data manipulation and analysis - **Drive:** You thrive in a challenging, intense environment that rewards initiative and rapid learning - **Curiosity:** You have a genuine desire to be hands-on with software and master new technologies - **Communication:** You are fluent in English with excellent verbal and written communication skills - **Analytical Mindset:** You are a strong critical thinker with a proven track record of analytical performance - **Integrity:** Veeva is a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) and a “do the right thing” company, and we expect that from all employees - **Work Ethic:** A commitment to excellence and passion for working hard to achieve results - **Travel:** Willingness to travel as needed (up to 20-30% of the time) - **Experience:** Open to recent graduates of Bachelor's or Master's programs (up to 2 years postgraduate experience maximum) ### How We Hire | Our process is different from most. It is designed to be fast, efficient and respectful. Here are the steps: - **Apply:** Submit your resume, a short cover letter, and take a quick personality test, unless you have already completed it with Veeva previously. - **Fast Response:** We will notify you of your next step typically within one week. - **Interview & Case:** Interview with a Veeva leader. If successful, we will give you a real-world scenario (with 3 days to prepare) to present to our team. - **Offer:** We make decisions quickly—usually within a week of your final presentation. ### What We Offer - **Starting Annual Salary**: 37,000 EUR - Perform well, and in one year you’ll receive a compensation increase and participate in our bonus program

KPFF Seattle’s Civil Team designs sites that enable land to be developed for commercial, residential, institutional, and recreational purposes. We also design critical public and private infrastructure systems that support the built and natural environments, including district energy, regional storm drainage facilities, utility grids, and trails. We support projects ranging from feasibility evaluations and master planning to design, permitting, and construction. Our group works in close collaboration with owners, architects, landscape architects, and other engineering disciplines to build a more sustainable, resilient, and thriving community. Located in downtown Seattle, our office is now accepting applications for the Summer 2027 Civil Engineering Internship. This position will provide the opportunity for you to dive headfirst into project work from day one. You will integrate into our teams, and we are excited to share our professional experience with you as we work on projects together. You will help solve real design problems, help complete active project work, as well as: Assist experienced engineers in solving complex engineering problems. Support engineers and CAD staff with design-related tasks such as calculations, plan production and review. Learn and use engineering and design software (e.g., AutoCAD, Civil 3D) to contribute to project development. Travel to project sites to observe existing conditions and construction of the systems we design. Research jurisdictional codes and manuals to determine design requirements. Participate in brainstorming sessions about sustainable civil engineering solutions. Perform calculations to support the design of stormwater conveyance, water quality, flow control, and green stormwater systems. Perform vehicle turning studies using Vehicle Tracking software programs. Prepare exhibits for reports and/or presentations. Help prepare drafts of drainage reports and feasibility studies. Apply core engineering principles and advanced mathematical techniques to tackle real-world challenges. Build familiarity in navigating federal, state, and local regulations, while aligning with KPFF’s and our clients’ standards and practices. Thrive in a vibrant, inclusive, and collaborative team environment that values creativity, curiosity, and excellence. (Job responsibilities will vary depending on team, project, and each individual intern’s interests.) Minimum Qualifications: Currently pursuing an ABET accredited bachelor's degree in civil (preferred) or environmental engineering. Completion of sophomore or junior year by the start of the 2027 Summer Internship. Basic knowledge of junior year engineering fundamentals. Strong written and verbal communication Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a team environment. Desire for continued learning. Desired Qualification: Coursework and/or familiarity with AutoCAD or Civil 3D This is an on-site position in Seattle, WA. All interns are expected to work from our office location. Physical Demands: Duties are primarily conducted in a standard office setting, requiring prolonged periods of sitting at a desk or computer table. Occasionally may be required to lift objects weighing up to 15 lbs. Travelling to project sites and performing field observations which may involve walking, standing, kneeling, or navigating uneven terrain. **Software Engineering Internship Program** **Location: Remote (US)\*** **Duration: 4 months (start in late February 2027)** **Hours: 40 hrs/week paid experience** *Application Deadline: All interested applicants must apply by November 20, 2026.* The Wikimedia Foundation is the non-profit organization that operates Wikipedia – one of the most popular websites in the world, accessed by over 1.8 billion unique devices every month. It is the only non-profit in the top 50 websites, supported by a community of millions of individual donors around the world. We are looking for **graduates, non-graduates, or those seeking a career change** who are interested in developing software engineering skills through an immersive “learn on the job” internship program. As an intern, you will be embedded into an engineering team within our Product and Technology departments and assigned a primary project with clear deliverables. Alongside your manager and dedicated mentor, you will learn the inner workings of our open source code that helps to create “a world in which everyone can freely share in the sum of all knowledge”. You will work with software that serves over half a billion page views per day through Wikipedia (and [other Wikimedia projects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Wikimedia_sister_projects)). The outcome of your work will impact how all people everywhere discover, share, and contribute to free knowledge. Additionally, you will have the opportunity to learn about various departments at the Foundation and connect with the wider volunteer movement and community. Applicants who identify from a group that is underrepresented in the global conversation of technology advancement are encouraged to apply. We’re also welcoming applicants from communities where access to free knowledge and Wikimedia projects are just emerging. **PROGRAM DETAILS** Successful candidates must be able to commit to a four month, 40hr/week internship which will fall between late February to late June 2027. We will provide laptops and necessary software installed for the duration of the program. This role is 100% remote, and in some cases there may be potential opportunities to participate in in-person events to meet other fellow interns and teams. **POTENTIAL TEAM OPPORTUNITIES** [**Mobile Apps Engineering Team**](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Wikimedia_Apps/Team)The Mobile Apps team's primary objective lies in constructing native Android and iOS applications for the Wikimedia Foundation. [**Editing**](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Editing_team)The Editing team is part of the [Contributors](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Contributors) group. They work on tools for editing across MediaWiki, principally [VisualEditor](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/VisualEditor), [DiscussionTools](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Extension:DiscussionTools), and [Edit check](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Edit_check). The team is currently working on [Suggestion Mode](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/VisualEditor/Suggestion_Mode), a feature for the VisualEditor that proactively suggests actions that people can consider taking to improve Wikipedia articles. [**Data Platform Engineering**](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Data_Platform_Engineering)The Mission of the Data Platform Engineering team is to empower Wiki Communities and the Wikimedia Foundation to gain insights, conduct research, and build compelling user experiences, through access to privacy-aware data and data platform services. The [Data Platform](https://wikitech.wikimedia.org/wiki/Data_Platform) is a collection of systems and services providing end-to-end capabilities for our data producers and consumers to collect, discover, and use data. [**Release Engineering**](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Wikimedia_Release_Engineering_Team)The Release Engineering team enables developers to confidently build, test, and deploy code changes across Wikimedia projects, including Wikipedia, by creating the tools, infrastructure, and automation that keep software delivery fast and reliable. [**Connection team**](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Connection_Team) The Connection team is part of the [Contributors](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Contributors) group. They aim to improve how contributors connect and understand their impact. The team was formed in 2021 to focus on the needs of campaign and event organizers and participants and hopefully improve the experience of [Wikimedia campaigns](https://wikimediafoundation.org/wikipedia20/wikimedia-campaigns/). role: AUSTIN - Junior Instrumentation and Controls Engineer
location: 101 W Louis Henna Blvd, Suite 400, Austin, Texas 78728
description: Your future begins here! BGE, Inc**.** is a nationwide civil engineering consulting firm offering diverse career opportunities in a wide range of disciplines for public and private infrastructure projects. Our employees enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes outstanding health care, generous 401(k) match, professional career resources, and highly competitive work-life balance programs, including personal-time allowances, dependent care, and flexible Fridays. In addition, BGE provides unlimited sick leave, floating holidays, and robust career growth guidance, including organization-wide leadership and mentorship programs to help you build connections and shape your career. BGE goes beyond competitive benefits to attract and retain the best in an environment that inspires excellence. **Summary** The Junior Instrumentation and Controls Engineer is an entry level engineer who supports the delivery of instrumentation, control, and automation solutions for the energy services sector. This role assists on projects involving field instrumentation, process measurement, control narratives, PLC and DCS systems, SCADA and telemetry, safety instrumented systems, metering, control panels, and industrial networks. The Junior Instrumentation and Controls Engineer works under the direction of senior technical staff on assigned project tasks, prepares calculations and drawings for review, supports project teams and client deliverables, builds knowledge through mentorship and training, and helps deliver safe, reliable, efficient, and cost-effective energy solutions. **Job Responsibilities** · Assist with instrumentation and controls design and production of deliverables for energy services projects, including field instrumentation, control panels, PLC and DCS systems, SCADA, telemetry, metering, and site automation. · Prepare, under the direction of a senior engineer, instrumentation and controls design documents, including instrument index, instrument datasheets, loop diagrams, P&ID markups, wiring and termination details, panel layouts, I/O lists, and cable and conduit schedules. · Support instrument sizing and selection calculations, including flow element sizing, control valve sizing, level, pressure and temperature sizing and range setting; loop power and signal calculations, for senior review. · Learn and apply control system architecture and communication requirements, and gather information needed for protocol selection such as HART, Modbus, Profibus, Foundation Fieldbus, Ethernet/IP, and OPC, along with network layouts and remote I/O or RTU interfaces. · Draft control narratives, functional descriptions, technical reports, specifications, cost estimate backup, equipment selections, construction documents, and other project deliverables for senior engineer review. · Perform self-checks on assigned work before submittal, assist with quality control reviews at project milestones, and help verify that deliverables are complete and follow applicable ISA, NEC, NFPA, and client standards as well as project scope. · Help resolve routine design and construction-phase issues, draft responses to RFIs, review vendor submittals and instrument data for conformance with the design, and escalate unusual or complex items to a senior engineer. · Support factory acceptance testing, loop checks, point to point verification, calibration records, commissioning, and startup under supervision, including punch list tracking and as-built markups. · Communicate with internal project teams, instrument and control system vendors, and contractors on assigned tasks, and participate in client, operations, and vendor meetings alongside a senior engineer, including taking notes and tracking action items. · Build technical knowledge through mentorship, formal training, self-learning, and hands-on project and field work, ask questions when direction is unclear, and share lessons learned with peers. · Support business development and proposal efforts by compiling background information and past project data, and contribute ideas for continuous improvement of design standards, workflows, tools, templates, and checklists. **Job Requirements** · Bachelor’s degree in Electrical or Control Systems Engineering from an accredited university required. · Must have passed or be eligible to sit for the FE exam by the time of graduation. · 0 to 2 years of instrumentation and controls engineering experience. Internships, co-ops, undergraduate research, or capstone work related to process control, automation, energy services, oil and gas, power systems, or engineering consulting preferred. · Coursework-level knowledge of process measurement for flow, level, pressure, temperature, and analytical variables, along with final control elements, control loop fundamentals, and PID control. · Exposure to PLC, DCS, SCADA, HMI, safety instrumented systems, custody transfer or allocation metering, control panels, or industrial networks through coursework, internships, or student projects preferred. · Awareness of applicable codes and standards, including NFPA, IEEE, ANSI, ISA, with a willingness to learn to apply them under supervision. · Exposure to instrument sizing calculations, hazardous area classification, intrinsic safety, cause and effect development, or alarm rationalization through coursework or internships preferred. · Familiarity with design and configuration tools such as AutoCAD, AutoCAD Electrical, Revit, SmartPlant Instrumentation, MATLAB, or Python preferred. · Demonstrated ability to follow technical direction, organize assigned work, manage deadlines on multiple tasks, and communicate clearly in writing and in person with team members, vendors, and project stakeholders, including in plant and field environments. · Strong analytical, problem-solving, attention to detail, organizational, and interpersonal communication skills, with a commitment to accuracy and to learning quickly. Some of our Benefits: - 401k Match: 100% up to 4% of your contributions with immediate vesting + 3% Safe Harbor Contribution with immediate vesting - Merit-Based Bonus Compensation - Medical, Dental, Vision Insurance; BGE contributes to HSA on eligible plans - 9 paid Holidays, including 3 Floating holidays - Personal Time Allowances - 2 to 4 weeks of Vacation, depending on experience-level. Unused vacation carries over to the next year. - "Unlimited" Sick Days. - Mentorship Program – Provides you with the opportunity to learn and receive guidance from seasoned professionals. - Employee Referral Program that pays you for bringing great people into the BGE family BGE is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We prohibit discrimination and all employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, Vietnam Era Veteran Status, Disabled Veteran Status, or any other classification protected by federal, state or local laws. NO SPONSORSHIP NO AGENCIES

role: Machine Learning Engineer, New Grad - Quora (Remote)
description: *[*[***Quora is a privately held, "remote-first" company***](https://www.quora.com/q/quora/Remote-First-at-Quora)***.** This position can be performed remotely from anywhere in the US or Canada. Please visit* [*](http://careers.quora.com/eligible-countries) *for details regarding employment eligibility by country.]* ## **About Quora:** Quora’s mission is to grow the world's collective intelligence. To do so, we have two platforms: - [Quora](http://quora.com): a global knowledge sharing platform with millions of monthly unique visitors, bringing people together to share insights on various topics and providing a unique platform to learn and connect with others. - [Poe](https://poe.com/): a cloud workspace where millions of users run multiple AI agents on shared context and tools. One subscription, every frontier model, and the collaboration layer that makes them work together. Behind these products are passionate, collaborative, and high-performing global teams. We have a culture rooted in transparency, idea-sharing, and experimentation that allows us to celebrate success and grow together through meaningful work. Join us on this journey to create a positive impact and make a significant change in the world. **This role will be working on our Quora product.** ## **About the Team and Role:** Our ML team is small and highly collaborative, working on challenging problems that impact hundreds of millions of Quora users. We encourage engineers to think big, experiment with new ideas, and continuously learn and improve. With over 100 ML models in production, engineers have opportunities to take ownership of meaningful projects, work closely with experienced teammates, and quickly see the impact of their work. We're building the next generation of AI-powered systems to improve content quality and safety across Quora. By leveraging LLMs and agentic workflows, we're transforming how we detect harmful content, automate complex decisions, and respond to evolving challenges at scale. As a **Machine Learning Engineer (New Grad)**, you'll work alongside experienced engineers to design, evaluate, and deploy these systems in production. **No previous trust and safety experience is required.** You'll learn from the engineers who built these systems. **Stack:** Python, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Spark, Kubernetes ## **Responsibilities:** - Design, build, and deploy LLM-powered agents to detect and address spam, harassment, and other policy-violating content at Quora's scale - Develop agentic workflows to automate complex tasks, improving the efficiency and effectiveness of our content and user moderation systems - Design and improve ML systems that adapt to evolving abuse patterns and new challenges - Evaluate agent performance through offline evaluations, online experiments, and production monitoring, balancing accuracy, reliability, latency, and cost - Investigate failure cases, experiment with new approaches, and iterate on solutions to improve system performance - Identify new opportunities to apply ML and LLMs to content quality and safety across Quora - Collaborate with experienced engineers and take ownership of projects from early development through production ## **Minimum Requirements:** - **Availability for meetings and impromptu communication during Quora's “**[**coordination hours**](https://quora.com/coordination_hours)**" (Mon-Fri: 9am-3pm Pacific Time)** - B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Engineering or a related technical field, completed or in progress - Strong understanding of mathematical foundations of Machine Learning algorithms - Coursework, research, or project experience with LLM applications or transformer models - Strong knowledge of Python - A passion for learning and always improving yourself and the team around you - **Able to start full-time in early 2027** ## **Preferred Requirements:** - Previous software engineering experience via an internship, work experience, open-source contribution or coding competition - Hands-on experience building and evaluating LLM agents, in projects, research, internships, or production - Regular use of AI coding tools such as Claude Code or Codex - Coursework or projects in natural language processing (NLP) - Genuine interest in content safety and quality - Passion for Quora's mission and goals **At Quora, we value diversity and inclusivity and welcome individuals from all backgrounds, including marginalized or underrepresented groups in tech, to apply for our job openings. We encourage all candidates who share a passion for growing the world’s knowledge, even those who may not strictly meet all the preferred requirements, to apply, as we know that a diverse range of perspectives can have a significant impact on our products and our culture.** ## **Additional Information:** We are accepting applications on an ongoing basis. This role is a backfill for an existing vacancy. Quora offers a wide range of benefits including medical/dental/vision coverage, equity refreshers, remote work reimbursement, paid time off, employee assistance programs, and more. Benefits are country-specific and may vary. For all other locations in Canada, the salary range is $128,661 - $146,590 CAD + equity + benefits. - In equity-eligible countries, we currently also offer a flexible equity program where a portion of equity compensation may be taken as cash. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from [utility inspectors](https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities) to [first responders](https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety), [soldiers in battlefield scenarios](https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr), and [beyond](https://www.skydio.com/solutions). **About the role:** Skydio’s mechanical systems are the backbone of reliable autonomous flight. An intelligent flying machine depends on world-class engineering and an eye for detail while optimizing for simplicity; you will help architect, develop, and refine the structures, mechanisms and solutions that bring autonomous flight to a broad audience in a highly collaborative environment. **How you’ll make an impact:** - Design mechanical parts and assemblies for our aircraft, ground stations, and accessories, working alongside senior engineers on new architectures and taking ownership of components as you grow. - Partner with electrical engineers to integrate custom PCBAs, flex circuits, antennas, and cable harnesses into mechanical designs. - Work with vendors on technical questions and part reviews, in collaboration with our operations and supply chain teams. - Plan and run engineering tests, and use analysis to evaluate design trade-offs and verify that your parts perform as intended. - Follow your designs through the full development cycle, from early prototypes to pre-production and mass production, and help our manufacturing teams with assembly processes and quality and inspection criteria. - Investigate and debug failures, digging into the details to find root causes. **What you’ll get:** - Mentorship from experienced mechanical engineers and regular design reviews that help you build judgment quickly. - Hands-on exposure to the whole hardware lifecycle on products that ship at scale. - A growing scope of ownership as you show what you can do. **What makes you a good fit:** - Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or a related field. - 0-3 years of hands-on product or hardware experience through internships, co-ops, student design teams (e.g., Formula SAE, robotics, rocketry), research, or personal projects. - Strong engineering fundamentals and the ability to use them to solve open-ended design problems. - Proficiency in 3D CAD (CATIA, SolidWorks, NX, Creo, or similar), including building multi-part assemblies. - Familiarity with common manufacturing processes such as injection molding, CNC machining, casting, or sheet metal, and how they affect design decisions. - Ability to create clear mechanical drawings, or eagerness to build this skill with mentorship. - Curiosity, attention to detail, and a love of well-designed hardware. - A collaborative mindset and comfort working in a fast-paced environment where priorities shift. **Nice to have:** - Experience with CATIA specifically. - Exposure to GD&T, tolerance analysis, or FEA. - Experience with composites or electromechanical systems (drones, consumer electronics, robotics, etc.). - Experience rapidly prototyping with 3D printing, machine shop tools, or similar. **Compensation:** At Skydio, our compensation packages for regular, full-time employees include competitive base salaries, equity in the form of stock options, and comprehensive benefits packages. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. Relocation assistance may also be provided for eligible roles. The annual base salary range for this position is $132,000 - $175,000\*. Fundamentally, we believe that equity is the key to long-term financial growth, and we ensure all regular, full-time employees have the opportunity to significantly benefit from the company's success. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to enroll in the Company’s group health insurance plans. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to receive the following benefits: Paid vacation time, sick leave, holiday pay and 401K savings plan. This position and all associated benefits are subject to applicable federal, state, and local laws, as well as the Company’s policies and eligibility criteria. \*Compensation for certain positions may vary based on the position’s location. #LI-JC2 At Skydio we believe that diversity drives innovation. Singlife is a leading homegrown financial services company, offering consumers a better way to financial freedom. Through innovative, technology-enabled solutions and a wide range of products and services, Singlife provides consumers control over their financial wellbeing at every stage of their lives. In addition to a comprehensive suite of insurance plans, employee benefits, partnerships with financial adviser channels and bancassurance, Singlife offers investment and advisory solutions through its GROW with Singlife platform. It also offers the Singlife Account, a mobile-first insurance savings plan. Singlife is the exclusive insurance provider for the Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Home Affairs and Public Officers Group Insurance Scheme. Singlife is also an official signatory of the United Nations Principles for Sustainable Insurance and the United Nations-supported Principles for Responsible Investment, affirming its commitment to finding a better way to sustainability. The merger of Aviva Singapore and Singlife was announced in September 2020 and created one of the largest homegrown financial services companies in Singapore in a deal valued at S$3.2 billion. It was the largest insurance deal in Singapore at the time. Singlife was subsequently acquired by Sumitomo Life in March 2024, one of Japan’s leading life insurers, which valued Singlife at S$4.6 billion, making the transaction one of the largest insurance deals in Southeast Asia. Please note that this position is specifically intended for students seeking a Polytechnic Internship. Professional Summary: Join Singlife as an AI Engineering Intern and be part of a team that uses technology to create better, simpler experiences for our customers and colleagues. You will learn how AI solutions are built, tested and improved in a real business environment, while working with supportive teammates who value curiosity, collaboration, and trust. Responsibilities: •Support the team in building simple AI prototypes and proof-of-concepts using Python, AWS AI services, and Generative AI tools. •Help develop and test AI assistants, knowledge-based tools and workflow solutions that support business needs. •Assist with testing, debugging and documenting solutions so they are easy for others to understand and use. •Research new AI tools, trends, used cases and share practical ideas with the team. •Work with engineers and business users to learn how AI can improve productivity, service experience and everyday work. Requirements: <1.Education>: Currently pursuing a Diploma in Information Technology, Artificial Intelligence, Data Analytics, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Cyber Security or a related field. 2.Skills: Basic knowledge of Python or programming concepts, with a willingness to keep learning. 3.Interest: AI, Generative AI, cloud technology, automation, or building digital solutions. 4.Mindset: A curious and positive attitude, with the confidence to ask questions, try new ideas and learn from feedback. 5.Teamwork: Good communication and teamwork skills with a responsible approach to handling work in a trusted financial services environment.

At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. **Opportunity** Our Development team is growing and we’re looking for a Junior Quality Engineer to join us as an active engineering partner whose primary objective is to eliminate manual testing through automation, AI coding agents, and robust test frameworks. In this role, you will leverage AI coding agents to translate requirements into clear test plans and reliable test automation, prepare code changes, review and validate diffs, integrate changes, and build and harden Playwright test suites. You will also investigate test failures and flaky tests while improving CI/CD pipelines and release-confidence workflows. Manual testing remains only a small, deliberate part of the role focused on exploratory testing and evaluating complex edge cases that automation cannot cover. **About Method** Method is on a mission to transform how small businesses operate by giving them real control over their customer workflows. Our flagship product, Method CRM is purpose-built for small businesses that have outgrown spreadsheets and generic tools. With deep QuickBooks integration and a powerful no-code customization engine, Method enables users to design workflows that truly fit their unique needs. As a scaling growth company, we’re now taking that mission further, leveraging AI to develop intelligent agents that assist users in rapidly building and customizing no-code apps. This innovation is at the heart of our next chapter, and we’re looking for people who are excited to build the future of work! **The Role** As a Quality Engineer, you will be part of a driven and supportive team that’s always striving to deliver value to our customers by: - Partnering actively across engineering to decide how test automation is designed, built, maintained, and continuously improved. - Leveraging AI coding agents to turn software requirements into comprehensive test plans and working test automation. - Preparing code changes, reviewing and validating diffs, and seamlessly integrating changes into the codebase. - Running, expanding, and hardening Playwright automation suites while investigating failures and resolving flaky tests. - Enhancing CI/CD automation pipelines and workflows to maximize release confidence. - Performing deliberate, targeted manual testing (such as exploratory testing and edge-case validation) to cover critical risks that automation cannot. **What You Bring***Before you read this next section, we want you to know that we know the “ideal candidate” doesn’t exist — everybody has a unique background and skill set. Even if you don’t check every box below, we’d love for you to apply - we are building for the future and growth potential is a priority for us!* - Post-secondary education in the following areas preferred: Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering or equivalent training/experience. - Good understanding of JavaScript/Typescript, Python and Java languages. - Good understanding of relational databases, especially SQL Server. - 1+ years of working experience in developing Integration Testing (API level) with Python or other languages. - 1+ years of working experience with Selenium based tools or Playwright. - Fluent with Git source control, and GitHub. - Passionate for building engaging user experiences. - Must be self-motivated, goal driven and possess the ability to multitask and prioritize. - A team player with a positive attitude and a willingness to contribute to the overall team’s success in a fast paced environment. - Experience with the following is a nice to have: exposure to Gatling, Postman, .NET Web stack: MVC, Web API, React, Redux, MongoDB, ElasticSearch and Redis, good understanding of OOD/OOP, and experience with Agile methodology, such as Kanban or Scrum. - Demonstrated AI-first mindset and initiative, with concrete examples of using AI tools or coding agents to improve speed and quality in engineering workflows (distinguishing simple chat assistance from agentic workflows). - Strong "trust-and-verify" judgment when validating AI-generated output, diffs, and test suites (demonstrated evidence through side projects or hands-on practice is welcome, but not strictly required). **Why You’ll Love Method** 🌐 **Flexible hybrid work model** – designed to support work-life balance while maintaining strong team collaboration; **About the company** General Matter enriches uranium. We are designing, building, and operating the world’s lowest-cost enrichment services, here in the US. In the process, we are restoring America’s ability to produce nuclear fuel to power AI, advanced manufacturing and critical industries our country relies on to remain competitive. Fuel drives the cost of advanced reactor electricity production, and enrichment drives the cost of the fuel that advanced reactors consume. Reliable, low-cost enrichment is the catalyst for the nuclear Renaissance now under way. Our mission is to make nuclear not only the cleanest and safest source of baseload power, but also the most affordable. We believe abundant nuclear energy will lead to a post-scarcity society. We were incubated inside Founders Fund, like Anduril and Palantir before us, and are backed by over a dozen of the world's top venture capital firms. Our lean, world-class team of engineers and operators is applying a first-principles approach to solving the problem of nuclear fuel production. We are a mission-driven company with a culture of urgency, accountability, and transparency. Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable. **About This Role** General Matter builds its own technology: the software, firmware, control systems, and infrastructure that run an industrial nuclear fuel facility. At most companies, a security bug costs you data. Here, the software we build, and any security vulnerabilities we miss, touch the real world. The Security team's job is to find those gaps before anyone else does. We do that through offensive testing, code audits, design reviews, and hardening the systems we ship. As an intern on the team, you'll attack General Matter's products and infrastructure, while working with the engineers who own them to fix what you find. Targets include web apps, APIs, Linux and Windows hosts, cloud environments, embedded devices, and industrial controllers. You'll own real projects from start to finish, and you won't be writing policy documents **Responsibilities** - Break everything you touch, then help us fix it. - Run penetration tests against General Matter networks, services, web applications, and APIs. Prove what you find with working proof-of-concept exploits. - Audit source code and features for security vulnerabilities in languages like Python, C, C++, Rust, Go, and TypeScript. Then build static analysis rules or CI checks so the same class of bug can't come back. - Reverse engineer and attack embedded devices and industrial equipment on an isolated test bench. That includes firmware extraction, binary analysis on x86 and ARM, debug interfaces (JTAG, SWD, UART), and PLC and industrial protocol implementations (Modbus, EtherNet/IP, OPC UA). - Do threat modeling and adversarial design reviews with software, controls, and hardware engineers. Help design a secure architecture for systems before they ship. - Assess third-party software, devices, and services before they get into our environment, and work with vendors and suppliers to get the issues fixed. - Attack cloud and identity infrastructure, including IAM misconfigurations, exposed secrets, privilege escalation paths, and CI/CD supply chain weaknesses. - Build automated tooling that spots known security exposures and keeps running after your internship ends. - Present your findings and fixes to the engineers and leaders who own the systems. **Basic Qualifications** - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Cybersecurity, or a related field - Security experience in one or more of the following: C, C++, Rust, Go, Python, x86, ARM, cryptography, reverse engineering, embedded systems, or network protocols. - A strong understanding of common vulnerability classes and how to exploit them, such as SQLi, XSS, CSRF, SSRF, memory corruption, and authentication or authorization flaws. - Experience auditing code and features, and comfort reading large codebases you didn't write. - Strong investigative and analytical problem-solving skills. You keep digging after the obvious attacks fail. - Clear written communication. A finding only counts if the engineer who owns the system understands it and can fix it. **Preferred Skills and Experience** - Hands-on offensive security experience. CTF competitions are ideal, and bug bounties, CVEs, security research, or homelab projects also count. - Experience with fuzzing (AFL++, libFuzzer), static analysis (Semgrep, CodeQL), and sandboxing or exploit mitigations. - Experience with tools like Burp Suite, Ghidra, IDA, Binary Ninja, Wireshark, or Metasploit. - Hardware hacking experience, such as firmware dumps, UART/JTAG/SWD, logic analyzers, or fault injection basics. - Experience with industrial control systems, PLCs, SCADA, or OT protocols. This is a plus but not required, and we'll teach you. - Experience attacking Windows/Active Directory, Linux, cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP), containers, or Kubernetes. - A GitHub, blog, CTF writeup, CVE, or bug bounty profile that shows us something you've broken. **Additional Requirements** - Willing and able to work on-site in Los Angeles, CA, full-time (40 hours/week), for the whole internship. - All testing is done on General Matter-owned systems, within an approved scope and rules of engagement. - This position may require extended hours, and interns are eligible for overtime pay. **Equal Opportunity Employer** General Matter is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with General Matter is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status. **Compensation and Benefits** The hourly pay range for this internship is $32–$46 per hour, depending on the candidate's current standing in school (i.e. sophomore, senior). Interns will receive a monthly housing stipend, and are eligible for overtime pay. Please note that the stated hourly range is an estimate and may be adjusted based on market conditions, business needs, or other factors.

role: Mid-Level Software Engineer (Backend and Integrations) - Fixed-term Contract
description: The Role: We are looking for a mid-level Software Engineer with a backend and integration focus to join Infrastructure Services. Your main focus will be building the backend services for charging software for electric aircraft, including the integration with a partner eVTOL charging company's systems. A frontend developer is already working on this, so you will do a lot of the backend heavy lifting and work side by side with them to deliver a joined-up product. You will also contribute to one or two other areas of work within Infrastructure Services as priorities require. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to get stuck in. You will be a visible, confident technical voice for Skyports with external partners, and you can expect to travel within the UK a couple of times during the contract, with the possibility of some overseas trips. Key Responsibilities: Build the backend . Design, build and maintain the backend services and APIs behind our charging orchestration software. Own the charging integration. Lead the technical integration with a partner eVTOL charging company's systems, from agreeing interfaces and data models through to testing and troubleshooting with their engineers. Work with real-time data . Build reliable, event-driven services that handle live charging and operational data, with sensible handling of failures, retries and monitoring. Build the platform. Provision and manage the Azure infrastructure our services run on using Terraform, and help shape the shared platform, deployment pipelines and observability used across Infrastructure Services. Collaborate closely. Work with the project's frontend developer, product and operations colleagues to turn requirements and user flows into working features. Represent Skyports externally . Take part in meetings and workshops with partners, aircraft manufacturers, operators and consortium members, explaining our approach clearly and helping to resolve technical issues. Support other work. Contribute to one or two other areas of Infrastructure Services work as priorities require. • Maintain quality. Write tested, documented, maintainable code, take part in code reviews and make effective, responsible use of AI coding agents to speed up delivery. Travel occasionally . Travel within the UK a couple of times during the contract to visit partner sites and Skyports locations, with the possibility of some overseas trips. Get stuck in . Pick up whatever is needed, including work outside your core area, and see it through. About You: Technical skills Backend development. Solid commercial experience building and running production backend services in Go, including databases and automated testing. Platform and cloud engineering. Hands-on commercial experience with Azure (required), including identity and authentication, networking, storage and managed services. Experience with infrastructure as code using Terraform, containerised deployments (for example Docker and Azure Container Apps), CI/CD pipelines, observability and running services reliably in production. API integration . Experience designing, consuming and integrating RESTful and/or gRPC APIs, with a good understanding of authentication, security and caching. Real-time and event-driven systems. Experience with WebSockets, SSE or event streaming platforms such as Kafka or Azure Event Hubs. AI fundamentals and coding agents. A good grasp of AI and LLM fundamentals, and practical experience using AI coding agents (for example Claude Code, GitHub Copilot or Cursor) as part of your day-to-day engineering workflow. Working style Outgoing and confident. You are comfortable in meetings with external partners, can explain technical topics in plain language and can hold your own in a technical discussion. Can-do attitude. You take initiative, get stuck in and take ownership of outcomes. Agile mindset . You work iteratively with Scrum and Agile methods and adapt well when priorities change. Global collaboration. You communicate well and stay resilient in distributed, cross-functional teams. Willing to travel. You are happy to travel within the UK a couple of times during the contract, and possibly overseas. Continuous learning . You keep up with new tools, practices and industry trends. Nice to Have Experience with EV charging, energy or industrial systems, including protocols such as OCPP. Experience integrating with hardware, IoT devices or third-party vendor systems. Background in aviation, transport or another regulated, safety-conscious sector. What We Offer: Competitive salary and benefits package. Opportunity to work in an innovative and growing industry. A collaborative and dynamic work environment with ample opportunities for professional development. Flexible working arrangements and a supportive team culture. How to Apply: If you’re passionate about technology and keen to be part of a pioneering company that is changing the future of transportation, we would love to hear from you. Please submit your CV and a cover letter outlining your experience and why you’re a great fit for this role. Skyports is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Job Title: Mid-Level Software Engineer (Backend and Integrations) Location: London (Hybrid) Department: Technology, Infrastructure Type: Full-time, Fixed-term (12-month contract) About Us: Founded in 2018, Skyports is at the forefront of the Advanced Air Mobility revolution, developing and operating cutting-edge infrastructure for electric air taxis and leveraging drone technology to transform business operations across industries. Our business is split into two key areas: Skyports Drone Services uses drones to streamline logistics, capture data, and enhance operational efficiency, with a focus on rural deliveries, surveying, surveillance, and maritime services. Overview Are you a recent or upcoming graduate with an interest in healthcare? Would you like to have an impact on the future of healthcare, helping to design and plan campuses and systems that change people’s lives? The transition from graduation to the design and planning world is an important step in your career, so finding the right firm that focuses on helping you be successful is critical. Flad Architects has established tools, practices, and an environment that helps new graduates acclimate to this next chapter. From an advocate program; to variety in project duties and assignments; to collaboration with healthcare experts; to resources for achieving licensure and sustainability accreditations; to current technology; and more. Helping you develop and succeed is a priority for Flad. How will your days be spent This one-year, immersive experience (beginning in June 2027) will allow you hands-on experience under the guidance of expert mentorship while collaborating with internal disciplines and external clients, users, and consultants. For the 2027-2028 year, the fellowship will be offered in either Tampa, FL, or Madison, WI. You can expect to: Participate in the research, planning, and design of innovative healthcare environments for top-tier healthcare organizations, including academic medical centers and large community health systems. Receive exposure to inpatient and outpatient health care environments and workflows and innovative technologies used for healthcare planning and design. Master’s degree in Interior Design with a certification in Healthcare Design or a healthcare-related thesis. Bachelor’s or Master’s degree from an accredited university with completion of a Design and Health program/courses. Beginner Revit knowledge required. Experience with SketchUp and/or Rhino and 3D rendering software preferred. Previous internship experience preferred. Sustainability accreditation preferred. How does it contribute to the healthcare field, society, or the advancement of knowledge? What motivates you to pursue this research topic? Share any personal experiences or inspirations that have led you to this path. If applicable, describe your prior research experiences. What did you learn, and how have those experiences prepared you for this fellowship? What challenges have you encountered in your research, and how did you overcome them? Essays can be uploaded along with your application as portfolio documents. They may also be emailed to and marked as Healthcare Fellowship to supplement your online application.
