Position Overview Novelis is one of the world leaders in aluminum recycling and rolling and a leading sustainable aluminum solutions provider. Driven by our purpose of shaping a sustainable world together, we work alongside our customers to provide innovative solutions to the aerospace, automotive, beverage packaging and specialty markets. Headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, Novelis has approximately 13,000 employees in 32 operating facilities on 4 continents. Responsibilities & Qualifications Position Overview The Global Beverage Packaging Technology team, located in Kennesaw, GA, has an opportunity to participate in our Co-op program. The team is seeking a materials engineering Co-op that can join the team from May 2027 to December 2027. This role is responsible for conducting metallurgical investigations of newly developed high recycled content (HRC) beverage end product, across the end manufacturing process, from casting through end conversion. The work will establish full process-microstructure-property-performance relationships and identify key opportunities to improve product performance and manufacturing efficiency. Responsibilities Conduct metallurgical characterization and analysis of advanced aluminum beverage packaging alloys using microstructural, mechanical, and physical property evaluation techniques. Investigate the effects of alloy composition and manufacturing processes, including casting, homogenization, hot rolling, cold rolling, coating, curing, and end making, on final product performance. Develop processing-microstructure-property-performance correlations through experimental testing and data analysis. Identify key process variables and optimization opportunities to improve manufacturing efficiency, product robustness, and commercial viability. Collaborate with research, manufacturing, and product development teams to interpret results and provide technical recommendations. Document findings and communicate results through technical reports and presentations. Minimum qualifications Enrolled in an accredited Bachelor's or Master's degree program in Materials Science and Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field. Rising junior, senior, or Master's student with a strong academic record. Basic understanding of materials science fundamentals, including microstructure-property relationships and mechanical behavior of materials. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and data interpretation skills. Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to document, summarize, and present technical findings. Preferred qualifications Coursework or project experience in physical metallurgy, materials processing, mechanical behavior, or materials characterization. Familiarity with metallographic sample preparation and characterization techniques such as optical microscopy (OM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), or electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD). Experience with mechanical testing methods, including tensile testing, hardness testing, or related material property evaluations. Understanding of metal manufacturing processes such as casting, heat treatment, rolling, forming, or coating operations. Proficiency with data analysis and visualization tools such as Excel, MATLAB, Python, or similar software. Experience designing and executing laboratory experiments and interpreting experimental results. Demonstrated ability to work independently and collaboratively in a laboratory or research environment. *Please note that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. The facility includes state-of-the-art lab equipment and a diverse mix of product pilot lines that bring innovative solutions to customers in the automotive beverage can and specialty markets. Kennesaw provides a diverse and family-friendly place to live with countless museums cultural opportunities and educational institutions. Novelis is committed to the Kennesaw community and supports a number of local charitable organizations including Habitat for Humanity as well as FIRST Robotics aimed at encouraging young people to pursue the Science Technology Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) fields in order to spur the next generation of scientists and innovators. Our platform gives hardware engineering teams a single place to ingest data, analyze performance, automate test execution, and collaborate across every phase of development, so they can move faster without sacrificing safety or precision. We're a fast-moving team that owns problems end-to-end, works across disciplines, and thrives at the intersection of hardware and software. We serve top-tier commercial and defense customers, from autonomy leaders like Anduril and Shield AI to next-generation aerospace teams like Hermeus and REGENT, and performance engineering teams like Pratt Miller Motorsports, alongside mission partners within the U.S. Navy and U.S. Air Force on programs where failure isn’t an option. We’re backed by Sequoia, General Catalyst, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, and Lightspeed. Our team draws from SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, Applied Intuition, and other leading companies, united by a common mission: giving hardware engineers the tools to build the future with speed, safety, and confidence. **The role** We’re looking for designers graduating in 2027 or sooner with solid visual and product design fundamentals to join Nominal full time. You’ll own design work for defined features and product improvements, with support from experienced designers and close collaboration with engineering and product. You’ll help bring new capabilities to life, learn directly from customers, and grow your judgment as a product designer. Your work will support engineers testing and validating complex hardware systems, including nuclear reactors, rockets, and supersonic aircraft. ### 🚀 **What you’ll do** - Turn complexity into clarity. Dive into high-frequency, high-volume hardware and data workflows and translate them into intuitive product experiences. - Design alongside real users. Partner with engineers and customers to understand their workflows, identify pain points, and test potential solutions. - Partner with design, engineering, and product to research, prototype with AI, and contribute directly to product improvements and features. - Own the design of defined features from initial exploration through implementation, working with your team to clarify scope and make tradeoffs. - Collaborate with engineers throughout development to refine interactions and deliver thoughtful, usable experiences. - Evolve our design system. Contribute reusable patterns and components that improve consistency and usability across the platform. - Help shape our design culture by sharing work early, giving constructive feedback, and using customer insights to inform product decisions. ### 🎯 Reach out if… - You’re graduating in 2027 (or sooner) and seeking a full-time product design role as a new graduate or early-career designer. - You have a portfolio that demonstrates strong visual design fundamentals and product thinking through academic work, personal projects, internships, or professional experience. - You can translate a user problem into clear flows, detailed interface designs, and prototypes. - You can explain your design decisions and refine them based on feedback, user needs, and technical constraints. - You take initiative to clarify unfamiliar problems and collaborate with others to move work forward. ### 🌟 Bonus, not required - You’ve collaborated with engineers to bring a design into a working product. - You’ve used AI tools to explore ideas or build prototypes. - You’ve designed data visualizations, complex workflows, or tools for technical users. ### ### **✨ Benefits/Perks** - 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance - Unlimited PTO and sick leave - Free lunch, snacks, and coffee - Professional Development Stipend - 401k Plan - In-office hardware lab with a $250 project stipend - Annual company retreat *All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin.* ITAR Requirements *To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. # Company Overview Each year, 2.5 trillion hours are spent on household chores. At Matic, we’re on a mission to recapture that lost time, and we’re doing it by revolutionizing home robotics. Our first product, also called Matic, is a Wall-E-esque floor cleaning robot. We've built what amounts to "full self-driving in the home” with real-time 3D mapping, adaptive path-tracking, and a precise semantic understanding of the home. Our breakthroughs in spatial AI allow Matic to work reliably in real homes, using only RGB cameras and neural networks running on-device. ## Privacy First What happens in the home, stays in the home. Our robots are private by design, with all data processing performed by the robot itself, not in the cloud. ## Our Approach Before the iPhone, consumers adopted several distinct devices; cell phones, PDAs, and portable music players each served a particular need. We believe in a similar progression for home robotics, starting with single-purpose robots and building iteratively toward more complex capabilities over time. ## Our Culture Matic is a tight-knit and collaborative team, singularly focused on building products our customers will cherish. We're ultra-hardworking people committed to solving tough problems that save precious time and energy. # **About the role** Help shape how people live with a robot in their home. At Matic, we’re bringing advanced robotics into everyday life, and design plays a central role in making that experience feel natural. We’re looking for a Product Design Intern with curiosity, a strong eye for craft, and a drive to turn ideas into something people can experience. You’ll work closely with design and engineering to explore new possibilities and make the product more intuitive, thoughtful, and delightful to use. Your time will be a mix of exploring concepts, building prototypes, sharing ideas, and refining interactions. You’ll use Figma and AI tools to bring concepts to life, test how they feel, and help the team decide what to build. With room to experiment, you’ll contribute to meaningful product work while developing your own design judgment. **What You Will Do** - Explore and design experiences that connect people, software, and the physical world. - Translate complex problems into clear flows, thoughtful interactions, and polished interfaces. - Build interactive prototypes with Figma and AI tools to evaluate concepts and communicate design intent. - Present your thinking, explore different directions, and refine your work through experimentation and team critique. - Collaborate with engineers to understand possibilities, work through constraints, and bring ideas into the product. - Follow designs through implementation, paying attention to the details that shape how an experience feels. - Contribute to a consistent visual and interaction language across Matic’s product experience. **What You Bring** - Curiosity about technology and a habit of asking how an experience could be better. - Strong foundations in interaction and visual design, including layout, typography, hierarchy, and composition. - A portfolio that shows thoughtful problem-solving, design craft, and your approach to developing ideas. School, personal, and internship projects are welcome. - Comfort working in Figma and enthusiasm for exploring AI tools in your design process. - The ability to communicate your ideas clearly and explain the decisions behind your work. - Openness to feedback and a willingness to experiment, iterate, and learn. - Care for the small details and an interest in how they contribute to the whole experience. **Nice to Have** - Experience building functional prototypes with AI tools or code. - Familiarity with motion design or spatial interactions. - An understanding of mobile design patterns, accessibility, or design systems. - Interest in consumer technology, robotics, and products that connect digital and physical experiences. **Portfolio (Required)** Show us how you think and what you make. We’d like to see the questions you explored, the approaches you tried, and the decisions that shaped your work. Interactive prototypes, experiments, and short demos are welcome alongside finished designs. If you used AI tools, tell us how they supported your process and where your design judgment guided the outcome. Please include your portfolio password, if applicable.

Three key areas of accountability for the Intern Analyst, Actuary include: (i) actuarial support for pension administrative services, (ii) various actuarial funding and investment calculations, and (iii) supporting other key UPP areas such as engagement and corporate finance. This is a fantastic opportunity for an undergraduate student to gain valuable work experience in a fast-growing, dynamic environment while being a part of a new pension plan. This role is based in downtown Toronto under a hybrid work policy, allowing employees the flexibility to work remotely and in-office (approximately two days per week in-office). Position Summary We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Engineering Intern to support External Foundry Operations and Manufacturing Engineering activities. The intern will work closely with Foundry Engineering to monitor wafer fabrication activities, analyze process control data, track engineering lots, and support qualification and production programs across multiple semiconductor foundries. This position provides hands-on exposure to semiconductor manufacturing, process monitoring, yield analysis, data management, new product introductions (NPI), and foundry qualification activities. Key Responsibilities Review and analyze Process Control Monitoring (PCM) data from external foundries. Monitor Engineering Lots (ELOTs) and wafer work-in-process (WIP) status. Track wafer scrap activities and maintain accurate engineering records. Support foundry transfer projects and process qualification activities. Assist with data mining, trend analysis, and engineering database maintenance. Generate daily and weekly PCM monitoring reports and process health dashboards. Run and maintain automated scripts for PCM data extraction and chart generation. Support Manufacturing Operations, Product Engineering, Test Engineering, and NPI teams with data collection and analysis. Participate in yield reviews, process monitoring, and engineering problem-solving activities. Help organize engineering documentation, qualification reports, and project records. Assist with cross-functional communication between internal teams and external foundries.

Our mission At Healthpeak, we give our Forward Deployed Software Engineers the autonomy of a startup with the backing, scope, and staying power of a well‑established organization. We exist to transform technology into a revenue‑generating arm of the real estate business, building products and platforms that directly support our tenants, partners, and the teams who serve them every day. We are looking for interns to join us for Summer 2027 ! As an FDSE, you will be part of a small, agile pod and will directly embed with business teams. You will work side‑by‑side with operators, asset managers, and customer‑facing colleagues to rapidly identify opportunities, design solutions, and deliver real value. This is a hands‑on, high‑impact role for engineers who thrive close to users, enjoy ambiguity, and want to see their work make a tangible difference. You will relentlessly prototype, test, launch, and scale new ideas—often moving from concept to production in the matter of weeks. Our first and most important customers are our peers inside Healthpeak, and our ultimate goal is to create delightful, seamless experiences for our tenants and partners by relentlessly minimizing friction. What we’re looking for Inquisitive engineers who care just as much about why we’re building it as how it should be built. Those who dare to reimagine how work can be done. Proven programming expertise across languages such as Python, Java, C++, and TypeScript/JavaScript, with hands-on experience developing alongside AI agents (e.g., Claude Code). Backgrounds in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, or Data Science are especially relevant. Strong technical problem-solving skills, including practical experience with data structures, storage systems, cloud infrastructure, front-end frameworks, and related technologies. Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, thriving in fast-paced environments with evolving goals and iterative user feedback. Self-directed and adaptable learner, capable of working independently and making sound decisions with minimal oversight. Expected hours: 40 hrs per week over 12 weeks Pay rate: $25/hr

Depending on experience level, you will contribute to project teams through technical design, analysis, documentation, coordination, and field support while working closely with engineers, project managers, clients, and other disciplines. Contribute to continuous improvement of engineering practices, tools, and project delivery methods. Support and mentor less-experienced team members as appropriate to experience level. Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, equipment documentation, and technical standards. Understanding of electrical power systems and related infrastructure appropriate to the role and project type. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Entry-Level experience in Microsoft Excel, Outlook, and other Microsoft Office applications. Strong customer service and problem-solving skills. role: Research Intern - Interactive Multimodal Futures Group (Situated, Social & Ubiquitous Computing)
description: **Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The **Interactive Multimodal Futures (IMF)** group at Microsoft Research seeks a PhD-level Research Intern to work on a project at the intersection of **situated interaction**, **social computing**, ubiquitous computing, and **human-centered Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems**. The project will include elements of multimodal sensing (physiology, speech, gaze, gestures, olfaction/gas, etc.), signal processing, and real-time interaction. Our group’s research spans several sub-areas: - Human-centered AI for **affective and social computing,** and adaptive experiences. - **Situated interaction**between humans and AI systems such as robots deployed in the physical world. - **Conversational AI Agents**that are **socially**and context aware. - **Ubiquitous sensing and ambient intelligence** with unobtrusive sensing in the real world. You will collaborate with IMF researchers to prototype systems, run user studies, develop machine learning models, and explore technical capabilities of generative AI for human-AI interaction. **Responsibilities** Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. #### Additional Responsibilities - Design and implement research prototypes for real-time situated and adaptive interaction. - Explore the use of the latest generative AI techniques related to interpreting multimodal interaction, conversation, and behavioral signals. - Conduct user studies and analyze multimodal data. - Contribute to publications and share findings with the research community. **Qualifications** #### Required Qualifications - Currently enrolled in a Doctorate degree program in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Human-Robot Interaction (HRI), Computer Science, Cognitive Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Psychology, or related STEM field. **Other Requirements** - Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. - Please include a cover letter indicating which of the above research topics you are most interested in and aligned with. Be sure to indicate which of the specific preferred qualifications (listed below) you possess. - Candidates can upload other documents under the “Resume Manager” tab in the top right of their careers profile #### #### Preferred Qualifications We are looking for some combination of the following qualifications (please address these in your cover letter): - 2+ years of research experience using human-centered approaches in HCI, HRI, Machine Learning (ML), Computer Vision (CV), Ubiquitous Computing, or Affective Computing. - Experience writing peer-reviewed publications. - Experience with generative AI techniques, ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch), and real-time interactive systems. - Proficient collaboration and communication skills. - Conducting human-subjects research. - Experience implementing research prototypes (frontend, backend, or both). - Using human-centered design & research methods. - Familiarity with reinforcement learning or time-series signal processing. - Working with large datasets (e.g., text, vision, physiology, behavioral). **Affective and Social Computing sub-area**: - Background in affective computing, behavioral, or physiological sensing. - Experience collecting data with wearable devices. - Hardware prototyping or wearable device experience. - Healthcare/wellbeing experience - e.g., pain assessment and modeling (nociceptive signals, stress/anxiety detection), or collaboration with clinical partners. - Olfaction & gas sensing - e.g., experience with electronic noses, breath analysis, or volatile organic compound sensing. **Situated Interaction sub-area**: - Demonstrated experience in programming multimodal systems that interact with real human users, e.g., robots or virtual agents, particularly by integrating multiple machine-learned components such as computer vision, speech recognition, dialogue handling, natural language generation, etc. - Demonstrated experience in conducting research outside of a controlled lab environment, e.g., field research, ethnography, in-the-wild studies, etc. **Conversational AI Agents sub-area:** - Experience prototyping real-time conversational AI agents using tools such as the OpenAI Realtime API, including function calling, and supporting interactions via text, voice, and other interfaces. - Designed, implemented, and evaluated different personality styles for AI agents, varying factors such as communication style, voice characteristics, and emotional tone to study their impact on user experience, engagement, and trust. - Incorporated multimodal sensory inputs (e.g., text, audio, contextual signals) to enhance interaction quality and make agent responses more adaptive and context aware. **Ubiquitous Computing and Ambient Intelligence sub-area**: - Leveraging the latest in AI techniques to perform sensing in the real world - Working with multimodal AI models The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. In this role, you will work alongside experienced engineers to improve production efficiency, optimize manufacturing processes, and support new product introductions. Your contributions will help drive quality, productivity, and operational scalability across our manufacturing operations. ## **How you'll make an impact:** - Support the development and continuous improvement of manufacturing processes to improve production efficiency, quality, and operator ergonomics. - Conduct time studies and analyze manufacturing cycle times to identify bottlenecks, reduce waste, and improve labor efficiency. - Assist in developing and maintaining standard work instructions, process documentation, and visual manufacturing aids. - Analyze production performance data, including cycle times, downtime, and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), to identify improvement opportunities. - Assist with production line layouts, workstation design, and material flow improvements to optimize space utilization and manufacturing efficiency. - Participate in Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives, including root cause analysis, waste reduction, and process standardization. - Support engineering projects from planning through implementation, including data collection, process trials, and validation of improvements. - Work directly with production operators and technicians to troubleshoot manufacturing challenges and implement practical solutions. ## **What makes you a good fit:** - Currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field. - Basic understanding of manufacturing processes, industrial engineering principles, and continuous improvement methodologies. - Familiarity with time study techniques, predetermined motion time systems such as MOST or MODAPTS, or work measurement principles is a plus. - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to collect, organize, and interpret data. - Proficiency with Microsoft Excel or similar data analysis tools; experience with Python, SQL, or Power BI is a plus. - Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing concepts, standard work, line balancing, or capacity analysis is a plus. - Experience with CAD software such as AutoCAD, Fusion 360, or SolidWorks is a plus. - Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks and projects in a fast-paced environment. - Excellent communication and teamwork skills with an eagerness to learn from engineers, technicians, and production operators. - Enthusiasm for hands-on engineering, manufacturing operations, and developing creative solutions to real-world challenges. **Compensation Range:** The hourly base salary range for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Graduate students, and $70/hr for PhD students\*. As a Staff Researcher, you will work on research questions that most AI labs simply do not have access to. ServiceNow AI Research is chartered to build the future of enterprise agentic AI, from a rare vantage point: we see how agents actually behave, inside complex enterprise environments, at scale. You will contribute to research initiatives on how agents accumulate and reuse tacit knowledge, learn and improve continuously, and on their resilience, their safety, and the privacy of the data they handle. These are the real obstacles to enterprise agentic deployment today, and they surface in operational reality well before they appear in the literature. While much of the AI and NLP community concentrates on core agent capabilities, our team explores the dimensions that determine real adoption: safety mechanisms, threat detection, privacy guarantees, and responsible AI practices. You will have the freedom to publish and advance the state of the art, with the rare advantage of testing your hypotheses against real deployments rather than against benchmarks. description: Job Description (JD) – Graduate Engineer Trainee (Electrical R&D – BESS) Position Details Designation Graduate Engineer Trainee (GET) Department Electrical R&D – BESS Experience 0–1 Year (Freshers) Qualification B.E./B.Tech in Electrical Engineering Reporting To R&D Engineer / R&D Manager Employment Type Full-time 1. Job Purpose To support the Research & Development team in the design, development, testing, validation, and continuous improvement of electrical systems used in Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). The role involves hands-on exposure to electrical components, power conversion systems, battery integration, electrical protection, control systems, and new product development. The GET will assist in developing reliable, safe, cost-effective, and high-performance electrical solutions for BESS products and applications. 2. Key Responsibilities A. Electrical Design & Development Assist in the design and development of electrical systems for BESS products and containerized battery storage solutions . Support the preparation and updating of Single Line Diagrams (SLDs), wiring diagrams, electrical schematics, and electrical layouts. Assist in the selection and sizing of electrical components such as circuit breakers, contactors, fuses, relays, cables, busbars, and connectors. Support the preparation of electrical Bill of Materials (BOM), technical specifications, and component datasheets. Assist in the integration of battery racks, Battery Management Systems (BMS), Power Conversion Systems (PCS), transformers, and auxiliary electrical systems. Participate in design reviews and suggest improvements under the guidance of senior engineers. B. Research & New Product Development Support R&D activities related to new BESS product development and electrical system optimization. Study emerging technologies, electrical components, and industry developments in battery energy storage. Assist in prototype development, component evaluation, and design feasibility studies. Support the development of electrical solutions for different BESS capacities and customer requirements. Participate in product cost optimization, design standardization, and value engineering initiatives. C. Testing & Validation Assist in electrical testing and validation of BESS components, assemblies, and prototypes. Support insulation resistance, continuity, functional, and electrical safety testing under authorized supervision. Assist in testing of protection devices, control circuits, and electrical interfaces. Record test results, identify deviations, and support root cause analysis of electrical failures. Help prepare test reports, validation documents, and product qualification records. D. BESS System Integration Develop an understanding of battery technologies, particularly Lithium-ion and Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP). Learn the working principles of BMS, PCS, Energy Management Systems (EMS), and SCADA. Assist in integrating AC and DC electrical systems within BESS containers. Support the study of power distribution, grounding, earthing, electrical protection, and auxiliary power systems. Assist in reviewing electrical interfaces between battery systems, inverters, transformers, and grid connection equipment. E. Documentation & Compliance Prepare and maintain electrical drawings, BOMs, test reports, design records, and technical documents. Support the preparation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), work instructions, and testing checklists. Assist in reviewing applicable IEC, IEEE, IS, and other relevant electrical safety standards. Maintain proper revision control of engineering documents. Ensure that R&D activities follow internal quality procedures and electrical safety requirements. F. Cross-functional Coordination Coordinate with Mechanical Design, BMS, Embedded Systems, Manufacturing, Quality, Procurement, and Project Engineering teams. Support prototype assembly, design verification, and resolution of technical issues. Assist in evaluating electrical components with suppliers and component manufacturers. Participate in technical meetings and provide updates on assigned R&D activities. 3. Educational Qualification B.E./B.Tech in Electrical Engineering or Electrical & Electronics Engineering. Candidates with academic projects, internships, or practical exposure to power electronics, renewable energy, electrical design, or battery energy storage will be preferred. 4. Technical Skills Required Basic understanding of electrical circuits, power systems, and electrical machines. Knowledge of AC/DC systems, electrical protection, earthing, and cable sizing. Basic understanding of power electronics, converters, inverters, and transformers. Familiarity with electrical drawings, circuit diagrams, and Single Line Diagrams. Working knowledge of MS Excel and MS Office. Basic knowledge of AutoCAD Electrical or similar electrical design tools is preferred. Exposure to MATLAB/Simulink, electrical simulation tools, or testing instruments will be an advantage. Basic awareness of BESS architecture, BMS, PCS, EMS, and battery technologies is desirable. 5. Behavioral Competencies Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities. Willingness to learn new technologies and engineering practices. Attention to detail and commitment to quality. Good written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work effectively in a cross-functional team. Proactive approach toward identifying and resolving technical issues. Flexibility to work in laboratory, prototype development, and manufacturing environments. 6. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Timely completion of assigned electrical design and R&D tasks. Accuracy and quality of electrical drawings, BOMs, and technical documentation. Successful completion of assigned testing and validation activities. Timely identification and reporting of technical deviations. Contribution to prototype development and new product development projects. Adherence to electrical safety, quality, and documentation procedures. Participation in cost reduction, design improvement, and standardization initiatives. 7. Career Development Opportunity The selected candidate will receive structured on-the-job training in BESS electrical engineering, electrical design, product development, testing, and system integration, with opportunities to progress into roles such as Electrical Design Engineer, Electrical R&D Engineer, or BESS System Engineer based on performance and organizational requirements. Reference: The role is aligned with common GET responsibilities in BESS engineering and R&D, including electrical design support, component evaluation, testing, documentation, and new product development.

role: Stagiaire en recherche - apprentissage automatique; Research Intern - Machine Learning
description: **Overview** ENGLISH TEXT FOLLOWS FRENCH Nous sommes à la recherche d’un.e stagiaire pour se joindre à notre équipe et contribuer à l’avancement des projets clés et du programme en cours au laboratoire de Montréal. Les auront l’occasion de collaborer étroitement avec d’autres laboratoires MSR, et en particulier avec le laboratoire de New York, le laboratoire de la Nouvelle-Angleterre et le laboratoire de Redmond. En tant que stagiaire, vous jouerez un rôle crucial dans le développement, l’amélioration et l’exploration des capacités des modèles d’IA. Votre travail aura un impact significatif sur le développement de technologies de pointe, en les faisant progresser et en apportant des solutions pratiques aux problèmes réels du monde. Notre objectif est de faire progresser la recherche sur les modèles de base selon trois axes: 1. **Raisonnement** et **vérification** — Permettre aux agents de décomposer des tâches de programmation complexes en étapes gérables, de planifier efficacement, de rechercher des solutions correctes, ainsi que de formuler et de vérifier leurs hypothèses. 2. **Interaction et mémoire** — Entraîner des agents capables d’évoluer dans des environnements de développement, d’exécuter du code, d’interpréter la rétroaction des outils et des tests, d’améliorer leurs résultats de façon itérative et de conserver en mémoire ce qui s’est produit. 3. **Génération d’environnements synthétiques et de données** — Créer à la demande des environnements dans lesquels les agents peuvent exercer leurs compétences. Microsoft Research Montréal offre un environnement favorable à la recherche de pointe, une politique de publications ouvertes et des liens étroits avec les meilleures institutions universitaires de la communauté de l’intelligence artificielle de Montréal, telles que MILA, et du monde entier. We are seeking Research Interns to join our team and contribute to the advancement of key projects around agentic coding in the Montreal lab. Research Interns will get an opportunity to interact with other MSR labs, and especially with the New York lab, New England lab and Redmond lab. As a Research Intern, you will play a crucial role in developing, improving, and exploring the capabilities of efficient, discovery-oriented AI coding models. Your work will have a significant impact on the development of cutting-edge technologies, advancing state-of-the-art and providing practical solutions to real-world problems. Our research agenda centers on building more capable and efficient coding agents via: 1. **Reasoning** & **Verification**— Enabling agents to decompose complex programming tasks into manageable steps, plan effectively, search for correct solutions, verbalize and verify their hypotheses. 2. **Interaction & Memory**— Training agents that can operate within development environments, execute code, interpret feedback from tools and tests, and iteratively refine their outputs and maintain a memory of what happened. 3. **Synthetic Environment and Data Generation**– Creating environments on demand where agents can practice their skills. Microsoft Research Montreal offers a supportive environment for cutting-edge research, an open publications policy, and close ties to top academic institutions in the Montreal artificial intelligence (AI) community, such as Mila, and around the world. **Responsibilities** Les stagiaires en recherche mettent en pratique l’enquête et la théorie. Aux côtés d’autres candidats au doctorat et de certains des meilleurs chercheurs au monde, les stagiaires en recherche apprennent, collaborent et établissent des réseaux pour la vie. Les stagiaires en recherche non seulement avancent dans leur propre carrière, mais contribuent également à des avancées passionnantes en recherche et développement. Pendant le stage de 12 semaines, les stagiaires en recherche sont à des et sont collaborer avec d’autres stagiaires en recherche et chercheur.euses, présenter leurs résultats et contribuer à la vie dynamique de la communauté. Les stages en recherche sont disponibles dans tous les domaines de recherche et sont offerts tout au long de l’année, bien qu’ils commencent généralement en été. Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. **Qualifications** **Qualifications requises** - Doit être actuellement inscrit à un programme de doctorat en informatique ou dans un domain STIM connexe. **Autres exigences** - Les stagiaires en recherche doivent être physiquement présents sur le site de travail Microsoft de leur responsable pendant toute la durée de leur stage. - En plus des qualifications énumérées ci-dessous, vous devrez soumettre au moins deux lettres de recommandation pour ce poste, ainsi qu’une lettre de motivation et tout échantillon de travail ou de recherche pertinent. Après avoir soumis votre candidature, une demande de lettres de recommandation pourra être envoyée en votre nom aux personnes figurant sur votre liste de références. Veuillez noter que les lettres de recommandation ne peuvent être demandées qu’après la soumission de votre candidature et qu’elles peuvent ne pas être automatiquement demandées pour toutes les candidatures. Nous vous recommandons d’informer à l’avance les personnes qui rédigeront vos lettres afin qu’elles soient prêtes à les soumettre. **Qualifications souhaitées** - Expérience dans la gestion de projets à grande échelle de l’entraînement préliminaire ou de l’affinage des transformateurs/grand modèle de langage. - Expérience en apprentissage par renforcement, y compris le clonage de comportements à grande échelle et l’optimisation des politiques. - Expérience en création, optimisation et exécution de canaux d’apprentissage automatique à grande échelle. - Expérience en création de canaux de collecte et de conservation de données. - Capacité à collaborer, à communiquer efficacement et à travailler au sein d’une équipe multidisciplinaire. - Avoir un vif intérêt à l’application de la technologie au monde réel et à son incidence. - Expérience dans la promotion de la diversité, de l’inclusion et de l’appartenance dans un environnement de recherche. **Required Qualifications** - Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science or a related STEM field. **Other Requirements** - Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. - In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. Maritime Digital Production is the software and digital systems function within Anduril's Heavy Metal division. We build and deploy the technology stack that powers Anduril's shipbuilding factories: the data infrastructure that makes every machine and sensor visible in real time, the manufacturing execution system that workers and planners use every shift, the scheduling engine that replans production in minutes instead of days, and the AI systems that remove manual toil from the shop floor and business operations. That includes Serapis, our program building components for the Virginia-class submarine. We operate at the boundary between Operational Technology and Information Technology, incubating solutions close to the production line, validating them with real operators, hardening them for reliability and security, and scaling them across sites. The environment is fast, physical, and consequential. When our systems go down, production stops. The output of our work is not a dashboard: it is a ship. We are scaling from a founding team to more than 70 engineers across multiple U.S. sites. As an intern you join early, on a problem that matters to production, with a defined project and a named engineer you work with every day. We have built a computational geometry engine that takes a 3D CAD assembly and works out the orders in which it can physically come apart, and therefore the orders in which it can be built. It finds where parts touch, builds directional blocking graphs from that contact geometry, searches for collision-free removal directions, and produces the precedence constraints our production scheduling system plans against. It works on small and mid-sized assemblies. It needs to work on the assemblies we actually build, which have hundreds to thousands of parts. Your job is to close that gap. This is algorithms engineering with a research flavor. You will profile the engine on real assemblies, find where the time and memory go, and attack it: search ordering, pruning, memorization, incremental updates, subassembly decomposition, and parallelism. The goal is a measurably faster engine rather than a paper, and every result is held to one rule: a faster answer that is a different answer is a bug. **WHAT YOU’LL DO** - Profiling a C++ computational geometry pipeline on real assemblies and reporting where time and memory go - Designing and implementing algorithmic improvements to a disassembly sequence search: candidate ordering, pruning, memoization, and incremental graph updates - Decomposing large assemblies into subassemblies that can be solved independently - Parallelizing expensive geometric tests across cores without losing determinism - Building a benchmark corpus and harness that run in continuous integration and catch regressions - Gating every optimization on output equivalence against a reference set - Writing up results and presenting them to the engineering team **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS** - Must be pursuing master’s degree or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related field. - Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester. - Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program. - Ability to complete an in-person co-op in Santa Ana, CA, in winter 2027. **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS** - Strong modern C++, C++17 or later. You have written and debugged performance-sensitive C++ in a codebase you did not write yourself, not only coursework. - Solid algorithms and data structures, including graph algorithms such as strongly connected components and topological ordering, combinatorial search and pruning, and complexity analysis. - Computational geometry fundamentals: triangle meshes, bounding volume hierarchies and other spatial indexes, intersection and collision tests, and reasoning about directions on the sphere. - Experience profiling and optimizing code. You have used a profiler and made something measurably faster. - Research or coursework in assembly sequence planning, disassembly planning, or motion planning. If you know what a non-directional blocking graph is, or have read Wilson and Latombe or the STAAT work by Romney and colleagues, we want to talk to you. - Publications at ICRA, IROS, RSS, SoCG, or Solid and Physical Modeling, or in the Computer-Aided Design journal. - Experience with Eigen, OpenCASCADE, OpenVDB, CGAL, or a collision or bounding volume hierarchy library. - Parallel programming in C++ with Intel TBB, OpenMP, or standard threads, with attention to determinism. - Familiarity with CAD data: boundary representations versus tessellated meshes, and formats such as STEP and JT. - Experience with CMake, GoogleTest, and reproducible builds. Nix is a plus. - Python for tooling and analysis, e.g. NumPy and trimesh. - Familiarity with infinitesimal motion analysis or rotational motions in assembly planning. role: Working Student - LLM Quantization & Inference Performance
description: **About Tensordyne (formerly Recogni)** AI is transforming our world. It can perform cognitive functions that previously only humans could do, such as perceiving interactions across different modalities and environments - with the ability to quickly learn and then solve complex problems. Tensordyne is an AI system solution company that builds very high-performance, low-power generative AI inference systems. Our mission, through the creation of custom silicon, hardware and software, is to enable multimodal Generative AI inference acceleration at scale, with safe, sustainable, high-performance systems for our hyperscaler and neocloud data center customers. We are at the leading edge of advancing the latest research and product improvements for generative Al inference solutions that will make Al even more advantageous for compelling new generative AI applications.Tensordyne is a well funded, fast-paced startup company with headquarters in both Sunnyvale, CA, and Munich, Germany. We also have many talented team members working remotely across North America and Europe. We take care of our people and their families with comprehensive benefits, competitive compensation, flexible spending options, and recognition programs, because building category-defining technology starts with a healthy, supported team. Come join us as we shape the future of multimodal generative artificial intelligence! ## **Role summary** How much numerical precision does an LLM need, and where in the model architecture does it matter most? When does quantization improve runtime, and what does it cost in model quality? We’re looking for a **motivated working student** to help turn these questions into experiments and experiments into maintainable code. You’ll explore optimization methods and build reusable evaluation tooling. You’ll work closely with our quantization, compiler, and runtime engineers, and your findings will directly influence how we optimize models for Tensordyne hardware. ## **What you will do** - **Model quality evaluation:** Measure how low-precision computation affects performance on coding and reasoning benchmarks. Diagnose where quantization has the greatest impact. - **Quantization research:** Implement and compare post-training quantization methods to improve inference efficiency while preserving task accuracy. - **Build reproducible tooling:** Automate evaluations, track configurations and results, and make experiments accessible to engineers and AI agents. - **Measure runtime performance:** Characterize latency, throughput, and memory usage to understand bottlenecks under different deployment scenarios. A first project could involve exploring the quality–performance Pareto frontier of a Qwen or LlaMa model. You’ll experiment with 16-bit, 8-bit, and 4-bit quantization configurations to find the best runtime-quality tradeoff. ## **Core qualifications** - Current enrollment in Computer Science, Mathematics, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related master’s degree program. - Strong Python and PyTorch skills, including the ability to understand and modify model implementations. - Effective use of AI coding tools and critical review of their output. - An experimental mindset: you can formulate hypotheses, design comparisons, and draw careful conclusions from noisy results. - Clear communication and the ability to present experimental findings and technical tradeoffs to the team. **Strong pluses:** experience with quantization, LLM evaluation, performance profiling, or inference optimization. This role is for you if you **thrive on responsibility, learn quickly, and are naturally proactive**. ## What we offer Join a deep-tech team building the next generation of AI inference systems. Put your university knowledge into practice with leading open-source LLMs, deepen your understanding of quantization and inference optimization, and build skills in experimental design, software engineering, and AI coding tools. You’ll own a focused project, receive close mentorship from experienced engineers, and have room to explore ideas that shape our optimization methods. ## **Tensordyne's culture was built on the following values** - Put people first. We only succeed when our people succeed. - Ethics and integrity always. Be open, honest, and respectful of everyone. - Think Big. Be ambitious and have audacious goals. - Aim for excellence. Quality and excellence count in everything we do. - Own it and get it done. Results matter! - Make each person better together than they would be as an individual. - Embrace each other’s differences, and embrace that there will be differences. **Tensordyne is an equal opportunity employer. We believe diverse teams are better equipped to solve complex problems and build exceptional technology. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, race, religion, pregnancy, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances.** **A note to recruitment agencies: Please do not contact Tensordyne employees or leaders regarding this role. We do not accept unsolicited agency resumes and are not responsible for fees associated with unsolicited submissions.**

role: Spring 2027: Product Design Engineering Co-op, Shark (January to June)
description: **About Us** SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. **Powered by two trusted, global brands, Shark and Ninja**, the company has a proven track record of bringing disruptive innovation to market and developing one consumer product after another has allowed SharkNinja to enter multiple product categories, driving significant growth and market share gains. Headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts with more than 4,100 associates, the company’s products are sold at key retailers, online and offline, and through distributors around the world. **AI at SharkNinja** At SharkNinja, we’re building an AI-native culture. We’re not waiting for the future; we’re creating it. Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. If you believe the best way to do your job hasn’t been invented yet, you’ll fit right in. **Work Period:** January through June **Location & Schedule:** This is a full-time, 40-hour-per-week position with a minimum of 5 days per week onsite in Needham, MA. **There is no relocation or housing assistance for this position.** **Compensation Range:** Ranges from$30/hr - $36/hr. Specific compensation is set according to a standardized scale aligned with your educational level at the time of hire. **Join the SharkNinja Early Edge Experience:** Built for early career talent. Geared toward impact. Driven by speed. Whether you're in a co-op or internship, our early talent program is designed to provide valuable exposure to the industry and a fast-paced professional environment. You’ll dive into meaningful projects and tasks that sharpen your skills and deepen your knowledge. Along the way, you’ll benefit from professional development opportunities, community events, and connections that make your experience well-rounded and enriching. Your time with us will culminate in an opportunity to showcase your contributions and learnings to SharkNinja leaders because this is a program for those ready to shape what’s next — fast. **This role:** *Product Design Engineering Co-op, Shark* Are you excited by the idea of building the future of home innovation? Do you thrive at the intersection of creativity and engineering? Are you ready to bring bold ideas to life through hands-on prototyping, user-first thinking, and technical problem-solving? If so, we invite you to learn more about the *Product Design Engineering Co-op* As a Product Design Engineering Co-op on the Ninja team, you’ll join a passionate group of hybrid thinkers working at the earliest stages of product innovation. Sitting between Industrial Design and Mechanical Engineering, this role is perfect for those who love to sketch, build, test, and iterate—with the consumer always top of mind. You’ll collaborate with cross-functional teams to imagine what’s next for Shark, transforming insights into elegant, viable, and exciting product solutions. If you’re a creative thinker, curious builder, and motivated problem solver who enjoys translating real-world challenges into tangible design opportunities, we want to hear from you! **Here are some of the EXCITING things you’ll get to do:** - Generate new product concepts with a user-centered approach, focusing on ergonomics, aesthetics, and functional innovation. - Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to define solutions that meet functional requirements while enhancing the user experience. - Lead and participate in design studies to solve technical and user-experience challenges. - Build and test quick turnaround, low fidelity prototypes, and be able to build key findings on user testing with them. - Approach everyday design challenges with curiosity and resilience, driven to rethink and innovate **ATTRIBUTES & SKILLS:** - **Education:** Current student in a related bachelor's or master’s program or has graduated from such a program within the past year - Must be able to work a full-time, 40-hour-per-week schedulewith 5 days per week onsite in Needham, MA - Strong communicator who can convey ideas, concepts, and solutions effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences. - Strong intuition for mechanical engineering and physics principles, with an emphasis on applying this in product design, ergonomics, and human-centered engineering. - Analytical and detail-oriented, with a creative approach to identifying and addressing potential issues. - Demonstrates intellectual curiosity, a hands-on attitude, and commitment to developing elegant, innovative solutions that balance technical and user-focused design principles. - Skilled at juggling multiple projects, with flexibility to pivot as needed while keeping sight of broader design objectives. - Enthusiastic about user-centered product design, form, and function. - Experience with CAD software (SolidWorks, Creo, or Rhino) and basic prototyping tools (3D printing, shop competency). - Hands-on experience building physical prototypes in various materials (e.g., plastic, metal) and familiarity with machine shop equipment. - Basic understanding of electronics and components commonly used in small appliances (motors, sensors, PCBAs) is desirable. - Experience with rapid prototyping tools like Arduino, Raspberry Pi, or other developer kits is a plus. **Please note that, due to the high volume of applications for early talent roles, response times may vary depending on the specific role and timeline. Our team appreciates your patience!** **Salary and Other Compensation:** The hourly salary range for this position is displayed below. Factors which may affect starting pay within this range may include geography/market, skills, education, experience and other qualifications of the successful candidate. The Company offers the following benefits for this position, subject to applicable eligibility requirements: medical insurance, health savings account (HSA) with company contribution, sick time, company holidays, employee product discount, product testing opportunities, referral bonuses, and more. Hourly Pay Range $27—$40 USD **Our Culture** At SharkNinja, we don’t just raise the bar—we push past it every single day. **Our Outrageously Extraordinary mindset** drives us to tackle the impossible, push boundaries, and deliver results that others only dream of. If you thrive on breaking out of your swim lane, you’ll be right at home. **What We Offer** We offer competitive health insurance, retirement plans, paid time off, employee stock purchase options, wellness programs, SharkNinja product discounts, and more. **We empower your personal and professional growth** with high impact Learning Programs featuring bold voices redefining what’s possible. **When you join, you’re not just part of a company—you’re part of an outrageously extraordinary community.** Together, we won’t just launch products—**we’ll disrupt entire markets.** At SharkNinja, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion are vital to our global success. Valuing each unique voice and blending all of our diverse skills strengthens SharkNinja’s innovation every day. We support ALL associates in bringing their authentic selves to work, making an impact, and having the opportunity for career acceleration. With help from our leadership, associates, and our community, we aim to have equity be a key component of the SharkNinja DNA. Learn more about us: [Life At SharkNinja](https://www.instagram.com/sharkninja/) [**Outrageously Extraordinary**](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLmRfBxyGu_mKl9SF12lM1NAIx-z07uLNQ) **SharkNinja Candidate Privacy Notice** - For candidates based in **all regions**, please refer to this [Candidate Privacy Notice](https://www.sharkninja.com/candidate-privacy-notice.html). - For candidates based in **China**, please refer to this [Candidate Privacy Notice](https://www.sharkninja.com/legal/candidate-privacy-notice-china.html). - For candidates based in **Vietnam**, please refer to this [Candidate Privacy Notice](https://www.sharkninja.com/legal/candidate-privacy-notice-vietnam.html). *We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, or any other class protected by legislation, and local law. SharkNinja will consider reasonable accommodations consistent with legislation, and local law. If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact SharkNinja People & Culture at [accommodations@sharkninja.com](mailto:accommodations@sharkninja.com)*

[](http://smile.io/) is the world’s largest loyalty platform, providing easy-to-use reward programs that help scaling ecommerce brands transform one-time sales into repeat purchases from loyal customers. Over 100,000 brands use Smile to turn transactional purchases into passionate repeat shoppers. We are looking for a Junior Product Designer at Smile, to help create thoughtful, intuitive experiences for merchants and their customers while building your skills across the full product design process. You’ll work closely with product managers, engineers, and other designers to turn ideas and user needs into polished product experiences, with plenty of support, feedback, and opportunities to take on more ownership as you grow. **This is a full-time remote role working Monday - Friday with a need for your schedule to overlap significantly with existing team hours (9 AM - 3 PM EST).** **At this time, only applicants based in Canada will be considered.** ### 🌍 About the Design Team Our design team is collaborative, curious, and focused on creating thoughtful experiences that make a real impact for merchants and their customers. Designers here don't just hand off mockups and wait to see what ships. We work closely with product and engineering, but you don't need permission to make the product better. With AI and modern tooling, if you spot a part of the experience that isn't good enough, you're encouraged to own it end to end: find the problem, shape the fix, prototype it, and, if you're up for it, push it to production yourself. You’ll also get the chance to work on a product used by thousands of merchants and millions of shoppers worldwide, while being part of a flexible, remote-first team that values collaboration and continuous growth. We want to cultivate designers who take initiative, and we'll back you when you do. We value strong craft, clear communication, openness to feedback, and a willingness to keep learning. As a growing team, there are lots of opportunities to build your skills, take on more ownership over time, and contribute to how design evolves at Smile. ### 🛠 What you’ll Work on - Support the end-to-end design process for product features, from early concepts and user flows through prototypes and final visual design - Collaborate closely with product managers, engineers, and designers to turn user needs and business goals into thoughtful product experiences - Contribute to Smile’s design system by creating, refining, and maintaining reusable components and patterns - Support design needs across the business when needed, including our website, social media, sales materials, and other marketing initiatives - Use AI tools throughout your design process, including turning designs into working prototypes that help engineers implement faster and closer to the intended experience ### 👋 What We’re Looking For - You don't need years of experience. Internships, freelance work, and personal projects all count. What matters most is your eye for craft, how you think, and that you're eager to learn and grow - You have projects you can share: a website, a Figma file, a live project. Personal and side projects count just as much as client work. One great project that shows how you approach design is more than enough, and bonus points if it shows how you used AI along the way - You're comfortable working in Figma, with a strong foundation in visual design, layout, typography, and UX principles. If you're exploring newer tools like Paper, Pencil, or Elyx, we're all for it - You're already using AI in your design work or side projects, and you're excited to explore how it can improve the way we work at Smile - You enjoy collaborating with others, asking questions, receiving feedback, and iterating on your work - You’re curious, organized, and excited to continue developing your product thinking and design skills ### ✅ You'll Be Successful In This Role If You - You take initiative. When you see something in the product that could be better, you go after it - You approach design problems with curiosity and take the time to understand the user before jumping to a solution - You communicate your thinking clearly and are comfortable sharing work in progress with teammates - You’re open to feedback and use it to make your work stronger - You balance attention to detail with the ability to move work forward and iterate. - You take ownership of your work, follow through on commitments, and are comfortable asking for support when you need it ### ⭐ Nice to Have (But Not Required) - Experience designing for SaaS, e-commerce, or other digital products - Experience working within or contributing to a design system - An interest in motion design, prototyping, or creating delightful product interactions - Experience working on a remote or distributed team - Some comfort with front-end code, or experience building with AI coding tools ### 🤝 You'll Enjoy Working With Us If You - Are open to trying new things, being wrong, and learning from mistakes - Prefer collaboration and shared success over individual heroics - Want to move fast, deliver real value, and own the progress of your work - Look for opportunities to improve how work gets done - for yourself and others ### 💰 Compensation & Benefits - **Base Salary:** $85,000 - $95,000 CAD - In addition, our generous total rewards package includes things like flexible vacation, a remote work allowance, and a monthly credit to use at any of the store 100,000+ stores that uses our software. - Check out our [careers page](https://smile.io/careers) to learn more. ### 💛 Why Smile? Smile is a remote-first company built on trust, ownership, and continuous improvement. We believe great work happens when people feel supported, challenged, and empowered to do their best work. You can learn more about our culture, values, and benefits on our [careers page](https://smile.io/careers).

The CIMA+ offices in Western Canada are in the middle of a large growth trajectory. This means new, exciting complex projects you will have the ability to shape and be a part of. We are actively looking for people who want to develop their skillsets, take on new challenges, and advance their careers within the organization. CIMA+’s Energy & Resources team is a key player in the energy transition. With more than 700 highly qualified professional in this business sector, we are one of the largest teams specializing in this discipline among consulting engineering firms in Canada. Guided by an entrepreneurial culture based on innovation, sustainability, multidisciplinary agility and collaboration, we support our clients at all stages of their projects, from feasibility studies to commissioning. From the production of electricity from renewable sources to resource transformation, our expertise markets are the driving force of a successful energy transition. Regardless of the delivery mode our clients choose, we have the skills and experience required to deliver innovative solutions adapted to their reality. Join us and immerse yourself in a dynamic, innovative, and collaborative environment where you’ll make a real impact. Together, we’ll push boundaries and go above what’s expected of us to meet the challenges of tomorrow and engineer a better world! The Junior Project Engineer will support the delivery of multidisciplinary electric utility projects across distribution, transmission, substations, protection and control, telecom, civil and structural disciplines. Working under the supervision of a Senior Project Engineer, this role will combine technical understanding with project coordination to review and integrate engineering deliverables, manage interfaces, and support safe, high-quality project execution. The position is intended to develop an emerging engineer into a multidisciplinary Project Engineer capable of independently leading utility projects. This is a hybrid position, preferably based out of our Vancouver, BC office, with Edmonton or Calgary, AB as additional options. Primary Responsibilities Supporting multidisciplinary technical coordination and integration of engineering deliverables across utility disciplines including distribution, transmission lines, substations, electrical, civil, structural, P&C, SCADA and telecom; Reviewing drawings, calculations, specifications, reports and other technical deliverables to identify discipline interfaces, inconsistencies, gaps and constructability concerns, and coordinating resolution with the appropriate technical leads; Supporting the Senior Project Engineer in defining engineering scope, design criteria, deliverables, responsibilities and technical interfaces for utility projects; Coordinating internal and client design reviews, tracking comments and actions, and supporting confirmation that deliverables meet applicable client requirements, codes, standards and CIMA+ quality processes; Supporting project planning and execution through development and maintenance of engineering schedules, work plans, deliverable registers, action logs and decision tracking; Supporting project controls activities including engineering budgets, forecasting, progress tracking, change identification and change management; Identifying technical and project delivery issues that may affect scope, schedule, budget, quality or safety, and working with the Senior Project Engineer and discipline leads to support timely resolution; Participating in client and stakeholder meetings, preparing technical and project information, documenting decisions and progressively taking on responsibility for leading coordination meetings; Supporting proposal development including scope of work descriptions, engineering estimates, schedules, assumptions and execution planning; Supporting construction through site visits, field reviews, RFIs, technical queries and coordination between engineering, construction and client teams; Collaborating with utility clients, contractors, regulatory authorities and other project stakeholders to support effective communication and information exchange; Contributing to project risk identification, lessons learned, continuous improvement and development of practical, safe and constructible engineering solutions; Developing broad knowledge of utility engineering and project delivery with the objective of progressing toward independent Project Engineer responsibilities. Three 3+ years of engineering experience in the electric utility industry; University Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Civil or Structural Engineering; Registered as an Engineer-in-Training (EIT) or Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) with the applicable provincial engineering association, or eligible to register; Experience working on electric utility projects involving one or more of distribution, transmission, substations, protection and control, telecom, civil or structural engineering; Demonstrated ability to understand and integrate multidisciplinary engineering information rather than working solely within a single design discipline; Knowledge of applicable Canadian codes, standards and utility engineering practices; Valid Canadian Driver’s License and willingness to travel to project sites as required; Strong verbal and written communication skills in English; knowledge of French is an asset; Strong organizational, analytical and problem-solving skills with initiative and attention to detail; Ability to organize work, manage priorities and coordinate multiple technical interfaces and deliverables in a dynamic project environment; Ability to review technical information, identify gaps or conflicts and work with senior engineers and discipline leads to drive issues toward resolution; Ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams and build effective working relationships with clients and project stakeholders; Experience supporting engineering scope, schedule, budget, forecasting or change management activities is an asset; Experience with construction support, site activities, RFIs or field reviews is an asset; Client focused, adaptable and motivated to develop into an independent multidisciplinary Project Engineer. Integrity, team spirit, and a commitment to excellence At CIMA+, we value diversity of talent and perspective. You think you can add value, but don't meet all the job requirements? **Advanced Reentry Technologies** **Who We Are:** Inversion is an aerospace and defense company pioneering advanced reentry technology to enable next-generation capabilities from space. By combining high-performance materials, precision aerodynamics, and mission-driven autonomy, Inversion is transforming reentry into an operational capability for an entirely new class of missions. Assist in developing, documenting, and improving manufacturing and assembly processes for complex mechanical and electromechanical systems. - Create and maintain manufacturing work instructions, process documentation, and assembly procedures. - Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing efficiency, quality, safety, and repeatability. - Collaborate with Design Engineering to review component and assembly designs for manufacturability, assembly, and serviceability. - Participate in design reviews and provide feedback on manufacturing constraints, tooling requirements, and assembly considerations. - Support the transition of engineering designs into executable manufacturing processes. - Work directly with manufacturing technicians and engineers to support hardware assembly, integration, and troubleshooting. - Assist in identifying root causes of manufacturing issues and implementing corrective actions. - Collect and analyze manufacturing data to identify process improvements and support engineering decisions. - Design, build, and proof-load assembly fixtures, tooling, and ground support equipment (GSE) using CAD. **Required Qualifications** - Rising Senior in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or equivalent technical experience. - Experience authoring detailed assembly procedures, managing build configurations, and driving floor execution. - Experience designing tooling, fixtures, or GSE in CAD (Siemens NX or equivalent) and applying standard GD&T per ASME Y14.5. - Demonstrated excellent verbal and written communication skills. **Desired Qualifications** - Experience with spacecraft, launch vehicle, or high-reliability aerospace hardware assembly. - Experience with aerospace cleaning, bonding preparations, and cleanroom operations. - Familiarity with high-pressure fluid systems, pyrotechnics installation, or flight avionics harnessing integration. - Familiarity with Thermal Protection System (TPS) manufacturing processes. **Our office headquarters is located in Playa Vista, CA. Pay Grades are determined by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. Support design feasibility studies, CAD modeling, system layouts, and technical documentation in partnership with experienced mechanical engineers - Develop a systems-level understanding of how components interact within the full product, balancing performance, reliability, cost, and manufacturability - Apply iterative engineering principles, learning from test results and design failures to refine mechanical systems efficiently and effectively **ATTRIBUTES & SKILLS:** - **Education:** Current student in a related bachelor's or master’s program, or has graduated from such a program within the past year -
