role: Stage - Product Content Manager Junior - Nantes (x/f/m)
description: Chez Doctolib, nous sommes fiers d'être une entreprise résolument tournée vers l'IA (**AI-First company**). Dans ce contexte passionnant, notre équipe Product Knowledge & Selfcare vit une véritable ère de transformation de ses métiers, de ses processus et de ses tâches quotidiennes. Rattachée à l'équipe du **Doctolib Assistant** (notre chat IA), notre mission est stratégique : la base de connaissances que nous créons constitue la source d'information principale de cet assistant. Notre rôle est d'en assurer la richesse et l'exactitude afin de fournir à nos utilisateurs une qualité de réponse optimale. Nous travaillons tous avec un objectif commun et ambitieux : **réduire le taux de contact tout en offrant la meilleure expérience utilisateur d'Europe.** En nous rejoignant, vous participerez au lancement de 100% des nouvelles fonctionnalités et nouveaux produits, en travaillant de concert avec la manager de l'équipe Selfcare France, pour accompagner cette révolution technologique. Pour effectuer vos missions, vous interagirez avec l'ensemble des équipes produit cross countries : Product Managers, Product Marketing Managers et AI Trainers. ### **Vos missions** Vos responsabilités seront réparties sur deux grands axes : ***Le cœur de métier (Run & Qualité des contenus) :*** - Rédiger des articles de FAQ de qualité en français et en anglais afin d’apporter des explications claires à nos utilisateurs sur le fonctionnement de nos produits. - Assurer la fiabilité des réponses du Doctolib Assistant via l'analyse des feedbacks, et œuvrer à son amélioration en synergie avec les AI Trainers. - Définir le plan d'accompagnement "in-product" en collaboration avec les équipes PM et PMM afin d'apporter le bon niveau d'explication aux utilisateurs et anticiper leurs questions. ***Les Projets IA & L'Amélioration continue :*** - Participer activement à des projets IA innovants pour accompagner la transformation de notre métier et de nos processus internes. - Utiliser l’IA comme un levier pour optimiser la rédaction de contenus et gagner en efficacité dans la production de nos supports. - Contribuer à l’amélioration continue de notre ligne directrice et du ton de la voix, notamment pour les rendre encore plus "AI readable". - Analyser la performance et l’impact des projets mis en place via des KPIs, identifier des plans d’action et les implémenter. ### **Les qualités attendues pour ce poste** Avant de poursuivre votre lecture, si vous n'avez pas le profil exact décrit ci-dessous, mais que vous pensez que cette description de poste correspond à vos compétences et à vos besoins, nous vous encourageons tout de même à postuler ! Vous pourrez être le prochain membre de notre équipe si vous : - Avez une **forte affinité pour le produit** et un réel intérêt pour son fonctionnement et son évolution. - Faites preuve d'une **rigueur** et d'une **structure** implacables dans votre travail au quotidien. - Êtes doté(e) d'un fort **esprit critique et d'analyse** (indispensable pour challenger, vérifier et prendre du recul sur le contenu généré par l'IA). - Faites preuve d'une **grande curiosité pour l'IA** et avez très envie d'explorer l'utilisation d'outils d'IA générative au quotidien pour transformer votre façon de travailler. - Avez un véritable **état d'esprit "learn"** : vous avez soif d'apprendre, envie d'évoluer et de monter en compétences avec humilité. - Maîtrisez **l'anglais (écrit et oral)**, une compétence indispensable pour collaborer avec nos équipes internationales. **Ce serait fantastique si :** - Vous avez une expérience en gestion de projet. - Vous êtes en école de commerce, école de communication, ou dans un cursus spécialisé dans le numérique et l'innovation. ### **Notre offre** - Des tickets restaurant d'une valeur de 8,5 € par jour, dont 4,5 € pris en charge par Doctolib - Un programme d'intégration complet de 3 mois incluant la Doctolib Academy et diverses formations (langues, soft skills, compétences techniques) - Un remboursement à 50% de l'abonnement aux transports en commun - Une politique de travail flexible avec un mode hybride et au bureau ### **Le processus de recrutement** - Un entretien RH visio avec notre Talent Partner (30 minutes) - Un entretien opérationnel avec notre manager de l'équipe Selfcare France, Mathilde (45 minutes) - Un cas pratique à restituer en personne à Mathilde et à un membre de l'équipe Product Knowledge (60 minutes) ### **Détails du poste** - Stage - Temps Plein - Nantes - Prise de poste : Janvier 2027 - Durée : 6 mois - Rémunération : selon niveau d'études *Chez Doctolib, nous sommes convaincus que nous devons améliorer la santé pour tout le monde. Cela se reflète dans notre processus de recrutement. Nous évaluons les candidatures uniquement sur la base des qualifications et de la motivation, sans aucune forme de discrimination.* *Plus les idées sont diverses, plus notre produit améliorera véritablement la santé pour tout le monde. Vous pouvez postuler chez Doctolib, quel que soit votre genre, religion, âge, orientation sexuelle, origine ethnique ou handicap.* *Afin de garantir l'égalité des chances, nous vous invitons à exclure les informations personnelles (par exemple : photos, âge) de vos candidatures. Rejoignez-nous pour construire la santé dont nous rêvons tous !* *Toutes les informations fournies sont traitées par Doctolib pour la gestion des candidatures. Pour plus de détails sur le traitement des données, cliquez* [*ici*](https://media.doctolib.com/image/upload/mkg/file/privacy_notice_recrutement_fr_1.pdf)*. Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities. **Overview:** This is the team that makes "it runs on Tenstorrent hardware" actually true for real models, at real scale, and builds the infrastructure that keeps the rest of engineering moving fast. **Location:** This role is on-site in Toronto, ON. **What you might work on:** This posting spans multiple teams within Kernels, Models, Inference, Scaleout & our Runtime teams. Teams include: - Kernels: Develops high performance kernels on Tenstorrent hardware - Models: Optimizes ML models (LLMs, vision models, video and image generation, and other architectures) for our hardware - Inference Server: development and serving-side optimization - Runtime: Builds the software engine that manages memory, task scheduling, and code execution on hardware while an application is actively running. - Scale Out: communication and coordination between devices in a distributed AI system. - Compiler & Infra: Create tools that optimize AI models into high-performance programs on Tenstorrent hardware, covering memory planning, profiling, debug, and emulation. **Who You Are** - Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Comp Sci, Comp Eng, Physics/Math or a related field. - Coursework or projects any of the following: parallel processing, machine learning or distributed systems. - A high comfort level as an end user of AI and agentic flows. **What We Need** - Experience with model quantization, kernel fusion, or other optimization techniques; or low level high performance programming. - Hands on experience working with Pytorch, experimenting with and deploying models, for inference or training. - Experience with C/C++ or kernel development in languages like CUDA, or Python and at least one ML framework (PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX). - Knowledge of RTL, HDL is nice to have on certain teams. **What You Will Learn** - How models get adapted to run well on specialized hardware - How to write high performance code that can get the most out of the underlying hardware - Production ML serving infrastructure at scale - How infrastructure choices affect the velocity of an entire engineering org *Tenstorrent offers a highly competitive compensation package and benefits, and we are an equal opportunity employer.* *This offer of employment is contingent upon the applicant being eligible to access U.S. export-controlled technology. role: Junior / Intermediate Capital Cost Estimator (Electrical & Instrumentation)
description: Junior / Intermediate Capital Cost Estimator (Electrical & Instrumentation) TWD is an engineering, procurement, and construction management consulting company providing project development, execution and specialty engineering services for the oil and gas industry with expertise ranging from refinery, pipelines, renewables, food and beverage, power, downstream chemical processing, and much more. Our team is dedicated to providing clients with effective business and technical solutions through exceptional levels of service, innovation and flexibility. TWD is currently seeking an Junior/Intermediate Capital Cost Estimator (Electrical & Instrumentation) in our Pittsburgh, PA office. If you would like to apply for this position, respond directly to this ad for consideration. Though we thank all applicants that apply for this role, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Position Overview: We are seeking an Junior/Intermediate Capital Cost Estimator specializing in Electrical and Instrumentation (E&I). You will quantify and price electrical power distribution, complex automation systems, and field instrumentation for high-speed manufacturing and Food & Beverage facilities. A key component of this role involves understanding how HACCP protocols dictate the selection, pricing, and installation methods of E&I components in washdown and food-safe environments. Key Responsibilities: E&I Take-offs: Perform detailed material take-offs from single-line diagrams, instrument indexes, cable schedules, and loop diagrams for power, control, and network architectures. HACCP & Sanitary Instrumentation: Account for HACCP requirements in E&I estimates, including washdown-rated (NEMA 4X/IP69K) enclosures, sanitary sensors for monitoring Critical Control Points (CCPs), standoffs for equipment, and hygienic cable routing practices that prevent debris accumulation. Automation & Controls: Estimate costs for process automation specific to F&B and manufacturing, including machine vision systems, PLCs, DCS, SCADA systems, and automated packaging controls. Greenfield vs. Brownfield: Accurately price greenfield underground duct banks while also estimating brownfield challenges such as upgrading legacy field instruments without disrupting production or compromising food safety. Labor & Installation: Apply appropriate labor hours for cable pulling (in sanitary stainless steel tray systems), terminations, instrument calibration, and loop testing, factoring in site-specific productivity and gowning/hygiene protocols. Documentation & Sourcing: Author the E&I section of the Basis of Estimate (BOE) document and engage with electrical/automation vendors to obtain current market pricing for specialized, food-grade instrumentation. Qualifications: 2–5 years of estimating experience dedicated to Electrical and Instrumentation scopes in process, manufacturing, or F&B environments. Degree or diploma in Electrical Engineering, Instrumentation Technology, or Journeyman Electrician/Instrumentation certification with equivalent estimating experience. Knowledge of instrumentation and control systems specifically designed for food safety, harsh washdown environments, and HACCP compliance. Familiarity with AACE Recommended Practices; actively working towards AACE certification is an asset. Experience with consulting cost and schedule risk assessments a plus If you would like to apply for this position, respond directly to this ad for consideration. Though we thank all applicants that apply for this role, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. We embrace diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for everyone. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome all qualified applicants. If you require accommodation at any time throughout the recruitment process, please contact our Human Resources Team.

We're looking for a mechatronics intern who can move fluidly between mechanical prototyping and controls work to support LeLamp's development. You'll build and iterate on prototyping rigs, take on lower-level controls and calibration work that currently competes for our engineers' time with deeper domain work, and support mechanical design tasks as needed. As the platform matures, this role will increasingly bridge mechanical and controls — running test-rig cycles, troubleshooting integration issues, and translating mechanical design changes into controls adjustments. This is a hands-on role for someone who'd rather be a generalist across the physical stack than specialize narrowly in one domain this early in their career. **In this role, you will:** - Build and iterate on prototyping rigs — mechanical assembly, wiring, and basic controls integration - Take on lower-level controls tasks (sensor wiring, calibration, simple test scripts) that free up our controls and mechanical engineers for deeper domain work - Support mechanical design tasks as needed — CAD iteration, fixture design, fit checks - Bridge mechanical and controls as the product matures — run reliability/test-rig cycles, troubleshoot integration issues, and translate mechanical design changes into controls adjustments - Explore mechanistic interpretability on the models behind LeLamp’s character and behavior, using techniques like probing and activation analysis to understand why the agent responds the way it does - Help us spot and characterize behavior we didn’t design for, especially as people interact with LeLamp in unexpected ways - Document test results and communicate issues clearly to the team **You may be a good fit if you:** - Are pursuing a degree in Mechatronics, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field - Have some exposure to CAD (SolidWorks, Onshape, Fusion360, or similar) and basic controls/embedded work, from class projects, personal builds, or prior internships - Have hands-on experience with rapid prototyping, machining, microcontrollers, or simple test rigs - Have exposure to mechanistic interpretability or model-internals work (probing, activation patching, sparse autoencoders, or similar). description: Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit [](https://shield.ai/). Follow Shield AI on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai), [X](https://x.com/shieldaitech), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai), and [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI). ### Job Description: As a **Simulation Framework Engineer** (L1) on the Simulation Framework Team, you will help develop and maintain the software that connects modeling and simulation (M&S) environments with core autonomy software. You will work alongside experienced engineers to write C++ and Python code, build adapters and plugins, and support reusable software components that reduce the simulation-specific complexity exposed to autonomy developers. This is a hands-on software engineering role intended for an early-career engineer who is interested in defense simulation, autonomy, distributed systems, and technical integration. You will contribute to simulation environments and frameworks such as NGTS, AFSIM, Aechelon, HMSSimBlocks, and the emerging Hivemind Simulation Framework (HMSF). You will support the team’s migration of HMSSimBlocks capabilities to HMSF by helping implement baseline adapters, port selected modules, test functionality, and maintain compatibility for programs that continue to use HMSSimBlocks. You will also assist integration teams by investigating framework, plugin, interface, and data-exchange issues under the guidance of senior engineers. ### What you'll do: - Develop, compile, test, and maintain C++ and Python software for simulation adapters, plugins, and interfaces. - Contribute to baseline integrations for simulation backends such as AFSIM, NGTS, Aechelon, HMSSimBlocks, and HMSF. - Assist with the transition from HMSSimBlocks to HMSF by porting simulation features, updating interfaces, validating behavior, and documenting migration considerations. - Help maintain and improve existing HMSSimBlocks integrations for programs that still depend on the legacy framework. - Support the development of reusable simulation components and plugin patterns that enable other engineering teams to integrate custom sensors, vehicle models, effects, or mission capabilities. - Assist with implementation and maintenance of CIGI-based plugins and interfaces that enable communication between simulation frameworks and Aechelon image generators. - Help verify functional behavior across simulation plugins, including Common Scenario Format (CSF) file loading, DDS communications, GRID interface requirements, and Hivemind SDK compatibility. - Diagnose simulation and autonomy integration issues by reviewing application logs, network traffic, DDS messages, API behavior, configuration files, and call stacks. - Write and maintain unit tests, automated integration tests, developer documentation, and example configurations. - Participate in code reviews, engineering design discussions, bug triage, and collaborative debugging with simulation, autonomy, and integration teams. ### Required qualifications: - Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline; equivalent practical experience may be considered. - Foundational programming experience in C++ and Python through coursework, internships, personal projects, research, or professional experience. - Familiarity with Linux development environments, including command-line tools, compiling software, and basic scripting. - Understanding of core software engineering practices, including Git-based version control, debugging, code review, and automated testing. - Familiarity with object-oriented programming, software interfaces, APIs, and modular software design. - Exposure to networking concepts such as TCP, UDP, client-server communication, message passing, or data serialization. - Interest in modeling and simulation, autonomy, robotics, distributed systems, game engines, visualization systems, or defense technology. - Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, attention to detail, and willingness to learn from senior engineers and cross-functional partners. - Ability to obtain and maintain an active U.S. SECRET security clearance; U.S. citizenship is required. ### Preferred qualifications: - Internship, academic project, research, or personal-project experience involving simulation, robotics, autonomy, game engines, embedded systems, or vehicle modeling. - Exposure to modeling and simulation tools or frameworks, including AFSIM, NGTS, Unreal Engine, Unity, Gazebo, ROS/ROS 2, MATLAB/Simulink, or similar environments. - Familiarity with middleware or distributed communications technologies such as DDS, ROS 2, ZeroMQ, gRPC, or message queues. - Basic familiarity with CIGI, DIS, HLA, CSF, or other simulation and interoperability standards. - Experience writing unit tests or automated tests using tools such as GoogleTest, pytest, CTest, or similar frameworks. - Experience using build systems such as CMake, Make, Bazel, or similar tools. - Familiarity with containerized development environments, including Docker or Podman.

About the Role We're hiring a Robotics Intern to help design, build, and ship the hands-on robotics kits we put in front of students. We're scaling a program that puts thousands of robotics kits, paired with AI-powered courses, into K-12 schools, colleges, and universities across the US, and we need someone who loves building things to help. You'll work on the full kit, not just one piece of it. That means assembling and testing hardware like SO-101 robot arms and drone kits, 3D printing and designing parts, and then building the courses on Honen that teach students how to use what's in the box. Your work will be used by real students and teachers in real classrooms. This is a hands-on role. You'll spend a lot of time at a workbench, and a lot of time figuring out how to explain what you just built to a student who's never touched a robot. What You'll Do Assemble, wire, calibrate, and test robotics hardware, including SO-101 arms, drone kits, and NVIDIA Jetson-based kits. Design, model, and 3D print custom parts, mounts, enclosures, and replacement components. Help decide what goes into each kit, source parts, and write bills of materials. Write clear build guides, setup instructions, and troubleshooting docs that a teacher with no robotics background can follow. Build robotics lessons and courses in Honen, including step-by-step projects, videos, quizzes, and hands-on challenges. Write and debug starter code students use to control their robots, for example in Python. Test kits and courses end to end, find where people get stuck, and fix it. Photograph and film builds for course content, marketing, and partner updates. Help pack and prepare kits for school deployments, and support teachers once kits are in the field. Bring ideas for new kits and projects to the team. What We're Looking For Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Computer Science, Mechatronics, or a related field. Strong self-taught builders are welcome too. Hands-on experience building robots, drones, or electronics projects, through a club, team, class, or on your own. Experience with 3D printing and CAD (Fusion 360, Onshape, SolidWorks, or similar). Comfortable with basic electronics: wiring, soldering, motors, servos, and sensors. Some programming experience, ideally Python. Good at explaining technical things in plain language. Patient with debugging hardware that doesn't work the first time. Organized and careful with parts, inventory, and documentation. Excited about getting students and new learners into robotics and AI. Bonus Points Experience with the SO-101 / SO-100 arms, Hugging Face LeRobot, or other open-source robot arms. Experience with NVIDIA Jetson, Raspberry Pi, or Arduino. Drone building or flying experience. ROS or ROS 2 experience. FIRST Robotics, VEX, or similar competition experience, as a student or mentor. Teaching, tutoring, camp counseling, or curriculum writing experience. Video editing or photography skills. What Strong Candidates Look Like We care more about what you've built than what classes you've taken. The strongest candidates can show us things like a robot they built and programmed, a drone they put together from parts, a 3D printed design they iterated on, a project they documented well enough for someone else to rebuild, or a time they taught someone else how to build something. Send us photos, videos, GitHub links, or anything else that shows your work. Position Details Position: Robotics Intern Focus: Robotics learning kits and curriculum Hours: Approximately 20 hours per week Location: On-site, Beverly Hills, CA Schedule: Flexible around coursework Compensation: $3,500/month This role is designed for someone who wants real experience building hardware and educational products that go straight into classrooms across the country. #LI-SF1 About Studyfetch StudyFetch is the #1 AI-native learning platform globally, transforming how millions of students learn through personalized AI-powered education. We’re growing fast with backing from top-tier investors and a mission that’s redefining the future of education and ethical learning.

About the role StudyFetch is hiring an IT & Security Operations Intern to keep our people, devices and systems running as the team grows. ## What we’re building The marine industry supports recreation, global commerce, and national defense. And yet it runs on technology that hasn't meaningfully changed in fifty years. Until now. Arc is on a mission to electrify the marine industry. We're rethinking powertrains, software, and vessel designs from first principles. And we're already executing. We started with consumers to develop and harden our core technology. We’re now scaling production of our flagship model with new models and sectors on the horizon. Now we’re extending our platform to commercial applications, starting with tugs, ferries, and defense, with years worth of signed contracts and a pipeline that spans every vessel type on the water. The technology is proven, the momentum is building, and the opportunity is enormous. The marine industry is going electric and Arc is building the platform that powers it ## Who we’re looking for We’re looking for someone who’s fired up by our mission and ready to build. You’ll thrive here if you adapt quickly, take ownership, and care about the details. You will join our Mechanical Engineer team as a summer intern from June 14th-August 20th 2027. You will work from our headquarters in Torrance, CA. Given that we’re a startup, you will be working in a fast-moving, dynamic environment that requires adaptability. That said, here are some responsibilities and qualifications we expect to stay relatively constant for this role. ## What You'll Do - Designing and releasing hardware, with mentorship from a full-time engineer, in areas such as: - Composite structures, Interiors & Mechanisms, Marine Systems, Test Fixtures, or Tooling - Owning a defined project from requirements through design, prototype, and test over the course of your internship - Building and testing prototypes in the shop and on the water, and helping root-cause failures - Creating CAD models, drawings, and supporting analysis for parts and assemblies - Presenting your work and results to the engineering team ## Minimum Qualifications - Currently a junior or senior pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering field - Hands-on engineering experience through a prior internship, project team, research, or personal projects - Proficiency in a 3D CAD tool (NX, CATIA, or SolidWorks) - Solid grasp of mechanical engineering fundamentals such as statics, mechanics of materials, and fluids - Willingness to get hands-on with fabrication, assembly, and testing - Ability to explain and defend your design decisions - Clear written and verbal communication - Eagerness to learn and adapt in a dynamic setting. ## Bonus Qualifications - Leadership or major design ownership on a student project team (Formula SAE, Baja, solar car, electric boat, rocketry, or similar) - Experience with composites, ideally fiberglass or carbon layups - Machining, welding, 3D printing, or other fabrication skills - Experience with FEA or other analysis tools - Exposure to design for manufacturing or tooling design - Experience with NX or a PLM system such as Teamcenter - Comfortable pushing a fast but sustainable pace - Enthusiasm for boating and the water At Arc, we encourage diversity and consider all qualified applicants equally for employment, regardless of background, identity, or status. You’re always welcome to reach out even if you don’t meet many of these qualifications. Passion and aptitude make up for a lot. ## What we offer The base pay for this role is $36 per hour. Additionally, as an Arc Intern, you'll also get: - **Boat days – Yes, we actually go out on the water. A lot.** - **Retirement savings — Traditional and Roth 401(k) access** - **Safety support — Reimbursement for PPE, ergonomic equipment, and anything that ensures we keep our crew safe** - **Relocation Assistance** - **Mentorship Opportunities** - **Office perks — Daily lunches, snacks, and good coffee while onsite** ## Our values We move with urgency and build with care. We value these five things above all else: - **Ownership** over both your work and the company’s success - **Empathy** for colleagues and for customers - **Humility** in problem solving and collaboration - **Pragmatism** for navigating ambiguity quickly and sensibly - **Inclusion** of different backgrounds, opinions, cultures, and perspectives. We want people who share and embody these values. It is vital that our values align - we’d be happy to elaborate on any or all of these during the interview process.

role: Junior Managers Program (Trainee) - Start your Leadership Journey in Corporate Research
description: Ready to push the boundaries of what is known today? We are looking for visionary pioneers with a PhD and an absolute drive to invent the technological future of Bosch in our Junior Managers Program. If you have a deep passion for fundamental research, think strategically, and want to shape the future as a leader in corporate research, we want to hear from you. ​ Over an intensive journey of up to 18 months, you will rotate through the key areas of our global research and development organization. Your mission: as a catalyst, identify and develop new technologies and business opportunities that secure Bosch's long-term innovative strength and competitiveness.​ You will lead highly innovative projects from concept to prototype, receive guidance from leading researchers and top executives, and gain practical experience with technologies that will shape our world of tomorrow.​ What you will learn and develop with us: ​ You will learn how strategic research works within a global technology group—spanning areas like AI, quantum computing, or semiconductor technology—from trend analysis and patent development to transferring technologies into our business sectors. ​ As a pioneer, you will shape the foundation for Bosch's future core technologies, whether it is the next generation of AI systems or the development of novel cloud architectures.​ You will collaborate with top international researchers in our global research centers to solve the technological challenges of the future, working alongside your personal top-management mentor to purposefully prepare you for your future role as a leader at Bosch.​ Your academic foundation: An excellent PhD in one of the following fields: Information/Cyber Security, System Design/Cloud Architecture, Data Management, Software/Quantum Computing, AI/Data Science, Machine Learning/Deep Learning, Distributed Systems, Power Electronics, or Semiconductors. Your passion for the world of research: You are naturally curious, think beyond the obvious, and are passionate about solving complex technological challenges. You have already gathered initial industry experience, e.g., through relevant internships.​ Your eye for the bigger picture: You find it fascinating how scientific insights transform into disruptive innovations for a global enterprise, and you are motivated to link your research findings with Bosch's strategic goals.​ Your understanding of human-centric leadership: You live by the conviction that breakthrough research is created in teams. Utilizing emotional intelligence and empathy, you foster a creative environment where you inspire others with your ideas and achieve outstanding results together.​ You think strategically and shape the future: You identify technology trends early on, derive a clear vision for new research areas as a leader, and develop the roadmap that takes us there. You possess profound knowledge of relevant programming languages and tools such as Java, C++, Python, Matlab, MLOps, or cloud systems.​ Your continuous development: You view research as a continuous learning process and bring a growth mindset to constantly develop yourself and your topics in a highly dynamic environment.​ Your language proficiency: You communicate fluently in English (negotiation level) and possess good German language skills to navigate confidently within our local and international research environments.​ Why you will love being part of our community We are deeply invested in the growth of our team members. We have created an environment where you are supported, valued, and empowered to do your best work. Mentoring & Sponsoring: An executive-level mentor will accompany you on your journey, actively support your development, and open doors for your next career steps with us. A culture of belonging: From day one, you will become part of a global community of trainees from diverse backgrounds and locations. Build authentic connections beyond formal projects through virtual hangouts, local meetups, or our (global) trainee summits. Flexible & hybrid working: We trust you to manage your work in a way that fits your life, with a flexible start date and a permanent employment contract. We offer a hybrid model that combines office and remote collaboration. Continuous learning: Benefit from up to 6 rotations across different departments, including an international rotation, supported by a generous budget for your professional development (courses, certifications, and conferences). Are you ready to shape the future of Corporate Research with us? Apply now and tell us why you are the perfect candidate to lead the digital revolution. Do you have questions about the application process? Claudia Mertens-Baaij (Human Resources) Telephone: 0711 811 7200 Our application process for the Junior Managers Program includes multiple steps: a Telephone Interview, Assessment Center and a Final Interview. Do you want to transform your ideas into useful and meaningful technologies? Whether in the field of Mobility Solutions, Consumer Goods, Industrial Technology, or Energy and Building Technology - with us, you improve the quality of life for people all over the world. Welcome to Bosch. Robert Bosch GmbH is looking forward to your application!

Deine Mission: Als Impulsgeber:in neue Technologien und Geschäftsmöglichkeiten zu identifizieren und zu entwickeln, die die langfristige Innovationskraft und Wettbewerbsfähigkeit von Bosch sichern.​ Du wirst hochinnovative Projekte von der Idee bis zum Prototypen leiten, von führenden Forscher:innen und Top-Führungskräften betreut und sammelst praktische Erfahrung mit Technologien, die unsere Welt von morgen prägen werden.​ Was Du bei uns lernen und entwickeln wirst: ​ Du lernst wie strategische Forschung im Bereich KI, Quantencomputing oder Halbleitertechnologie in einem globalen Technologiekonzern funktioniert, von der Trend-Analyse über die Patententwicklung bis hin zum Transfer in die Geschäftsbereiche. ​ Du gestaltest als Vordenker:in die Grundlagen für zukünftige Kerntechnologien von Bosch, sei es die nächste Generation von KI-Systemen oder in der Entwicklung von neuartigen Cloud-Architekturen.​ Du arbeitest mit internationalen Spitzenforscher:innen in unseren globalen Forschungszentren zusammen, um die technologischen Herausforderungen der Zukunft zu lösen, sowie deinem persönlichen Mentor aus dem Top-Management, der dich gezielt auf deine Rolle als zukünftige Führungskraft bei Bosch vorbereitet.​ Dein akademisches Fundament: Eine exzellente Promotion in einem der folgenden Bereiche: Information/Cyber Security, System Design/Cloud Architecture, Data Management, Software/Quantum Computing, AI/Data Science, Machine Learning/Deep Learning, verteilte Systeme, Powerelectronics oder Semiconductor.​ Deine Begeisterung für die Welt der Forschung: Du bist von Natur aus neugierig, denkst über das Offensichtliche hinaus und brennst dafür, komplexe technologische Herausforderungen zu lösen. Welcome to the DNC Technology Internship Application! The DNC Technology department is accepting applications for our Spring 2027 Internship Program! This is a separate application from the DNC General Internship Application because it requires specific experience. Interning with DNC Tech is a unique opportunity for future leaders to gain real life, hands-on experience in Democratic political technology, learn and experience industry data & analytics processes, strengthen their understanding of the political process, and prepare them for future political opportunities. The program will run from January 11, 2027 - March 19, 2027 and will be conducted in an in-person, hybrid, or remote format. Interns who are based in the Washington D.C. area will have an opportunity to perform in-person work for the DNC at the Democratic National Committee Headquarters and DNC events. You must be located in the United States to apply for this internship. The DNC Internship Program provides a stipend of $3,700. Housing is not provided. During the upcoming term, interns are expected to work 20 hours per week. The deadline for applications is November 27, 2026. Position Summary: As an intern with DNC Tech, you will work on a project or projects designed to support the work of the overall Tech team and your own skills and experience. You will build your skills as a technology professional, in data analytics, engineering, or data science; software engineering; product; or supporting users of data and technology products, or cybersecurity. You will participate in team meetings and work closely with mentor(s). In addition to working on project/s, you may work on a variety of additional tasks relevant to the team you’re interning with. As an intern with DNC Tech, you’ll learn a lot about the interesting ways in which technology intersects politics. As part of the internship program, you will also be expected to assist the DNC Operations team by attending weekly phone shifts and any mandatory onboarding/offboarding sessions. In addition, through the internship program, you will have opportunities to participate in grassroots organizing, assist at DNC functions, receive personal development training, and network with DNC leadership and staff. NOTE: The Data team at the DNC are fully remote teams. Tech interns may work from any contiguous US time zone. If working from AK or HI, you must be able to do work during either Pacific, Mountain, Central, or Eastern time working hours. You will arrange a schedule with a supervisor. Technology interns still have the opportunity to choose among in-person, hybrid, or remote work like every DNC intern, but be aware that your supervisor and mentors will likely be remote. An internship at DNC Tech may be a great fit for you if: You’re willing to learn new things, and you feel comfortable learning and problem-solving on your own, with guidance from a mentor. You enjoy problem-solving and have strong communication skills. You are excited to learn about the ways that tech can support Democratic politics, and to work on things that help others. You have previous experience in politics, e.g. using Votebuilder, or volunteering for a Democratic campaign. (This is NOT required.) For the data internship, we recommend: You have completed at least a semester, ideally two semesters, of computer programming-related courses, OR have equivalent experience. We expect interns on the Data team to have done some computer programming or data manipulation / analysis previously Our team uses a lot of SQL, Python, and R but it is okay if you’ve never used one of those before, as long as you have some familiarity with programming or spreadsheet software including Excel or Google Sheets. If you’ve used one of those languages or software, or something else similar to one of those, we encourage you to apply! For the cybersecurity internship, we recommend: You have at least an entry-level skill-set in using MacBooks and Google Suite applications Our team constantly has to adapt to industry changes that happen almost daily – therefore, having a passion for technology and learning new things is required Basic Scripting: Ability to write entry-level scripts in Python, Bash, or PowerShell to automate simple tasks or parse data. Security Core Concepts: Understanding of fundamental principles such as the CIA triad, authentication mechanisms, common threats (phishing, malware), and industry recognized security frameworks (CIS, NIST, etc.). AI Security & Tool Awareness: Familiarity with basic AI security concepts such as prompt injection and data privacy risks. Include in your application for a DNC Tech internship: In your cover letter, tell us why do you want to intern here, specifically? Tell us about a time you solved a problem or learned something new. (Briefly - 1 paragraph or less is fine!) Share in your resume and/or cover letter what software / technology / programming skills, and experiences you have. What are the titles of a couple relevant classes you’ve taken? What technology related project /s (ex. an assignment from a class) have you worked on? This information helps us determine whether we have a project that will match your experience and interest. About the team: The DNC Technology department (aka DNC Tech) is a small, collaborative, multi-disciplinary tech team – we provide the tech foundation for Democratic politics. You can learn more about the team here . We build tools and applications that help elect Democrats year over year. Our work is an incredibly important background part of running successful Democratic campaigns around the country, including: Ensuring permissions and onboarding/offboarding work properly and that our data tools are secure, Ensuring we have accurate, accessible data, Building tools so that people working hard on campaigns and in other political roles can save time and energy, Making it possible for those with voter protection expertise to share accurate information about how to vote, Supporting people throughout the Democratic ecosystem with secure hardware, software, device management, and other technology problems, … and much more. Eligibility Requirements: Applicants must be 18 years of age on or before the first day of the internship and meet at least one of the following criteria: Currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a college, community college, or university (two-to-four year institution). It is highly recommended that applicants complete at least one full term prior to submitting an application. Graduated from an undergraduate or graduate program at a college, community college, or university (two-to-four year institution) no more than two years before the first day of the internship. A veteran of the United States Armed Forces who possesses a high school diploma or its equivalent and has served on active duty, for any length of time, in the two years preceding the first day of the internship. Applicants must meet all of the following criteria: Commitment of 20 hours per week during the program Physically present in the United States to participate in this internship program Required Application Materials: Resume Cover letter References SECTION: CLOSING Due to the volume of applications, we cannot review materials submitted outside the application form. All applicants must complete the application to be considered. To ensure you have the most up-to-date information, we recommend reading our FAQ page before contacting us with questions. ### Who we are At Ecosystem we believe we should be accountable for results. That’s why we've integrated engineering and construction, seeing our projects through from design concept to implementation and commissioning. And that's how we can efficiently solve complex energy and decarbonization challenges in the built environment. Here are some of the projects we've been working on recently: [Adelphi University](https://youtu.be/tjySXaQ_RSo?si=3ntwlt9jbrGumZCi), [Brown University](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Nxa-kQwsAw) and [San Diego Padres Stadium](https://ecosystem-energy.com/case-studies/san-diego-padres-stadium/). ### Why this role matters At Ecosystem, we operate as an integrated engineering and construction firm: We design with construction expertise, build with operations in mind, and optimize every decision to hit the target. As a Construction Manager, you will be deeply involved throughout all phases of the project: you will have a strong influence during the design stage; ensuring constructability and operational efficiency, before leading its execution on site. Here, you won’t be given a step-by-step playbook. Instead, we define what the building needs to achieve—and you’ll have the flexibility, resources, and the full toolbox to determine how to get there. ### What you'll do As part of an integrated multidisciplinary team working from design through completion, you will be responsible to: - Help ensure compliance with health and safety requirements on project sites and contribute to the application of best practices. - Support on-site construction operations by coordinating with subcontractors, clients, and internal stakeholders. - Collaborate with the Project Coordinator and the Construction Managers to identify permit requirements and ensure timely project delivery. - Assist in identifying and resolving technical challenges on site, applying problem-solving skills to support efficient and cost-effective project delivery. - Help track and manage changes and scope adjustments by documenting impacts on costs, schedules, and resources, and escalating risks as needed. - Support the preparation of project upgrades, including estimates and documentation, for review and presentation to the client. - Develop an understanding of energy performance measures and sustainability considerations prior to implementation. - Assist with day-to-day execution of construction activities, helping ensure alignment with budget, schedule, and quality requirements. Your professional development is an integral part of your role. At Ecosystem, you are encouraged to learn, experiment, and step outside conventional boundaries. We value audacity: where others wait for solutions to be proven, we choose to be among the first to innovate. ### Your profile - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline. - 0-2 years of construction project management and on-site experience. - Interest in complex mechanical construction. - Strong communication (written and verbal), listening, skills in English. - Team player with a positive attitude, resilience, and determination. - Quick critical thinking ability under pressure. - Top-notch organizational skills. - Field-based role with 4-5 days/week on active project sites. ### What Ecosystem offers - Annual base salary ranging from $85,000 - $100,000, with final compensation determined based on a candidate’s experience, technical expertise, and skillset, as well as geographic location. - 401K matching and comprehensive group insurance package (medical, dental, vision, life insurance, long term disability)— including a High-Deductible Health Plan (HDHP) option with no employee payroll deductions. - Paid time off per year: 10 public holidays, a minimum of 15 days of vacation, and 5 personal days. We have paid time off between December 25 and January 1 when our offices close for the holiday period for a well-earned break. - Lunch reimbursement and atypical construction schedule averaging of 40 to 45 hours per week. - Tailored career growth and development opportunities through mentorship, training, and career planning, with no cap. - Thriving people-first culture: we put our values in action in DEI, CSR, Innovation, and Social committees. We celebrate our successes together at Ecofest- watch the video [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hwnDpzNrcVU). ***Those who change the world don’t just make recommendations- they make decisions and act on them. This is what we do at Ecosystem.***

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit [](https://shield.ai/). Follow Shield AI on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai), [X](https://x.com/shieldaitech), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai), and [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI). We are seeking Autonomous Software Engineers for full-time roles starting in 2027! This is a paid, in-person, full-time position for students graduating during the 2026-2027 academic year. We are now reviewing applications for positions starting after graduation in 2027. ## What you'll do - Design, implement, test, and ship C++ and/or Python features, tools, and tests alongside experienced engineers. - Write embedded firmware in C/C++ for real-time software that controls our advanced UAV while in flight. - Develop tests, reporters, and tooling in Python to validate software behavior and performance. - Develop and evaluate autonomy software across areas such as mission behavior, planning, multi-agent coordination, decision-making, platform integration, or perception (object detection, tracking, sensor fusion, localization, situational awareness, or AI/ML-enabled workflows). - Build unit and integration tests, run and analyze simulation or bench results, and investigate failures using logs, telemetry, traces, and debugging tools. - Support software integration across autonomy capabilities, platform/vehicle interfaces, sensors, perception products, mission compute, and operator or command-and-control (C2) systems, including simulation, software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, and bench testing. - Work with real and simulated data from cameras, EO/IR sensors, IMUs, GPS, radars, or other mission payloads. - Work cross-functionally with electrical and mechanical engineers to help determine and validate software requirements. - Write documentation for setup steps, interface assumptions, configuration, test procedures, and findings to make workflows repeatable. - Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and test debriefs, and take on more ownership of features and fixes over time. ### Required Qualifications - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field, graduating between December 2026 and August 2027. - Proficiency in C++ and/or Python. - Solid foundation in data structures, algorithms, and software fundamentals. - Ability to own well-scoped tasks with limited guidance and communicate progress clearly. - Must be able to work in-person full-time. ### Preferred Qualifications - Hands-on project experience (competition team, research lab, capstone, or personal projects) involving robotics, controls, planning, computer vision, or machine learning. - Prior internship or co-op experience writing software. - Familiarity with simulation tools, ROS/ROS2, or hardware-in-the-loop/software-in-the-loop testing. - Experience with sensor data (cameras, EO/IR, IMU, GPS, radar) or multimodal AI/ML data (vision-language or vision-language-action models). - Experience writing unit/integration tests and debugging using logs or telemetry. - Comfortable working in a Linux environment and using version control (e.g., Git). - Exposure to embedded systems, real-time software, or safety-critical software practices.

role: Customer Reliability Engineer or Technical Specialist (Entry-Level)
description: The Customer Reliability Engineer or Technical Specialist works on-site at a customer facility, participating in activities with the customer to comply with the partnership agreement. The Engineer makes independent seal and equipment evaluations, selections and recommends with oversight from the account manager and/or regional engineer. Also, they may lead one or more customer reliability personnel at a customer facility. * Reviews customer applications proactively and makes specific recommendations for MTBR improvement with over site from the salesman and/or the regional engineer. * Analyzes and evaluates specific customer applications. Then submits to salesman and/or regional engineer recommendations for improvement via the John Crane Application Data Information Sheet for approval. * Directs the installation and commissioning of mechanical seals and their auxiliary support systems. * Observes, collects, and evaluates customer data while working with the account manager and/or regional engineer. Then reports seal program’s results utilizing John Crane’s current reliability management software, e.g. ServiceMax. * Maintains John Crane's equipment survey. Communicates orally and in writing with customers, company personnel, and vendors while providing counseling, recommendations, and technical assistance. * May include making technical presentations to customers or management with over site from the account manager or the regional engineer. * Provides customer training for maintenance and operations personnel as required. * Assists customer with the Management of Change process. * Collects new equipment data sheets from customer’s project engineers for review by the account manager and/or regional engineer. The candidate must be willing and able to travel as needed to support assignments. * Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering preferred for the Customer Reliability Engineer title. * High school diploma or equivalent required for the Technical Specialist title. * Experience with mechanical seals, rotating equipment and basic engineering principles applied to perform work assignments in addition to PC and software knowledge. * Knowledge of labor reporting, work order variances, QAD, MFG-PRO, SAP, or equivalent * Previous participation in continuous improvement activities including but not limited to Kaizen, SMED, and Lean activities or equivalent. * Strong knowledge of personal computers, MS Office, and machining practices. * Moderate level of understanding of the financial aspects of a manufacturing operation. * Capable of handling multiple priorities simultaneously in a high-stress environment. * Effective training, leadership, facilitation, influencing, negotiating, and interpersonal skills. * Effective written and verbal business communications * Ability to complete tasks in a timely and efficient manner. * Ability to work flexible hours including weekends as needed to meet business demands. * Experience working in a diverse environment with a global company is a plus. Job grade and compensation will be determined based on qualifications and relevant experience All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. We believe that different perspectives and backgrounds are what make a company flourish. All qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment regardless of color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, economic status, disability, age, or any other legally protected characteristics. We are proud to be an inclusive company with values grounded in equality and ethics, where we celebrate, support, and embrace diversity. At no time during the hiring process will Smiths Group, nor any of our recruitment partners ever request payment to enable participation – including, but not limited to, interviews or testing. Avoid fraudulent requests by applying jobs directly through our career’s website ( Careers - Smiths Group plc ) John Crane, a business of Smiths Group, is a global leader in mission-critical flow control solutions for energy and process industries that enable efficient and sustainable operations. Our products include mechanical seals and systems, couplings, bearings, filtration systems, and predictive digital monitoring technologies. We have a global network of more than 200 sites in over 50 countries and employ more than 6,000 people worldwide. We partner with our customers to help them keep their operations safe, reduce downtime, improve efficiency, and meet the latest environmental standards. John Crane is part of Smiths Group. For over 170 years, Smiths has been pioneering progress by engineering for a better future. We serve millions of people every year, helping to create a safer, more efficient, productive, and better-connected world across four global markets: energy, security & defence, space & aerospace, and general industrial. Listed on the London Stock Exchange, Smiths employs approximately 16,000 colleagues in over 50 countries

Open-minded and a positive attitude. Strong knowledge of basic layout composition and typography. Experience in basic-to-intermediate level photography. Maintain professionalism when interacting with or around members of basketball operations staff. Ability to work nights, weekends and holidays as the schedule requires. Excellent communication, time management and multitasking skills. Able to maintain confidentiality and use discretion with sensitive information. Strong knowledge of the NBA and the Hornets is preferred.

role: New Graduate Project Engineer I - Transportation Design
description: Are you ready to take the first step in your civil engineering career with a company that values innovation, collaboration, and professional growth? Timmons Group is looking for a motivated and detail-oriented Civil Project Engineer I candidates for in our Raleigh, NC office's Transportation Design group. ## **About us** At Roadrunner, we’re replacing the broken CPQ software that Sales teams have complained about, worked around, and given up on for years. Not improving it - replacing it. We’re building a new agentic stack called PQA - Prompt, Quote, Approve, designed for the enterprise, on a data model built for how pricing actually works today. We’re Kleiner Perkins’ first incubation since Glean, led by second-time founders with successful exits, and a team of engineers from Snowflake, Databricks, Citadel, Meta, Robinhood, Brex, and so on. We’re in-person in San Francisco, and we’re just getting started. ## **What you'll do** - **Embed with our customers.** You'll sit with the RevOps and Sales leaders who live inside Roadrunner every day, turn their hardest pricing and approval problems into shipped features, and stay on the hook until they're actually solved - not just handed off to support. - **Own delivery end-to-end, in production.** From technical discovery through go-live, you're the engineer who scopes it, builds it, and keeps it running. - **Turn one-off solutions into product.** Every customer-specific integration or workflow you build feeds back into Roadrunner's core platform. The pattern you build for customer #1 is the feature customer #10 gets out of the box. - **Ship AI agents in the field.** Deploy and tune proactive agents - quoting recommendations, deal modeling, multi-step approval workflows - against real customer data and real deal pressure, then iterate on what actually breaks. - **Be the fastest feedback loop in the company.** You're often the first to see where the product breaks under real enterprise complexity. You carry that back to the core team the same day, not next sprint. ## **What you'll bring** - **Strong engineering fundamentals** - from coursework, internships, or projects. You don't need a track record of shipping to production yet; you need to be able to build fast without cutting the corners that matter. - **Real curiosity.** You want to know why something broke, not just that it broke - and you'll dig through an unfamiliar codebase or a customer's system until you find the actual answer. - **Ambition.** You want real ownership fast, not a backlog of tickets, and you're ready to earn it. - **Comfort with ambiguity** - from a hackathon, a research project, or an internship where nobody handed you a spec. - **Clear, direct communication** - with engineers and with the non-technical people you'll be sitting across from. - **Willingness to travel occasionally** to be onsite with customers when it matters. - **Based in SF or excited to relocate** - we're an in-person team. ## **Bonus points if…** - You've interned somewhere and shipped code that real users touched. - You've built something on your own - an app, a tool, a research project - because you wanted it to exist, not because a class required it. - You've spent time close to customers or end users, even outside of engineering (support, tutoring, ops), and know what it's like to translate someone's problem into something you build. - You've picked up a new language, framework, or domain fast because a project needed it. - You have a side project. Tell us what it is and why you built it. ## **What we offer** - Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family. - Lunch and dinner, as well as snacks and coffee to keep you energized. - Take what you need vacation policy. ## **Equal opportunity** We value our differences, and we encourage all to apply — especially those whose identities are traditionally underrepresented in tech organizations. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected by law. Roadrunner is an equal opportunity employer.

[Relay](https://relaypro.com/) is the Intelligent System of Action for the physical economy. While the digital revolution has often left the deskless workforce behind, we are closing that gap by transforming analog frontline operations into a data-rich, AI-powered ecosystem. We aren't just selling radios, we're building the digital foundation for the 80% of the global workforce that doesn't work at a desk. **Why Join Relay?** - **A Proven Winner:** Join a hyper-growth company trusted by over 10% of the Fortune 500, continuing to move upmarket with massive impact. - **High Value, High Impact:** With 47% of our revenue from $100K+ ARR customers and 135% Net Revenue Retention (NRR), you'll be joining a company rooted in value creation. - **Market-Leading Innovation:** The Relay platform captures 1 billion new data points weekly and features award-winning AI tools like TeamTranslate™, with 500% YoY growth. - **World-Class Leadership:** Our stellar leadership team is built to help us scale toward our next major milestones. - **The Relay Culture:** We're dedicated to helping you do the best work of your life (BWIML), investing in your growth, living out our CHASE values, and learning from talented teammates who make the work and the wins better every day. **Now, here's what we're building, and where you come in.** ## **About the Role** Value Engineering at Relay is the bridge between frontline operational reality and enterprise investment decisions. Our Value Engineers parachute into a prospect's world, learn how they operate, and build the financial case that proves Relay's ROI at the C-suite level. This is analytical, customer-facing, high-stakes work. This internship puts you in the middle of it. The Value Engineering Internship is a two-phase opportunity: a Spring semester engagement (January start, part-time) that potentially feeds into a full-time 40-hour/week Summer internship for top performers. Both phases are on-site at Relay's world-class Raleigh HQ, located near the Lenovo Center. Strong performance creates a pathway to a return offer for a Summer or Fall 2027 internship and full-time consideration upon graduation, based on business needs. You'll work directly with our Manager, Value Engineering, and the broader GTM org. This includes Account Executives, Customer Success Managers, and senior leadership — on live enterprise deals. ## **About the Team** The Value Engineering team exists to close two critical gaps: leadership isn't always in touch with the factory floor, and new technology doesn't always translate into operational impact. We bridge both by quantifying Relay's value proposition, building investment-grade business cases, and acting as a forcing function for customer ROI. Our work shapes the enterprise sales motion, customer relationships, product roadmap, and company strategy. ## **Responsibilities** - Support the development of executive-level business cases that translate frontline operational data into P&L-level ROI. - Map prospect workflows and analyze operational metrics to identify Relay's highest-impact use cases. - Build financial models that quantify the value Relay delivers across manufacturing, logistics, hospitality, and healthcare. - Partner with AEs and CSMs on pilot strategies and account planning for key enterprise opportunities. - Conduct research on industry operations and competitive benchmarks to strengthen Relay's value narratives. - Assist in developing internal tools, ROI frameworks, and proofs-of-concept that scale across the sales org. - Synthesize customer and field insights to support product roadmap and pricing strategy conversations. - Contribute to the company's wildly well-attended intern showcase — presenting your work to Relay's full team at summer's end. ## **Required Qualifications** - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Statistics, Data Science, or a related field. - Expected graduation between December 2027 and May 2029. - Minimum GPA of 3.7 - No employer work authorization sponsorship available — candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship, now or in the future. - Strong quantitative and analytical skills; comfortable building models and working with data. - Excellent written and verbal communication — ability to synthesize complexity into a clear, executive-ready narrative. - Available to work onsite at Relay's Raleigh HQ (near the Lenovo Center) for both the Spring engagement and the full-time Summer program. ## **Preferred Qualifications** - Coursework or project experience in operations research, systems engineering, supply chain, or financial analysis. - Exposure to manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, or hospitality environments through coursework, co-op, or personal experience. - Familiarity with data analysis tools (Excel, Python, SQL) and/or data visualization. - A genuine curiosity about how physical-world businesses operate and where technology creates real impact. ## **What success and impact look like in this role** By the end of the Spring engagement, you've shipped at least one analysis or framework that's been used in a live enterprise deal. By mid-summer, you're running financial models and contributing to business cases with real ownership — not just support. By the final showcase, you've presented work that a senior leader would put in front of a Fortune 500 prospect. Top performers earn a return Summer or Fall 2027 internship offer and are on the radar for full-time consideration upon graduation. ## **What Makes This Internship Different** - **Executive exposure:** Regular touchpoints with Relay's senior leadership team, including Q&A sessions, Breakfast with the CEO, and working sessions. - **Real ownership:** You'll own a project from kickoff to final presentation — not a shadow assignment. - **Cross-functional cohort:** Work alongside interns from across the business, not just your team. - **Structured learning:** Skill-building sessions covering financial modeling, operations strategy, sales craft, and professional development. - **Intern showcase:** Present your work to the full company at the end of the summer. - **Raleigh HQ experience:** Team lunches, volunteer Intern Impact Day, social events, and a front-row seat to how a scaling tech company operates. - **Pathway that matters:** This isn't a résumé builder for its own sake. Strong performers get return offers and full-time pipeline consideration. ## **Why Join Relay?** Our culture hinges on Relayers getting LIT up in an environment that fosters Learning, Impact, and Teamwork, where we CHASE the best work of our lives. BWIML - Best Work In My Life. **The future of frontline work is being built here. Come build it with us. role: KIP Spring 2027 - Economic Research Intern - Fulcrum Foundation
description: **[The Koch Internship Program](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/koch-internship-program/) (KIP)** is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the [admissions process](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/application-process/) early! **Overview** [The Fulcrum Foundation](https://www.fulcrumregs.org/) seeks an intern to support research on state government regulatory policy and its effects on economic growth, entrepreneurship, labor markets, housing, occupational licensing, permitting, and related public policy issues. Interns will work closely with senior researchers to gather and organize data, review proposed rules and administrative records, assist with research for public comment letters submitted to state agencies and legislatures, and contribute to policy briefs and reports intended for policymakers and the broader public. The internship is designed for undergraduate students, recent graduates, and early-stage graduate or law students interested in public policy, economics, law, or government. Prior research experience is helpful but not required; we are looking for careful, curious people who write well and can work independently in a remote setting. **Research Areas** Potential areas of work include: - Administrative law, rulemaking, and the public comment process - Occupational licensing - Business permitting and approvals - Housing and land-use regulation - Small business and entrepreneurship policy - State economic development - Regulatory impact analysis - Government modernization and process reform - Labor market regulation - Institutional determinants of economic growth **Responsibilities** - Assist with research for public comment letters on proposed state rules and regulations, including reviewing rulemaking notices, summarizing proposed rule text and agency justifications, and identifying relevant statutes, prior comments, and existing research. - Help draft and fact-check sections of comment letters, and compile supporting evidence, citations, and data appendices under the direction of senior staff. - Track state regulatory proposals, legislative activity, and agency actions relevant to Fulcrum’s research agenda. - Collect, organize, and document data from government websites, administrative records, and other publicly available sources. - Help maintain measures of regulatory burden, permitting processes, occupational licensing requirements, and related policy variables. - Conduct literature reviews and summarize academic and policy research for ongoing projects. - Draft sections of policy briefs, research summaries, and other written products, and assist with editing and citation. - Assist with basic descriptive analysis, tables, and charts using spreadsheet or statistical software. - Participate in research team meetings and contribute to project planning. **Qualifications** Required: - Current undergraduate, graduate, or law student, or recent graduate, in economics, public policy, political science, law, public administration, or a related field. - Strong writing skills and attention to detail. - Ability to read and accurately summarize dense material such as proposed rules, statutes, and academic research. - Proficiency with Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets. - Ability to work independently and meet deadlines in a remote environment. - Located in and authorized to work in the United States for the duration of the program, and able to attend all required KIP programming, including the two-day summit in Arlington, Virginia. Preferred: - Coursework in economics, statistics, public policy, or administrative law. - Familiarity with R, Stata, Python, or another statistical program (not required). - Prior research experience through coursework, a research assistant position, or an internship. - Interest in state government policy, regulatory institutions, and economic development.

description: At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive. Our Machine Learning Engineers are excited to work on these challenging problems and redefine solutions to directly impact various aspects of Lyft's primary business. Working closely with a Staff ML Engineer mentor, you'll scope the problem, develop and evaluate new methods on real data, and take the work far enough that it can be shared with the research community, with the goal of a paper submission to a top ML venue. A track record of ML research, shown through publications, preprints, or substantial research projects - Strong foundation in reinforcement learning and sequential decision making, especially problems with delayed or long-horizon rewards - Solid grounding in both causal inference and counterfactual evaluation - Good understanding of ML libraries like PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX - Strong programming skills in Python or a similar language - Proven ability to effectively turn research ML papers into working code - Curiosity and ability to quickly learn new concepts and technologies - Strong problem solving mindset, resourcefulness, and willingness to figure things out independently through research or collaboratively through brainstorming - Demonstrated oral and written communication skills - **Bonus Points** - Publications at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, KDD, WWW, RecSys, or AAAI - Experience with offline reinforcement learning, off-policy evaluation, or learning from logged interaction data, recommender systems or personalization - description: ## **DRYFT** Ideas only change the world when you build them at scale. That’s what Dryft is here for. Dryft builds models that automate complex human decisions in manufacturing operations. We capture the knowledge of experienced operators across supply chain, production planning, engineering and more, simulate the consequences of their decisions, and use this understanding to help run their business. Our customers include some of the largest robotics, machine and component manufacturers in the world. We’re a small, talent-dense team with modest roots and a love for the physical world: cars, machines, planes. Our team includes graduates from Stanford, Berkeley, CDTM and TUM, winners of Stanford TreeHacks, recipients of Fulbright & Haniel scholarships, and people who have built everything from robots and race cars to software with millions of downloads. What matters more to us than credentials is how people work: humility, hard work, speed, kindness, deep customer care, and a willingness to take on problems others avoid. Working at Dryft is hard. You get unusual ownership early on, with real responsibility. But that’s also what makes it one of the biggest learning experiences of your life. We’re backed by founders and operators behind some of the most legendary tech companies of our time, Tier-1 U.S. venture firms, and board members of global industrial companies. ERPs ran the physical world for half a century. Dryft is building the intelligence layer that will power the next. ​ ## **THE ROLE** As a **Member of Technical Staff Intern**, you'll build the system that decides how some of the largest manufacturers in the world operate. That means combining agent-based reasoning with mathematical optimization and simulation on large-scale industrial data. - **Build agents people trust** – when an agent runs a factory's week, the largest industrial companies in the world have to trust it with their critical processes and understand every decision it makes; you build the routing, orchestration and guardrails behind that - **Ship features end-to-end** – you understand the user need, and you get the freedom to build it across the LLM pipeline, infrastructure, backend and frontend, in production in your first weeks - **Work close to the users** – sit with the planners who use it, see what would make their work 10x faster, and build it You'll own your own features from day one, and what you ship decides what a plant does next week. ​ ## **YOU** - **Full-stack shipper** – you've shipped production code end-to-end, you build scalable backend and infra that handles massive amounts of structured and unstructured data, and you build the interface that makes it usable - **Highly technical** – you've built something technically hard, and you can walk us through every decision behind it - **Product sense** – you spot the feature hiding in a user's complaint, and you've deleted your own favorite one because nobody used it - **You care about getting it right** – you know when it has to be 100% and when to keep it simple, and when it matters, you're still chasing the root cause at 2am - **Sense of urgency** – you'd rather ship it tonight than sleep on an open PR - **Relocation** – you're ready to work onsite in San Francisco (we support visa) ​ ## **TECH STACK** - **FE (TypeScript):** React, Chakra UI v3, TanStack Router, TanStack Query, Vite - **BE (Python):** FastAPI with Pydantic v2, Temporal, Postgres with pgvector, dagster - **AI:** Pydantic AI, Langfuse
