Description de l’équipe Au sein de la Direction des Achats Accor, vous rejoindrez l’équipe Data et contribuerez à des projets structurants autour de la gouvernance et de la valorisation des données. L’équipe déploie actuellement un Data Catalog au sein de la Direction des Achats afin de mieux documenter, structurer et faciliter l’usage des données. Ce stage s’inscrit au démarrage de ce déploiement, avec des enjeux concrets de documentation, d’accompagnement des contributeurs et d’adoption de l’outil auprès d’une communauté potentielle de 300 utilisateurs. Vos missions Rattaché(e) à l’équipe Data, vous interviendrez sur les sujets suivants : Participer à la cartographie des actifs data à documenter au sein du périmètre Achats. Identifier les data owners et les accompagner dans la contribution, la clarification et la validation des contenus. Alimenter le Data Catalog avec les éléments de documentation nécessaires : dictionnaire de données, définitions, lineage, indicateurs clés. Suivre et analyser des KPI du Data Catalog (adoption, couverture, complétude, gaps d’information, fraîcheur des contenus) afin d’identifier les priorités d’action et de valoriser les progrès réalisés auprès des sponsors. Contribuer à la structuration de la gouvernance de données et à la formalisation de bonnes pratiques de documentation et de gestion de la donnée. Accompagner les équipes Dev et Business dans l’adoption de ces bonnes pratiques. Participer à l’animation de la communauté data : communication, partage d’informations, collecte de retours et amélioration continue. Et vous? Étudiant(e) en Bac +4/5, en école d’ingénieur, école de commerce ou université, avec une spécialisation en data, BI, data management ou domaine équivalent. Une première expérience (stage ou alternance) en data, BI, gouvernance ou gestion de projet est appréciée. Bonne maîtrise d’Excel. La connaissance d’outils de data visualisation est un plus, notamment Tableau. Bases en SQL et/ou Python appréciées. Rigueur, sens de l’organisation, capacité d’analyse et de synthèse. Bon relationnel et aptitude à collaborer avec des interlocuteurs variés, en français comme en anglais. Curiosité, motivation et envie de contribuer à des projets data concrets et structurants. 💡 Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? Des échanges réguliers pour vous accompagner tout au long de votre expérience chez Accor. Votre talent et votre motivation sont nos seuls critères de sélection. Nous valorisons la richesse des diverses nationalités, personnalités et parcours. Nous nous adaptons aux besoins spécifiques de nos collaborateurs, notamment ceux en situation de handicap. Pour nous, le recrutement est avant tout une histoire de rencontres. 📋 Notre processus de recrutement Cette mission vous attire ? Postulez et nous vous proposerons : Un ou deux échanges avec le manager et les membres de l'équipe, Un feedback personnalisé. Convention de stage obligatoire, délivrée par un établissement d'enseignement supérieur diplômant. 🌍 Rejoignez Accor — une aventure professionnelle au cœur d'un groupe engagé, international et en transformation Accor, leader mondial de l'hospitalité, présent dans plus de 110 pays avec 5 500 hôtels, vous ouvre ses portes, situées à Issy-les-Moulineaux. C'est ici que convergent les expertises globales du Groupe : stratégie, finance, ressources humaines, juridique, technologies, marketing, développement durable, communication, audit, achats, etc. Rejoindre Accor en stage, c'est contribuer à des projets concrets et gagner en expérience auprès d'équipes internationales engagées.

***Mechanical Engineering Intern*** ***- Position Description -*** **Position Overview:** As a Mechanical Engineering Intern you’ll step into the world of automation innovation by supporting our skilled engineering team, including Project Managers, Controls Engineers, and Mechanical Design Engineers. You’ll contribute to the design, development, and testing of cutting-edge automation systems. This internship offers a hands-on introduction to CAD modeling, robotic systems, and manufacturing processes, providing a dynamic platform to apply your academic knowledge, develop technical skills, and launch your engineering career under expert mentorship. **Rotational Development Path:** - Rotation 1 – Foundations: Gain familiarity with SolidWorks, mechanical drawings, Axis standards, common purchased components, project release procedures, and documentation. Contribute to projects by creating basic drawings, completing documentation packages, and executing simple design tasks. - Rotation 2 – Expansion: Execute more complex design tasks including detailing and revisions to existing tooling. Be able to create purchase requisitions and complete design release procedures in full. Assist in creating drawing packages for projects. Work with other departments to provide machine layouts, simulation files, controls component lists, and certification files. - Rotation 3 – Application: Be able to complete drawing packages for full project scopes. Gain further understanding of principles of designing for machining, assembly, and maintenance. Support customer projects through revisions, simple assembly design, and completion of more complex drawing packages. Demonstrate increased design independence and meet assigned deadlines, while continuing to maintain design quality. **Key Responsibilities:** - Assist in creating 3D models and 2D technical drawings for automation components (e.g., fixtures, conveyors) using CAD software (SolidWorks preferred). - Support the design of basic mechanical parts, such as brackets or mounts, under the guidance of senior engineers. - Participate in prototype assembly, testing, and troubleshooting, gaining practical experience with robotic and automated systems. - Help maintain engineering documentation, including Bills of Materials (BOMs) and design records, ensuring accuracy and organization. - Conduct introductory tolerance analyses or component measurements to support design validation. - Research industry standards (e.g., OSHA, ANSI) and material properties to assist project teams. - Collaborate with engineers to brainstorm solutions and document findings for ongoing projects. **Qualifications:** - **Education:** Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree program in Mechanical Engineering or a related field (minimum 2 years completed preferred). - **Experience:** No prior professional experience required; coursework, projects, or personal engineering pursuits a plus. - **Technical Skills:** - Basic familiarity with CAD software (e.g., SolidWorks, AutoCAD) from coursework or self-study. - Introductory knowledge of mechanical principles, fasteners, or robotics concepts. - Comfort with Microsoft Word and Excel for documentation and data tracking. - **Communication:** Clear verbal and written skills, eager to learn and engage with a team. - **Problem-Solving:** Curious, detail-oriented mindset with an aptitude for tackling technical challenges. - **Attributes:** Enthusiastic, proactive, and adaptable, with a strong desire to grow in automation - **Teamwork:** Be open to feedback and collaborate effectively with engineers and cross functional departments. - **Initiative:** Show curiosity, take on small tasks proactively, and seek learning opportunities. - **Adaptability:** Adjust quickly when project scopes or priorities shift.

role: R&D Intern - Fairness in Deep Learning - Paris
description: **Contexte :** Offre de stage de recherche de master d’une durée de 4 à 6 mois, débutant en hiver 2026-2027. Ce document liste les possibles directions pour le stage, qui seront ajustées au fil du stage. Le stage aura lieu au sein du centre de recherche d’Artefact à Paris. L’objectif est d'étudier les réseaux de neurones dans un cadre où l’on souhaite garantir l'indépendance des prédictions vis-à-vis d'une variable sensible continue (telle que l'âge, le revenu, la couleur de peau, etc.). **Présentation d’Artefact :** Artefact est une société internationale de services autour de la data, spécialisée dans le conseil en transformation data, dont la mission est de transformer la donnée en délivrant des résultats tangibles sur l’ensemble de la chaîne de valeur des entreprises. L’approche unique d’Artefact, qui fait le pont entre la donnée et le business, permet à nos clients d’atteindre leurs objectifs business de façon dédiée et efficace. Nos 2500 employés allient leurs compétences pluridisciplinaires au profit de l’innovation business des entreprises. Nos technologies de pointe en Intelligence Artificielle, nos méthodes agiles garantissent le succès des projets IA de nos clients, de la conception au déploiement, jusqu’à la formation et l’accompagnement au changement. **Sujet :** Les réseaux de neurones sont aujourd'hui au cœur de nombreuses applications industrielles. Leur capacité à extraire des représentations riches à partir des données en fait des outils de choix, mais elle les rend aussi susceptibles d'encoder et d'amplifier des biais présents dans les données d'apprentissage, renforçant ainsi des discriminations chez les populations traitées par ces modèles [1]. Cet enjeu est un domaine de recherche dénommé fairness, et est particulièrement dynamique, avec la réglementation des modèles d’IA qui évolue, comme par exemple avec l’AI Act de l’Union Européenne. Pour mesurer et mitiger les biais discriminatoires dans les modèles, la littérature s'est majoritairement concentrée sur des variables sensibles binaires ou catégorielles (genre, origine ethnique, etc.), pour lesquelles les groupes sont bien définis [2-5]. Cependant de nombreuses variables sensibles sont intrinsèquement continues : l'âge, le revenu, ou encore la couleur de peau. Discrétiser ces variables en groupes est une pratique courante mais problématique : le choix des seuils est arbitraire, de l'information est perdue, et un modèle peut sembler équitable pour un découpage donné tout en restant fortement biaisé pour un autre [6]. Contrôler la dépendance entre les sorties d'un modèle et une variable continue reste un problème ouvert, notamment pour les réseaux de neurones, où il faut à la fois mesurer cette dépendance et la pénaliser de façon différentiable au cours de l'apprentissage. Durant ce stage, le/la stagiaire explorera les méthodes de réduction des biais par rapport à une variable sensible continue pour des réseaux de neurones. Le travail commencera par l'implémentation des méthodes existantes (régularisations basées sur des mesures de dépendance telles que la corrélation maximale de Hirschfeld-Gebelein-Rényi ou “Generalized Disparate Impacte”, etc.), listées dans les références [7-8], et par la mise en place d'un protocole robuste pour les comparer, en tenant compte du compromis entre performance et fairness. Dans un second temps, le stage se concentrera sur la conception et l'expérimentation de nouvelles méthodes de réduction de biais adaptées aux variables continues. Pour cela, le/la stagiaire pourra s'appuyer sur des bibliothèques open source (PyTorch, scikit-learn), afin de rester dans un cadre de code reproductible et facile à adopter. **Pré-requis** Le profil recherché pour ce poste est le suivant : BAC+4/BAC+5 : Formation en mathématiques appliquées, statistiques ou machine learning au sein d’une université ou école d’ingénieur Stage de césure ou stage de fin d’études Date de début : Hiver 2026-2027 Durée : 4 à 6 mois **Références** 1. Risser, L., Sanz, A. G., Vincenot, Q., & Loubes, J. M. (2022). Tackling algorithmic bias in neural-network classifiers using wasserstein-2 regularization. *Journal of Mathematical Imaging and Vision*, *64*(6), 672-689. 2. Buolamwini, J., & Gebru, T. (2018, January). Gender shades: Intersectional accuracy disparities in commercial gender classification. In *Conference on fairness, accountability and transparency* (pp. 77-91). PMLR. 3. Cho, J., Zala, A., & Bansal, M. (2023, October). Dall-eval: Probing the reasoning skills and social biases of text-to-image generation models. In *2023 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)* (pp. 3020-3031). IEEE. 4. Li, X., Chen, Z., Zhang, J. M., Sarro, F., Zhang, Y., & Liu, X. (2023). Dark-skin individuals are at more risk on the street: Unmasking fairness issues of autonomous driving systems. *CoRR abs/2308.02935*. 5. Thong, W., Joniak, P., & Xiang, A. (2023, October). Beyond skin tone: A multidimensional measure of apparent skin color. In *2023 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)* (pp. 4880-4890). IEEE. 6. Shilova, V., Malherbe, E., Palma, G., Risser, L., & Loubes, J. M. (2025). Fairness-aware grouping for continuous sensitive variables: Application for debiasing face analysis with respect to skin tone. In *ECAI 2025: 28th European Conference on Artificial Intelligence 25-30 October 2025, Bologna, Italy-Including 14th Conference on Prestigious Applications of Intelligent Systems (PAIS 2025) Proceedings* (pp. 5344-5351). 7. Mary, J., Calauzenes, C., & El Karoui, N. (2019, May). Fairness-aware learning for continuous attributes and treatments. In *International conference on machine learning*(pp. 4382-4391). PMLR. 8. Giuliani, L., Misino, E., & Lombardi, M. (2023, July). Generalized disparate impact for configurable fairness solutions in ML. In *International Conference on Machine Learning* (pp. 11443-11458). PMLR.

role: R&D Intern - Fairness in Deep Learning - Paris
description: **Contexte :** Offre de stage de recherche de master d’une durée de 4 à 6 mois, débutant en hiver 2026-2027. Ce document liste les possibles directions pour le stage, qui seront ajustées au fil du stage. Le stage aura lieu au sein du centre de recherche d’Artefact à Paris. L’objectif est d'étudier les réseaux de neurones dans un cadre où l’on souhaite garantir l'indépendance des prédictions vis-à-vis d'une variable sensible continue (telle que l'âge, le revenu, la couleur de peau, etc.). **Présentation d’Artefact :** Artefact est une société internationale de services autour de la data, spécialisée dans le conseil en transformation data, dont la mission est de transformer la donnée en délivrant des résultats tangibles sur l’ensemble de la chaîne de valeur des entreprises. L’approche unique d’Artefact, qui fait le pont entre la donnée et le business, permet à nos clients d’atteindre leurs objectifs business de façon dédiée et efficace. Nos 2500 employés allient leurs compétences pluridisciplinaires au profit de l’innovation business des entreprises. Nos technologies de pointe en Intelligence Artificielle, nos méthodes agiles garantissent le succès des projets IA de nos clients, de la conception au déploiement, jusqu’à la formation et l’accompagnement au changement. **Sujet :** Les réseaux de neurones sont aujourd'hui au cœur de nombreuses applications industrielles. Leur capacité à extraire des représentations riches à partir des données en fait des outils de choix, mais elle les rend aussi susceptibles d'encoder et d'amplifier des biais présents dans les données d'apprentissage, renforçant ainsi des discriminations chez les populations traitées par ces modèles [1]. Cet enjeu est un domaine de recherche dénommé fairness, et est particulièrement dynamique, avec la réglementation des modèles d’IA qui évolue, comme par exemple avec l’AI Act de l’Union Européenne. Pour mesurer et mitiger les biais discriminatoires dans les modèles, la littérature s'est majoritairement concentrée sur des variables sensibles binaires ou catégorielles (genre, origine ethnique, etc.), pour lesquelles les groupes sont bien définis [2-5]. Cependant de nombreuses variables sensibles sont intrinsèquement continues : l'âge, le revenu, ou encore la couleur de peau. Discrétiser ces variables en groupes est une pratique courante mais problématique : le choix des seuils est arbitraire, de l'information est perdue, et un modèle peut sembler équitable pour un découpage donné tout en restant fortement biaisé pour un autre [6]. Contrôler la dépendance entre les sorties d'un modèle et une variable continue reste un problème ouvert, notamment pour les réseaux de neurones, où il faut à la fois mesurer cette dépendance et la pénaliser de façon différentiable au cours de l'apprentissage. Durant ce stage, le/la stagiaire explorera les méthodes de réduction des biais par rapport à une variable sensible continue pour des réseaux de neurones. Le travail commencera par l'implémentation des méthodes existantes (régularisations basées sur des mesures de dépendance telles que la corrélation maximale de Hirschfeld-Gebelein-Rényi ou “Generalized Disparate Impacte”, etc.), listées dans les références [7-8], et par la mise en place d'un protocole robuste pour les comparer, en tenant compte du compromis entre performance et fairness. Dans un second temps, le stage se concentrera sur la conception et l'expérimentation de nouvelles méthodes de réduction de biais adaptées aux variables continues. Pour cela, le/la stagiaire pourra s'appuyer sur des bibliothèques open source (PyTorch, scikit-learn), afin de rester dans un cadre de code reproductible et facile à adopter. **Pré-requis** Le profil recherché pour ce poste est le suivant : BAC+4/BAC+5 : Formation en mathématiques appliquées, statistiques ou machine learning au sein d’une université ou école d’ingénieur Stage de césure ou stage de fin d’études Date de début : Hiver 2026-2027 Durée : 4 à 6 mois **Références** 1. Our work spans the full hardware stack designing and integrating sensing systems (LiDAR, camera, TOF, IMU, GPS), embedded compute (CPUs, GPUs, microcontrollers, Linux, ROS), electrical systems (power distribution, communication), and mechanical components (structures, thermal regulation, ingress protection). The team focuses on both development (research, design, prototyping, testing) and operations (production, testing, QA, debugging). We’re a small, fast-moving team, and we care deeply about improving: 1) core capabilities, 2) system reliability, 3) system scalability. As a growing team we are also building operational systems and procedures from the ground up. **Mechanical Systems Intern Role:** As a Mechanical Engineer Intern on the Hardware Team at Field AI, you will contribute to the design and implementation of mechanical systems that house and support sensing and compute platforms in real-world environments. From ruggedized enclosures to thermal management to manufacturability, your work will be critical to ensuring our systems operate reliably in the field. Responsibilities may span the full lifecycle from CAD through production to field support. You will collaborate closely with electrical, compute, and systems engineers to build tightly integrated solutions ready for deployment in challenging field environments. Additionally while your focus will be on mechanical systems you will likely contribute across all hardware domains. ### What You Will Get To Do **Mechanical System Design** - **Structures:** Design and model mechanical structures including external enclosures, internal compute frames, and load-bearing chassis. - **Mounts:** Design and validate robust sensor mounts, payload attachment points, and mechanical interfaces. - **Ingress Protection:** Implement IP-rated solutions with gaskets, seals, membranes, and coatings to meet water/dust ingress standards. - **Thermal Management:** Incorporate thermal mitigation strategies such as fans, heat sinks, conductive paths, and airflow guides. - **Mass & Volume Budgets:** Ensure adherence to payload constraints, including tight volumetric envelopes and weight limitations. **Mechanical System Implementation** - **CAD & Simulation:** Build detailed SolidWorks CAD assemblies. Run FEA and thermal simulations to validate strength, durability, and heat dissipation. - **Material & Component Selection:** Choose materials and components to meet mass, strength, thermal, and manufacturability constraints. Design for Production: Apply DFM, DFA, DFS principles throughout the design lifecycle. - **System Testing:** Conduct mechanical load testing (shock, vibration), thermal validation, ingress tests, and sensor alignment assessments. - **Prototyping:** Rapidly iterate on prototypes for fit checks, thermal evaluations, and integration trials. - **Documentation & Budgets:** Generate mechanical drawings, GD&T annotations, BOMs, and assembly instructions for fabrication and QA. Manage weight, volume, and thermal budgets. **Mechanical System Production & Servicing** - **Build:** Work with vendors and contract manufacturers to procure mechanical hardware. Develop QA checks for incoming units. Support payload integration and scaling. - **Debug:** Investigate mechanical failures, deformation, and environmental weaknesses during testing and deployments. - **Monitor:** Develop protocols for monitoring the system mechanical health and loads. ### What You Have - **Education:** Current student pursuing a B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, or related field. - **CAD Expertise:** Proficient with SolidWorks or equivalent mechanical CAD platforms. - **Thermal & Structural Analysis:** Familiarity with FEA and thermal modeling tools. - **Field-Ready Design:** Experience designing hardware that survives vibration, shock, thermal cycling, and environmental exposure. - **Manufacturing Knowledge:** Experience designing for CNC, sheet metal, additive manufacturing, and assembly workflows. - **Mechanical Systems Integration:** Experience working across teams to integrate mechanical systems with compute, sensors, and power electronics. - **Lab Skills:** Comfort with mechanical debugging, thermal test setups, vibration tables, and ingress testing. - **Cross Functional Robotic Skills:** Ability to contribute electrical, sensing, and embedded computing work to deliver robust integrated systems. ### What Will Set You Apart - **Scaling:** Experience taking systems from prototype to large scale production. - **Field Environments:** Experience developing systems for harsh field environments. - **Deployed Robotics:** Experience working on robotics deployed in real world settings such as autonomous vehicles, drones, or ruggedized robots. - **Systems Level Robotics:** Fluency across mechanical, electrical, and software systems. - **Reliability Engineering:** Experience designing to meet IP ratings, MIL-STD, or equivalent ruggedness standards.

### **About the Company** We are a renewable energy and ocean technology company committed to rapidly developing and deploying technologies that will ensure a sustainable future for Earth by unlocking the vast energy potential of its oceans. Our focus is on capturing civilizational levels of ultra-low-cost renewable energy for applications including computing and affordable renewable fuels delivered to shore. The company is a public benefit corporation headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and backed by leading venture capitalists, philanthropic investors, university endowments, and private investment offices. We operate as an idea meritocracy in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis. Our staff have worked at organizations such as SpaceX, Blue Origin, Boeing, Tesla, Apple, Virgin Orbit, Astra, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, New Relic, Bridgewater, Raytheon, Disney Imagineering, and the US Army and Air Force, as well as research universities, startups, and small companies across a range of industries. ### **About the Job** Our core technology is the node, a device that produces energy in the ocean’s harshest conditions for years at a time without human maintenance or intervention. As a Summer 2027 Engineering Intern, you will work on real technical problems that directly support the development and scaling of our Node technology. We expect to hire interns across several engineering disciplines, including mechanical engineering, manufacturing, and software. Your specific project and responsibilities will depend on your background, interests, and the highest-priority technical needs of the team. You will work alongside experienced engineers, technicians, and operators. We are looking for exceptional students who have demonstrated technical ability, intellectual curiosity, initiative, and a track record of building, solving, or shipping difficult things. You will be expected to learn quickly, ask thoughtful questions, document your work, communicate openly, and take meaningful ownership of your project. Candidates should have effective interpersonal skills and be able to thrive in a creative, scrappy, and collaborative environment. ### **Responsibilities** Responsibilities will vary by discipline and project, but may include: - Own and execute a clearly defined technical project supporting our Node technology with guidance from experienced team members. - Apply engineering fundamentals and analytical reasoning to solve technical problems. - Build, test, troubleshoot, or improve physical or software systems. - Analyze technical data and use results to inform engineering or process decisions. - Create clear technical documentation, including designs, analyses, test results, software documentation, or process records. - Participate in technical reviews and clearly communicate findings, tradeoffs, and recommendations. - Take ownership of assigned work and proactively communicate progress and blockers. - Incorporate feedback quickly and adapt as project priorities or requirements evolve. ### **Required Qualifications** - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s, master’s, or doctoral degree in an engineering, computer science, physics, or other closely related technical field. - Strong technical fundamentals relevant to your area of study. - Demonstrated experience applying technical skills through coursework, research, internships, student teams, independent projects, or other hands-on work. - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. - Comfortable working on problems where requirements or solutions may initially be ambiguous. - Able to work full-time and on-site in Portland, Oregon for the duration of the internship, approximately mid-June through early September 2027. - Authorization to work in the United States for the full duration of the internship. ### **Desired Qualifications** - Mechanical design, CAD, structural or thermal analysis, or hardware testing. - Manufacturing engineering, process development, tooling, automation, quality, production systems, or design for manufacturability. - Software development, data systems, automation, simulation, controls, infrastructure, or developer tooling. - Skills with machining, fabrication, welding, electronics assembly, and prototyping. - Designing and executing technical tests and analyzing the resulting data. - Participation in technically demanding student teams or projects such as Formula SAE, Baja SAE, robotics, rocketry, solar car, marine engineering, or similar programs. - Experience taking a project from an ambiguous initial problem through implementation and validation. - Exposure to renewable energy, marine systems, robotics, aerospace, industrial systems, manufacturing, or other complex hardware environments. - Experience working in a fast-moving technical environment where designs, processes, or software are tested and iterated quickly. The above qualifications are desired, not required. We encourage you to apply if you are a strong candidate with only some of the desired skills and experience listed. ### **Compensation** If hired for this internship, you will receive: - Cash compensation of $42.00 per hour. ### **Location and Duration** - This is an on-site position. Our offices, lab, and shop are located in **Portland, Oregon**. You must commit to being in person, in Portland, for the duration of this internship. - This internship will run from **mid-June through early September**, with exact dates to be confirmed. ***This is a short-term posting, and we will be accepting applications until end of day Tuesday, November 10th 2026 . Please ensure your application is submitted by this date as we will not be accepting late applications. We will begin reviewing submissions after the posting closes.***

OUR COMPANY BACKGROUND & CULTURE UPP is the first pension plan of its kind in Ontario’s university sector, proudly serving over 46,000 members across six universities and nineteen sector organizations. Our purpose is to bring greater retirement peace of mind to the university sector by investing with integrity and serving members with care. As a sector-wide plan designed for growth, our doors are open to all Ontario universities. UPP is recognized as one of Greater Toronto’s Top Employers for 2026. Together, we’re a team of progressive thinkers and agile doers operating within a fast-paced culture of collaboration and respect. We believe in bringing smart and capable people together to create, solve, and grow with a clear shared vision and values of integrity, inclusivity, ingenuity, and impact. Our culture is intentionally welcoming and purposefully rooted in equity, diversity, inclusion, and reconciliation (EDI&R). We believe diverse teams, perspectives, and lived experiences contribute to better decisions and a better workplace. As a pension plan, UPP approaches investing through a long-term lens to generate and safeguard value. Our commitment to investing responsibly accounts for material risks that impact our investment portfolio to generate sufficient risk-adjusted returns to meet the pension needs of our members. Join us in building a bright future for our members, our organization, and each other. THE ROLE We are actively looking for an Intern Analyst, Private Markets, to join our team in May 2027, for a 4-month internship (May 2027 – August 2027). This role will be part of a growing and dynamic Investment team. The incumbent will be responsible for providing research support for projects related to private markets. This is a fantastic opportunity for an undergraduate student to gain valuable work experience in a fast-growing, dynamic environment while being a part of a new pension plan. This role is based in downtown Toronto in a hybrid work environment, allowing employees the flexibility to work remotely and in-office (minimum two days per week in-office). Application Details: We ask that you submit a one-page resume, transcript, and a cover letter as part of the application process. This posting is for a existing vacancy. SPECIFIC ACCOUNTABILITIES • Secondary research and due diligence • Coordinating with internal and/or external stakeholders • Editing and writing support for internal and external presentations • Support asset management reporting and related deliverables • Contribute to UPP’s reputation as a respectful employer, partner, and participant in the financial sector. • Collaborate with other industry participants to promote a sustainable economy and society. • Other duties as required. QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE • Pursuing a degree in Business, Commerce, Finance, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field • Secondary research skills • Solid grasp of MS Office applications – particularly Excel and PowerPoint • Strong oral and written communication skills • Familiarity with / keen interest in global business, investment, and private markets ATTRIBUTES • Independent problem solver • Critical thinker • Ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects in a time-sensitive manner • Comfort interacting in a global setting and with international stakeholders • Adaptability, resourcefulness, and persistence EXPECTED COMPENSATION The expected compensation for this role is an annualized base salary in the range of $58,000 to $68,500. This range reflects base salaries for all intern levels and is subject to change and may be modified in the future. Salaries are aligned to academic year and role scope. LIFE AT UPP Do work that matters. We are duty-bound to serve our members’ interests, and it’s a responsibility we don’t take lightly. That’s why we’ve ingrained sustainability in our work from day one—to ensure our members have a resilient future to retire into, both today and for generations to come. Stronger together. Collaboration is how UPP was born, and it’s how we work with each other and our partners day in, day out. No one at UPP is just a number (even if they are excellent at math) and every win is a shared win. Grow every day. The Brennan Center for Justice at NYU School of Law is a nonpartisan law and policy institute that seeks to improve the systems of democracy and justice in the United States. We work to hold our political institutions and laws accountable to the twin American ideals of democracy and equal justice for all. The Brennan Center’s work ranges from voting rights to campaign finance reform, from ending mass incarceration to preserving constitutional protections in national security policies. Part think tank, part advocacy group, part cutting-edge communications hub, we start with rigorous research. We craft innovative policies. And we fight for them — in Congress and the states, in the courts, and in the court of public opinion. We are seeking an intern to join our Communications department on the Creative team to provide design and administrative support to staff. Note: This internship is in-person at our New York City office. Responsibilities: The intern will assist with graphic and motion design, archival, and photo research. Additionally, there will be opportunities to attend and observe substantive meetings, events, and conversations on program work. Applicant must be open to evolving responsibilities. In addition to duties listed above, specific responsibilities for the Creative team include: Producing still and motion graphics for digital channels Completing extensive image and archive research and research on Brennan Center issues to develop engaging graphics Supporting development of institutional, campaign, and brand videos/graphics; motion and still research, cataloging and organization of visual assets Maintaining multimedia archive: graphics, images and video. Qualifications: The ideal candidates are independent self-starters; detail-oriented; energetic; punctual; and highly organized. Interns must also have excellent design skills, as well as a passion for our issues. Experience with Adobe applications, including InDesign and Photoshop is a must. A link to your portfolio, or a pdf, containing your best quality work must be submitted for your application to be considered. We are committed to considering a wide range of candidates, including those with diverse experiences and backgrounds. If you're uncertain about meeting 100% of our qualifications, we encourage you to apply anyway. In your cover letter, please share your interest in the position and what you hope to contribute to the role. This internship is only open to undergraduate students in Spring 2027. Hours: Approximately 10-20 hours per week Pay: $18.40 per hour Duration: Spring Semester 2027 Application Deadline: November 23, 2026 Note: The Brennan Center will follow the rules of your school regarding internships. Therefore, if a school doesn’t allow you to do a paid internship for some reason (i.e., receiving credit, etc.), then your internship will not be paid. In addition, if you are participating in a formal school internship program that allows you to work more than our stated hours, we will make a determination based on our needs and further assessment of your school’s program. To Apply: Please visit >>LINK HERE with “Spring Creative Internship” in the subject line, after registering in the online system. Applying through our website is strongly preferred. The Brennan Center for Justice is committed to a workplace based on equal opportunity and a strong belief in the increased effectiveness that comes from a diverse workforce. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, ethnicity, gender identity, socioeconomic identity, sexual orientation, national origin, previous incarceration, disability, military veteran/status, or any other basis prohibited by applicable law. To this end, we welcome all qualified applicants to apply.

About CONXAI CONXAI has built an agentic AI platform for the Architecture, Engineering and Construction (AEC) and physical industries, focused on knowledge-automation . We automate high-stakes, knowledge-intensive workflows traditionally trapped in siloed data, fragmented tools and tacit (undocumented) human expertise. Our multi-agent systems perform complex reasoning in the physical world; and transform bespoke, service-heavy processes into scalable Service-as-a-Software automation. CONXAI is trusted by some of the leading AEC companies in Europe, US, LATAM and Japan. Your Role Help encode the DNA of Construction into our AI We are looking for a highly motivated and analytical intern who sits at a rare intersection: a Civil Engineering student who speaks the language of Data Science . In this internship, you will learn how AI understands construction concepts, logic, workflows, and site dynamics. Working closely with our senior Domain Experts, Product Managers, and AI Engineers, you will get hands-on experience ensuring our AI models deliver practical, high-fidelity value to the construction site. Domain Modeling Support: Assist in mapping and translating traditional AEC workflows and methodologies (like Lean, TVD, IPD) into logical structures that our AI agents can understand Framework Implementation: Help the team build out our platform’s Domain Knowledge Base, learning how to connect BIM-to-Field relationships with productivity metrics Data Strategy & Processing: Work alongside our Machine Learning team to clean, structure, and categorize AEC datasets (visual, sensor, and textual) used to train our agentic models Product Insights: Shadow our product team to understand the "voice of the customer." Help analyze user feedback and construction pain points to assist in organizing the product backlog Testing & Validation: Help test AI outputs against real-world construction scenarios and industry standards to ensure accuracy and practical value Who You Are Education: Currently pursuing (or recently graduated with) MS or PhD in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Data Science, or a closely related field Data Science Foundation: Basic literacy in data science concepts with academic or project experience using Python, SQL, or statistical modeling AEC Knowledge: Familiarity with modern delivery frameworks (Lean Construction, TVD, IPD) through coursework or previous internships is a strong plus Analytical Mindset: You are fascinated by the idea of structuring complex domain knowledge into formats that computers can learn from Communication: Excellent English communication skills, with a knack for translating technical engineering concepts into plain language Why CONXAI Edge of Innovation: Be at the absolute forefront of AI in the construction tech space Mentorship & Growth: Work side-by-side with a global team of senior ML engineers, software engineers, and industry practitioners who are invested in your learning Impact: Contribute to a product that directly impacts how global infrastructure is built Future Opportunities: Competitive intern salary with the potential to transition into a full-time role

Junior Electrical Engineer Overview: The Junior Electrical Engineer is a full-time, on-site role based in either Fremont, CA or Reno, NV. This role supports the design, testing, and optimization of electronics integrated into Pivotal’s flow control products, working closely with senior engineers and cross-functional teams. Day-to-day responsibilities include assisting with electrical schematics and layouts, performing basic calculations and simulations, supporting lab testing and troubleshooting, and documenting design changes and test results. The engineer collaborates with manufacturing and operations to resolve issues, ensure product reliability, and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives. The role also involves maintaining compliance with relevant safety and industry standards and participating in technical reviews and design updates. Key Responsibilities: Support the design of analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuits for flow control electronics, including sensor interfaces, valve drivers, power regulation, and communication interfaces. Create and update schematics and assist with PCB layout in Altium or KiCad under the guidance of senior engineers. Select and qualify electronic components, maintain part data and BOMs, and support replacements for obsolete parts. Build, bring up, and debug prototype boards; perform lab testing using oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, and signal generators. Perform basic circuit calculations and simulations (e.g., SPICE), including power budgets, tolerance analysis, and thermal derating. Design and maintain electrical test fixtures, cable harnesses, and test procedures for engineering and production use. Document test results and design changes, and support the engineering change (ECO) process. Support manufacturing and field troubleshooting, including failure analysis of returned or nonconforming assemblies. Help ensure designs meet applicable safety and EMC requirements and industry standards (e.g., CE, SEMI S2). Collaborate with firmware, mechanical, and test engineers during product development and design reviews. Required Skills and Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a closely related field. 0–2 years of electrical engineering experience; relevant internships, co-ops, or project work are considered. Foundational knowledge in Electrical Engineering, with the ability to apply core concepts to product development and troubleshooting. Skills in electrical design, including reading and creating schematics, selecting components, and supporting prototype development. Understanding of low-voltage DC power conversion and distribution relevant to industrial and high-tech equipment. Ability to use common engineering tools and software (e.g., Altium, KiCad, and standard test equipment such as multimeters and oscilloscopes). Strong analytical, problem-solving, and documentation skills, with attention to detail and a commitment to quality. Effective communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work in cross-functional teams in an on-site environment. The ideal candidate will also have: Exposure to semiconductor, manufacturing, or industrial automation environments. Exposure to Copy Exactly! / Copy Exact! and related design replication methodologies. Hands-on PCB design, assembly, or soldering experience. Basic microcontroller or firmware experience (C/C++). Experience with test automation or data analysis tools such as Python or LabVIEW. Familiarity with relevant electrical safety standards and best practices.

**The Role** We're looking for an engineer early in their career who wants to build things, break them, and figure out why they broke. This is a hands on role from day one. You'll be in the shop as much as at a desk, and the work spans mechanical design, fabrication, testing, and the software and electronics that make hardware actually do something. You do not need to have done this professionally yet. What matters is that you've built real things, whether that was a competition car, a robot, or something you made at a makerspace because you wanted to see if it would work. Please note that this role is located at our warehouse in Mountain View that will soon be relocating to Fremont. **What You'll Do** - Design mechanical components and assemblies in CAD, and take them from concept through fabrication and test. - Build, wire, and bring up prototypes yourself. Machining, 3D printing, soldering, and assembly are part of the job, not someone else's job. - Run tests, collect data, and figure out what the results mean. Then iterate. - Write scripts and simple control code to support testing and to get hardware moving. - Work alongside other engineers and teams on integration. - Document what you build so the next person can pick it up. - Work out of our warehouse in Fremont, CA on testing, bring up, maintenance, and repair of hardware in service. **What We're Looking For** - 0 to 2 years of experience, with a degree in mechanical engineering, mechatronics, electrical engineering, or something adjacent. New graduates are welcome. - Solid mechanical fundamentals: statics, materials, tolerancing, and a working command of CAD. - Comfort with code. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you should be able to write Python or C to read a sensor, drive a motor, or process test data. - Shop skills and the instinct to build rather than only model. You've used a mill, a lathe, a printer, or a soldering iron and you aren't precious about getting your hands dirty. - Genuine eagerness to learn. You ask questions, you chase down answers, and you'd rather be told what you got wrong than left alone with it.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program. - Ability to complete an in-person co-op in one of our offices in winter 2027. **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS** - Prior internship experience and/or leadership on a collegiate project team or laboratory. - Demonstrated hands-on fabrication skills. - Exposure to test plan development, test data acquisition, data analysis, and failure analysis techniques - Exposure to reliability analysis techniques, such as FMEA/FMECA, predictive modeling, Weibull analysis, and Fault Tree Analysis - Technical writing experience developing standards, specifications, user guides, and policies - Collegiate project team, machine shop, or laboratory experience. - High competence with, and fluid use of, engineering first principles. - Strong problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate cross-functionally - Proficiency with the Microsoft Office Suite of tools US Hourly Range $40—$48 USD The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. ## What we’re building The marine industry supports recreation, global commerce, and national defense. And yet it runs on technology that hasn't meaningfully changed in fifty years. Until now. Arc is on a mission to electrify the marine industry. We're rethinking powertrains, software, and vessel designs from first principles. And we're already executing. We started with consumers to develop and harden our core technology. We’re now scaling production of our flagship model with new models and sectors on the horizon. Now we’re extending our platform to commercial applications, starting with tugs, ferries, and defense, with years worth of signed contracts and a pipeline that spans every vessel type on the water. The technology is proven, the momentum is building, and the opportunity is enormous. The marine industry is going electric and Arc is building the platform that powers it ## Who we’re looking for We’re looking for someone who’s fired up by our mission and ready to build. You’ll thrive here if you adapt quickly, take ownership, and care about the details. You will join our Electrical Engineering team as a summer intern from June 14th-August 20th 2027. You will work from our headquarters in Torrance, CA. Given that we’re a startup, you will be working in a fast-moving, dynamic environment that requires adaptability. That said, here are some responsibilities and qualifications we expect to stay relatively constant for this role. ## What You'll Do - Supporting with diagnosing problems, designing hardware, prototyping, testing, and high-volume manufacturing. - Designing tools for production end of line testing - Getting hands on with building and testing ## Minimum Qualifications - Hands on circuit building experience - Excellent grasp of electrical engineering fundamentals - Basic experience with electrical simulation software (LTSPICE, PSPICE, etc.) - Clear written and verbal communication - Basic experience with lab equipment (DMM, Oscilloscope, etc.) - Eagerness to learn and adapt in a dynamic setting. ## Bonus Qualifications - Familiarity with high performance electric vehicles, solar cars, Formula SAE, or similar - FEA experience (any platform) - Prior experience in a fast-paced manufacturing setting - Strong time management skills - Comfortable pushing a fast but sustainable pace - Enthusiasm for boating and clean energy - Experience with Python and data analysis and visualization - Experience with CAN-bus devices and networks - Enthusiasm for boating and clean energy At Arc, we encourage diversity and consider all qualified applicants equally for employment, regardless of background, identity, or status. You’re always welcome to reach out even if you don’t meet many of these qualifications. Passion and aptitude make up for a lot. ## What we offer The base pay for this role is $40 per hour. Additionally, Arc offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: - **Boat days – Yes, we actually go out on the water. A lot.** - **Retirement savings — Traditional and Roth 401(k) access** - **Safety support — Reimbursement for PPE, ergonomic equipment, and anything that ensures we keep our crew safe** - **Relocation Assistance** - **Mentorship Opportunities** - **Office perks — Daily lunches, snacks, and good coffee while onsite** ## Our values We move with urgency and build with care. We value these five things above all else: - **Ownership** over both your work and the company’s success - **Empathy** for colleagues and for customers - **Humility** in problem solving and collaboration - **Pragmatism** for navigating ambiguity quickly and sensibly - **Inclusion** of different backgrounds, opinions, cultures, and perspectives. We want people who share and embody these values. It is vital that our values align - we’d be happy to elaborate on any or all of these during the interview process.

**Position Overview** Join the team building computer vision applications for the construction trades. Contractors spend dozens of hours per project doing takeoffs by hand. We're automating that with models that need to perform reliably on messy, real-world drawings. As a CV/ML Engineering Intern, you'll work on real production problems alongside our ML team, not a side project. # **About Mercor** Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents. Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices. ## **About the Role** As a Research Scientist Intern at Mercor, you’ll work on research at the frontier of post-training, reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), data generation, and model evaluation. You’ll investigate how datasets, rewards, and training methods affect the capabilities and behavior of large language models. This may include designing controlled experiments, developing new evaluation methodologies, conducting systematic failure analysis, and testing approaches to improve tool use, agentic behavior, and real-world reasoning. You’ll work closely with research scientists, research engineers, and domain experts to turn open-ended questions into rigorous experiments. Your work will contribute to Mercor’s research agenda and may support external publications, benchmark releases, and the development of frontier AI systems. ## **What You’ll Do** - Develop and investigate research questions related to post-training, RLVR, data quality, and model evaluation. - Design and run controlled experiments to understand how datasets, rewards, and training strategies affect model performance. - Study reward-shaping and post-training methods, including approaches such as GRPO and DAPO. - Develop methods for measuring data quality, usability, and performance uplift on key benchmarks. - Design and evaluate datasets, rubrics, evaluators, and scoring frameworks for complex model capabilities. - Conduct systematic error analysis to identify model failure modes and opportunities for improvement. - Analyze experimental results and communicate findings through clear reports, research artifacts, and presentations. - Build the research tooling and data pipelines needed to conduct experiments at scale. - Collaborate with research scientists, research engineers, applied AI teams, and domain experts producing training and evaluation data. - Contribute to research publications, benchmark releases, and other public research outputs where appropriate. ## **What We’re Looking For** - Currently pursuing a master’s or PhD in computer science, machine learning, statistics, mathematics, or another relevant field. - Demonstrated ability to formulate research questions, design experiments, and draw sound conclusions from empirical results. - Demonstrated experience in at least one of the following: - Training, fine-tuning, or evaluating language models. - Agentic AI system, RL environments - Developing benchmarks, evaluation methodologies, or data-quality measures. - At least one publication or open source project. - Strong programming skills, particularly in Python, and the ability to write reliable research code. - Familiarity with machine learning fundamentals, experimental design, and statistical analysis. - Intellectual curiosity. - Comfort operating in a fast-paced research environment with rapid iteration and a high degree of ownership. ## **Nice to Have** - Previous research experience in language models, reinforcement learning, model evaluation, or post-training. - Experience training, fine-tuning, or evaluating language models. - Familiarity with RLVR techniques, reward modeling, or agentic AI systems. - Experience developing benchmarks, evaluation methodologies, or data-quality measures. - Research publications or submissions at competitive CS conferences such as ACL, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, or EMNLP. - Research papers, technical reports, open-source projects, or other work samples demonstrating relevant skills. **Why Mercor** **Impact**: Your work powers how AI labs train and deploy their models **Learning**: Get early exposure to frontier AI research and engineering **Growth**: Work with a high-velocity team where interns ship to production **Benefits** - Mentorship from experienced researchers. - Work on real, high-impact projects. - $1.5K monthly stipend for meals - $200 monthly laundry reimbursement - $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement - Free Equinox membership - Team events and offsites. - Potential full-time return offer.

role: Software Engineer II, Developer Portal (New Grad / Early Career)
description: ## **Company Overview** IDMe is the next-generation digital identity wallet that simplifies how individuals securely prove their identity online. Consumers can verify their identity with IDMe once and seamlessly login across websites without having to create a new login and verify their identity again. Over 175 million users experience streamlined login and identity verification with IDMe at 22 federal agencies, 50 state government agencies, and more than 100 healthcare organizations. Over 600 consumer brands use IDMe to verify communities and user segments to honor service and build more authentic relationships. IDMe’s technology meets the federal standards for consumer authentication set by the Commerce Department and is approved as a NIST 800-63-3 IAL2 / AAL2 credential service provider by the Kantara Initiative. IDMe is committed to “No Identity Left Behind” to enable all people to have a secure digital identity. To learn more, visit . IDMe is a full-time, in-office culture. Unless a specific job description explicitly states otherwise, all roles are on-site five days per week at one of our offices in McLean, VA; Mountain View, CA; New York City, NY; or Tampa, FL. Certain roles — such as field-based sales or other remote-by-design positions — may have different work arrangements as noted in their individual postings. At IDMe, we embrace the thoughtful use of AI tools in our daily work and there are even occasions where we leverage AI in our hiring process. However, during the interview process, we want to understand your individual skills and experiences. Therefore, we have guidelines on how AI can be appropriately used during your application and interviews which can be found [here](https://insider.id.me/candidate-ai-use-in-interviewing/). **Location:** Mountain View, CA (Onsite 5 days per week) ## **Role Overview** IDMe is seeking a **Software Engineer II** to join the **Developer Portal** team, where we're building the self-service platform that enables organizations to rapidly integrate IDMe. Identity proofing is fundamentally complex. Integrating an identity proofing flow requires many steps while meeting standards-body assurance requirements. The Developer Portal is the product that brings those pieces together for the external developer. Today, much of that onboarding is still performed manually by in-house Solutions Consultants who have many other responsibilities. Our mission is to enable customers and their developers to register their application, configure their identity needs, test in a production-like sandbox, and launch to production, all through a modern self-service experience. This is an **early-career role** for engineers who are 0 to 2 years into their career and write excellent code. You don't need years of industry experience. You need strong fundamentals, a track record of building real things, and an **AI-native** way of working: you already use AI coding tools as a core part of how you design, build, test, and debug, and you have the judgment to know when their output is right and when it isn't. This is a **backend-leaning full-stack role**. You'll work on the services, APIs, and data models behind the portal (application registration, authorization, and the developer-facing APIs our customers integrate against), and you'll ship the user-facing surfaces those services power in our Next.js and React frontend. You'll start with well-scoped features alongside senior engineers and grow quickly into owning features end-to-end, from API contract to production. Our backend services are primarily **Java (Spring Boot)** alongside legacy **Ruby** services. The frontend is a micro-frontend platform built with **Next.js**, **React**, and **TypeScript**. You don't need to know all of these on day one. If your fundamentals are strong, we're confident you'll pick up whatever the problem requires. ## **What You'll Do** ### **Build and Ship Developer Features** Design, implement, test, and deploy Developer Portal capabilities across the stack: backend APIs, database changes, and the frontend experiences customers use. Start with well-defined features and bugs, then take on progressively larger and more ambiguous work as you grow. ### **Write High-Quality, Well-Tested Code** Write clean, readable, maintainable code with strong test coverage. Participate actively in code review, both getting feedback and giving thoughtful feedback to teammates, including senior engineers. ### **Build AI-First** Use AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) every day to move faster on implementation, testing, debugging, and understanding unfamiliar code. Help the team find better ways to use these tools, and hold AI-generated code to the same bar as code you wrote by hand. ### **Learn the Identity Stack** Build hands-on depth in authentication and authorization, including OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, enterprise SSO, multi-tenant access control, and credential management, working with our Wallet, Organizations, and Platform Engineering teams. ### **Operate What You Ship** Help keep the systems our team owns healthy in production: monitoring, alerting, debugging live issues, and participating in on-call once you're ramped up. ### **Collaborate and Grow** Work closely with Product, Design, and engineers across teams. Learn to break down problems, write short technical designs, and communicate clearly about tradeoffs and progress. You'll have a dedicated mentor and a clear path toward end-to-end feature ownership. ## **Required Qualifications** - Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. - 0 to 2 years of professional software engineering experience. - **Excellent coding skills** and strong computer science fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, complexity, and debugging. - Fluency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., Java, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Kotlin, C#, Ruby). - Evidence that you build real software: internships, substantial class or team projects, open-source contributions, hackathons, or side projects that other people use. - **AI-native development workflow**: daily, hands-on use of AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) to build and ship software, paired with the ability to critically evaluate AI-generated code for correctness, security, performance, and maintainability, and to explain every line you submit. - Experience building with LLMs or agentic workflows (e.g., using the Claude or OpenAI APIs, MCP, or agent frameworks) in projects or coursework. - Understanding of how web applications work, including HTTP, REST APIs, and relational databases/SQL. - Ability to learn unfamiliar systems quickly through independent research and by working with mentors and subject-matter experts. - Clear written and verbal communication. You can explain what you built, why, and what tradeoffs you made. ## **Preferred Qualifications** - Internship experience building backend services or full-stack web applications. - Experience with Java and Spring Boot, or another backend framework (Rails, Node.js/Express, Django, Go). - Experience with React, TypeScript, or Next.js. - Experience with PostgreSQL or another relational database, including schema design. - Exposure to authentication and authorization concepts such as OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWTs, SSO, or access control models. - Experience building developer tools, APIs, SDKs, or documentation that other developers use. - Experience writing automated tests (unit, integration, or end-to-end with tools like Jest, JUnit, or Playwright). - Familiarity with cloud platforms (GCP, AWS, Azure), containers, or CI/CD pipelines. - Interest in security, identity, fraud prevention, or regulated systems. ## **What Success Looks Like** - **First 30 days:** Your dev environment is set up, you've shipped your first production change, and you understand how the Developer Portal fits into IDMe's identity platform. - **First 90 days:** You're independently delivering well-scoped features across backend and frontend, contributing meaningfully to code reviews, and using AI tooling to raise both your speed and your quality bar. - **First year:** You own a meaningful Developer Portal capability end-to-end, from API contract and data model through production operation, and you're a go-to person for at least one part of the system. ## **You're Encouraged to Apply** We're not looking for someone who checks every box. If you write great code, learn fast, and are excited about building the tools that let developers integrate trusted identity, we want to hear from you, even if your background doesn't match this description exactly. The annual base salary listed does not include a company bonus, incentive for sales roles, equity and benefits which will be determined based on experience, skills, education, relevant training, geographic location and role. IDMe offers comprehensive medical, dental, vision, health savings account, flexible spending accounts (medical, limited purpose, dependent care, commuter benefit accounts), basic and voluntary life and AD&D insurance, 401(k) with company match, parental leave, ability to participate in unlimited paid time off subject to the terms and conditions of the PTO policy, including 8 company wide holidays, short and long-term disability insurance, accident and critical illness insurance, referral bonus policy, employee assistance program, pet insurance, travel assistant program, wellbeing and childcare discounts, benefit advocates, and a learning and development benefit. role: Junior Writer: Spanish Proofreading & AI Localization (Latam)
description: **Role Overview** You will be the human quality layer in our English-to-Spanish adaptation workflow. This is primarily a proofreading, localization review, and quality assurance role, not a from-scratch creative writing job. You will take AI-generated Spanish scripts and turn them into clean, consistent, AI-voice-ready scripts that are ready for production. You'll work closely with Senior Writers, AI production team, and Voice Artists, and your reviews will help improve the quality of our adaptations over time. You will then run the English Scripts through our AI adaptation tool to generate Spanish scripts. Most of your day goes to the careful line-by-line review of that AI-adapted scripts: fixing errors, smoothing phrasing, checking continuity, and making sure the script is ready for AI voice production. You will also apply feedback from Senior Writers,AI Production team, and voice artists, and log any recurring AI issues you spot. ### Key Responsibilities ### **1. Proofread and Refine AI-Adapted Scripts** - Review AI-generated Spanish scripts for grammar, spelling, punctuation, accents, sentence structure, and register. - Catch mistranslations, literal or awkward phrasing, missing context, dropped lines, and tonal inconsistencies against the English source. - Make sure the adaptation keeps the meaning, tone, emotion, and narrative intent of the original. - Check that dialogue sounds natural for each character and situation, and that the Spanish reads fluently rather than like a translation. - Align every script with Pocket FM's editorial standards and deliver clean, production-ready drafts. ### **2. Make Scripts AI-Voice Friendly** - Format scripts correctly for the AI voice pipeline, with clear speaker labels, clean dialogue and narration separation, and no stray symbols or formatting errors. - Check that emotion tags are present, accurate, and matched to the scene and character, wherever they are required. - Use punctuation, sentence length, and rhythm that guide AI voices toward natural pacing and delivery. - Rewrite anything an AI voice is likely to mispronounce or misread, such as numbers, dates, abbreviations, symbols, foreign words, and unusual names. - Flag lines that are too long, too dense, or hard to perform so they can be reworked before production. ### **3. Build Localization Sheets and Keep Them Consistent** - Prepare localization sheets and concept notes that adapt names, locations, entities, and cultural references from English-language settings to Spanish-speaking contexts. - Make sure localization choices are culturally appropriate, audience-friendly, and applied consistently across every episode. - Flag references, idioms, humor, or situations that may confuse or fall flat with Spanish-speaking listeners, and suggest alternatives. ### **4. Protect Story Continuity** - Keep character names, relationships, places, terminology, and recurring story elements consistent across episodes. - Make sure the adapted episodes follow the original storyline, character arcs, emotional beats, and episode flow. - Track plot details and tone across a series so nothing drifts from one episode to the next. ### **5. Deliver Quality at Scale** - Balance speed and accuracy in a high-volume workflow, keeping your attention to detail sharp on repetitive review work. - Make sure every final submission is accurate, consistent, localized, and ready for the next production stage. ### **6. Act on Feedback and Improve the Process** - Revise scripts based on feedback from Senior Writers, editorial and production teams, and listener comments, and apply those lessons to future scripts. - Document recurring AI issues in translation, tone, formatting, or storytelling, and share them with the team with suggested fixes. - Review published episodes and user comments to see how adaptations land with listeners, and give structured feedback. ### Qualifications **Must have** - Native Spanish with excellent grammar, spelling, and punctuation - Strong English comprehension, to interpret source scripts accurately - Bachelor's degree in Literature, Languages, Translation, Communications, Journalism, Media, or a related field - Sharp attention to detail, with an eye for linguistic, contextual, and continuity errors - Ability to stay accurate and consistent across high-volume deliverables - Comfort with structured workflows, feedback cycles, and deadline-driven production - Clear communication and collaboration with Senior Writers and cross-functional teams **Nice to have** - Experience in proofreading, editing, translation review, localization, or content QA - Familiarity with AI-assisted writing, translation, or adaptation tools - Basic understanding of storytelling, such as narrative structure, character, and pacing - Ability to read user feedback and spot patterns ## **Who Thrives Here** You enjoy working with language at the sentence level. You catch the small things, like a stiff phrase, a wrong accent, or a line an AI voice will stumble over, and you care whether a story *sounds* right to a listener. You stay focused through large volumes of review and treat feedback as a way to get better. ## **Why It Matters** AI helps us adapt faster, but human review is what makes a localized story feel natural, emotional, and relevant. Your work directly shapes the listening experience of audiences.

**Who we are** Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress. Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that. Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive. This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale. We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life. If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us. **What you’ll do** As an Electrical Engineering Intern, you will work alongside senior hardware engineers to help expand our autonomous transport platforms. You will get hands-on experience designing, testing, and integrating real-world hardware solutions for next-generation, on-road autonomous vehicles. - **PCB & Carrier Board Design:** Support the design and revision of custom circuit boards and carrier boards for vehicle compute, sensors (camera, radar, lidar), GPS, and actuation systems. - **Vehicle & Protocol Integration:** Assist with analyzing and debugging automotive communication protocols (CAN, CAN FD, Ethernet) on real vehicle test platforms. - **Hardware Validation & Testing:** Help design, assemble, and execute test procedures and hardware test fixtures to validate board designs and troubleshoot edge cases. - **Fleet Support:** Work directly with hardware and software engineers on vehicle bring-up, fleet installations, and physical hardware troubleshooting on-site. **What we’re looking for** - **Education:** Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical field. - **Core Technical Knowledge:** Solid foundation in circuit design, analog/digital fundamentals, and basic embedded systems logic. - **Hands-on Experience:** Practical experience with PCB design tools (e.g., Altium, KiCad, Eagle) and bench equipment (oscilloscopes, multimeters, logic analyzers) through lab work, student design teams (e.g., Formula SAE, Robotics Club), or personal projects. - **Protocols & Hardware:** Familiarity or coursework covering common hardware communication protocols (CAN, SPI, I2C, UART). - **Mindset:** Proactive problem solver who thrives in a fast-paced, highly collaborative startup environment and is excited to work with physical hardware. **Why join us** At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow. **What else you need to know** This role is based in our San Franciscooffice. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week. **Program Dates:** Our internship is a 12-weeks program. Cohort sessions run as follows: - **Winter 2027:** January – April - **Summer 2027:** Late May – September The base salary range for this role is **$50.00 per hour.** Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications. **Ready to join us as we serve those who serve others?** *#LI-Onsite*

What we do at Detectify We’re Detectify, and we’re not your average cybersecurity company. We’re a team obsessed with building cutting-edge tech that actually makes a difference in making the internet a safer place. We’re talking about real-life hackers who know their stuff—you’ll learn from the best and join a team that combines human ingenuity with automation to streamline asset discovery and vulnerability assessments. Our software allows the Waymo Driver to perceive the world around it, make the right decision for every situation, and deliver people safely to their destinations.
