As an Applied Science Intern, you'll have the unique opportunity to work alongside world-renowned experts, gaining invaluable hands-on experience with cutting-edge robotics technologies. You'll dive deep into exciting research projects at the intersection of AI and robotics. This internship is not just about executing tasks – it's about being a driving force behind groundbreaking discoveries. You'll collaborate with cross-functional teams, leveraging your expertise in areas such as deep learning, reinforcement learning, computer vision, and motion planning to tackle real-world problems and deliver impactful solutions. Throughout your journey, you'll have access to unparalleled resources, including state-of-the-art computing infrastructure, cutting-edge research papers, and mentorship from industry luminaries. This immersive experience will not only sharpen your technical skills but also cultivate your ability to think critically, communicate effectively, and thrive in a fast-paced, innovative environment where bold ideas are celebrated. Join us at the forefront of applied robotics and AI, where your contributions will shape the future of intelligent systems and propel humanity forward. Seize this extraordinary opportunity to learn, grow, and leave an indelible mark on the world of technology. Amazon has positions available in San Francisco, CA. The ideal candidate should possess: - Strong background in machine learning, deep learning, and/or robotics - Publication record at science conferences such as NeurIPS, CVPR, ICRA, RSS, CoRL, and ICLR. - Experience in areas such as multimodal LLMs, world models, image/video tokenization, real2Sim/Sim2real transfer, bimanual manipulation, open-vocabulary panoptic scene understanding, scaling up multi-modal LLMs, and end-to-end vision-language-action models. - Proficiency in Python, Experience with PyTorch or JAX - Excellent problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work collaboratively in a team Apply now and embark on an extraordinary journey of discovery and innovation! Key job responsibilities - Develop novel, scalable algorithms and modeling techniques that advance the state-of-the-art in areas at the intersection of LLMs and generative AI for robotics - Tackle challenging, groundbreaking research problems on production-scale data, with a focus on robotic perception, manipulation, and control - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to solve complex problems, and to communicate research findings clearly, leveraging your expertise in areas such as deep learning, reinforcement learning, computer vision, and motion planning - Demonstrate the ability to work independently, thrive in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment, and communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders Leverage AI-powered tools where applicable to accelerate research, experimentation, and prototyping. Critically review and validate outputs from AI tools and automated systems.

Who you'll work with Arista Networks is looking for Graduate Engineers interested in learning world leading product development in C/C++, Go and other languages. Join us at Arista Networks advancing the Software Defined Networking (SDN) revolution. What You’ll Do Writing Linux user space and kernel code to allow 32-bit drivers to DMA 64-bit virtual memory spaces using both Intel and AMD IOMMU controller. Working on the hardware/software boundary for chips and the kernel. Where an x86 chip might have tens of registers, you will routinely work on ASICs with thousands of registers, tables, and special TCAM memories. You will program networking chips to provide latency analysis and keep accurate counts of events happening billions of times per second. You will write Python to bootstrap new hardware. You will build software agents that mediate and translate between the requirements of switching ASICs, high capacity custom FPGAs, media adapters, and PCIe bridges. You might tune lasers and measure and correct error rates measured in parts per billion. Implementing communications protocols between routers and switches at layer 2 (such as LLDP, 802.1x, BFD, etc), and layer 3 (such as BGP, OSPF, ISIS). Updating the forwarding state of the hardware, using platform-independent abstractions. Reconciling the linux kernel routing model with the switch's forwarding state. Implementing a policy language used for filtering and manipulating routing data received and advertised to peers Accessing ASIC registers over SPI bus, SMbus, PCIe and I2C, to implement high resolution timers (sub-100ns accuracy) and read ASIC hardware specifications to gather near-real-time information on large numbers of packet flows and to generate network congestion statistics. Developing configuration management services using Go and Python to support YANG, OpenConfig, NETCONF and RESTCONF over gRPC, ssh and ssl for standardised switch configuration, combined with tools such as git, gerrit, Jenkins, Slack and Trello. Developing routing protocol agents (for BGP, OSPF, ISIS) in C/C++ within a Fedora Linux embedded environment. Coding of fault-tolerant, concurrent agents capable of handling the demands of future data centres where high performance and high availability are basic requirements. Fully automated, developer owned, Python based, continuous test harness with 100s of devices under test at any one moment. #LI-EO1 Any of the following:- C, C++, Java, Python, Go, react.js, redux.js, node.js Networking, Linux Embedded Systems, Algorithms, Programming, Software Development. description: Hermeus is a venture-backed defense aviation company reclaiming the lost art of rapid iterative prototyping to build the fastest aircraft in the world today. By prioritizing relentless hardware iteration, we deliver high-speed systems at the pace of the modern battlefield. We work with the Department of War to provide the high-speed capabilities our nation and its allies need to maintain a durable, asymmetric advantage. ### **About the Team:** You'll join a small, fast-moving team building the avionics and flight software for a new flight vehicle program from clean sheet. Everything is actively being built, integrated, and tested on real hardware supporting real tests. This role will focus on developing simulation and hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) infrastructure, combining software development, flight simulation, and hands-on hardware integration. Small team, big ownership, and we move at speeds the rest of the industry doesn't. Spring-Summer: Around 28 weeks (January - August) ### Responsibilities: - Support development of a 6-DOF flight simulation including vehicle dynamics, sensor/actuator models, and engine/plant models to verify flight software in closed loop. - Support hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) testing, including integrating flight computers, avionics, sensors, actuators, and cable harnesses. - Write simulation and test software primarily in C++, with Python and MATLAB used for modeling and tooling. - Troubleshoot and integrate hardware using schematics, pinouts, connectors, and common bench tools. - Build tooling that makes simulation and HITL testing fast, repeatable, and data-rich through logging, playback, and automation. - Independently own simulation and integration tasks from initial setup through testing and troubleshooting. ### Required Qualifications: - Currently pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field. - Working proficiency in C++. - Strong understanding of physics and dynamics fundamentals, including rigid-body dynamics, classical mechanics, reference frames, and equations of motion. - Comfortable working hands-on with hardware, including reading schematics and pinouts, building or terminating cables, and troubleshooting hardware. - Comfortable using common bench tools such as a multimeter, oscilloscope, and power supply. - Comfortable working in a Linux command-line environment. - Demonstrated ability to work effectively on multidisciplinary technical teams. - GPA of 3.0 or above. ### Preferred Skills and Experience: - Working knowledge of MATLAB and/or Python for simulation modeling, analysis, and tooling. - Experience with 6-DOF simulation, flight or vehicle dynamics modeling, or software-in-the-loop (SITL). - Hardware-in-the-loop (HITL), real-time, or embedded systems experience. - GNC coursework or projects involving controls, state estimation, navigation, or flight dynamics. - Soldering, connectorization, or wire-harness fabrication experience. - Hands-on experience with robotics, UAVs/drones, rocketry, FSAE, CubeSat, or similar technical teams. - Previous simulation, GNC, avionics, or flight software internship experience. - Currently pursuing a graduate degree (MS or PhD) in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical field.

## Join the team bringing autonomy to the built world At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs. In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks. This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us. ## **About the Role & Team** Before an autonomous excavator digs its first trench on a new site, it's already dug thousands in simulation. The Simulation team builds the virtual environments our autonomy stack trains and tests against — and the closer sim looks and behaves like the real world, the faster we move. Neural rendering is the next step: replacing hand-authored assets and approximations with learned representations that capture the visual complexity of real jobsites — dust, lighting, deformable terrain, heavy equipment in motion. As our Simulation intern, you'll push neural rendering techniques into our sim pipeline and measure whether they actually close the visual gap that matters for downstream autonomy performance. ## **What You'll Do** - Research, implement, and benchmark neural rendering methods (NeRF, 3D Gaussian splatting, or related techniques) for generating realistic construction-site imagery within our simulation stack - Train models on real-world site data captured by our fleet and evaluate visual fidelity, temporal consistency, and render speed - Integrate neural rendering outputs into the simulation pipeline so perception and planning teams can train and test against them - Build evaluation metrics and tooling that quantify how well rendered scenes match real fleet data — and whether that improvement transfers to autonomy performance - Identify and address failure modes: dynamic objects, deformable terrain, dust, harsh lighting, and other construction-specific challenges - Document findings, limitations, and a recommendation on where neural rendering should (and shouldn't) replace traditional sim assets ## **What We're Looking For** ### **Required** - Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in computer science, computer graphics, robotics, or a related field — or bringing equivalent research or industry experience - Strong Python and hands-on experience with PyTorch (or equivalent) - Solid understanding of 3D graphics fundamentals: rendering pipelines, scene representations, camera models, and coordinate systems - Familiarity with neural scene representations (NeRF, Gaussian splatting, neural radiance fields, or related methods) - Comfort with real-world data — construction sites are messy, dusty, and nothing like an indoor dataset ### **Preferred** - Published work or substantial project experience in neural rendering, novel view synthesis, or differentiable rendering - Experience with simulation engines (Unreal, Unity, NVIDIA Isaac Sim, or similar) - Background in autonomous vehicle simulation or synthetic data generation - Familiarity with C++ and GPU programming (CUDA, OpenGL, Vulkan) **About This Internship** This is a **fixed-term, project-based internship** designed strictly for **students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure** rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, **opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited**." **Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer** We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic. **Reasonable Accommodations** We want our hiring process to be accessible to everyone. ## **What does it take to build the interfaces and tools that help people get more from Coveo?** Are you curious about how frontend development can make complex technology easier to use? Coveo is looking for Frontend Developer interns to join two teams within Research & Development. Depending on the team, you could help developers build search experiences or help customers manage their Coveo organization. You’ll work with experienced teammates, contribute to meaningful projects, and grow your skills in a collaborative engineering environment. Depending on the team you join, you could work on one of the following areas: - **Developer Experience UI (DXUI) team:** This team builds and maintains the frontend libraries that developers use to integrate Coveo search experiences into their applications. Its work provides reusable building blocks for experiences such as conversational product discovery and tools that let administrators preview search changes. As an intern, you’ll help develop the foundations that make these interfaces easier for other teams and developers to build. - **Platform, Resource and Insights (PRI) team:** This team builds features in Coveo’s admin console that help customers understand and manage their Coveo organization. As an intern, you’ll take ownership of a well-scoped frontend feature, from understanding the problem through implementation, testing, code review, and release. You’ll work alongside frontend and backend developers and collaborate with UX and QA teammates. #### **Your impact, day to day:** - Engage actively in daily stand-up meetings to discuss progress, roadblocks, and plans. Collaborate with team members to ensure alignment and effective communication. - Manage and resolve assigned Jira tickets, ensuring timely completion of tasks. - Contribute to real-world projects that support Coveo’s clients. Your work could involve building reusable frontend tools or improving features in the admin console. - Develop your skills by drawing on your mentor’s expertise. Watch, learn, and apply best practices in project management and software development. - Take an active role in code review sessions. Offer constructive feedback and use the feedback you receive to improve the quality of your code and strengthen your programming skills. #### **The Essentials:** - You are currently studying Software Engineering or Computer Science in a Bachelor’s degree or higher in the province of Québec. - You are able to work from one of our offices 2 days a week. Our hybrid work model offers flexibility: office days provide opportunities to learn face-to-face from your team, while home days give you time to focus on complex work. - You are legally entitled to work full-time in Canada for the duration of the 15-week internship. #### **Think you’ve got what it takes? Let’s see!** - You have a foundation in JavaScript and have built something for the web using frontend technologies. Depending on the team, you also bring experience with or an interest in learning: - **DXUI:** React, TypeScript, and Angular, along with an interest in building reusable frontend foundations for other developers. - **PRI:** React, TypeScript, Angular and/or another frontend framework. Experience with testing or projects involving both frontend and backend development is an asset. - You have completed an internship and are ready to take ownership of a project with guidance from your team. - You’re curious, comfortable asking questions, and able to act on feedback. - You have a strong sense of ownership and are proud of what you create. - You’re passionate about the tech industry and lead with a proactive mindset. - You’ve participated in hackathons and/or have a few personal projects. #### **Join the Coveolife!** Do you think you can bring this role to life? Send us your application—we want to hear from you! We encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of, for example, age, gender, disability, gaps in CV, national or ethnic background. *This job description was written by humans, assisted by AI. location: PT Bumi Santosa Cemerlang, Jakarta Pusat, Jakarta Raya, Indonesia
description: About Us Pluang is Indonesia’s leading multi-asset investment platform, offering products such as Indonesian Stocks, Crypto, US Stocks, Mutual Funds, and Gold. Our mission is to make investing accessible, seamless, and secure, so more Indonesians can achieve financial independence. As Pluang continues to grow across products and markets, the way we manage and understand our data becomes increasingly important. Our teams work across data, finance, product, and technology to make sure we have the right information to make better business decisions. Role Overview We are looking for a Business & Data Analytics Intern based in Jakarta to help us improve how we use data across the business. You will work closely with the FP&A, Data, Product, Engineering, and other business teams to help clean and structure data, improve existing processes, migrate reporting and workflows, and turn data into actionable insights . This is a hands-on role. You will not just be preparing reports or updating spreadsheets. You will help us understand how data flows through the business, identify where things can be improved, and build better ways for teams to work with financial and product information. You will have the opportunity to work on real business problems, from understanding the source of a number in a financial report to building analysis that helps stakeholders make better decisions. What You Will Do 1. Help build clean and reliable data flows Work with different teams to understand where financial and product data comes from and how it flows into reporting. Help clean, validate, and structure data from multiple sources. Identify inconsistencies, manual adjustments, and gaps in existing processes. Help improve data definitions so that Finance, Accounting, Data, and business teams are working from the same numbers. Document data sources, business logic, and processes so they are easier to understand and maintain. 2. Support data migration and process automation Help migrate existing reports, workflows, and manual processes into more structured and scalable systems. Work with the team to map existing processes and identify opportunities for automation. Help build or improve data pipelines, dashboards, and internal tools. Make existing workflows simpler, more transparent, and easier to maintain. Work on real problems where the data, process, and business logic may not always be perfectly clean. 3. Turn data into actionable insights Analyze financial and product data to answer real business questions. Build analysis around revenue, costs, AUM, transactions, product performance, and other key business metrics. Help stakeholders understand not only what happened , but also why it happened and what we can do about it . Build dashboards, reports, and analyses that help teams monitor performance and make better decisions. Translate analytical findings into clear and actionable insights for stakeholders. 4. Work across teams to solve real business problems Collaborate with FP&A, Data, Product, Engineering, Operations, and other teams. Help translate business questions into data requirements and analytical solutions. Learn how different parts of a fintech business connect, from product transactions all the way to financial reporting. Take ownership of projects and work with stakeholders to bring them from problem definition to implementation. Communicate your findings and ideas clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. What You Will Need Currently pursuing a degree in Mathematics, Computer Science, Finance, or a related quantitative field . Comfortable working with data, numbers, and analytical problems. Basic experience with SQL and/or Python is preferred. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Able to work with messy or ambiguous problems and structure them into clear steps. Good attention to detail, especially when working with financial and business data. Strong communication skills and willingness to work with different teams. role: 2027 Summer Intern, PhD, Machine Learning Research, Planning/Prediction
description: Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states. Software Engineering builds the brains of Waymo's fully autonomous driving technology. Our software allows the Waymo Driver to perceive the world around it, make the right decision for every situation, and deliver people safely to their destinations. We think deeply and solve complex technical challenges in areas like robotics, perception, decision-making and deep learning, while collaborating with hardware and systems engineers. If you’re a software engineer or researcher who’s curious and passionate about Level 4 autonomous driving, we'd like to meet you. The subteam for this role will be: The Predictive Planning team (PrePlan) develops and deploys state of the art machine learning solutions that predicts the future state of the world and plans the Waymo Driver's Behavior. Our mission is to transform Waymo's unprecedented scale of driving data into robust, generalizable, and perform at deep neural networks. These models enable the autonomous vehicle to navigate complex environments safely and efficiently. Waymo interns partner with leaders in the industry on projects that create impact to the company. We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Hourly PhD Pay $85—$85 USD

Ben jij een ambitieuze AI-innovator? In ons AI-traineeship van 12 maanden dompelen we je onder in de nieuwste technieken, inzichten en vaardigheden op het gebied van kunstmatige intelligentie en innovatie. Ons doel? Een succesvolle kickstart van jouw carrière bij een van onze opdrachtgevers of in onze Bit Innovatie Studio na het traineeship. > Het volgende programma start 1 maart 2027. Tip: Solliciteer zo snel mogelijk, er is een beperkt aantal plekken beschikbaar Not your average traineeship Als Bit-trainee vervul je geen bestaande rol in een organisatie, maar werk je een jaar lang aan een opdracht die we samen met de opdrachtgever vormgeven, op basis van hun meest uitdagende problemen die met new tech zijn op te lossen. We matchen jou met de uitdaging en opdrachtgever die het beste bij jou past, zodat je optimaal kunt bijdragen en groeien. Maatwerk dus, waarbij je écht impact kunt maken. Impact maken met AI op echte projecten, zoals: ✈️ Ontwerpen en ontwikkelen van AI-oplossingen om de CO2-uitstoot van een luchtvaartmaatschappij te verminderen. 📦 Het bouwen van een op computer vision-gebaseerde sensor om de snelheid van pakketbezorging te verbeteren. ⚙️ Het prototypen van een voorspellingsmodel voor het onderhoud van windturbines. 🛍️ Onderzoek doen en adviseren over toekomstige AI-technologieën voor een retail- en designbedrijf. 🌱 AI en datavisualisatie inzetten om het stikstofbodemoverschot en naijl-effect inzichtelijk te maken en hiermee datagedreven beleid mogelijk te maken voor de overheid. Meer weten over wat we doen? Check Training & begeleiding Je start direct met ons trainingsprogramma voor een vliegende start op jouw opdracht. Op dag 2 start je al bij je opdrachtgever, waar je 4 dagen per week (hybride) werkt. Je krijgt dus de kans om je kennis en vaardigheden meteen toe te passen in een echte omgeving. Vanuit Bit wordt je begeleid door een talent manager die wekelijks bij je incheckt. Elke vrijdag kom je met de andere trainees samen bij Bit en neem je deel aan trainingen en workshops van ervaren professionals. Bij de opdrachtgever koppelen we je aan iemand met een invloedrijke positie binnen de organisatie, wat betekent dat er deuren geopend kunnen worden die voor veel starters vaak gesloten blijven - al zul je ze wel zelf moeten openen... Onze mentaliteit? Do it scared! Onze waarden & cultuur Als je bij ons begint, ben je gelijk part of the team: een zeer behulpzame groep jonge mensen die van elkaar willen leren en elkaar uitdagen om tot de slimste oplossingen te komen. We beloven je een omgeving waar je verantwoordelijkheid, vertrouwen en vrijheid krijgt. Wat we daarvoor terugvragen is passie, plezier en prestatie. Cultuur staat bij ons op #1. Daarom organiseren we veel team events en vinden we het belangrijk dat je je kunt identificeren met onze kernwaarden: 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Team first 🧠 We lead, we learn 🚀 Pushing status quo Bij Bit vieren we verschillen. Immers, de beste ideeën komen voort uit diversiteit van denken. Daarom moedigen we mensen uit alle achtergronden aan om te solliciteren. Als je aan de functieomschrijving voldoet, krijg je volledige en gelijke overweging voor de functie - ongeacht ras, religie, genderidentiteit, seksuele geaardheid, handicap of leeftijd. Dit heb je nodig om binnen ons traineeship te excelleren: Kennis: Je hebt een afgeronde Master in AI (of een aanverwante opleiding zoals Data Science, Econometrie, Natuurkunde, Wiskunde of Informatica, met een specialisatie in AI) óf je hebt een Master in Industrieel Ontwerpen en grote affiniteit met technologie en innovatie. Je hebt 0-1 jaar werkervaring. Je beheerst Python en minimaal één andere programmeertaal, of je bent een innovator die haarfijn kan uitleggen hoe nieuwe technologie werkt. Je hebt ervaring met en passie voor machine learning, large language models, GPT, natural language processing en andere relevante AI-technologieën. Vaardigheden: Je hebt een positieve vibe. Je hebt sterke analytische en probleemoplossende vaardigheden. Je bent een conceptueel & strategisch denker met een 'creatieve touch'. Je hebt uitstekende communicatie- en samenwerkingsvaardigheden en kunt zowel in een team als zelfstandig werken. Je hebt een ondernemende instelling en een trackrecord van initiatief nemen en proactief zijn. Je hebt het vermogen om te werken in een snel veranderende omgeving. Je bent leergierig en gaat uitdagingen graag aan. Klinkt goed? Meld je nu aan! Als je klaar bent om te starten aan een leerzame & indrukwekkende tech-innovatiereis, horen we graag van je. Are you ready to become a Future Tech Leader?!

role: Summer 2027 Undergraduate Intern, Speech, Privacy and Technology Project
description: ## **About the Role** The ACLU seeks a full-time **Summer** **Undergraduate** Intern in the **Speech, Privacy and Technology Project**of the ACLU’s National office in **New York City.** This position can be remote or hybrid. **Qualifying applicants must currently be matriculated undergraduate students and must be based in the U.S. for the entire duration of the internship.** ## **The Team:** The Speech, Privacy and Technology Project is dedicated to protecting and expanding the First Amendment freedoms of expression, association, and inquiry; expanding the right to privacy and increasing the control that individuals have over their personal information; and ensuring that civil liberties are enhanced rather than compromised by new advances in science and technology. The project is currently litigating cases and conducting other advocacy efforts on a variety of issues, including political protest, freedom of expression online, privacy of electronic information, journalists’ rights, scientific and academic freedom, openness in the courts, privacy rights at the border, and the impact of big data and algorithmic decision-making. ## **What You’ll Do:** The undergraduate summer internship is designed to provide interns with the opportunity to learn about public interest work, explore personal research opportunities, and engage in legal advocacy and public writing for issues on which the Speech, Privacy, and Technology Project focuses. There are no educational prerequisites for the position, and applicants need not have any background nor prior knowledge in pre-law, technology, or science-related fields. The Project strongly encourages people of color, women, LGBTQ+ people, and people with disabilities to apply. ## **Your Day to Day:** - Conducting research on issues relating to free speech, privacy and technology - Preparing, producing and developing litigation and advocacy materials - Drafting posts for the ACLU blog - Conducting research on Freedom of Information Act requests - Attending meetings to gain firsthand knowledge of active cases and advocacy projects - Assisting with litigation and advocacy projects - Assisting with the maintenance of case files - Assisting in administrative support and other maintenance tasks to support the work of the project - Proposing independent research projects relating to free speech, privacy and technology This posting provides a general but not comprehensive list of the opportunities of the internship. ## **What You'll Bring:** The undergraduate internship is open to students who have completed at least one year of their undergraduate program before the internship commences. Undergraduate interns should possess the following: - Enthusiasm for issues related to free speech, privacy, and technology as well as a commitment to social justice and civil liberties. - Strong research, writing, and communications skills. - Initiative to see projects through to completion. - Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (i.e. Word, Excel, and PowerPoint). ## **Future ACLU'ers Will:** - Be committed to advancing the mission of the ACLU - Center and embed the principles of equity, inclusion and belonging in their work by demonstrating commitment to diversity with an approach that respects and values multiple perspectives - Be committed to work collaboratively and respectfully toward resolving obstacles and conflicts ## **Internship Logistics** - **Location**: Our internship program offers a limited number of remote or hybrid intern positions. This internship may be **remote or** **hybrid and based in our New York City office.** - **Time Commitment**: Summer internships require a full time (35 hour/week) commitment for 10 consecutive weeks. - **Internship Duration**: Internships have a start date of **May 24 or June 7.** - **Stipend**: A stipend is available for those students who are lawfully authorized to work. Undergraduate interns receive a stipend amount $20/hour (stipends are taxed) ## **Why the ACLU** For over 100 years, the ACLU has worked to defend and preserve the individual rights and liberties guaranteed by the Constitution and laws of the United States. Whether it’s ending mass incarceration, achieving full equality for the LGBTQ+ community, establishing new privacy protections for our digital age, or preserving the right to vote or the right to have an abortion, the ACLU takes up the toughest civil liberties cases and issues to defend all people. ## **Our Commitment to Accessibility, Equity, Diversity & Inclusion** Accessibility, equity, diversity, and inclusion are core values of the ACLU and central to our work to advance liberty, equality, and justice for all. For us diversity, equity and inclusion are not just check-the-box activities, but a chance for us to make long-term meaningful change. We are a community committed to learning and growth, humility and grace, transparency and accountability. We believe in a collective responsibility to create a culture of belonging for all people within our organization – one that respects and embraces difference; treats everyone equitably; and empowers our colleagues to do the best work possible. We are as committed to anti-oppression and anti-racism internally as we are externally. Because whether we’re in the courts or in the office, we believe ‘We the People’ means all of us. With this commitment in mind, we strongly encourage applications from all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, marital status, citizenship, disability, veteran status and record of arrest or conviction, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. *The ACLU is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to individuals with disabilities. If you are a qualified individual with a disability and need assistance applying online, please complete the*[Accommodation Request Form](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=6XZWc5QkD0q_MUveoekZhpx9FkPMtDFAmz3e2gWC_wNUOTVFRTRINjdRT0FLSTVPUUU3N0NXQ0dDTS4u&route=shorturl) *If you are selected for an interview, you will receive additional information regarding how to request an accommodation for the interview process.* ***In order to be considered for this position, all candidates must formally submit an application.**The ACLU does not accept unsolicited calls or emails from candidates regarding their application status.***

role: Summer 2027 Legal Intern, National Security Project
description: ## **About the Role** The ACLU seeks a **Summer** **Legal** Intern in the **National Security Project**of the ACLU’s National office in **New York City.** This position is hybrid. **Qualifying applicants must currently be matriculated legal students and must be based in the U.S. for the entire duration of the internship.** ## **The Team:** The National Security Project fights for people and communities harmed by the government in the name of national security. Recognizing the danger of expansive claims of state power, we advocate for a robust system of checks and balances and for policies that comply with the Constitution, civil liberties, and human rights. Through the courts, Congress, and public education, we strive to ensure that people are able to participate fully in civic life and are free from discrimination, unwarranted suspicion and surveillance, unlawful force and detention, and the stigma and other injustices that result from these abuses. ## **What You’ll Do:** The Legal Internwill be responsible for supporting the National Security Project’s legal and advocacy work over the course of the summer. ## **Your Day to Day:** - Conduct legal and policy research - Draft memoranda, affidavits, and briefs - Research prospects for new litigation, including both factual and legal claims - Research and draft materials for public education ## **What You'll Bring:** The internship is open to students enrolled at U.S. law schools who will have completed at least one year of law school before the internship commences. Interns should possess the following: - Excellent research skills, including conducting internet and legal database research - Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written - Ability to analyze complex legal issues - Initiative to see projects through to completion - Commitment to civil liberties, civil rights, and social justice, particularly as they relate to national security, and to the mission of the ACLU - Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite ## **Future ACLU'ers Will:** - Be committed to advancing the mission of the ACLU - Center and embed the principles of equity, inclusion and belonging in their work by demonstrating commitment to diversity with an approach that respects and values multiple perspectives - Be committed to work collaboratively and respectfully toward resolving obstacles and conflicts ## **Internship Logistics** - **Location**: Our internship program offers a limited number of remote or hybrid intern positions. This internship is hybrid based in our national office in New York, NY. - **Time Commitment**: This internship is full-time (35 hrs/wk) for a duration of 10 consecutive weeks. - **Internship Duration**: This internship has a start date of **May 24 or June 7.** - **Stipend:** A stipend is available for those students who are lawfully authorized to work. Students who receive outside funding are eligible for a partial stipend to bring their total funding up to the level of the ACLU’s stipend amount for the summer. Legal interns receive a stipend amount of $24/hour (stipends are taxed) **Priority Application Deadline:** **2L students: October 18, 2026** **1L Students: November 2, 2026** While there is a priority deadline, our project is committed to reviewing all applications on a rolling basis until the closing of posting. ## **Why the ACLU** For over 100 years, the ACLU has worked to defend and preserve the individual rights and liberties guaranteed by the Constitution and laws of the United States. Whether it’s ending mass incarceration, achieving full equality for the LGBTQ+ community, establishing new privacy protections for our digital age, or preserving the right to vote or the right to have an abortion, the ACLU takes up the toughest civil liberties cases and issues to defend all people. ## **Our Commitment to Accessibility, Equity, Diversity & Inclusion** Accessibility, equity, diversity, and inclusion are core values of the ACLU and central to our work to advance liberty, equality, and justice for all. For us diversity, equity and inclusion are not just check-the-box activities, but a chance for us to make long-term meaningful change. We are a community committed to learning and growth, humility and grace, transparency and accountability. We believe in a collective responsibility to create a culture of belonging for all people within our organization – one that respects and embraces difference; treats everyone equitably; and empowers our colleagues to do the best work possible. We are as committed to anti-oppression and anti-racism internally as we are externally. Because whether we’re in the courts or in the office, we believe ‘We the People’ means all of us. With this commitment in mind, we strongly encourage applications from all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, marital status, citizenship, disability, veteran status and record of arrest or conviction, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. *The ACLU is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to individuals with disabilities. If you are a qualified individual with a disability and need assistance applying online, please complete the* [Accommodation Request Form](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=6XZWc5QkD0q_MUveoekZhpx9FkPMtDFAmz3e2gWC_wNUOTVFRTRINjdRT0FLSTVPUUU3N0NXQ0dDTS4u&route=shorturl) *If you are selected for an interview, you will receive additional information regarding how to request an accommodation for the interview process.* ***In order to be considered for this position, all candidates must formally submit an application.**The ACLU does not accept unsolicited calls or emails from candidates regarding their application status.*** ## ACLU’s internship program is supported in part by the Arnie Miller Fund for the Next Generation: [The Arnie Miller Fund For The Next Generation | American Civil Liberties Union](https://www.aclu.org/the-arnie-miller-fund-for-the-next-generation).

Position Overview Novelis is one of the world leaders in aluminum recycling and rolling and a leading sustainable aluminum solutions provider. Driven by our purpose of shaping a sustainable world together, we work alongside our customers to provide innovative solutions to the aerospace, automotive, beverage packaging and specialty markets. Headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, Novelis has approximately 13,000 employees in 32 operating facilities on 4 continents. Responsibilities & Qualifications Position Overview The Global Automotive Technology team is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented co-op student to support automotive research, competitive benchmarking and data analytics. This co-op will begin May 2027 and end December 2027. The student will organize vehicle and market information, develop analytical tools, identify trends and communicate findings to technical and business stakeholders. Responsibilities Research vehicle specifications, technologies, market trends and publicly available competitive information. Collect, organize and maintain structured automotive datasets from approved sources. Support vehicle benchmarking and lightweighting-related analyses across selected vehicle segments and systems. Develop Excel- or Power BI-based tools, dashboards and visualizations. Apply basic statistical and data-quality methods to identify trends, gaps and inconsistencies. Prepare concise updates, summaries and presentations for technical and business audiences. Collaborate with engineering, materials, sustainability and commercial team members. Key Projects Automotive benchmarking database development and data-quality review. Assessment of vehicle features, specifications and market positioning. Lightweighting opportunity screening and decision-support tool development. Dashboard creation, data visualization and executive communication. Minimum Qualifications Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Automotive Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Data Science, Business Analytics or a related field. Strong Excel and analytical skills; Power BI, Python, database or statistical-tool experience is a plus. Interest in automotive technology, vehicle design, sustainability, materials or product strategy. Ability to research technical information, work with large datasets and document sources carefully. Strong attention to detail, problem-solving ability and communication skills. Ability to work independently and collaborate in a cross-functional environment. What We Offer: Novelis' benefits say a lot about how we care for each other. Our employees and their families have many different needs. As a result, our benefits offer choices on many levels and are high in quality, driven by the marketplace, and affordable. In addition to core benefits, we provide these unique to the industry benefits: Combined housing and relocation stipend for out of state interns or interns outside an extended radius for select positions Competitive pay Location Profile Novelis’ Global Research and Technology Center located in Kennesaw Georgia within the greater Atlanta metropolitan area is a cutting-edge full-service research and technology hub that employs approximately 200 people including world-class engineers metallurgists chemists scientists technologists and technicians. The facility includes state-of-the-art lab equipment and a diverse mix of product pilot lines that bring innovative solutions to customers in the automotive beverage can and specialty markets. Kennesaw provides a diverse and family-friendly place to live with countless museums cultural opportunities and educational institutions. Novelis is committed to the Kennesaw community and supports a number of local charitable organizations including Habitat for Humanity as well as FIRST Robotics aimed at encouraging young people to pursue the Science Technology Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) fields in order to spur the next generation of scientists and innovators. Novelis recognizes its talented and diverse workforce as a key competitive advantage. Novelis provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants. These measurements include, but are not limited to, S-Parameters, DC and/RF pulse power, IP3, IP2, P1dB, harmonics, thermal imaging, and switching speed. About Sync Sync is a Canadian company building zero-knowledge, end-to-end encrypted cloud storage and collaboration for over two million people and businesses worldwide. Unlike most of our competitors, we own and operate our own storage infrastructure rather than renting it. Our customers’ data lives on our hardware, in our racks, in Canada. That is a core part of our product promise, and it means the physical infrastructure is not a back-office concern here. It is the product. About the role We are hiring a Junior IT Infrastructure Technician to help maintain the JBODs, servers, and network gear in our Toronto colocation facility. This is a hybrid role based in Toronto, with regular travel to our Toronto Data Centre required to do hands-on work, and a genuinely strong entry point into storage and infrastructure engineering, you will be working directly on petabyte-scale storage systems from your first week. You will rack and maintain hardware, replace failed drives and components, own the RMA process end to end, manage procurement, and support the day-to-day IT needs of the team. We are looking for someone early in their career who is curious about how things work and who moves toward problems instead of waiting to be assigned them. You will not be expected to arrive knowing everything. You will be expected to ask good questions, document what you learn, and take real ownership of the things you touch. Once you're ramped up, this role will also include participation in an on-call rotation. What you will do Maintain our JBOD storage enclosures: identify and replace failed drives, verify rebuilds complete cleanly, and track drive health and failure trends over time. Install, cable, configure, provision and decommission servers and storage chassis in our Toronto colocation cage. Diagnose and resolve hardware faults across drives, memory, PSUs, HBAs, SAS expanders, backplanes, and network components. Support network infrastructure: rack and cable switches, maintain accurate port maps, and assist with configuration changes under supervision. Support the team during critical situations: respond to monitoring alerts, work the relevant runbook, and help recover systems from unexpected failures. Own the RMA process end to end: identify the failure, open the case with the vendor, track the shipment, install the replacement, and confirm the fix. Then make sure the inventory reflects reality. Manage procurement for hardware and IT equipment, including quoting, purchase orders, receiving, and day-to-day vendor communication. Maintain an accurate asset inventory covering serial numbers, warranty status, rack and slot locations, and lifecycle state. Keep the cage clean and auditable through disciplined structured cabling, labelling, and cable management. Handle media sanitization and secure disposal of decommissioned drives in line with our security policies. Coordinate with the colocation provider on remote hands, access approvals, power and cooling questions, and scheduled maintenance windows. Provide general IT support to internal staff, including laptop provisioning, account setup, and endpoint troubleshooting. Write and improve runbooks so the next person can do the task without having to ask. Participate in an on-call rotation for incidents after an onboarding period. What we are looking for 0 to 2 years of experience in IT support, datacenter operations, or a related hands-on technical role. Co-op terms, internships, home labs, and personal projects all count. A proactive mindset. You notice the drive that keeps throwing errors before it fails outright, and you raise it. Real curiosity about infrastructure. You want to understand why a system behaves the way it does, not just which button restarts it. Working knowledge of server and storage hardware, and comfort using hand tools in a rack environment. Linux fundamentals at the command line: navigating the filesystem, reading logs with journalctl and dmesg, and using basic disk and filesystem tooling such as lsblk, smartctl and df. Basic networking knowledge: IP addressing, VLANs, switching, subnetting, routing and the ability to read and maintain a cable map. Care and precision around data. In a live storage environment, pulling the wrong drive matters — we need someone who checks twice before executing any task. Clear written communication. A significant part of this job is leaving a good record for the next person. Strong organizational habits, particularly around tracking assets, tickets, and open vendor cases. Ability to work on-site in Toronto and to lift and position equipment weighing up to 50 lbs. Eligibility to work in Canada. Nice to have Exposure to a colocation or datacenter environment. Familiarity with SAS or SATA storage topologies, RAID or erasure coding concepts, or distributed storage systems such as ZFS or Ceph. Scripting in Bash or Python to automate repetitive work such as drive health checks or inventory reconciliation. Experience with out-of-band management tools such as iDRAC, iLO, or IPMI. Any exposure to a switch CLI – Cisco NX-OS or IOS, HP ProCurve, or similar –even if only show commands. Any exposure to monitoring and alerting tooling such as Prometheus, Grafana, Zabbix. Familiarity with Containers (Docker, LXC) or with a directory and identity service for user and device management. Certifications such as CompTIA A+, Network+, Server+, or equivalent coursework. Perks: Compensation range: $50,000 to $58,000 CAD Generous WSA program Best-in-the-class health benefits Paid vacation with carry-over Flexible Hybrid Direct hands-on experience with petabyte-scale storage infrastructure that very few companies our size operate themselves. A clear growth path toward storage, systems, or network engineering, with mentorship from the senior staff who built this infrastructure. Budget for certifications and training. is an equal opportunity dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive team. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates and will accommodate applicants’ needs throughout the recruitment, assessment, and selection process. If selected to participate in the process, please inform us of the nature of any accommodation(s) that you may require. #LI- Hybrid

description: RF Power Amplifier Design Intern Role Overview: As a member of the RF Power Product Design team, the RF Power Amplifier Design Intern will work alongside experienced engineers providing mentoring, guidance, and introductions to colleagues. The design intern will be working at the Morgan Hill Design Center alongside a highly knowledgeable team of RF engineers and will initially be tasked with RF power device design of MACOM’s high power GaN transistor products geared towards, Multi Market, Base Station and 5G markets. description: Come work with the founders building what's next. Some of the most important companies of the next decade are being built right now, in Southern California, by two or three people and an idea. We're looking for someone who wants a front-row seat to all of them, and the technical chops to help make them real. You'll work across AI/ML, FinTech, ClimateTech, healthcare, consumer, B2B SaaS, and whatever gets invented next, with many of these companies coming straight out of Y Combinator and other top accelerators or freshly backed by leading VC firms. They need a trusted technical voice in their corner from day one, and you get to be it. Picture a small team with a technical founder and maybe a couple of engineers, moving fast with Claude Code, Codex, and whatever tool shipped last week, trying to make every product, architecture, and business decision at once. There's no VP of Engineering to align with, no platform team to hand things off to, and no multi-quarter roadmap, so for the startups you work with you become the closest thing they have to a fractional CTO or chief architect. That's what makes this an adventure rather than a support role: you and the founders are figuring it out together, and a single good decision can save six months of runway while a bad one can quietly sink the whole thing. The work is bigger than architecture, and it changes week to week. One week you're helping a team understand the architecture their coding agent quietly built for them and untangling the decisions they didn't realize they'd made, the next you're figuring out how to scale after an unexpected viral launch, and the week after that you're working a compliance problem with a FinTech startup that has to move fast but can't cut corners, or talking a founder through a hard pivot and helping them separate what they've already built from where the data says they should actually go. You'll prototype alongside them, experiment with frontier AI, and carry what you learn from hundreds of founders back into AWS so the products we build reflect what the leading edge actually needs. We hire for a specific kind of person, and it starts with founder empathy over enterprise process. You get that every dollar spent on infra is a dollar not spent on talent or growth, that their timeline is measured in months of runway, and that they're emotionally all-in on this idea, so you earn trust by genuinely caring whether the team survives rather than by showing off enterprise-grade architecture. That empathy shows up as survival-first thinking: before you recommend anything, you understand their runway, their burn, their signals of product-market fit, and their next milestone, whether that's demo day, a fundraise, or a first paying customer. To advise this well you have to see the full stack of the business, letting technical choices, product, business model, runway, and the founder's own risk tolerance all inform your recommendations, because you can't advise on architecture without understanding burn rate. You stay a builder at heart, since you don't stop being an engineer when you join this team; you prototype, write code, and get your hands dirty with new models, Bedrock, agents, and RAG because that's how you stay credible with people who build for a living. And you act as a scout for the future, spotting when a single startup's tool choice becomes a cohort-wide trend twelve to twenty-four months before the rest of the market, then carrying that signal back to AWS product and service teams. You don't have to already be a Solutions Architect to do this. Great people on this team have come from founding-engineer roles, senior software engineering, AI engineering, and traditional SA backgrounds, and if you're an excellent builder who loves customers, we can teach you the AWS you need. Key job responsibilities - Act as a trusted technical advisor to a portfolio of early-stage founders, designing architectures that are right-sized for where they are today and built to grow if and when they scale - Get hands-on: prototype, build reference patterns, and demo working solutions alongside founders rather than handing them a generic playbook - Help founders understand and improve the architectures their coding agents generated, making sense of the decisions and tradeoffs baked into what they've already shipped - Help startups navigate the fast-moving GenAI landscape, from selecting the right foundation models and AI services to shipping production-ready AI-powered products - Guide founders through the real challenges of building GenAI applications, including model cost, latency, accuracy, safety, and AI best practices - Help founders make pragmatic build-and-scale decisions, including when to keep architectures disposable and adaptable while the direction is still being validated - Stay technically sharp by experimenting with new models, agent frameworks, and emerging tools, so you can advise credibly across the entire stack - Build and deepen relationships across San Francisco's startup ecosystem, including top accelerators like Y Combinator, incubators, and leading VC firms - Be a voice for your founders, connecting their feedback and needs directly to AWS product and engineering teams to shape the tools being built for them - Scout emerging technology trends across the startups you work with and translate those signals back into AWS product roadmaps - Share your expertise at startup events, demo days, and developer meetups across the San Francisco ecosystem to build trust and visibility in the community

role: Junior AI Engineer / Forward Deployed Engineer
description: ABOUT VERIAN Verian is a world-leading, purpose-led and independent research, evidence, evaluation and communications agency, providing services to governments and the public realm. We combine expertise in human understanding with advanced technologies and data science to help clients solve complex public policy challenges. At Verian , we are looking for a Junior AI Engineer / Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to help build and deploy AI solutions alongside researchers, project teams and clients. This is a hands-on role at the intersection of AI engineering, applied research and real-world problem solving. Depending on the project and your strengths, you may focus on LLM applications and agentic systems, machine learning and data science, experimentation, client-facing solution development, or AI-enabled policy research. If you are early in your career, enjoy learning by building, and want to apply AI to complex questions with real societal impact, this could be a strong next step. WHAT YOU WILL DO Our projects vary, so your day-to-day work may span several areas. You will initially receive guidance on more complex or ambiguous tasks and take on increasing ownership as your skills grow. AI engineering and agentic systems: Build LLM applications and agentic workflows for research and analysis, including agent harnesses, context and memory systems, tool integrations and orchestration, with appropriate permissions and human oversight. Solution scoping and experimentation: Help define problems, test alternative architectures and compare approaches such as agentic RAG, GraphRAG, single- or multi-agent systems, or simpler solutions when they are more appropriate. Use evidence to balance quality, reliability, complexity, cost and research needs. Technical implementation and testing: Turn promising prototypes into reliable, deployable tools. Build pipelines, APIs and interfaces; test performance and failure handling on realistic tasks; and support data protection, reproducibility and monitoring. Research and analysis: Work with policy researchers to apply AI and data science methods to real research questions. Validate results against expert judgement and simpler methods, preserve source references and reproducible workflows, and contribute to analytical outputs. Client engagement and communication: Work with project teams and clients to understand needs, define requirements and success criteria, demonstrate solutions, gather feedback and support adoption. You may also contribute to technical proposals and policy-relevant findings. WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR We welcome talented recent graduates and early-career applicants. You do not need to arrive with expertise in every area; we are looking for strong foundations, curiosity and evidence that you learn quickly. Relevant foundation: A degree in computer science, artificial intelligence, data science, statistics, computational social sciences, economics or a related field. Other backgrounds and equivalent practical experience are welcome when supported by relevant skills and projects. Evidence that you like to build: Experience creating and testing AI applications, ML models or analytical workflows through studies, personal projects, internships or professional work. We are interested in what you contributed, how you evaluated the result and what you improved. Programming skills: Working knowledge of Python and confidence learning or working with JavaScript/TypeScript. Familiarity with APIs, version control and structured development practices is valuable. AI curiosity and practical judgement: You follow relevant AI research, model releases and developer tools, test new approaches yourself, challenge assumptions constructively and use evidence to decide what is worth adopting, improving or stopping. Research mindset: Curiosity about research questions, data quality, evidence and the limitations of an analysis. An interest in public policy, social research or how governments make decisions is important. Communication and ownership: Full professional proficiency in English, strong written communication, and the ability to take ownership of well-scoped work while asking for guidance when needed. NICE TO HAVE (NOT ESSENTIAL) Experience with model APIs, RAG or GraphRAG, agent orchestration, MCP tool integrations, context or memory systems, structured outputs, evaluations or execution traces. Exposure to cloud services, deployment, permissions, monitoring or production AI workflows. Familiarity with policy evaluation, EU institutions or public-sector decision-making processes. GROW WITH US Our AI team offers significant autonomy and dedicated time for experimentation, supported by training, coaching and feedback. We want you to explore methods, test tools, share what works and what does not, and become increasingly independent over time. Meaningful impact: Apply your skills to evidence and tools that help governments and third-sector organisations address societal challenges and improve people’s lives. Training and coaching: Develop through practical experimentation and feedback across AI engineering, machine learning, data science, policy research methods, cloud services and project delivery. Room to experiment: Propose ideas, test approaches and learn from both successful and unsuccessful experiments. Salary: EUR 1,800 – 2,800 gross per month , depending on your qualifications and experience. Flexibility and wellbeing: We operate with no fixed office hours and offer remote-working options. For office-based employees, remote work is available for up to half of the time. Additional benefits include private employee health insurance*, extra days off and access to the Mindletic Emotional Intelligence Training App. *For office-based employees. DON’T SELF-SELECT OUT We do not expect candidates to meet every single requirement. We value complementary strengths and, especially at junior level, your trajectory matters: how you learn, respond to feedback and turn new understanding into better work. If you are strong in some of these areas and motivated to develop in others, we encourage you to apply. HOW TO APPLY Please submit your CV through our application system. Where relevant, include links to GitHub, a portfolio or projects that help us understand what you have built. We review applications based on relevant skills, experience, projects and motivation. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We value diversity and welcome applications from people with different backgrounds and experiences. If you require reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know.

description: ## Join the team bringing autonomy to the built world At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs. In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks. This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us. ## **About the Role & Team** Putting an autonomous 40-ton excavator on a live jobsite means being able to say, precisely, what we know about its safety and what that knowledge rests on. Today that argument lives in hazard analyses, requirements, tests and logs, linked by hand. As a Safety Engineering intern, you’ll explore how formal methods and LLM-assisted proving can strengthen that argument. Working at the intersection of formal methods, statistics, and field robotics, you’ll formalize a narrowly scoped safety claim, verify a checker in Lean, and evaluate it on real fleet data, with explicit assumptions and auditable results. ## **What You'll Do** - Become fluent in Bedrock's safety case and trace safety claims through the hazards, requirements, mitigations, and evidence that support them - Build an end-to-end demonstration for one claim: define the property and assumptions, implement a checker in Lean, prove its correctness against the specification, and run it on fleet data - Develop checks for assumptions that can be monitored in fleet data, and document those that require other evidence - Build audit tooling for LLM-assisted proving: record proof dependencies, document toolchain trust assumptions, and reject proof placeholders or unapproved axioms in automated builds - Work with Safety, Systems, and Autonomy teams to review formal specifications and turn findings into safety case improvements - Document the results, limitations, and recommendations for adoption in our review process ## **What We're Looking For** ### **Required** - Hands-on experience with Lean and mathlib experience, particularly real analysis or probability. - Working knowledge of probability and statistics (distributions, confidence intervals, tail bounds). - Familiarity with knowledge graphs or structured document analysis - Ability to translate informal claims into precise specifications and identify their assumptions - Experience evaluating LLM-generated code or proofs. - Background in autonomous vehicles, heavy equipment, or other safety-critical robotics. ### **Preferred** - Exposure to safety or assurance-case practice (GSN, UL 4600, ISO 13849, IEC 61508) or runtime verification. - Experience with Rust verification tools (Aeneas, Verus, Kani) or differential/property-based testing. - Familiarity with knowledge graphs or structured document analysis - Background in autonomous vehicles, heavy equipment, or other safety-critical robotics **About This Internship** This is a **fixed-term, project-based internship** designed strictly for **students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure** rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, **opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited**." **Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer** We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic. **Reasonable Accommodations** We want our hiring process to be accessible to everyone. Raise the quality of aircraft requirements and interfaces by making testability, observability, fault isolation, and verification strategy explicit early in design. - Develop senior technical talent and create durable practices that allow the organization to deliver more capability through the team rather than through individual heroics. ### What you'll do: - Own the technical strategy, architecture, and roadmap for electrical test equipment supporting X-BAT avionics, power, communications, actuation, and other aircraft subsystems. - Identify program verification risks and capability gaps; convert them into prioritized investments, platform decisions, development plans, and clear technical ownership. - Define common architectures for racks, stands, interface units, power and fault insertion, instrumentation, data acquisition, timing, automation, diagnostics, and operator interfaces. - Lead the most complex or novel test-equipment programs through requirements, trade studies, architecture, detailed design, build, integration, acceptance, deployment, and sustainment. - Set and uphold engineering standards for schematics, PCB and harness design, calibration, documentation, and release readiness. - Establish system-safety expectations for energized test equipment, including hazard analysis, safe-state design, interlocks, isolation, emergency stops, access control, and verification of protective functions. - Chair high-consequence architecture, design, and readiness reviews; make or drive closure on cross-domain technical decisions and unresolved risks. - Partner with systems and design engineering to define testable requirements, electrical interfaces, built-in observability, fault isolation, and verification approaches before aircraft designs are released. - Develop strategies for equipment reliability, availability, maintainability, calibration, obsolescence, spares, vendor support, and recovery from failures during critical test campaigns. - Lead cross-functional root-cause investigations that span test equipment, units under test, software, facilities, manufacturing, and supplier processes; ensure corrective actions improve both products and test capability. - Make informed build-versus-buy decisions and provide technical direction to vendors, integrators, technicians, and partner teams delivering portions of the test ecosystem. - Define and use meaningful operating metrics such as first-pass acceptance, schedule predictability, equipment uptime, test repeatability, recurring anomalies, action closure, and reuse of proven designs. - Mentor senior and developing engineers, delegate architecture and project ownership effectively, and improve the quality of technical reasoning and review across the organization. ### Required qualifications: - B.S. in Electrical Engineering or a related STEM discipline, or equivalent practical experience. - 8+ years of relevant industry experience developing complex electrical hardware, automated test equipment, or multidisciplinary verification systems. - A record of leading multiple hardware development cycles and delivering equipment or products from ambiguous requirements through release, deployment, and sustained use. - Deep expertise in several relevant domains, such as power electronics, analog and digital design, RF and communications, instrumentation, data acquisition, control systems, signal integrity, grounding, or system safety. - Demonstrated ability to architect systems that span custom electronics, commercial instruments, harnessing, embedded control, automation software, mechanical equipment, and facility interfaces. - Strong command of requirements decomposition, interface control, verification planning, design reviews, configuration management, acceptance testing, and technical documentation. - Experience establishing technical standards or reusable platforms and influencing teams beyond direct project authority. - Demonstrated success resolving complex cross-domain failures using data, first-principles reasoning, structured root-cause analysis, and disciplined corrective action. - Ability to communicate technical decisions, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to engineers, operators, program leaders, and executives. - A record of mentoring engineers, raising technical quality, and delivering exceptional outcomes in a fast-moving environment. ### Preferred qualifications: - Experience architecting aerospace or defense ground-test, qualification-test, hardware-in-the-loop, or production-test systems for flight-critical hardware. - Experience across several aircraft electrical domains, including high-voltage or high-power systems, batteries, motors and drives, RF, avionics networks, sensors, flight controls, or mission systems. - Experience scaling a test capability from early prototype equipment to configuration-controlled platforms used across multiple teams, sites, or product phases. - Experience applying safety and reliability methods such as hazard analysis, FMEA, fault-tree analysis, proof testing, fault insertion, redundancy, and safe-state verification. - Knowledge of environmental and qualification testing such as thermal, vibration, shock, HALT, HASS, ESS, EMI or EMC, and the controls and instrumentation required to execute it well. - Working knowledge of standards such as DO-160, MIL-STD-810, MIL-STD-461, IPC, IEEE, NFPA 70E, or equivalent standards relevant to prior work. - Experience with calibration systems, measurement uncertainty, metrology, data traceability, equipment cybersecurity, or regulated lab and production environments. - Experience developing capital-equipment plans, managing technical suppliers or integrators, and balancing capability, schedule, cost, and lifecycle risk. - Eligibility to obtain a U.S. security clearance if required by the program.
