### Introduction We value candidates who have significant experience with managing complexity, working independently, and are motivated by hard problems. ### **What We Offer** - The ability to have real impact on mission-critical workflows - The chance to use state-of-the-art tech to solve novel problems with mission partners - The opportunity to define your role through time as we grow - Competitive salary and equity upside with annual merit refreshes based on impact **Position Overview** As a Software Engineer Intern, you’ll work alongside our engineering team to build ConductorAI’s core application: a user-facing web platform for large-scale document search, review, and AI-powered workflows. You’ll contribute to real production systems, including document-processing pipelines, agentic workflow execution, database scaling, and applications that push state-of-the-art LLMs to their limits. This is a product engineering role as much as a systems role. You’ll help design and build intuitive interfaces for complex, document-centric workflows and see how the software you build is used to solve real problems across defense, government, and regulated commercial environments. You won’t be confined to low-stakes intern projects. You’ll be trusted with meaningful work on our product’s critical path and given the opportunity to own features from problem definition through implementation. You’ll work closely with experienced engineers who will provide mentorship and technical guidance while giving you the autonomy to experiment, learn quickly, and take on increasingly challenging problems. We’re looking for interns with strong computer science fundamentals, a generalist mindset, and the curiosity and drive to learn new technologies quickly. This internship is intended to be a pathway to future opportunities at ConductorAI. Strong performers may have the opportunity to return for additional internships or co-ops or join the team full-time after graduation. **Location** This internship is open to candidates based in the US, with a strong preference for candidates who can work from our **NYC or DC offices** for the summer. ### **Key Responsibilities** - Build and improve search, review, and AI-powered agents for accuracy and consistency - Build polished, reliable user-facing features in our Next.js/React application - Develop backend APIs, data models, and workflow execution paths that support responsive frontend experiences - Write high-quality, maintainable code alongside a small team of experienced engineers - Contribute to the design and architecture of production systems - Own meaningful features and technical problems from initial idea through implementation - Work closely with engineers, product teammates, and users to understand problems and help translate them into product improvements - Learn quickly, ask thoughtful questions, and take increasing ownership as you become familiar with our product and codebase ### **Qualifications** - US citizenship required; this role supports work subject to US government contract obligations and export control regulations (ITAR/EAR) - Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field - Strong computer science fundamentals and demonstrated software engineering ability through internships, coursework, research, projects, or other experience - Proficiency in at least one modern programming language, with an ability and willingness to work across our Python and TypeScript/React stack - Strong problem-solving skills and an ability to learn unfamiliar technologies quickly - Strong written and verbal communication skills - Product-minded approach with an interest in building software that is intuitive and useful - Proactive, high-ownership mindset and willingness to tackle challenging, ambiguous problems ### **Nice to Haves** - Previous software engineering internship or meaningful experience building and shipping software - Experience with Python, TypeScript, React, or Next.js - Experience building with LLMs, AI agents, RAG, or other AI engineering techniques - Experience with backend systems, APIs, databases, or distributed systems - Familiarity with document processing or search/retrieval systems - Experience contributing to open-source software, research, technical clubs, hackathons, or substantial personal projects - Experience working in a startup or other fast-paced technical environment - Interest in defense, intelligence, national security, or other complex operational domains - Active or current security clearance

## Company Overview Lydian is developing the lowest cost sustainable fuels from waste CO2, water, and renewable electricity to decarbonize the aviation industry. Our breakthrough technology replaces oil and gas refining with fully electrified, modular, and flexible reactor systems that produce fuel with 95% lower emissions than traditional jet fuel. Since our founding in 2021, Lydian has achieved key milestones in record time, including the production of our first liquid fuel from our pilot system, capable of producing 10,000 gallons of fuel per year for a fraction of the capital and time of alternative approaches. We are building a motivated, diverse, and collaborative team that is passionate about addressing the growing climate crisis and is committed to excellence in their work. In particular, we look for tenacious people who are energized by solving the hardest, highest impact problems that come their way. ## Position Overview Lydian is looking for a 6-month Coatings Engineer/Scientist Co-op for Spring 2027 to develop and optimize coating materials, including slurry formulation, monolith coatings, and coatings characterization, as well as optimization and scale-up of these methods to enable pilot-scale demonstrations. In this role, you will work at the intersection of materials chemistry and process engineering, developing slurries that can be applied uniformly and reliably to ceramic substrates and then survive demanding high-temperature operation. You will interface with engineers and scientists across various domains in order to inform your experimental design and research priorities, and your work will directly determine how our catalysts are manufactured at scale. This is an hourly position based in Boston, MA and has a minimum commitment of 6-months. The role is fully in-person and hands-on in the lab. ## Responsibilities - Development of slurry coatings with different powders, binders, rheology modifiers and solvents, including characterization of slurry properties (e.g., viscosity, particle size, solids loading) and their effect on coating quality - Application of coatings to monolith substrates and evaluation of coating loading, uniformity, adhesion, and thermal stability - Scale-up of promising formulations to coat large substrates (catalyst monoliths > 5 in long), translating small-sample recipes into repeatable processes for full-size parts - Working effectively with partners, including automotive catalyst suppliers, to develop scalable manufacturing techniques and transfer Lydian coating processes to partner equipment - Using advanced characterization techniques (e.g., microscopy, XRD, surface area and porosity, thermal analysis) to develop understanding of materials and coatings, and working with external partners who can perform some techniques under our guidance - Building, upgrading, and maintaining coating and materials test equipment as needed to support experiments - Collaborating with the other projects to understand and incorporate requirements and cooperatively solve problems, particularly with the catalyst synthesis and reactor teams - Documenting procedures and results, analyzing data, and communicating findings and recommendations to the team ## Qualifications - B.S. or M.S. candidate in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Ceramic Engineering, or related field - Hands-on, proactive mentality when it comes to lab work and pushing ideas forward - Interest in high-temperature materials science. Experience in slurry formulation and coatings (e.g., washcoating, dip coating, rheology, dispersion of ceramic powders) preferred but not necessary - Understanding of reaction kinetics, heat transfer, and mass transport at an undergraduate level; familiarity with heterogeneous catalysis concepts is a plus - Experience documenting experimental procedures, collecting data and performing statistical analyses of datasets - Focus on safety and assessing/mitigating risks when running experiments in a lab, including handling of fine powders, solvents, and high-temperature furnaces - Curiosity, eagerness to learn, and a proactive mindset; comfortable asking questions and taking initiative in an environment where procedures are still being developed - Strong written and verbal communication skills for sharing results with a cross-functional team - Desire to work in a fast-paced environment and solve interesting technical problems ## **Company culture and benefits** - Paid lab/engineering-focused internship with a collaborative in-person technical team - Challenging, meaningful work that can directly impact company success - Opportunities for networking/exposure within the climate tech community - Mentorship from a great team of engineers and scientists

role: Student Marketeer - Savannah College of Art and Design (SCAD), Atlanta
description: BE A BRAND & PRODUCT AMBASSADOR Live and breathe the brand personality traits and company values, representing the brand in a premium way through everyday interactions with consumers or customers. Build and execute a tailored and innovative campus plan that engages students and brings the brand to life at your university. Create a strong network on and around your campus, establishing and maintaining relationships with key local individuals. Identify local collegiate content creators in relevant Red Bull scenes and work with your FMS to bring them into the World of Red Bull. Grow the user base by inviting positive trial and awareness of Red Bull through product sampling to consumers at the right place and right time - answering any questions and concerns from consumers. Work at Red Bull events, collegiate activations, and supported events to help ensure an unforgettable brand experience for consumers. Build awareness and encourage participation in the World of Red Bull, including collegiate events and activations. Increase brand engagement on your Social Media handles through authentic content. BE A SALES EXPERT Build relationships with local sales account managers and ensure Red Bull is available and visible in outlets, on your campus and in your region. Collaborate with sales to open new distribution points for Red Bull within your university campus and beyond. Leverage relevant assets from the world of Red Bull in order to keep us top of mind in sales accounts. Ensure perfect execution of defined store standards. EXECUTIONAL EXCELLENCE Deliver executional excellence and show love for the details in all areas of your role. Share ideas and collaborate with your team through regular face-to-face and online interaction. Plan & report your activities in the dedicated online platform in a timely manner and with accuracy. Contribute to business development by providing local insights, trends and overall opportunities. Must be at least 18 years of age Must have a valid US driver’s license University or college enrollment required Must be fluent in English, additional languages an advantage Able to work flexible part-time hours, including some evenings and weekends for a minimum of 15 hours per week Immersed in student life with an understanding of the collegiate landscape and local city, including behind-the-scenes activities & hot-spots Connected with a diverse range of influential groups and individuals on campus Affinity for project management, working 'behind the scenes’, and winning sales A team player, willing to represent Red Bull with branded outfits and onboard the Red Bull Mini Employees may be required to lift and/or move items weighing 25 pounds or more, as needed. The hourly rate for this position is $16.00/ hour. The hourly rate is subject to change and may be modified. Red Bull North America, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status, age, or any other classification protected by Federal, state, or local law. As a Red Bull Student Marketeer, you are part of the most dynamic and empowered brand and product ambassador program in the world. Reporting to the local Field Marketing Specialist (FMS), you will learn Red Bull’s target group and are responsible for driving the brand image and product understanding on your campus and in the region. You will reach new consumers, excite university students, increase sales, and drive visibility of the Red Bull brand. This includes direct contact with consumers and customers, inviting product trials, and working at Red Bull events to ensure an unforgettable brand experience for consumers. Student Marketeers value flexibility over a 9 to 5 job and love to work in a creative and inclusive working atmosphere.

description: Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states. Software Engineering builds the brains of Waymo's fully autonomous driving technology. Our software allows the Waymo Driver to perceive the world around it, make the right decision for every situation, and deliver people safely to their destinations. We think deeply and solve complex technical challenges in areas like robotics, perception, decision-making and deep learning, while collaborating with hardware and systems engineers. ## **About AlayaCare** At AlayaCare, we’re more than just a fast-growing SaaS company, we’re a team of people passionate about transforming home healthcare. Our cloud-based platform empowers care providers around the world to deliver better outcomes for their clients. With 550+ employees across Canada, the US, Australia, and Brazil, we’re united by a shared mission and a strong culture of transparency, growth, and human connection. Whether you're early in your career or a seasoned expert, AlayaCare offers the opportunity to grow your impact, your skills, and your career. ## **About the Role** We are seeking a Security Analyst Intern to join our AlayaCare’s Security & Privacy team division. Reporting to the Director, Information Security and Privacy, As a Security Analyst Intern, you will support the protection of the company’s systems, data, and customers. In this role, you will gain hands-on exposure to real-world cybersecurity operations within a fast-growing B2B SaaS healthcare environment, while contributing to the ongoing strengthening of AlayaCare’s security posture. You will collaborate with experienced security professionals and cross-functional teams across the organization, assisting with initiatives related to security operations, governance, risk management, and compliance. Through this experience, you will develop practical skills and a strong understanding of how modern cloud-based security programs operate at scale. This internship offers the opportunity to contribute to meaningful security initiatives while developing hands-on experience across security operations and governance. Our team members have the opportunity to do their best work and to grow their careers, in a high-growth company, while making an impact in an industry that genuinely helps people. This role is based in Montreal. At AlayaCare, our hybrid model includes 2 set in-office collaboration days/week, and it is expected that team members are present in the office on those days to foster connection, innovation, and teamwork. ## **What You’ll Do** - Monitor and triage alerts from security tooling and help investigate suspicious activity across our platform. - Support incident response activities by helping analyze events, gather evidence, and document findings. - Track and help drive remediation of vulnerabilities and security findings across cloud and application environments. - Assist in reviewing AWS security configurations and identifying opportunities to improve our cloud security posture. - Contribute to collecting and organizing evidence for compliance frameworks such as SOC 2 and HITRUST. - Support identity and access reviews to ensure the right people have the right level of access. - Participate in vendor security reviews and help assess third-party security risks. - Help maintain and improve internal security documentation, playbooks, and operational procedures. - Assist with phishing simulations and internal security awareness initiatives. - Build and maintain simple dashboards or reports that help track security metrics and operational health. - Research new security threats, vulnerabilities, and defensive techniques relevant to modern SaaS platforms. - Collaborate with engineers, infrastructure teams, and product teams to help continuously improve AlayaCare’s security posture. ## **What You Bring to the Team** - Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, or a related technical field. - Strong curiosity for cybersecurity and how modern cloud and SaaS platforms are built and secured. - Solid understanding of networking, operating systems, authentication, and common security vulnerabilities. - Comfortable working in Linux environments and using scripting or programming languages such as Python. - Interest in automation and improving security workflows through code and tooling. - Exposure to cloud platforms (AWS preferred), Git, or modern development workflows is a strong plus. - Curious about AI and emerging technologies, and how they can improve security operations and enhance productivity. - Analytical mindset with the ability to investigate problems and communicate findings clearly. - Demonstrates grit, ownership, and persistence when tackling unfamiliar problems. - Relevant certifications such as Security+, Network+, eJPT, or AWS Cloud Practitioner are considered an asset. - Participation in Capture The Flag (CTF) competitions, HackTheBox, TryHackMe, bug bounty programs, or open-source security projects is strongly encouraged. - Strong communication and collaboration skills in both French and English, with the ability to communicate clearly with technical and non-technical audiences. English fluency is required to collaborate effectively with colleagues, clients, and partners outside Quebec, where English is the primary working language. **What will make you stand out for this internship** - You have built scripts, tools, or small automations that made security or system tasks easier. - You have explored cloud environments (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and understand how security works in a modern SaaS stack. - You are curious about how AI can improve security operations, detection, or developer workflows. - You maintain projects, experiments, or write-ups on GitHub, a blog, or similar platforms. - You enjoy learning by doing — building labs, breaking things, and figuring out how they work. ## Why Join AlayaCare? ### **Work With Purpose** At AlayaCare, you’ll help build technology that empowers care providers and improves outcomes for patients and families. Every line of code and every customer interaction contributes to making care more connected, accessible, and human. ### **Grow in a High-Trust Culture** We believe in transparency, feedback, and assuming positive intent. Here, you’ll feel safe to share your ideas and career goals, and be supported to achieve them through mentorship, career mobility, and a promote-from-within philosophy. ### **Inclusive by Design** We celebrate diverse perspectives and foster belonging through our DEIB initiatives. Employee-led events, summits, and social activities — both in-person and virtual — create meaningful connections across our global teams. ### **Location and Work Model** This role is based in **Montreal at our offices on** 4200 Boulevard Saint-Laurent. AlayaCare hybrid model includes a minimum of in-office days to foster connection, innovation, and teamwork. ### **Ready to Join Us?** Apply today and be part of a company that makes a real difference in the future of home and community care. role: Human-Centered AI Research Intern, Causal Reasoning Models
description: At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences. This is a paid 12-week internship opportunity and is a hybrid, in-office role. [Here’s a glimpse into the Internship experience from some of our TRI interns!](https://www.tri.global/tri-internship-program) At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team in Human-Centered AI, Large Behavior Models, Robotics, Automated Driving, Energy & Materials and Human Interactive Driving. **The Team** This internship opportunity falls within the Adaptive Behavior Systems team of Human-Centered AI Division (HCAI). We are an integrated team of ML researchers and social and behavior scientists. At the core of our work, we aim to enable decisions through human-centered AI that advance collective well-being for people and the planet. **The Internship** We are seeking a highly motivated and talented PhD research intern to join our adaptive behavior systems team to push the boundaries of causal reasoning in LLMs. The intern will collaborate with our interdisciplinary team of machine learning, behavioral, and social scientists to study how well language-based generative machine learning models can reason causally and to develop methods for testing and improving causal reasoning. The project will be focused on researching in a specific sub-area of the overall goal, towards publication in a top-tier venue. The intern will further engage in strategy discussions about how the research connects to business impact at Toyota. This is a Winter 2027 paid 12-week internship opportunity. Please note that this internship will be a hybrid in-office role. ### Responsibilities - Perform research and publish in a relevant venue. Publication target venues include NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CLeaR, UAI, and COLM, with ACL or EMNLP where the contribution is primarily linguistic, and TMLR as a journal option. Findings may also be presented at ACIC or EuroCIM. The exact topic is to be finalized with the mentor. - Take ownership of the project from project inception and ideation to validation of the developed methods. - Collaborate cross-functionally with researchers in multiple fields to research and develop technology that leverages generative AI to understand human behavior. ### Qualifications - Ph.D. student in related fields - AI/ML, computer science, data science, statistics, or related field. - Publication record or demonstrated research experience in causal inference (structural causal models, identification, counterfactual reasoning). - Hands-on experience with one or more of: LLM evaluation and benchmarking; mechanistic interpretability; and methods for improving LLM reasoning, including prompting and prompt optimization, post-training (supervised fine-tuning or reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards), pretraining, or architectural changes. - Experience with Python programming and DL frameworks like Pytorch. - Interest in human-centered research (e.g. behavioral science, computational social science), including qualitative and/or quantitative methods such as experiments and user studies. - Excellent communication and teamwork skills.

# ABOUT CYVL The best infrastructure is invisible. You only notice it when it fails. For decades, the people responsible for our roads, bridges and sidewalks have been asked to manage the physical world with tools that can't see it. Cyvl is the Physical AI company changing that. We build purpose-built sensors, computer vision and AI that turn every drive into current data: what exists, where it is and what condition it's in. 500+ cities and towns use our Infrastructure Intelligence Platform to direct the work and fix problems before they fail. 1 in 30 Americans drive on roads managed with Cyvl data. The proof isn't a dashboard. It's a smoother commute, a safer walk to school and public dollars going where they matter most. We're a fast-moving team in Boston building hardware, software and AI for the real world. If you believe technology's highest calling is public good, come build with us. # THE ROLE You'll join the Data Operations team, the group that turns raw street-level capture into the map layers 500+ cities rely on. Every day, sensor data from the field flows through our processing pipelines and comes out as road conditions, sidewalk inventories, sign catalogs, and pavement scores. You'll own pieces of that pipeline: running deliveries end to end, catching data problems before a customer does, and writing the scripts that make the next delivery faster than the last. ## WHAT YOU'LL DO - Process customer deliveries end to end: run geospatial data through our Python pipelines, validate the output, and publish the final layers to the Cyvl platform. - Build QC checks that review data automatically. - Investigate failed and stalled processing jobs in our AWS pipelines, find the root cause, and document the fix. - Automate recurring manual steps into repeatable scripts and runbooks, and measure the time saved. - Partner with engineering and customer success to turn field-reported issues into code fixes or process improvements. ## WHAT YOU BRING - Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Data Science, or a related field - Proficiency in Python; comfortable writing scripts that read, transform, and validate data - Comfort working in a terminal and with version control - Available full-time for 10-12 weeks in Summer 2027, based in our Somerville office ## NICE TO HAVE - GIS experience (QGIS or ArcGIS, and formats like GeoJSON, shapefiles, GeoPackage) - Familiarity with cloud infrastructure, especially AWS - SQL and experience querying real datasets - Exposure to geospatial Python libraries (geopandas, shapely) - Interest in civic infrastructure, transportation, or public-sector technology - A knack for the business side: you think about how data drives decisions and like problems like "how do we track this better" or "how do we make this visible to the team" - Experience building dashboards or turning data into something a non-technical person can act on # WHY CYVL **Hard tech. Real streets. Your name on it.** - **Hard problems in the real world.** You build end-to-end: our own hardware, software and AI, with work that shows up on the street in the real world. - **Ownership that compounds.** You own outcomes, not tasks. You work directly with customers and across our team, and you'll own more, sooner, than almost anywhere else. - **Intense, with heart.** We're building a category, so it's not a place to coast. We also take care of each other, have genuine fun together, and believe in what we are doing. ## WHAT WE ASK - **Cross lanes.** "Not my job" doesn't exist here. - **Own without a playbook.** The plan is still being written, often by you. - **Try, miss, try again.** We make big bets. Some won't land, and we learn fast. - **Be in the room.** We're on-site in Somerville about 90% of the time. We're a startup building a category. If that sounds like the draw, not the risk, we'd love to talk. ## OUR VALUES - **Real:** Authentic and transparent. Focused on solving real problems with simple, effective solutions. - **All Out:** Bold, driven, and committed to delivering results that matter. - **Accelerating:** Always learning, growing, and moving with intention. - **Reliable:** We follow through and deliver at a consistently high bar. - **Empowering:** We lift each other up and help governments build infrastructure they can be proud of. ## SEE OUR WORK - [How Atlanta cut downtown potholes by 60%](https://cyvl.com/case-studies/atlanta-ga) - [How Buffalo turned a campaign promise into a paving plan](https://cyvl.com/case-studies/buffalo-ny) - [How to rebuild US infrastructure smarter](https://www.theengineer.co.uk/content/opinion/how-to-rebuild-us-infrastructure-smarter-and-stronger) ## WANT TO GO THE EXTRA MILE? (OPTIONAL) If you're excited about this role and want to tell us more, email with the subject line "Data Ops Intern, [Your Name]" and answer any or all of these: 1. Why Cyvl, and why a startup? What draws you to this kind of work, and to a small team where your work ships right away? 2. What's the coolest thing you've built with AI? A class project, side project, script, or experiment all count. Tell us what it did and what you learned. 3. Tell us about a time you solved a problem by fixing the process instead of just working harder. What was slowing you down? What did you change? What happened? A few honest paragraphs beat an AI-slop essay. Links to code, notebooks, or demos are welcome. **We build for every community, so we hire from all of them.** The best people for this work come from different backgrounds, paths, and places, and many of them don't check every box. If this role excites you, apply anyway. If you need an adjustment to our interview process, tell us and we'll make it work.

### **Relay Launchpad Intern: Software Engineer - Device Team** [Relay](https://relaypro.com/), a dynamic and rapidly growing tech startup based in Raleigh, NC is on a mission to revolutionize frontline work. For decades, technology has supercharged the desk worker while leaving behind the 80% of the global workforce who don’t sit at a desk. The builders, the caregivers, the operators, the movers—the frontline—still rely on walkie-talkies, paper notes, and shouted instructions. At Relay, we believe it’s time for a change. Our smart, rugged radios and connected cloud ecosystem harness the power of voice and AI to close this digital chasm. We’re building tools that meet frontline workers where they are, capturing tribal knowledge, and turning communication into action. By transforming every spoken word into intelligence, we’re delivering safety, productivity, and empowerment to the workers who keep our world moving. We are looking for a Software Engineer Intern who is a motivated and ambitious undergraduate (or graduate) student with an expected graduation date of December 2027 or Spring 2028 to join our mobile device product team. You'll collaborate with engineers in a high-growth environment, working on custom communication devices at the heart of the Relay platform, from application-layer features to deep OS and hardware integration. Interns will gain hands-on experience across the full device stack, from Android application development and OS-level systems programming to embedded firmware and Linux hardware interfaces — contributing to a product that ships to real customers every 6 weeks. We work with a diverse set of languages, including C, C++, Java, Kotlin, Rust, and Bash/Python. Our devices run Android on custom in-house hardware, and our development environments are Linux-based. Our culture is based on Impact, Team, and Learning. #### **What You Will Do** You'll work on product development for Relay's custom communication devices — Android-based hardware designed entirely in-house. We own the full stack, from hardware to software, and ship updates to customers approximately every 6 weeks. Depending on your background, you'll contribute across one or more layers: - **Android** — fix bugs and build new features spanning application development (Kotlin, Java) and OS-level programming, which may touch the Linux Kernel, Java-based frameworks, shell scripts, or C/C++/Rust daemons - **Linux OS** — work below the Android layer on operating system tasks and hardware interfaces - **Embedded systems** — develop new embedded products or microcontroller firmware that runs inside or alongside existing Relay devices #### **What You Will Bring** - Currently enrolled in a Computer Science or related technical field with a **GPA of 3.5 or above.** - Strong proficiency in C, Java, or Kotlin. Android/AOSP systems programming experience is a plus but not required — if you're a solid developer with a Linux systems background, you can learn Android. - Or experience in embedded systems programming — e.g., NRF or ST-based products running Zephyr, ThreadX, or Linux. - Or experience programming Linux at or below the POSIX API layer, typically in C/C++ (Rust experience is increasingly relevant as AOSP adopts it). - Or solid experience with scripting languages such as Bash, Python, or similar. - Familiarity with IP networking concepts (HTTP, TCP/UDP sockets) is preferred. - Comfort with desktop and server Linux distributions — our development environments and internal tooling are Linux-based. - An analytical, methodical approach to problem-solving. - Strong communication skills and a habit of documenting what you build. - Ability to manage multiple workstreams and self-prioritize. - Exposure to Agile development practices. - Genuine curiosity and drive to learn. #### We use AI tools to transcribe and summarize interviews for internal hiring purposes. Transcripts are accessible only to authorized hiring personnel and retained consistent with our data retention policies. Candidates who prefer not to have AI notetaking used may request to opt out without impact to your candidacy. For more information, please see our Candidate and Employee Privacy Notice [linked here.](https://relaypro.com/legal/candidate-privacy-notice/)

role: Civil Engineering Assistant - Coop Student (Traffic Engineering)
description: You’re a civil engineering student who’s ready to get your hands on a real engineering project. You perform best in groups where you know what’s expected of you. Binnie is looking for an Engineering Assistant to join our Traffic Engineering Division, which provides traffic engineering services for traffic operations reviews, traffic safety studies, traffic modelling and analysis, transportation planning reports, and traffic management studies. Some recent assignments include traffic engineering support on the Owner’s Engineer Team for the Pattullo Bridge Replacement and Fraser River Tunnel Projects, traffic management support on the Broadway Subway Line, and traffic modelling support for TransLink’s new rapid bus lines. You will be a member of our diverse team in a challenging role that offers mentorship opportunities. YOUR ROLE: Modifying basic design drawings in AutoCAD and Civil 3D Completing field assignments as required by Project Managers Performing design calculations as required by Project Managers and Engineers Preparing technical reports under the direction of Project Managers and Engineers Plotting, assembling, and delivering drawing submission packages Preparing project documentation including hard copy and electronic file transfers Maintaining file naming and layer management conventions set by Binnie Completing quality control procedures WHAT YOU BRING: Previous work experience in a civil engineering environment is preferred. Currently completing Degree in Civil Engineering (3rd year student or equivalent preferred) Previous exposure to AutoCAD and Civil 3D is preferred. We’re small enough to know each other’s names, and big enough to be where we’re needed. As an employee-owned firm, which has been recognized as a great employer for many years, we take pride in our work and are respected as one of the top engineering firms in British Columbia. We support some of the most important infrastructure in the province and beyond. We’re looking for professionals who want to build careers and communities that last. We can’t do it without you. **Overview** Inferact's mission is to grow vLLM as the world's AI inference engine and accelerate AI progress by making inference cheaper and faster. Founded by the creators and core maintainers of vLLM, we sit at the intersection of models and hardware, a position that took years to build. **About the Role** We're looking for exceptional University of Waterloo co-op students who want to work on the systems that determine how fast, efficiently, and reliably frontier AI models run on frontier workloads at scale. This is not a sandboxed internship project. We will match your strengths and interests to a real engineering problem across the vLLM stack, from model execution and low-level accelerator code to distributed serving and the cloud platform that makes it all usable. You'll work alongside the creators and core maintainers of vLLM on work intended to ship into open source, production systems, or the tooling that supports both. You will have a primary technical track, meaningful ownership, and mentorship from a small, senior team, with opportunities to collaborate across models, compilers, accelerators, networking, and distributed systems. The goal is to let exceptional students learn at the frontier while making contributions used by developers and AI teams around the world. **Potential Focus Areas** Your co-op will have a primary home in one of the following tracks, with opportunities to contribute across others: - **Inference Runtime:** Bring new model architectures and inference techniques to life in vLLM. Implement ideas from research papers; support mixture-of-experts, multimodal, diffusion, and agentic workloads; and improve scheduling, continuous batching, KV-cache memory management, prefix caching, and hybrid model serving. - **Performance & Scale:** Build the distributed serving data plane that lets vLLM run across many GPUs and nodes. Work on tensor, expert, or context parallelism; prefill/decode separation and KV-cache transport; fault tolerance and multi-tenancy; and high-performance communication using NCCL, DeepEP, NVSHMEM, RDMA, or InfiniBand. - **Kernel Engineering:** Raise the hardware performance ceiling by writing and optimizing attention, GEMM, sampling, KV-cache, fused, and quantization kernels. Use CUDA, Triton, TileLang, CUTLASS/CUTE, or related tools; reason about memory hierarchy, occupancy, and tensor cores; and prove speedups through profiling, correctness tests, and reproducible benchmarks. - **AMD GPU Performance:** Help make vLLM first-class on AMD accelerators. Work across ROCm, HIP, Triton, CK, AITER, kernels, runtime paths, quantization, compiler integration, and performance-regression infrastructure while learning how AMD-specific execution, memory, and toolchain constraints shape inference. - **TPU Performance:** Help make vLLM fast and correct on Google TPUs. Build backend, runtime, and compiler integrations with JAX, XLA, Pallas, MLIR, and related tooling; inspect compiler artifacts; work on lowering, fusion, and code generation; and benchmark production-relevant serving across correctness, latency, and throughput. - **Cloud Orchestration:** Build the operational platform that makes large-scale inference deployable and reliable. Work on Kubernetes and custom operators, topology-aware GPU scheduling, zero-downtime vLLM rollouts, token-aware routing, observability, infrastructure-as-code, automated recovery, and bring-your-own-cloud or multi-cloud fleet management. You are not expected to arrive with experience in every track. We care most about unusual depth or learning velocity in one area, strong fundamentals, and evidence that you can turn a difficult problem into working, measurable software. **Skills and Qualifications** Minimum qualifications: - Currently pursuing a bachelor's, master's, or PhD degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics, or a related technical field, and eligible for a University of Waterloo co-op work term. - Strong programming ability in Python, C++, Rust, Go, or another systems-oriented language. - Strong computer science fundamentals and the ability to learn from research papers, technical documentation, and complex systems code. - Evidence that you have built and debugged nontrivial software through coursework, research, a prior internship, open-source work, or an ambitious side project. - A builder mindset: you define what success means, measure results, validate correctness, communicate clearly, and keep iterating until the system works. Preferred qualifications: - Depth in at least one relevant area such as ML or inference systems, distributed systems, GPU or accelerator programming, compilers, high-performance computing, operating systems, networking, Kubernetes, or cloud infrastructure. - Hands-on experience with one or more relevant technologies such as PyTorch, vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, CUDA, Triton, TileLang, ROCm/HIP, JAX/XLA, Pallas, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, Ray, or SLURM. - Experience profiling or benchmarking software, validating numerical or systems correctness, or building tests that protect against performance regressions. - Experience with systems beyond a single local process or device, including multi-GPU, multi-node, research-cluster, high-throughput, or production-like workloads. Bonus points if you have: - Contributed to open-source ML, systems, compiler, or infrastructure projects, especially vLLM or adjacent projects. - Built a research system, benchmark suite, compiler or kernel project, distributed service, or infrastructure tool that demonstrates unusual technical depth and initiative. - Worked across more than one layer of the stack and enjoy moving between algorithms, runtimes, systems, and hardware rather than staying inside a single abstraction. - Created a technical artifact such as a paper, design document, blog post, demo, or talk that clearly explains what you built and what you learned. **Meet Inferact at Waterloo** Interested in learning more about Inferact, vLLM, and the engineering problems you could work on during your co-op? Join us for our **University of Waterloo Employer Information Session** to meet the team, learn more about Inferact, and hear about the Inference Engineering Co-op opportunity. - **Venue:** Tatham Centre, Room 2218 - **Date:** Monday, October 5, 2026 - **Time:** 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM ET **Logistics** - **Location:** San Francisco, California. This co-op is in-office only at Inferact's San Francisco office and is intended for the University of Waterloo co-op program. - **Work term:** Co-op / internship. Exact dates will align with the applicable Waterloo work term. - **Compensation:** Competitive compensation based on the applicable co-op market and candidate background, plus a housing stipend for the duration of the co-op term. ***Inferact, Inc. is an E-Verify company, and you may review the*** [***Notice of E-Verify Participation***](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1TWSDK2aZycxydMvPle230QSwuQtuNIyM/view?usp=sharing) ***and the*** [***Right to Work posters in English and Spanish***](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1WxUM6hcXhb3CuJ_nWgnMmHF99XsuT9sI/view?usp=sharing)***.***

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. **ABOUT THE JOB** We are looking for a Systems Engineer Co-op to join our rapidly growing team. In this role, you'll get hands-on exposure to how Anduril develops technical strategy and executes complex, integrated hardware and software programs — from pre-award demonstrations through early contract phases and full execution. You'll support a multi-disciplinary engineering team working toward efficient development and delivery of solutions for our customers. You'll gain exposure to how systems engineering spans company boundaries in an agile, CI/CD-oriented development approach, balancing the development of new capabilities with the integration of existing Anduril technologies. You'll also see firsthand how technical status gets communicated to customers and leadership throughout a program's lifecycle. Systems Engineering at Anduril touches every phase of program execution — from proposals through design reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR), qualification testing, and delivery — and spans disciplines including mechanical, thermal, structural, electrical, software, firmware, GNC, reliability, and manufacturing (integration and test). A strong Systems Engineer Co-op is someone who's technically curious across disciplines and eager to learn how these pieces fit together across a program's full lifecycle. **WHAT YOU'LL DO** You will own one or more scoped projects end to end, with mentor support, over the engagement. Candidate projects include: - **Trade study support** — Perform a system-level trade study balancing risk, cost, and performance for a defined design decision. Deliverable: trade study writeup and recommendation reviewed by the engineering team. - **Requirements decomposition exercise** — Take a defined complex system requirement and decompose it into executable sub-requirements, under mentor guidance. Deliverable: requirements decomposition document validated against an existing design. - **Design review support** — Prepare supporting technical materials for an upcoming design review (SRR, PDR, or CDR) for a defined subsystem. Deliverable: review package contribution and follow-up action summary. - **Test planning support** — Support the development of qualification or acceptance test requirements and pass/fail criteria for a defined component, including coordination with a vendor or subsystem owner. role: Internship in Stretchable Electronics & Optics for Artificial Skin Demonstrators - 4 to 6 months
description: Joining Mines Saint-Étienne means committing to an institution where science and innovation build a more sustainable future . It is a school of excellence where everyone has the opportunity to unlock their full potential and contribute to tackling the challenges of tomorrow . Ranked among the top engineering schools in France and recognized worldwide, our school, a member of the Institut Mines-Télécom , educates the talents of tomorrow while actively addressing major industrial, digital, and environmental challenges. By joining us, you become part of a community of 500 members of staff, 2,500 students and take part in an ambitious project: combining academic excellence, cutting-edge research, and positive societal impact. The Institut Mines-Télécom brings together France’s leading Grandes Ecoles to tackle major industrial, digital, energy, and environmental challenges. With its eight public Grandes Écoles and two affiliated Graduate Schools, it is the leading public institute dedicated to engineers and managers. Together, we imagine and build a sustainable future by educating the leaders who will shape tomorrow’s transitions. 🎯 What we expect from you ? As an intern, you will perform innovation and research activities in the field of soft electronics for eskin applications. Within this centre of Microelectronics and the flexible electronics department, you will combine your passion for science and for societal impact. The flexible electronics department develops technological and scientific knowledge in the field of soft electronics. The department has a strong knowledge in the field of material and interface electrical and mechanical characterization. The activities of the department are regrouped in the 660m2-area platform. This technological platform regroups facilities and technological equipment for R&D activities in Micropackaging, micro and nano-electronics, in a clean room of 220m² 1000-class and 400m² 10000-class. Stretchable electronics can also be declined with optical systems such as waveguides. These devices will be developed within the project in order to create an artificial skin with pressure and temperature sensing capabilities. Within this project , our work will focus on the fabrication and characterization of stretchable optical waveguides as well as fabrication and integration techniques of optical components (LEDs / Photodiodes). Related publication is “Transparent, Optical, Pressure‐Sensitive Artificial Skin for Large‐Area Stretchable Electronics” . An important part of the work will be: · Update our characterization setup è knowledge in Python and electronics (Arduino & Rasperry Pi) is important · Fabrication and characterization of these waveguide (elastomer) for pressure or temperature sensors applications. · Integration of optically pressure or temperature sensitive material into the elastomer waveguide · Characterization of the complete devices. Fabrication process and experimental setups are already existing. However, knowledges in Python is important in order to use these test benches. Hands-on lab work is essential , and will be partly performed in our clean room facility. Demonstrations of radically new devices, possessing features and functions that cannot be achieved with existing electronics would be the exciting outcome of this work. 🔍 What we are looking for ? You hold a: · Master and engineer students in engineering sciences, electronics and embedded systems, material science or a related field. And you have: • Basic knowledge of electronic design and circuitry would be highly appreciated • You should be autonomous, curious, and passionate about technological innovation. • A strong interest in practical work and experimentation is essential, along with the ability to develop a rigorous scientific approach in the spirit of a "maker" culture. • Knowledge in bioelectronics is an asset 🌍 Why join Mines Saint-Étienne ? We support each of our employees on the path to excellence, with the conviction that together, we can have a lasting and significant impact on our world. Joining Mines Saint-Etienne is the opportunity to find: • A stimulating environment: Cutting-edge experimental resources, a welcoming working environment and a solid international network (T.I.M.E., EULIST). • A real impact: Contractual research projects worth €11 million/year, mainly with industrial partners, A science culture centre, La Rotonde , which has been committed to science outreach for 25 years, welcoming over 50,000 visitors per year. • 75% of public transportation costs covered (subject to conditions), • Staff lounge (Sports and cultural activities, employee benefits for leisure and social events) • 1 day off per month (to be taken subject to the supervisor’s approval) 📩 Apply now ! • Application deadline : January 10, 2027 • Internship duration : 4 to 6 months • Start date : beginning in March 2027 • Internship location : Gardanne (13) – France • Compensation : hourly rate of €4.50 per hour of actual work Applications must be submitted via the RECRUITEE platform by January 10, 2027 This position is open to all, with accommodations available upon request for candidates with disabilities. As part of its Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion policy, the École des Mines de Saint-Étienne is an employer committed to ensuring equal treatment of all applicants. Candidates selected for an interview will be notified as soon as possible. description: **Datadog AI Research — Scholars Program with Carnegie Mellon University** Datadog AI Research (DAIR) is partnering with Carnegie Mellon University to support a small number of PhD students working on open research problems grounded by ongoing efforts at Datadog/DAIR. You will frame a problem, run your own experiments, and write up what you find, with compute and data at a scale most academic labs cannot provide. You will collaborate with colleagues working on the same questions. **The Lab And The Research:** DAIR is an industrial research lab motivated by practical challenges in observability and software operation: detecting and diagnosing failures, understanding complex production environments, and helping engineers operate software more effectively. The lab focuses on creating specialized foundation models, post-training and evaluating AI agents, and building frontier-scale machine learning systems. By combining fundamental research with Datadog's large-scale, real-world data and infrastructure, the lab develops new AI capabilities and translates them into practical systems with meaningful impact. Internship projects are shaped with your DAIR mentor and your CMU faculty advisor. You do not need prior experience with observability, monitoring, or infrastructure. **What You'll Do:** - Own a research project end to end: framing the question, running the experiments, writing it up - Work directly with a DAIR mentor engaged in the same problem, and stay connected to your advisor and lab - Publish, and use the work toward your dissertation - See research reach production, when it works **Who You Are:** - Currently enrolled in a PhD program at Carnegie Mellon in machine learning, computer science, statistics, or a related field - Depth in at least one area relevant to the research above - Comfort running real experiments — training models, working with GPUs, reading and reimplementing recent papers - Evidence you can do research: conference or workshop papers, preprints, open-source contributions, or a lab project you can discuss in depth - Research taste. You can explain why a problem matters and what would change if it were solved. - Honest empiricism. You report the ablation that didn't work. - Support from your faculty advisor. **Not Required:** - A long publication record. How you think matters more than how much you've published. - Observability, monitoring, or SRE background. - A perfect match to the areas above. Datadog values people from all walks of life. We know not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That’s okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your experience, we encourage you to apply. *This job is available in various departments within our company; to conform to US export control regulations, some of these roles may require candidates to be eligible for any required authorizations from the US government.* **If possible, please apply using your personal email address instead of your university email address.** Students can sign up for a [free Datadog Pro account](https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/datadog-github-student-developer-pack/) to learn more about our platform and products. #LI-Hybrid Datadog offers a competitive salary for this role and may include additional compensation elements. role: Summer Placement Student - Ground Engineering - Leeds (FY27)
description: Our Ground Engineering team in the United Kingdom and Ireland (UK&I) comprises 150 professionals who provide a comprehensive range of services, including project management, feasibility studies, ground investigation design and interpretation, detailed design, contract administration, and construction supervision. We work on ground engineering projects across the UK&I and internationally, supporting both internal and external clients. Our primary focus areas include energy, water, nuclear (decommissioning and new build), power, road and rail, aviation, ports and harbours, as well as commercial and industrial developments, and landslip investigation and remediation. We work for leading UK and International clients, including National Grid, BP, Sellafield, Associated British Ports, Transport Scotland, National Highways, Transport Infrastructure Ireland, Network Rail, and local authorities, as well as for prominent contractors and developers. Our impressive portfolio features a range of regional and national projects, such as the Great Grid Upgrade, STEP Fusion, pumped storage hydro projects in the Scottish Highlands, Snowdonia VIP, A83 Rest and be Thankful, M54-M6 Link Road, water schemes for various water utilities clients (UK&I) and HMNB Devonport redevelopment. Additionally, we are involved in overseas projects such as Eastlink in Sweden. As a Ground Engineering intern at AECOM, you will contribute to a variety of projects, gaining hands-on experience in activities such as: Support Ground Investigation Projects – Assist with desk studies, site inspections, rockface surveys, and geomorphological mapping. Help plan and procure ground investigations, and support senior staff in supervising on-site activities. Data Collection and Analysis – Contribute to the gathering, management, and interpretation of geological and geotechnical data using tools such as Openground for data management and Leapfrog for 3D geological modelling. Technical Reporting – Assist in preparing interpretative and design reports, ground models, and technical documentation, ensuring accuracy and adherence to relevant guidelines and standards. Design Support – Help in the design and assessment of foundations, retaining walls, slope stability, earthworks, and rock slope stabilisation under the guidance of experienced engineers and geologists. Numerical Modelling – Develop skills in 2D and 3D numerical analysis using AECOM’s software packages, supporting geotechnical modelling and simulations. Tender Documentation – Assist in preparing Ground Engineering tender documents for construction. E.g., Works Requirements and drawings Collaboration and Teamwork – Work alongside multidisciplinary teams, including engineers, engineering geologists, and environmental specialists, to deliver integrated project solutions. Health, Safety, and Sustainability Awareness – Apply health and safety practices during site and office-based tasks, with consideration for environmental and sustainability principles in all project work. Currently pursuing a degree in Civil Engineering, Engineering Geology, or Geology, with an expected 2:1 classification (or equivalent) or higher. Proficient in Microsoft Office; experience with AutoCAD or Civil 3D is advantageous but not essential. Strong interest in geotechnics and enthusiasm for engaging with multi-disciplinary colleagues and clients. Willing to travel for work, including visits to project sites and possibly other AECOM offices. Effective communicator in English, skilled in writing, presenting, creating drawings, and preparing reports. Highly organised, able to prioritise tasks, and work collaboratively within a team or independently with initiative. Creative, practical, and detail-oriented, with a methodical approach to problem-solving, planning, and design. Comfortable using computers for design work and calculations. Driven to achieve excellent results for clients and the business, while balancing project goals, budgets, and timelines. Aware of health & safety, environmental, and sustainability considerations in engineering. A clean driving licence is a plus but not essential. Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible, as CVs will be reviewed, and candidates selected on a rolling recruitment basis for either immediate or advanced offer starts. Please include a covering letter with your application, detailing all predicted and/or obtained academic grades, the dates you are able to work (to/from), and the locations you are interested in. We support and encourage office attendance across all grades to foster a collaborative working culture and facilitate on-the-job learning for early career staff. You must have the right to work in the UK. At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment. About AECOM AECOM is the world’s trusted infrastructure consulting firm, delivering professional services throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. On projects spanning transportation, buildings, water, new energy and the environment, our public- and private-sector clients trust us to solve their most complex challenges. Our teams are driven by a common purpose to deliver a better world through our unrivaled technical and digital expertise, a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, and a commitment to environmental, social and governance priorities. role: Industrial or Summer Placement Student - Ground Engineering - Birmingham (FY27)
description: Our Ground Engineering team in the United Kingdom and Ireland (UK&I) comprises 150 professionals who provide a comprehensive range of services, including project management, feasibility studies, ground investigation design and interpretation, detailed design, contract administration, and construction supervision. We work on ground engineering projects across the UK&I and internationally, supporting both internal and external clients. Our primary focus areas include energy, water, nuclear (decommissioning and new build), power, road and rail, aviation, ports and harbours, as well as commercial and industrial developments, and landslip investigation and remediation. We work for leading UK and International clients, including National Grid, BP, Sellafield, Associated British Ports, Transport Scotland, National Highways, Transport Infrastructure Ireland, Network Rail, and local authorities, as well as for prominent contractors and developers. Our impressive portfolio features a range of regional and national projects, such as the Great Grid Upgrade, STEP Fusion, pumped storage hydro projects in the Scottish Highlands, Snowdonia VIP, A83 Rest and be Thankful, M54-M6 Link Road, water schemes for various water utilities clients (UK&I) and HMNB Devonport redevelopment. Additionally, we are involved in overseas projects such as Eastlink in Sweden. As a Ground Engineering intern at AECOM, you will contribute to a variety of projects, gaining hands-on experience in activities such as: Support Ground Investigation Projects – Assist with desk studies, site inspections, rockface surveys, and geomorphological mapping. Help plan and procure ground investigations, and support senior staff in supervising on-site activities. Data Collection and Analysis – Contribute to the gathering, management, and interpretation of geological and geotechnical data using tools such as Openground for data management and Leapfrog for 3D geological modelling. Technical Reporting – Assist in preparing interpretative and design reports, ground models, and technical documentation, ensuring accuracy and adherence to relevant guidelines and standards. Design Support – Help in the design and assessment of foundations, retaining walls, slope stability, earthworks, and rock slope stabilisation under the guidance of experienced engineers and geologists. Numerical Modelling – Develop skills in 2D and 3D numerical analysis using AECOM’s software packages, supporting geotechnical modelling and simulations. Tender Documentation – Assist in preparing Ground Engineering tender documents for construction. E.g., Works Requirements and drawings Collaboration and Teamwork – Work alongside multidisciplinary teams, including engineers, engineering geologists, and environmental specialists, to deliver integrated project solutions. Health, Safety, and Sustainability Awareness – Apply health and safety practices during site and office-based tasks, with consideration for environmental and sustainability principles in all project work. Currently pursuing a degree in Civil Engineering, Engineering Geology, or Geology, with an expected 2:1 classification (or equivalent) or higher. Proficient in Microsoft Office; experience with AutoCAD or Civil 3D is advantageous but not essential. Strong interest in geotechnics and enthusiasm for engaging with multi-disciplinary colleagues and clients. Willing to travel for work, including visits to project sites and possibly other AECOM offices. Effective communicator in English, skilled in writing, presenting, creating drawings, and preparing reports. Highly organised, able to prioritise tasks, and work collaboratively within a team or independently with initiative. Creative, practical, and detail-oriented, with a methodical approach to problem-solving, planning, and design. Comfortable using computers for design work and calculations. Driven to achieve excellent results for clients and the business, while balancing project goals, budgets, and timelines. Aware of health & safety, environmental, and sustainability considerations in engineering. A clean driving licence is a plus but not essential. role: Research Intern, Compiler Instrumentation with hardware assistance for Morphing
description: Helsinki System Security Lab (HSSL) Internship Compiler Instrumentation with hardware assistance for Morphing Dynamic code randomization and code morphing (churned randomization, encryption in memory) are effective mechanisms to thwart memory attacks in the AI era, where machine learning has proven to be very effective to find shortcomings (bugs) in deployed software, and 50-70% of all bugs in C/C++ code are still today memory safety issues. In this work we will use new hardware architecture (instructions) to prototype solutions that by a combination of code randomization and encryption makes it harder for an attacker to pinpoint the location where to apply an exploit in deployed code in the field. Primarily this project relates to compiler instrumentation to leverage existing architecture and instructions in in-house hardware. The work may also encompass augmenting hardware emulators (such as QEMU) for testing the compiler instrumentation results with standard benchmarking tests. If selected, the intern will be working with experienced security experts in the Helsinki System Security Laboratory, and plan, design and implement the work under their guidance. This work is conducted as a internship where the results are not necessarily public-facing (closed IP), i.e., without further negotiation the results of this research may be chosen to remain proprietary, and therefore is not immediately suitable e.g. as a . topic or part of a PhD studies. We are looking for: A student who has completed most of their . courses, in the field of CS/E.Eng, or a recent graduate / PhD student Compiler familiarity, e.g. through coursework or prior exposure to LLVM / GCC modifications An understanding of low-level (system / OS) architecture, and hardware emulators is considered a plus Sufficient skills to work and interact in English Good team-working skills The following we count as advantage: Background (courses) in compiler technology, hardware architecture, platform security, cryptography or equivalent An interest to do research and explore new challenges. Location and internship period: This is a 6-month internship based at our Helsinki, Ruoholahti office. The Helsinki Systems Security Laboratory in Huawei Finland (HSSL) drives renewal and mastery in the field of platform / device related security technologies for consumer devices such as mobile phones and PCs. Our topical expertise lies in hardware-assisted memory protection, trustworthy execution (processor isolation primitives, hypervisor, TEE, kernel hardening), as well as functionality like device key management, attestation and integrity. We are also making inroads in the areas of security testing and AI protection on terminal devices

role: Junior Performance Engineer Meet- en Regeltechniek (Starter / Young Professional)
description: Je komt terecht bij MEET RIVM, binnen Strukton Nederland dé specialist in gebouw gebonden onderhoud voor het nieuwe RIVM‑complex op het Utrecht Science Park. MEET RIVM is een organisatie in opbouw. Dat betekent dat je niet alleen meewerkt, maar ook meedenkt over hoe processen, planning en samenwerking het beste worden ingericht voor de exploitatiefase. Je werkt volledig op locatie samen met collega’s uit onderhoud, beheer, contractmanagement en externe partners. De lijnen zijn kort, de verantwoordelijkheden duidelijk en jouw rol is essentieel voor een stabiele operatie. Zo maak je het verschil Je bent nieuwsgierig, leergierig en hebt interesse in techniek en data. Verder herken jij jezelf in: Een afgeronde mbo 4 of hbo‑opleiding of bijna afgestudeerd, bijvoorbeeld in elektrotechniek, installatietechniek, mechatronica of werktuigbouwkunde. Interesse in meet- en regeltechniek, gebouwbeheersystemen of automatisering. Affiniteit met data, duurzaamheid en slimme gebouwen. Een analytische mindset en de drive om dingen te begrijpen en te verbeteren. Je werkt graag samen en durft vragen te stellen. Ervaring is mooi meegenomen, maar zeker geen must. Zo investeren wij in jouw ontwikkeling Bij MEET RIVM en Strukton draait het om groeien. Daarom krijg je: Training on the job met begeleiding van ervaren collega’s. Extra technische opleidingen wanneer nodig. Deelname aan het Strukton Starters Programma voor young professionals. Samen optrekken met andere starters binnen Strukton. Trainingen op vakinhoud, persoonlijke ontwikkeling en samenwerken. Tijd en ruimte om bewust te werken aan jouw groei van young professional naar professional. Dit bieden wij jou Bij MEET RIVM krijg je veel verantwoordelijkheid en de ruimte om jouw expertise verder te ontwikkelen. Een goed salaris tussen €3.400,- en € 4800,- per maand, afhankelijk van je ervaring. 30 vakantiedagen per jaar volgens de Bouw & Infra CAO. Een ruim keuzebudget boven op je salaris, inclusief vakantiegeld. Jij kiest: extra vrije dagen (tot 13 extra) of extra inkomen. Een goede pensioenregeling met werkgeversbijdrage bij bpf bouw. Zit je nu in een ander fonds? Houd er rekening mee dat bpf bouw op 1 januari 2026 al overstapte op het nieuwe pensioenstelsel. Volop opleidings- en ontwikkelmogelijkheden, zowel technisch als persoonlijk. Flexibele werktijden en de mogelijkheid om hybride te werken; Woon je niet om de hoek? Geen probleem. Wij vergoeden je reiskosten per kilometer, zodat je zorgeloos op pad kunt. Fiets voordelig naar je werk met een leasefiets via onze regeling. Werken op een unieke, maatschappelijk relevante locatie in Utrecht. Onze locatie is ontzettend goed bereikbaar met het OV en met de fiets. Wij adviseren dan ook hier gebruik van te maken. Er zijn eventueel wel (betaalde) parkeermogelijkheden in de buurt, maar wij beschikken niet over een eigen parkeerplaats. Voor deze functie vragen we een Verklaring Omtrent het Gedrag (VOG) — niet spannend, wél belangrijk om samen een veilige en vertrouwde werkomgeving te waarborgen. Enthousiast geworden? Solliciteer nu! Heb je vragen over deze functie of wil je meer weten over MEET RIVM? Neem gerust contact op met Martine Bom, Teamlead Recruitment, via +31 (0)6 15 00 24 81. Solliciteren Klinkt dit als jouw nieuwe uitdaging? Wacht dan niet langer en solliciteer vandaag nog door op Solliciteer te drukken! Wij kijken ernaar uit om jou te ontmoeten! Heb je je cv nog niet klaar? Geen probleem, je kunt ook zonder cv solliciteren en deze later alsnog toesturen. Bij Strukton geloven we dat diversiteit en inclusie bijdragen aan een sterkere organisatie. Wij bieden gelijke kansen aan iedereen en streven naar een werkomgeving waarin verschillen worden gewaardeerd, talent zich kan ontwikkelen en iedereen zich welkom voelt. #LI-MB1 Kickstart jouw carrière in meet- en regeltechniek Sta jij aan het begin van je carrière en wil je werken met slimme techniek en data in een van de meest hightech gebouwen? Zoek je een baan waarin je niet meteen alles hoeft te kunnen, maar wél alles kunt leren? Dan is dit jouw next step. Als Performance Engineer Meet- en Regeltechniek bij MEET RIVM, onderdeel van Strukton Nederland, krijg je de kans om je te ontwikkelen tot specialist in het optimaliseren van gebouwprestaties. Je werkt in en aan het nieuwe RIVM‑gebouw op het Utrecht Science Park: een van de meest complexe en duurzame gebouwen van Nederland. Hier leer je on the job, krijg je gerichte technische opleidingen én neem je deel aan het Strukton Starters Programma. Samen met andere young professionals groei jij van starter naar professional. Dit Maak jij Je komt te werken bij MEET RIVM, dé beheer- en exploitatiepartner van het RIVM‑complex in Utrecht. Een team van technische specialisten dat dagelijks samenwerkt op locatie. De sfeer is open, de lijnen zijn kort en er is veel ruimte om vragen te stellen en initiatief te nemen. Omdat MEET RIVM nog volop in ontwikkeling is, mag jij actief meedenken over processen, tooling en verbeteringen. Je staat er nooit alleen voor: je werkt samen met ervaren engineers, onderhoudsteams en projectleiders die jou begeleiden in jouw groei. Dit ga je leren en doen In deze rol leer je hoe meet- en regeltechniek, data en gebouwprestaties samenkomen. Stap voor stap groei je in verantwoordelijkheden. Denk aan: Analyseren van meet- en trenddata uit gebouwbeheersystemen en leren hoe je deze vertaalt naar concrete verbeteringen. Meewerken aan het opzetten en door ontwikkelen van dashboards en KPI‑rapportages binnen GBS-, BMS- en EMS‑omgevingen. Dagelijkse monitoring van technische installaties zoals klimaat-, energie- en regelsystemen. Samenwerken met onderhoudsteams en servicepartners en leren hoe je verbeteracties uitzet en opvolgt. Testen en controleren van sensoren en regelkringen, zodat data betrouwbaar is. Meedenken over slimme regelstrategieën, energie‑optimalisatie en comfortverbetering. Vastleggen van analyses en resultaten, zodat iedereen kan sturen op dezelfde inzichten. Je hoeft dit niet allemaal al te kunnen. Wij zorgen voor begeleiding, training en tijd om te leren.

As a junior engineer, you'll work across a diverse software portfolio—improving UIs, adding optimization workflows, fixing C++ bugs, and building MCP servers for LLM integration—rather than being tied to one product. You will work across our software portfolio rather than on a single product. On any given week that might mean improving the UI of a simulation control tool, adding a new optimisation workflow, fixing a bug in a C++ codebase, or building an MCP server that exposes one of our tools to an LLM agent. UI quality and AI-friendliness are both priorities here, and they reinforce each other. A well-designed tool with clear inputs, predictable behaviour, and informative feedback is easier for a scientist to use and easier for an LLM to drive reliably. You will think about both audiences. Part of your work will be making our existing tools usable by AI agents, designing tool interfaces that behave well when an LLM is at the controls, and building agent pipelines that integrate with our simulation workflows. We also have new projects to start from scratch. As you build familiarity with the domain and demonstrate ownership, there is genuine opportunity to lead one of those projects end-to-end. No prior background in simulation or optimisation is expected. The domain is learnable and we will support that process. What matters is that you are genuinely curious, pick things up quickly, and enjoy building tools that serious technical users depend on. C++ Programming Language; BS in Computer Science or applicable experience; must be fluent in English. Minimum 1-4 years experience in this type of role and preferably in the semi-conductor industry. For over four decades, Silvaco, based in Silicon Valley, California and with global locations around the world has solved semiconductor design challenges by offering affordable and competitive TCAD (Technology Computer Aided Design) software, EDA (Electronic Design Automation) software, proven design IP (intellectual property), and world class support to engineers and researchers across the globe.
